Then Baldr and Höðr will come from Hel. They will all sit together and talk, recalling their secrets and speaking of past events, of the Midgard serpent and of Fenrir, and they will find in the grass the golden chess pieces the Æsir once owned. In a place called Hoddmímir's wood two people, Líf and Lífþrasir — 'life' and 'one striving for life' — will have hidden from Surtr's fire, living on the morning dew, and from them will come so many descendants that the whole world will be peopled. And the sun, before the wolf swallows her, will bear a daughter as fair as herself, who will drive her mother's course.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第53章。

body_zh: 高座上的人最后说：如果你还能问得更远，我不知道你会从哪里得到答案，因为我从没听说过有谁能讲述世界更遥远的未来。愿你好好利用你所听到的这一切。就在这时，甘格勒里听见四面八方传来巨大的声响。他转过身去，四下张望，却发现自己站在一片空旷的原野上，什么大厅也没有，什么城堡也看不见了。他回到自己的国家，把他的所见所闻讲给人们听，这些故事就这样一代代地流传下来。斯诺里在全书开头曾说，阿萨神族是从亚洲迁来的人，用这些故事迷惑了古鲁菲；这个框架让故事以“幻象”的形式结束，也让这位基督徒作家能够在不认同古老信仰的前提下，把这些神话记录下来。可是那些故事本身——众神的诞生与死亡，世界的毁灭与重生——就这样被保存了下来，成为后人了解北欧神话最重要的文献之一。
body_en: The figure on the high seat says at last that if Gangleri can ask further, he does not know where the answer will come from, for he has never heard anyone tell more of the world's future; let him make good use of what he has learned. Then Gangleri hears great noises all around him, and when he looks about he finds himself standing on an open plain, with no hall and no stronghold to be seen. He returns to his own kingdom and tells what he has seen and heard, and the stories are passed on from man to man. Snorri's framework, which presents the Æsir as men from Asia who beguiled Gylfi, lets the tales end as an illusion and lets a Christian author record them without endorsing the old faith. Yet the stories themselves — the birth and death of the gods, the destruction and renewal of the world — were preserved, and became one of the most important sources for Norse myth.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第53–54章。

heading_en: The wolves swallow sun and moon
body_zh: 接着，最可怕的事情发生了：一直追赶着太阳的狼吞下了太阳，人们会觉得这是巨大的灾难；另一只狼抓住了月亮，也造成了巨大的破坏。在斯诺里讲世界起源的时候，他已经说过，这两只狼一只叫斯库尔，一只叫哈提，它们日日夜夜在天上追逐日月，太阳和月亮之所以走得那么快，正是因为害怕被它们追上。现在它们终于得手了。星星从天空中消失了。然后，大地剧烈地震动起来，树木被连根拔起，高山崩塌，所有的锁链和束缚都断裂了。被众神用魔法锁链格莱普尼尔束缚的巨狼芬里尔挣脱了出来——当年为了把它锁住，战神提尔把自己的右手放进了狼嘴里作为担保，失去了这只手。现在，什么也挡不住它了。被锁在岩石上、受着毒液折磨的洛基，也在这时挣断了锁链。世界的秩序，从这一刻开始崩溃。
body_en: Then will happen what seems the greatest disaster: the wolf will swallow the sun, and the other wolf will seize the moon and do great harm. Snorri has told earlier, in his account of the world's beginning, that two wolves, Sköll and Hati, chase the sun and moon across the sky, which is why they move so fast. Now they catch them. The stars vanish from the sky. Then the earth shakes so that trees are uprooted and mountains crash down, and every fetter and bond breaks. The wolf Fenrir, bound by the gods with the magic fetter Gleipnir — for which Týr gave his right hand in pledge — runs free, and nothing can hold him now. Loki too, bound to the rocks and tormented by venom, breaks loose. From this moment the order of the world begins to fall apart.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

heading_en: The ship of dead men's nails
body_zh: 大海翻腾着涌上陆地，因为尘世巨蛇耶梦加得在巨人般的狂怒中翻滚着，爬上了岸。耶梦加得是洛基的孩子，众神曾把它扔进环绕世界的大海，它在海底长得那么大，竟然绕着整个人间一圈，咬住了自己的尾巴。这时，一条名叫纳吉尔法的船也挣脱了缆绳。这条船是用死人的指甲造成的。斯诺里在这里插进了一句告诫：所以，如果有人死的时候指甲没有剪，就会给纳吉尔法号增添材料，而众神和人们都希望这条船晚一点造成。在汹涌的洪水中，纳吉尔法号漂浮起来，驾驶它的是巨人赫利姆。巨狼芬里尔张开大嘴向前冲去，它的上颚碰到了天空，下颚贴着大地，如果还有更大的空间，它还会张得更大；它的眼睛和鼻孔里喷着火焰。尘世巨蛇喷出的毒液弥漫了天空和海洋，可怕至极。它就在巨狼的身旁。
body_en: The sea surges onto the land, because the Midgard serpent, Jörmungandr, writhes in giant rage and comes ashore — Loki's child, cast by the gods into the ocean round the world, where it grew until it encircled the earth and bit its own tail. Then the ship Naglfar is loosed. It is made of dead men's nails, and Snorri adds a warning: if a man dies with untrimmed nails, he adds much material to Naglfar, which gods and men alike would wish finished late. In the flood Naglfar floats, and the giant Hrymr steers it. Fenrir advances with gaping mouth, his upper jaw against the sky and the lower against the earth — he would gape wider if there were room — and fire blazes from his eyes and nostrils. The Midgard serpent spits so much poison that sky and sea are spattered with it, terrible to see, and it is at the wolf's side.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

body_zh: 在这一片喧嚣之中，天空裂开了，穆斯贝尔之子们从裂缝中骑马而来。穆斯贝尔是世界最南方的火焰之国，在世界形成之前就已经存在，那里炽热明亮，不是那片土地上出生的人根本无法进去。守卫着它的边界的，是一个名叫苏尔特的巨人。现在，苏尔特骑在最前面，他的前后都燃烧着火焰；他手中的剑非常耀眼，比太阳还要明亮。当他们骑马越过连接人间和众神之城的彩虹桥比弗罗斯特时，桥断裂了——斯诺里早先就说过，这座桥虽然坚固，却经不住穆斯贝尔之子们的马蹄。穆斯贝尔之子们一路前进，来到了一片名叫维格利德的平原上。巨狼芬里尔和尘世巨蛇也来到了这里。洛基和赫利姆也来了，赫利姆身后跟着所有的霜巨人，而洛基带领着冥界女王赫尔的全部人马。穆斯贝尔之子们自成一支队伍，那支队伍光芒四射。维格利德平原的长和宽都有一百里格，众神与巨人的最后决战，将在这里展开。
body_en: Amid the din the sky splits open and the sons of Muspell ride through. Muspell is the realm of fire in the south, which existed before the world was made, so bright and burning that none not born there can enter, and its border is guarded by Surtr. Now Surtr rides in front with fire burning before and behind him; his sword is brilliant, brighter than the sun. As they ride over Bifröst, the rainbow bridge between earth and the gods' city, it breaks, as Snorri said earlier it would beneath the sons of Muspell. They advance to the plain called Vígríðr, where Fenrir and the Midgard serpent also come. Loki and Hrymr are there too, Hrymr with all the frost giants and Loki with all Hel's people, while the sons of Muspell form a battle array of their own, shining brightly. The plain of Vígríðr is a hundred leagues each way, and there the last battle of gods and giants will be fought.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

body_zh: 当这一切发生的时候，众神的守望者海姆达尔站了起来。他住在彩虹桥边，日日夜夜守护着众神之城，他的耳朵能听见草在地上生长、羊毛在羊身上生长的声音，眼睛在夜里也能看见一百里格远。现在，他举起了加拉尔号角，用尽全力吹响。号角声响彻九个世界，唤醒了所有的神。众神聚在一起举行会议。奥丁骑着马来到密米尔之泉，向密米尔请教自己和他的部下应该怎么办——当年他曾为了喝一口智慧之泉的水，把自己的一只眼睛留在了那里。这时，世界之树伊格德拉西尔颤抖起来，天上地下，没有一样东西不感到恐惧。斯诺里在这里又引用了《女巫的预言》：海姆达尔高高地吹响号角，号角举在空中；奥丁和密米尔的头颅交谈；高耸的白蜡树伊格德拉西尔在颤抖，古老的树在呻吟，巨人挣脱了束缚。阿萨神族和英灵殿的战士们披上了铠甲，拿起了武器，向维格利德平原进发。
body_en: As all this happens, Heimdall, the gods' watchman, stands up. He dwells by the rainbow bridge guarding the gods' city; he can hear grass growing on the earth and wool on sheep, and see a hundred leagues by night. Now he blows a mighty blast on the Gjallarhorn and wakes all the gods, and they hold a council. Odin rides to Mímir's well to seek counsel for himself and his people — the well where long ago he left an eye for a drink of its wisdom. The ash Yggdrasil shakes, and nothing in heaven or on earth is without fear. Snorri quotes the Seeress's Prophecy again: Heimdall blows loud, his horn aloft; Odin speaks with Mímir's head; the ash Yggdrasil trembles, the old tree groans, and the giant is loose. The Æsir and all the einherjar arm themselves and advance to the plain.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

body_zh: 众神的队伍向维格利德平原进发，走在最前面的是奥丁。他头戴金盔，身穿美丽的锁子甲，手握长矛冈格尼尔，径直向巨狼芬里尔冲去。雷神索尔走在奥丁身边，可是他帮不了父亲，因为他自己有一场搏斗要打：他要与尘世巨蛇耶梦加得决一死战。索尔和巨蛇是宿敌：索尔曾经和巨人许米尔一起出海，用牛头作饵钓起了巨蛇，差一点就用锤子打死了它，可惜许米尔吓得割断了钓线，让巨蛇逃回了海里。现在，他们终于要一决胜负了。丰饶之神弗雷与苏尔特交战，两人展开了一场激烈的搏斗，可是弗雷倒下了。斯诺里说，弗雷之所以战死，是因为他没有了自己的那把好剑——当年他为了娶巨人的女儿格尔德，把那把能自己挥舞作战的宝剑送给了仆人斯基尼尔。如今在最需要它的时候，他却赤手空拳，只能用一只鹿角来作战。
body_en: The gods advance to Vígríðr, and Odin rides in front with a golden helmet, a beautiful mail-coat and his spear Gungnir, and goes against the wolf Fenrir. Thor is at his side but cannot help him, for he has his hands full fighting the Midgard serpent — his old enemy, which he once hooked from the sea with an ox-head as bait while fishing with the giant Hymir, and would have killed with his hammer had not Hymir in terror cut the line. Freyr fights Surtr, and there is a hard struggle before Freyr falls. Snorri says his death is due to his lack of the good sword he gave to his servant Skírnir to win the giant's daughter Gerðr, a sword that would fight by itself; at the hour of need he has none.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

heading_zh: 提尔与加姆，索尔与巨蛇
heading_en: Týr and Garmr, Thor and the serpent
body_zh: 这时，被锁在格尼帕洞穴前的猎犬加姆也挣脱了锁链。斯诺里说，它是世上最大的灾祸。加姆与战神提尔交战，两个互相杀死了对方——这位曾经为了束缚芬里尔而失去右手的勇敢的神，最终和另一头恶兽同归于尽。另一边，雷神索尔与尘世巨蛇展开了殊死搏斗。索尔举起雷神之锤妙尔尼尔，一次又一次地砸向巨蛇的头，终于杀死了它。可是巨蛇临死前向他喷吐了大量的毒液。索尔从巨蛇身边走开了九步，就倒在地上死去了。斯诺里引用的诗句这样写：大地之子——索尔——走了九步，从无所畏惧的毒蛇身边离开。这位一生守护着众神和人类、与无数巨人搏斗过的雷神，在打死了他最可怕的敌人之后，也倒在了战场上。众神的阵营里，一个个最强大的战士都在倒下。
body_en: Then the hound Garmr, bound before the cave Gnipahellir, breaks loose — the worst of monsters, says Snorri. He fights Týr, and each kills the other: the brave god who lost his right hand binding Fenrir dies together with another beast. Thor slays the Midgard serpent with his hammer Mjöllnir, but steps away only nine paces before he falls dead to the earth from the poison the serpent has spat at him. The verse Snorri quotes says that the son of Earth, Thor, walked nine steps from the serpent that feared no shame. The thunder god who guarded gods and men all his life and fought countless giants falls after killing his most terrible enemy; one by one the strongest of the gods are falling.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

body_zh: 巨狼芬里尔张开大嘴，一口吞下了奥丁。众神之父就这样死去了。可是立刻，奥丁的儿子维达大步走上前来。维达平时沉默寡言，被称作沉默之神，却非常强壮，几乎和索尔一样有力，众神在危难的时刻常常依靠他。他把一只脚踏进巨狼的下颚。在这只脚上，他穿着一只特别的鞋，这只鞋是用人们做鞋时从脚趾和脚跟处裁下来的边角皮料拼成的，从世界开始以来就在收集。斯诺里说：所以，想要帮助阿萨神族的人，就应该把这些碎皮料扔掉。维达用一只手抓住巨狼的上颚，用力一撕，把狼嘴撕成了两半，巨狼就这样死了。奥丁的仇报了。与此同时，洛基与海姆达尔交战，两个互相杀死了对方。洛基——那个曾经和众神同饮、又一次次陷害众神、害死了巴德尔的诡计之神——终于在最后的战斗中，死在了众神的守望者手里。
body_en: The wolf swallows Odin, and that is his death. But at once Víðarr, Odin's son, strides forward — the silent god, almost as strong as Thor, on whom the gods rely in every peril. He sets one foot in the wolf's lower jaw. On that foot he wears a shoe that has been gathered through all time from the scraps people cut from their shoes at toe and heel; therefore, says Snorri, anyone who wants to help the Æsir should throw those scraps away. With one hand Víðarr seizes the wolf's upper jaw and tears its mouth apart, and that is the wolf's death; Odin is avenged. Loki fights Heimdall, and each kills the other: the trickster who drank with the gods, betrayed them and brought about Baldr's death dies at last at the hands of the gods' watchman.
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

body_zh: 最后，苏尔特把火焰抛向大地，整个世界都燃烧起来。众神死了，巨人死了，英灵殿的战士们死了，人类也都死了。斯诺里再一次引用《女巫的预言》，描绘这最后的景象：太阳变黑了，大地沉入大海，明亮的星辰从天上坠落；烟雾翻滚，火焰吞噬着养育生命的世界之树，高高的火光直冲天空。在斯诺里的讲述中，这一刻世界彻底毁灭了：从混沌的金伦加鸿沟中诞生的世界，众神用巨人尤弥尔的身体造成的大地和天空，奥丁的英灵殿，索尔的雷声，人类的城市，全都在火焰和洪水中消失了。甘格勒里听到这里，心中充满了恐惧，他问：天空、大地和整个世界都被烧毁了，众神和英灵殿的战士们以及所有的人类都死了，那以后还会有什么呢？你们不是说过，每个人都将在某个世界里永远活下去吗？
body_en: Then Surtr flings fire over the earth and burns the whole world. Gods, giants, the einherjar and all mankind die. Snorri quotes the Seeress's Prophecy once more: the sun turns black, earth sinks into the sea, the bright stars fall from the sky; steam rages and fire, the nourisher of life, and high flame plays against heaven itself. In Snorri's telling the world that rose from Ginnungagap, the earth and sky the gods made from the giant Ymir's body, Odin's Valhalla, Thor's thunder and the cities of men all vanish in fire and flood. Gangleri, filled with dread, asks what will be after heaven and earth and all the world are burned and the gods, the einherjar and all mankind are dead — for had they not said that every man would live in some world for ever?
evidence_note: 《欺骗古鲁菲》第51章。

body_zh: 西古尔德在丹麦国王希亚尔普雷克的宫中长大，母亲约尔迪斯嫁给了国王的儿子阿尔夫，国王一家都非常爱护这个孩子。萨迦说，他是所有人中最出众的少年，人人都喜欢他。他的养父是一个名叫雷金的人，雷金是赫雷德玛的儿子，身材矮小，像矮人一样，却是一个手艺高超的铁匠，又聪明又狡猾，精通各种技艺。雷金教西古尔德下棋、学卢恩文字、说多种语言，这些都是王子应该学的本领。有一天，雷金对西古尔德说：你的养父们对你不够好，你应该向他们要一匹马。西古尔德去向国王要马，国王说：你自己去挑吧，想要哪一匹都行。第二天，西古尔德走进森林，遇到了一个长着长胡子的老人，老人问他要去哪里。西古尔德说要去挑马。老人说：我们一起把马群赶进布西尔塔恩河里去吧。他们把马群赶下河，所有的马都游回了岸上，只有一匹灰色的骏马留在水里，不肯回来。老人说：这匹马是斯雷普尼尔的后代，好好养它，它会成为最好的马。说完，老人消失了。西古尔德给这匹马取名格拉尼。萨迦说，那个老人就是奥丁。
body_en: Sigurðr grew up at the court of King Hjálprekr of Denmark, whose son Álfr married his mother Hjördís, and he was the most outstanding of youths, loved by all. His foster-father was Reginn, son of Hreiðmarr, small in stature like a dwarf, a master smith, wise, cunning and skilled in every art, who taught him chess, runes and many tongues, as befitted a king's son. Reginn told him his foster-kin treated him meanly and he should ask for a horse; the king told him to choose any he liked. In the forest Sigurðr met a long-bearded old man who suggested they drive the horses into the river Busiltjörn. All swam back to land except a grey stallion that stayed in the water. The old man said the horse was of Sleipnir's kin and should be reared well, for it would be the best of horses, and vanished. Sigurðr named the horse Grani; the old man, says the saga, was Odin.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第13章。

body_zh: 西古尔德骑着格拉尼向南走，来到了辛达山。他看见山上有一片光亮，像火焰一样照亮了天空。走近一看，那里有一座用盾牌围成的城堡，上面飘着一面旗帜。他走进盾牌堡，看见一个人全副武装地躺着睡觉。他先取下那人的头盔，才发现原来是一个女人。她身上的铠甲非常紧，仿佛已经长进了肉里。西古尔德用格拉姆从领口往下，再沿着两只袖子，把铠甲割开，铠甲像布一样被剑划开了。她醒了过来，坐起身，看见了西古尔德，问道：是谁割开了我的铠甲，把我从睡梦中唤醒？是西格蒙德的儿子西古尔德吗？他手里拿着法夫纳的头盔和杀死法夫纳的武器。西古尔德说：是一个沃尔松格家的人。她告诉他，她叫布伦希尔德，是一个女武神。从前有两个国王打仗，一个叫赫亚尔姆贡纳，奥丁答应让他获胜；另一个叫阿格纳尔。布伦希尔德却在战斗中杀死了赫亚尔姆贡纳，让阿格纳尔赢了。奥丁大怒，用一根睡眠之刺刺了她，让她沉睡，还宣布她再也不能在战斗中赢得胜利，必须出嫁。她却发誓：她只嫁给一个不知道恐惧的人。
body_en: Sigurðr rode south to Hindarfjall, where a light shone like fire up to the sky. There stood a shield-burg with a banner above it, and inside lay a sleeping warrior in full armour. When he took off the helm he saw it was a woman. Her mail was so tight it seemed grown into her flesh; he cut it with Gram from the neck down and along both sleeves, and it parted like cloth. She woke and asked who had cut her mail and roused her from sleep — was it Sigurðr, son of Sigmundr, with Fáfnir's helm and his slayer's sword? He said he was of the Völsungs. She told him she was Brynhildr, a valkyrie: two kings had fought, Hjálmgunnarr, to whom Odin had promised victory, and Agnarr; she had felled Hjálmgunnarr and given Agnarr the victory, and Odin in anger pricked her with a sleep-thorn, decreed that she would never again win victory in battle and must be married. But she had vowed to marry no man who knew fear.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第20章。

body_zh: 西古尔德请布伦希尔德教给他智慧，因为她知道世界上的一切事情。布伦希尔德端来一角蜜酒，说：这是一杯满含力量与荣耀的酒，里面混着咒语和卢恩。她教给他各种卢恩：胜利的卢恩要刻在剑柄和剑刃上，同时两次念诵提尔的名字；酒的卢恩能防止被别人的妻子欺骗；助产的卢恩能帮助妇女分娩；海的卢恩要刻在船首和舵上，能保护船只平安；肢体的卢恩能治病；言语的卢恩能让人在议会上不受仇人陷害；心智的卢恩能让人比所有人都聪明。她又给了他许多忠告：对亲人要宽厚，即使他们冒犯了你也不要报复；不要发虚假的誓言，因为违背誓言会带来可怕的后果；不要在会议上与愚人争吵；路过时遇到死人要好好安葬他们；不要相信杀了你亲人的人的儿子，哪怕他们还年幼，因为狼可能藏在小孩的身体里；要提防朋友的背叛。西古尔德说：世上再没有比你更聪明的人了，我发誓，我要娶你为妻，因为你最合我的心意。布伦希尔德说：即使我能在所有的男人中选择，我也宁愿选择你。他们互相发了誓，西古尔德骑马离开了。
body_en: Sigurðr asked Brynhildr to teach him wisdom, for she knew the tidings of all the worlds. She brought a horn of mead full of might and fame, mixed with spells and runes, and taught him the runes: victory-runes to carve on hilt and blade while twice naming Týr; ale-runes against another's wife's deceit; help-runes for women in childbirth; sea-runes on prow and rudder to keep ships safe; limb-runes for healing; speech-runes so that enemies cannot harm one at the assembly; mind-runes to be wiser than all. She gave him counsel: be kind to kin and take no vengeance though they wrong you; swear no false oaths, for oath-breaking brings grim reward; do not wrangle with fools at assemblies; bury the dead you find; trust not the son of one whose kin you have slain, however young, for a wolf may lurk in a little son; beware the treachery of friends. There was no one wiser, said Sigurðr, and he swore he would have her, for she was after his own heart; she answered that she would choose him though she might choose among all men. They swore oaths to each other, and he rode away.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第20–21章。

body_zh: 萨迦描写了西古尔德的模样：他的盾牌上画着一条深褐色的龙，铠甲是金色的，头发是褐色的，又长又美，胡子浓密，眼睛锐利，很少有人敢直视他的目光；他是那么高大，当他佩着格拉姆在长得很高的麦田里走过时，剑鞘的末端刚好碰到麦穗。他来到了赫利姆谷，住在赫米尔家里。赫米尔的妻子是布伦希尔德的姐姐，布伦希尔德也住在这里，她是一个女武士，戴着头盔、穿着铠甲上战场。一天，西古尔德的猎鹰飞到了一座高塔的窗台上，他追上去取鹰，从窗口看见一位美丽的女子坐在里面，正用金线在织锦上绣着他自己的事迹。那正是布伦希尔德。他的心被深深地打动了，茶饭不思。他去见她，布伦希尔德说：我是一个持盾的少女，在战场上和国王们并肩作战，我不愿意嫁人；你注定要娶居基王的女儿古德伦。西古尔德说：我不会娶任何一个国王的女儿，我只要你。他们再次立下了誓言，西古尔德把那枚安德瓦拉诺特戒指送给了她，作为婚约的信物。可是谁也不知道，这枚戒指上的诅咒，和他们许下的誓言，将会以怎样的方式纠缠在一起。
body_en: The saga describes Sigurðr: his shield painted with a dark-brown dragon, his armour golden, his hair brown, long and fair, his beard thick, his eyes so keen that few dared look into them, and so tall that when he walked with Gram through a full-grown field of rye the end of his scabbard just touched the ears. He came to Hlymdalir and stayed with Heimir, whose wife was Brynhildr's sister; Brynhildr lived there too, a shield-maiden who went to war in helm and byrnie. One day his hawk flew to a window of a high tower; going after it, he saw a beautiful woman inside, working his own deeds in gold on a tapestry — Brynhildr. Lovesick, he went to her. She said she was a shield-maiden who fought beside kings and would not marry, and that he was fated to wed Guðrún, daughter of King Gjúki. He said he would have no king's daughter but her; they swore their oaths anew, and he gave her the ring Andvaranautr as a pledge — none knowing how the ring's curse and their oaths would be entangled.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第22–24章。

body_zh: 雷金常常催促西古尔德去做一番大事业，有一天，他给西古尔德讲了一个故事。他说：我的父亲赫雷德玛有三个儿子。大哥法夫纳最强壮、最凶狠，什么东西都想据为己有；二哥奥特是个出色的渔夫，白天变成水獭的样子，在河里捕鱼；我是最小的，是个铁匠。在安德瓦利瀑布下有很多鱼，奥特常在那里捉鱼。有一天，众神中的奥丁、洛基和霍尼尔路过那里，看见奥特正闭着眼睛，在岸边吃一条刚捉到的鲑鱼。洛基捡起一块石头，扔过去打死了水獭，三位神很得意，剥下水獭的皮，带着它来到了赫雷德玛的家，向主人炫耀他们的收获。赫雷德玛一看，那正是自己儿子的皮。他和儿子们抓住了三位神，要他们赔偿性命。众神答应用黄金来赔偿：先把水獭皮里面装满黄金，再把它的外面也用黄金完全盖住，不露出一根毛来。赫雷德玛同意了，众神派洛基去弄黄金。
body_en: Reginn often urged Sigurðr to great deeds, and one day told him a story. His father Hreiðmarr had three sons: Fáfnir, strongest and fiercest, who wanted everything for himself; Otr, a fine fisherman who by day took the shape of an otter; and Reginn, the youngest, a smith. Below Andvari's falls there were many fish, and there Otr fished. One day Odin, Loki and Hœnir passed by and saw the otter on the bank with its eyes shut, eating a salmon; Loki threw a stone and killed it, and the gods, pleased with themselves, skinned it and brought the skin to Hreiðmarr's house. Hreiðmarr recognised his son's skin, and he and his sons seized the gods and demanded a life-price. The gods agreed to fill the otter-skin with gold and cover it outside so that not a hair showed, and they sent Loki to get the gold.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第14章。

body_zh: 雷金接着讲：洛基到海神的妻子兰那里借来了她的网，来到安德瓦利瀑布。那里住着一个名叫安德瓦利的矮人，他变成一条梭子鱼，生活在瀑布下的水中。洛基撒下网，把梭子鱼捉住了，对他说：你要想活命，就拿你所有的黄金来赎身。安德瓦利只好带洛基来到他藏宝的岩洞，把所有的黄金都交了出来。可是他悄悄地把一枚小小的金戒指藏在手里。洛基看见了，命令他把戒指也交出来。安德瓦利哀求说：请让我留下这枚戒指吧，有了它，我还能重新积攒起财富。洛基不答应，一把夺走了戒指。安德瓦利走回岩洞，转身说出了一个诅咒：这枚戒指，还有这些黄金，将给每一个拥有它们的人带来死亡。洛基却满不在乎地说：这正好，我会把这个诅咒告诉拿到它的人。这枚戒指后来被称作安德瓦拉诺特，意思是“安德瓦利的宝物”。从这一刻起，这批黄金就成了一笔被诅咒的财宝，它将在之后的故事里，一个接一个地夺去它的主人们的生命。
body_en: Loki, Reginn went on, borrowed the net of Rán, the sea-god's wife, and went to Andvari's falls, where the dwarf Andvari lived as a pike. He caught the pike and demanded all his gold as the price of his life. Andvari showed him the gold in his rock and gave it up, but kept back one small gold ring in his hand. Loki saw it and made him give it up too. Andvari begged to keep it, for with it he could gather wealth again, but Loki took it. Going back into his rock, Andvari cursed it: the ring, and all the gold, should be the death of everyone who owned it. Loki answered carelessly that this suited him, and he would tell the curse to whoever took it. The ring was called Andvaranautr, 'Andvari's gift', and from that moment the hoard was cursed, and would claim its owners one after another.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第14章。

heading_en: The brother who became a dragon
body_zh: 洛基带着黄金回到赫雷德玛家里，众神先把水獭皮里面塞满了黄金，然后把它竖起来，用黄金把外面盖住。赫雷德玛走过来仔细检查，发现还有一根胡须露在外面，没有被盖住，要众神把它也盖上。奥丁从手上取下那枚安德瓦拉诺特，把那根胡须盖住了。赎金付清了，众神被放走。临走前，洛基转过身来，对赫雷德玛说：你们得到了丰厚的赎金，可是这些黄金会成为你和你儿子们的灾祸，安德瓦利的诅咒会落在你们身上。诅咒很快就应验了。法夫纳和雷金向父亲要求分一份赎金，赫雷德玛不肯。法夫纳就趁父亲睡着的时候杀死了他，独自霸占了所有的黄金，一点也不分给雷金。他带着黄金来到格尼塔荒原，在那里挖了一个窝，变成了一条巨大的恶龙，躺在黄金上，谁也不敢靠近。雷金说：从那以后，我就来到希亚尔普雷克国王这里当铁匠。我说这个故事，是要告诉你，我失去了父亲的遗产，也失去了兄弟。西古尔德说：你失去了很多，你的亲人也都很坏。
body_en: Loki brought the gold, and the gods filled the otter-skin and set it up and covered it outside with gold. Hreiðmarr looked it over and found one whisker still bare; Odin drew the ring Andvaranautr from his hand and covered it. The ransom paid, the gods were let go, but Loki turned and told Hreiðmarr that the gold would be the bane of him and his sons. The curse soon worked: Fáfnir and Reginn asked their father for a share and he refused, and Fáfnir killed him in his sleep and took all the gold, giving Reginn nothing. He went to Gnitaheiðr, made himself a lair, and became a huge serpent lying on the gold, so that none dared come near. 'Since then,' said Reginn, 'I have been a smith with King Hjálprekr; I have lost my father's inheritance and my brothers.' Sigurðr answered that he had lost much, and that his kinsmen had been very evil.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第14章。

body_zh: 雷金说：你若要杀死法夫纳，就需要一把好剑，我来为你打造。他打造了一把剑，西古尔德拿着它往铁砧上一砍，剑断成了两截。雷金又打了一把，西古尔德又一砍，剑又断了。西古尔德对雷金说：你和你的家族一样，都靠不住。他去找母亲约尔迪斯，问她父亲临终时是否把那把剑的碎片交给了她。母亲说是的，把碎片交给了他。西古尔德把碎片带给雷金，让他用它们打造一把剑。雷金很不高兴，可是还是打造了。当他从锻炉里取出这把剑时，学徒们觉得剑刃上仿佛燃烧着火焰。西古尔德举起剑，向铁砧砍去，把铁砧从上到下劈成了两半，一直劈到底座，剑刃却没有一点损伤。他又拿着剑来到河边，把一团羊毛扔进上游的水里，让羊毛顺着水流漂下来，碰到剑刃，羊毛就被切成了两半。西古尔德满意地回家了。这把剑就是格拉姆，当年奥丁插进橡树、又亲手折断的那把剑，现在在西古尔德的手中重新获得了生命。雷金对他说：现在你要遵守诺言，去杀死法夫纳。西古尔德说：我会去的，但在那之前，我要先为我的父亲报仇。
body_en: Reginn said he would forge a sword for the slaying of Fáfnir. Sigurðr struck the first on the anvil and it broke; the second broke too. 'You are untrustworthy, like your kin,' said Sigurðr, and asked his mother whether his father had given her the shards of the sword; she gave them to him, and he brought them to Reginn. When Reginn drew the new sword from the forge, it seemed to his apprentices that flames burned along its edges. Sigurðr struck the anvil and split it to the base, and the blade was unharmed; at the river he let a tuft of wool drift down onto the edge, and it was cut in two. This was Gram — the sword Odin had thrust into the oak and broken, alive again in Sigurðr's hand. Reginn reminded him of his promise to kill Fáfnir; Sigurðr said he would, but first he would avenge his father.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第15章。

body_zh: 在去复仇之前，西古尔德去拜访了他的舅舅格里皮尔，格里皮尔能预知未来，把西古尔德一生的命运都告诉了他，萨迦只说他把将要发生的事情都讲了出来。然后，西古尔德向国王借来了战船和人马，率领大军出海，去攻打杀死他父亲的洪丁的儿子们。海上起了可怕的风暴，巨浪滔天，船帆被撕裂。这时，他们看见一个人站在海边的悬崖上，说他叫赫尼卡尔，要求上船。他上了船，风暴立刻平息了，船顺风到达了洪丁的儿子们的国土。萨迦暗示，这个神秘的人就是奥丁。西古尔德上岸后，与吕恩吉国王和他的兄弟们展开了激战。西古尔德走在军队的最前面，手握格拉姆，砍杀着敌人，他的剑所到之处，敌人纷纷倒下，人和马都被劈开。吕恩吉和他的兄弟们都被西古尔德杀死了。西古尔德为父亲西格蒙德和外祖父埃利米报了仇，带着大量的战利品和崇高的荣誉回到了丹麦。雷金对他说：现在你该去推翻那个躺在格尼塔荒原上的恶龙了。
body_en: Before his vengeance Sigurðr visited his mother's brother Grípir, who could see the future and told him all that would befall him. Then, with ships and men from the king, he sailed against the sons of Hundingr, who had killed his father. A fearful storm arose until they saw a man on a cliff who called himself Hnikarr and asked to come aboard; when he did, the storm abated and they came with a fair wind to the land of Hundingr's sons — the saga hints that he was Odin. In the battle Sigurðr went in front with Gram, hewing down men and horses, and he killed King Lyngvi and his brothers, avenging Sigmundr and Eylimi, and returned to Denmark with great booty and honour. Now, said Reginn, it was time to bring down the serpent on Gnitaheiðr.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第16–17章。

body_zh: 西古尔德和雷金骑马来到格尼塔荒原，找到了法夫纳每天爬去喝水的路。那条路从它的窝一直通到水边，足迹宽大，萨迦说，那片悬崖有三十噚高。西古尔德说：你说这条龙不比一般的蛇大，可是它的足迹太大了。雷金说：你在路上挖一个坑，坐在坑里，等恶龙爬过去喝水的时候，你从下面刺进它的心脏，你就会赢得巨大的名声。说完，雷金害怕地逃走了。西古尔德开始挖坑。这时，一个长着长胡子的老人走了过来，问他在做什么。西古尔德告诉了他。老人说：这不是好办法。你应该多挖几条沟，让龙血流进沟里，你坐在其中一条沟里，从那里刺它的心脏。说完，老人就离开了。西古尔德照着老人的话挖好了沟。不久，恶龙爬出来喝水了，大地剧烈地震动，它一路喷着毒液。西古尔德既不害怕，也不惊慌。当巨龙从坑上爬过的时候，西古尔德举起格拉姆，从下面刺进了它的左肩下面，一直刺到剑柄。他从坑里跳出来，拔出宝剑，两只手臂直到肩膀都沾满了鲜血。巨龙受了致命的伤，痛苦地扭动着头和尾巴，把周围的一切都打得粉碎。
body_en: Sigurðr and Reginn rode to Gnitaheiðr and found the track by which Fáfnir crawled to water, down a cliff thirty fathoms high, says the saga. Sigurðr said the beast's tracks were far greater than Reginn had told him. Reginn told him to dig a pit in the track, sit in it, and stab the serpent to the heart from below as it crawled over, and so win great fame — and he fled in fear. As Sigurðr dug, a long-bearded old man came by and told him that was ill counsel: he should dig several trenches for the blood to run into, and sit in one of them; then he went away. Sigurðr did so. The serpent came crawling to the water, the earth shaking and venom blowing before it; Sigurðr was neither afraid nor dismayed, and as it passed over him he thrust Gram in under its left shoulder up to the hilt. He leapt out of the pit and drew out the sword, his arms bloody to the shoulders, while the dying dragon lashed its head and tail and shattered everything around it.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第18章。

body_zh: 法夫纳知道自己受了致命的伤，问：你是谁？你父亲是谁？你的家族是什么人，竟敢拿武器来对付我？西古尔德起初不肯说出自己的名字，因为古人相信，垂死的人如果知道仇人的名字，诅咒他就会更加灵验。他说自己是“高贵的野兽”，没有父亲也没有母亲，独自一人。法夫纳不相信，西古尔德最后说出了实情：我叫西古尔德，我的父亲是西格蒙德。法夫纳说：是谁怂恿你来杀我的？西古尔德说：是我的勇气和我的手，还有这把锋利的剑。法夫纳说：我知道，是我的兄弟雷金害死了我，他也会害死你。我警告你：这些黄金，还有那枚红色的戒指，将成为你的祸根。我曾经戴着令人恐惧的头盔，所有人都怕我，可是现在我躺在这里死去了。他又回答了西古尔德关于命运女神诺恩和最后之战的问题。临死前，法夫纳劝西古尔德骑上马赶快离开，不要碰那些黄金。西古尔德回答：每个人总有一天会死，我会带着这些黄金回家。法夫纳说：雷金背叛了我，他也会背叛你，说完就死了。
body_en: Mortally wounded, Fáfnir asked who he was, who his father and kin, that dared bear weapons against him. At first Sigurðr hid his name — for in old times men believed a dying man's curse was strongest if he knew his slayer's name — calling himself 'the noble beast', with neither father nor mother. Then he told the truth: he was Sigurðr, son of Sigmundr. Asked who had urged him on, he said his own courage, his hand and his sharp sword. Fáfnir said he knew Reginn had brought about his death and would bring about Sigurðr's too, and warned him that the gold and the red ring would be his bane; once he had worn the helm of terror and all feared him, and now he lay dying. He answered Sigurðr's questions about the Norns and the last battle of the gods, and urged him to ride away and leave the gold. Every man must die one day, said Sigurðr; he would take the gold home. Reginn betrayed me and will betray you, said Fáfnir, and died.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第18章。

heading_en: The dragon's heart and the speech of birds
body_zh: 雷金回来了，他用刀割开法夫纳的心，喝了龙血，然后对西古尔德说：你杀死了我的哥哥，我也有罪，可是请你帮我一个忙：把这颗心烤熟给我吃。西古尔德把龙心穿在木棍上烤着。他用手指去摸龙心，看它是否熟了，烫着了手指，赶紧把手指放进嘴里。龙心的血一沾到他的舌头，他立刻就听懂了鸟的语言。树上有几只山雀在说话：一只说，西古尔德坐在那里为别人烤龙心，他应该自己吃了它，他就会成为最聪明的人。另一只说，雷金躺在那里，想要欺骗信任他的人。第三只说，应该砍下他的头，那么所有的黄金就都归西古尔德了。第四只说，如果他能明白这一点，就会骑马去找睡在辛达山上的布伦希尔德，从她那里学到很多智慧。西古尔德说：我不能让雷金成为我的死因，两兄弟应该去同一个地方。他拔出格拉姆，砍下了雷金的头。他吃了一部分龙心，把其余的留了下来。然后他骑马来到法夫纳的窝，找到了大量的黄金，还有令人恐惧的头盔、一件金铠甲和一把名叫赫罗提的剑。他把黄金装进两个大箱子，放在格拉尼的背上。格拉尼却一动不动，直到西古尔德骑了上去，它才迈开步子。
body_en: Reginn came back, cut out Fáfnir's heart and drank the blood, and asked Sigurðr to roast the heart for him. Sigurðr roasted it on a spit, and when he touched it to see if it was done and burned his finger, he put the finger in his mouth; as the heart's blood touched his tongue, he understood the speech of birds. Nuthatches in a tree were talking: one said Sigurðr was roasting the heart for another when he should eat it himself and be wisest of men; another that Reginn meant to betray the one who trusted him; a third that Sigurðr should cut off his head and have all the gold; a fourth that he should ride to Brynhildr sleeping on Hindarfjall and learn wisdom from her. Sigurðr said Reginn should not be his bane — the brothers should go the same road — and cut off Reginn's head with Gram. He ate some of the heart and kept the rest, rode to Fáfnir's lair and found great gold, the helm of terror, a golden byrnie and the sword Hrotti; he loaded two great chests onto Grani, but Grani would not move until Sigurðr mounted him.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第19章。

body_zh: 萨迦从奥丁的一个儿子讲起，他的名字叫西吉。有一次，西吉和一个名叫布雷迪的奴隶一起去打猎，布雷迪是另一个人斯卡迪的奴隶。到了傍晚清点猎物，布雷迪打到的野兽比西吉的多得多。西吉觉得受了奴隶的羞辱，嫉恨在心，竟然杀死了布雷迪，把尸体埋在雪堆里。从此人们就把大雪堆叫作“布雷迪的雪堆”。事情很快败露了，人们宣布西吉是“圣地里的狼”，也就是被放逐的罪人，他不能再在家乡生活。可是奥丁没有抛弃自己的儿子，他亲自领着西吉离开了那片土地，走了很远的路，又给他准备了战船和人马。西吉成了一个伟大的战士，在战争中赢得了一个国家，做了匈人之地的国王，娶了一位有名望的妻子。他统治了很久，十分强大，直到年老的时候，他妻子的兄弟们背叛了他，趁他身边人少的时候袭击他，把他杀死了。他的儿子勒里尔召集了大军，为父亲报了仇，杀死了所有背叛者，继承了父亲的王国。
body_en: The saga begins with Sigi, a son of Odin. Out hunting with Breði, a thrall belonging to a man called Skaði, Sigi found at evening that the thrall had taken far more game than he; jealous and shamed, he killed Breði and buried him in a snowdrift, which is why great drifts are called Breði's drifts. The deed was discovered and Sigi was declared a wolf in holy places, an outlaw, and could no longer live at home. But Odin led his son far away and gave him warships and men, and Sigi became a great warrior, won a kingdom and ruled as king of Hunland with a noble wife. He ruled long and mightily until in old age his wife's brothers betrayed and killed him when few men were with him; his son Rerir gathered a host, avenged his father on all the traitors, and took the kingdom.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第1章。

body_zh: 大仇得报，西格蒙德回到了父亲的国家，赶走了趁他不在时占据王位的人，做了一个伟大的国王。他娶了一位名叫博格希尔德的妻子，生了两个儿子，其中的赫尔吉后来成为杀死洪丁国王的著名英雄，赢得了女武神般的公主西格伦。辛菲奥特利也一直跟随着父亲，四处征战。有一次，他和博格希尔德的兄弟同时爱上了一个女人，两人在争斗中，辛菲奥特利杀死了他。博格希尔德要求把辛菲奥特利赶走，西格蒙德不肯，宁愿用黄金赔偿。博格希尔德表面上接受了，暗地里却决心报复。在为她兄弟举行的葬礼宴会上，她亲自给众人倒酒，端了一角酒给辛菲奥特利。辛菲奥特利看了看，说：这酒浑浊。西格蒙德接过来替他喝了。第二次又是这样。第三次，博格希尔德讥讽说：你还算是沃尔松格家的人吗？西格蒙德这时已经喝醉了，对儿子说：用你的胡子把它滤过去吧，儿子。辛菲奥特利喝下了酒，立刻倒地而死。西格蒙德悲痛欲绝，抱着儿子的尸体走到一个海湾边，一个撑着小船的人说愿意把他们渡过去，可是船太小，只能装下尸体。西格蒙德把尸体放上船，那人撑船离岸，转眼就消失了——那是奥丁来接他的孙子了。
body_en: Vengeance done, Sigmundr returned to his father's land, drove out the usurper and became a great king. He married Borghildr and had two sons, of whom Helgi became the famous slayer of King Hundingr and won Sigrún. Sinfjötli fought at his father's side; but he and Borghildr's brother wooed the same woman, and Sinfjötli killed him. Borghildr demanded he be driven out; Sigmundr would only pay compensation in gold, and she seemed to accept it. At her brother's funeral feast she bore the drink herself and gave Sinfjötli a horn; he said the drink was cloudy, and Sigmundr drank it for him — twice. The third time she taunted him with being no Völsung, and Sigmundr, now drunk, said: 'Let your beard strain it, son.' Sinfjötli drank and fell dead. Grief-stricken, Sigmundr carried the body to a fjord, where a man in a small boat offered to ferry it across; the boat could hold only the body, and as soon as it was laid in, the man pushed off and vanished — Odin had come for his kinsman.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第9–10章。

body_zh: 博格希尔德被赶走，不久死去了。西格蒙德年纪老了，却听说岛国国王埃利米的女儿约尔迪斯是世上最美丽、最聪明的女子，就去向她求婚。洪丁国王的儿子吕恩吉也来求婚。约尔迪斯选择了年老而名声显赫的西格蒙德。吕恩吉怀恨在心，带着大军来攻打西格蒙德。西格蒙德虽然年老，仍然奋勇作战，他的剑在敌阵中左右砍杀，敌人纷纷倒下，他的手臂上沾满了鲜血。就在这时，一个人出现在战场上：他披着一件蓝色的斗篷，戴着宽边帽，只有一只眼睛，手里握着一支长矛。他走到西格蒙德面前，举起长矛挡住了西格蒙德砍来的剑。西格蒙德的剑砍在长矛上，断成了两截。从这一刻起，胜负就决定了。西格蒙德的人马纷纷倒下，国王自己也受了致命的伤，他的岳父埃利米也战死了。那把当年由奥丁插在橡树里、只有西格蒙德能拔出来的剑，最终由奥丁亲手折断。萨迦没有解释奥丁为什么这样做，可是西格蒙德自己明白：他的时候到了。
body_en: Borghildr was driven out and soon died. Old as he was, Sigmundr wooed Hjördís, daughter of King Eylimi, the fairest and wisest of women; Lyngvi, son of Hundingr, wooed her too, but she chose the old and famous Sigmundr. Lyngvi came against him with a great host. Old Sigmundr fought fiercely, his sword hewing down men until his arms were red with blood. Then a man appeared on the field in a blue cloak and broad hat, one-eyed, holding a spear, and he held up the spear against Sigmundr's stroke, and the sword broke in two. From that moment the battle turned; Sigmundr's men fell, he himself was mortally wounded, and his father-in-law Eylimi was slain. The sword Odin had thrust into the oak for Sigmundr alone was broken by Odin himself. The saga does not say why; but Sigmundr knew his time had come.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第11章。

body_zh: 夜里，约尔迪斯来到满是尸体的战场上，找到了垂死的西格蒙德，问他能不能医治。西格蒙德说：许多人死于不太有希望的情况，可是我的运气已经离开了我，我不愿意医治。奥丁不愿意我再挥剑，因为他折断了它。只要他愿意，我曾经一直能打胜仗。他对约尔迪斯说：你怀着一个儿子，好好抚养他，他将成为我们家族最伟大、最著名的人。好好保管这把剑的碎片，用它们能打造出一把好剑，名叫格拉姆，我们的儿子将用它做出许多伟大的事业，他的名字将永远流传。说完这些话，西格蒙德在天亮时死去了。这时，丹麦国王希亚尔普雷克的儿子阿尔夫率领战船来到海边。约尔迪斯和侍女交换了衣服，侍女扮作王后，约尔迪斯扮作侍女。阿尔夫怀疑侍女的举止，就问她们：在天亮之前，你们怎么知道天快亮了？侍女说：我小时候常常在天亮前起来喝酒，所以到了那个时候就会醒。约尔迪斯说：父亲给了我一枚金戒指，天快亮时，戒指就会在我手指上变凉。阿尔夫立刻明白了谁是真正的王后，他善待约尔迪斯，后来娶了她。不久，约尔迪斯生下了西格蒙德的儿子，取名西古尔德。
body_en: That night Hjördís came to the field of the dead, found Sigmundr dying and asked if he could be healed. Many live when hope is small, he said, but his luck had left him and he would not be healed; Odin did not wish him to draw sword again, since he had broken it, and while Odin willed it he had always won. She was carrying his son, he told her: let her rear him well, for he would be the greatest and most famous of their kin; and let her keep the shards of the sword well, for from them a good sword called Gram would be made, and their son would do great deeds with it, and his name would live as long as the world. He died at dawn. Then Álfr, son of King Hjálprekr of Denmark, came with his ships. Hjördís had exchanged clothes with her maid; Álfr, suspicious, asked how they knew in the dark that dawn was near. The maid said she had been used to drinking before dawn as a girl; Hjördís said her father had given her a gold ring that grew cold on her finger toward daybreak. Álfr knew the true queen, treated her honourably and later married her, and she bore Sigmundr's son, Sigurðr.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第12–13章。

heading_en: The apple and the six-year child
body_zh: 勒里尔国王和王后很久都没有孩子，他们为此十分忧愁，向众神祈求，希望能有一个儿子。女神弗丽嘉听见了他们的祈祷，告诉了奥丁。奥丁派他的愿望侍女——巨人赫利姆尼尔的女儿赫柳德——变成一只乌鸦，把一个苹果带给勒里尔。那时勒里尔正坐在一座土丘上，乌鸦飞过，把苹果扔在了他的膝上。勒里尔明白了这是神的恩赐，把苹果带回去给王后吃了。不久，王后怀孕了。可是勒里尔国王出征时病死了，王后的身孕却迟迟不能分娩，一直怀了六年。她知道自己活不长了，就命人剖开她的身体，取出孩子。生下来的是一个已经长得很大的男孩，他在母亲死前亲吻了她。这个孩子就是沃尔松格。沃尔松格长大后做了匈人之地的国王，娶了当年送苹果的赫柳德为妻，生了十个儿子和一个女儿，最大的是一对双胞胎：儿子西格蒙德和女儿西格妮。沃尔松格建了一座宏伟的大厅，大厅正中长着一棵巨大的橡树，树枝穿过屋顶向外伸展，开着美丽的花，人们把它叫作“孩子树”布兰斯托克。
body_en: Rerir and his queen long had no child and prayed to the gods for a son. Frigg heard and told Odin, who sent his wish-maiden Hljóð, daughter of the giant Hrímnir, in the shape of a crow with an apple, which she dropped into Rerir's lap as he sat on a mound. Rerir understood, and the queen ate the apple and conceived. But Rerir died of sickness on a campaign, and the queen carried the child six years without giving birth; knowing she would not live, she had him cut from her, and the boy, already well grown, kissed his mother before she died. He was Völsungr. He became king of Hunland, married Hljóð, who had brought the apple, and had ten sons and a daughter, the eldest being the twins Sigmundr and Signý. He built a splendid hall round a great oak whose blossoming branches spread out through the roof, called the Branstock.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第2章。

body_zh: 高特兰的国王西格尔来向西格妮求婚。沃尔松格和儿子们觉得这门亲事不错，答应了，可是西格妮自己并不愿意，只是听从了父亲的安排。婚宴在沃尔松格的大厅里举行，大厅中央的橡树周围燃着火堆。宴会正热闹的时候，一个陌生人走进了大厅。他身材高大，年纪很老，只有一只眼睛，披着一件带帽的斗篷，赤着脚，裤子用亚麻布绑在腿上。他手里握着一把剑，走到橡树前，把剑一直插进树干，只露出剑柄。大厅里的人都不敢和他打招呼。他说：谁能把这把剑从树干里拔出来，这把剑就送给谁；他会发现，这是他手中握过的最好的剑。说完，老人走出大厅，谁也不知道他是谁，去了哪里——这是奥丁。众人纷纷上前拔剑，一个接一个，都拔不动。最后，西格蒙德走上前去，伸手一拔，那把剑就像放在那里等着他一样，轻轻松松地被拔了出来。这是一把无与伦比的好剑。西格尔国王想要这把剑，提出用三倍于剑重的黄金来换。西格蒙德回答：你和我一样，本来也可以把它拔出来，如果它是给你的话。可是现在它到了我的手里，就是给我你所有的黄金，我也不换。西格尔听了这番话，觉得受到了嘲弄，心中暗暗怀恨。
body_en: Siggeir, king of Gautland, asked for Signý. Völsungr and his sons favoured the match, and Signý, though unwilling, obeyed. At the wedding feast in Völsungr's hall, fires burning round the great oak, a stranger came in: very tall and old, one-eyed, in a hooded cloak, barefoot, with linen breeches bound round his legs. He drove a sword into the trunk up to the hilt, said that whoever drew it out should have it as a gift and find no better sword ever in his hand, and went out; no one knew who he was or where he went — it was Odin. Man after man tried and failed, until Sigmundr took hold and drew it out as if it lay loose. Siggeir offered three times its weight in gold, but Sigmundr answered that Siggeir could have drawn it as well as he if it had been meant for him; now that it had come to his hand, he would not give it up for all Siggeir's gold. Siggeir took it as mockery and nursed his grudge.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第3章。

body_zh: 第二天，西格妮请求父亲让她早点离开，她说她不愿意跟西格尔走，她预感到这门亲事会带来灾难。可是沃尔松格说，答应了的事不能反悔，否则会给两家带来耻辱。西格尔国王带着西格妮回国前，邀请沃尔松格和他的儿子们三个月后到高特兰做客。到了约定的日子，沃尔松格带着儿子们乘三条船来到高特兰的海岸。西格妮趁夜里来到船上，对父亲说：西格尔已经集结了大军，要背叛你们，杀死你们。你们赶快回去，召集自己的军队再来吧。沃尔松格回答：我还在母亲腹中的时候，就说过一句话，我发誓无论遇到火还是铁，都绝不逃跑，我一直遵守着这个誓言。现在我老了，更不能违背它。女儿，你回到你丈夫身边去吧。第二天一早，沃尔松格和儿子们上岸迎战，他们八次冲进敌阵，杀死了许多人，可是寡不敌众，沃尔松格在阵前战死，他的十个儿子全部被俘。西格妮恳求丈夫：不要马上杀死我的兄弟们，把他们锁在木枷里，放在树林里吧，让我能多看他们几眼。西格尔答应了，心想这样他们会死得更痛苦。
body_en: Next day Signý begged her father to let her stay, foreseeing disaster from the marriage, but Völsungr said a promise could not be broken without shame. Siggeir invited Völsungr and his sons to Gautland in three months. When they came with three ships, Signý went to them by night and warned that Siggeir had gathered a host to betray them: let them go home and raise an army. Völsungr answered that while still unborn he had sworn never to flee from fire or iron, and he had kept that vow; old as he was, he would not break it now — let her go back to her husband. At dawn they went ashore and fought, charging through Siggeir's ranks eight times, but Völsungr fell before his men and all ten of his sons were captured. Signý begged Siggeir not to kill her brothers at once but to put them in stocks in the forest, so that she might see them a while longer, and Siggeir agreed, thinking they would suffer more.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第4–5章。

body_zh: 十个兄弟被锁在森林里的一根巨大的木枷上。第一天夜里，一头又老又大的母狼从森林里走出来，咬死了其中一个兄弟，把他吃掉了，然后离去。第二天夜里，母狼又来了，又吃掉了一个。就这样，一连九夜，九个兄弟都被母狼吃掉了，只剩下了西格蒙德。有人说，这头母狼是西格尔的母亲，她用魔法变成了狼的样子。西格妮每天都派人去打听消息，知道只剩下西格蒙德一个了，她想出了一个办法。她叫来一个心腹，让他带着蜂蜜去森林里，把蜂蜜涂在西格蒙德的脸上，再放一些在他的嘴里。到了夜里，母狼又来了，闻到了蜂蜜的香味，就去舔西格蒙德脸上的蜂蜜，然后把舌头伸进了他的嘴里。西格蒙德一口咬住了母狼的舌头，母狼拼命挣扎，用脚蹬着木枷，竟把木枷蹬裂了，西格蒙德紧咬不放，把狼的舌头连根扯了出来，母狼就这样死了。西格蒙德挣脱了木枷，逃进了森林深处。西格妮派人给他送去所需的东西，他在森林里挖了一个地洞住了下来。西格尔以为沃尔松格家的人都死光了。
body_en: The ten brothers were set in a great stock in the forest. On the first night an old, huge she-wolf came out of the wood and killed and ate one of them; so it went for nine nights, until only Sigmundr was left. Some say the wolf was Siggeir's mother in the shape of a wolf by witchcraft. Signý sent a trusted man to smear honey on Sigmundr's face and put some in his mouth. That night the she-wolf came, licked the honey from his face and thrust her tongue into his mouth; Sigmundr bit hard on it, and as she struggled and braced her feet against the stock she split it, while he held on until he tore out her tongue by the roots, and she died. Sigmundr escaped into the forest, and Signý sent him what he needed; he made himself an earth-house there, while Siggeir thought all the Völsungs were dead.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第5章。

body_zh: 西格妮心中只有一个念头：为父亲和兄弟们报仇。她和西格尔生了两个儿子。大儿子十岁的时候，她把他送到森林里西格蒙德那里，让他帮助舅舅复仇。可是复仇的人必须有勇气。在送去之前，西格妮先试探孩子：她把他袖子的边缝在他的手臂皮肤上，孩子疼得叫了起来。到了森林里，西格蒙德让孩子揉面做饭，自己出去砍柴。等他回来，面还没有揉好，孩子说，他不敢碰那袋面粉，因为里面有个活的东西在动。西格蒙德把这件事告诉了西格妮，西格妮说：这孩子没有勇气，留着他没用，杀了他吧。西格蒙德照做了。第二年，西格妮又把小儿子送来，结果也是一样。萨迦就这样冷酷地讲述了西格妮的决心：在她眼里，西格尔的儿子不配成为沃尔松格家的复仇者，她宁可牺牲自己的孩子，也不让复仇落空。她明白了，能和西格蒙德一起复仇的，必须是一个纯粹的沃尔松格家的孩子。
body_en: Signý thought only of vengeance. When her elder son by Siggeir was ten, she sent him to Sigmundr in the forest to help, first testing him by sewing the cuffs of his sleeves to the skin of his arms, at which he cried out. Sigmundr set the boy to knead dough while he fetched wood; the boy did not dare touch the meal-sack because something alive was moving in it. When Sigmundr told Signý, she said the boy had no courage and should be killed, and so it was done; the next year the younger son fared the same. The saga tells Signý's resolve coldly: Siggeir's sons were unfit to be the Völsungs' avengers, and only a child of pure Völsung blood could share the vengeance.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第6章。

body_zh: 有一天，一个会魔法的女巫来到西格妮的住处。西格妮对她说：我想和你交换容貌。女巫用魔法让两人换了样子，女巫变成西格妮的模样留在西格尔身边，而西格妮变成女巫的样子，来到了森林里西格蒙德的地洞，请求借宿。西格蒙德没有认出她，留她住了三夜，与她同床。然后，西格妮回到了家，和女巫换回了容貌。不久她生下了一个儿子，取名辛菲奥特利。他是西格蒙德和西格妮的儿子，有着纯粹的沃尔松格家的血统。辛菲奥特利长到十岁时，西格妮也用同样的方法试探他：把袖子缝在他手臂的皮肉上，他一声不吭；她把袖子连皮一起撕下来，问他疼不疼，他说：对沃尔松格家的人来说，这点疼算不了什么。她把他送到西格蒙德那里。西格蒙德让他揉面，自己出去砍柴。回来时，面已经做好了。西格蒙德问他有没有在面里发现什么东西，辛菲奥特利说：开始揉的时候，面里好像有个活的东西，我没管它，把它一起揉进面里了。西格蒙德笑着说：今晚你别吃这面包了，你把一条最毒的蛇揉进去了。西格蒙德能吃毒蛇而不受伤害，辛菲奥特利能抵挡外面的毒，却不能吃下毒物。
body_en: One day a sorceress came to Signý, who asked to exchange shapes with her. The sorceress, in Signý's likeness, stayed with Siggeir, while Signý in her likeness went to Sigmundr's earth-house in the forest and asked for shelter; not knowing her, he kept her three nights and lay with her. Then she went home and they changed back, and in time she bore a son, Sinfjötli, child of Sigmundr and Signý, a Völsung on both sides. When he was ten she tested him the same way: he did not flinch when the sleeves were sewn to his skin, and when she tore them off with the skin, he said such a pain was little to a Völsung. Sent to Sigmundr and set to kneading, he had the bread baked by the time Sigmundr returned; asked if he had found anything in the meal, he said something alive had been in it at first, but he had kneaded it in. Sigmundr laughed and told him not to eat that bread, for he had kneaded in the most venomous of serpents. Sigmundr could eat poison unharmed; Sinfjötli could bear venom on his skin but not eat it.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第7章。

body_zh: 西格蒙德觉得辛菲奥特利还太年轻，复仇之前应该让他经受更多的磨炼。父子二人在夏天里走遍森林，杀人抢劫。西格蒙德一直以为辛菲奥特利是西格尔的儿子，只觉得他有着沃尔松格家的勇猛。有一天，他们来到森林里的一座小屋，看见里面有两个人睡着，身上戴着粗大的金环，墙上挂着两张狼皮。原来这两个人是国王的儿子，中了魔法，只能每隔十天从狼皮里出来一次。西格蒙德和辛菲奥特利穿上了狼皮，却再也脱不下来了，他们也变成了狼，像狼一样嚎叫。他们约定：如果一个人遇到七个以上的敌人，就要嚎叫，叫另一个来帮忙。可是辛菲奥特利遇到了十一个人，没有呼救，独自把他们全杀了。西格蒙德见了大怒，扑上去咬住了他的喉咙。辛菲奥特利倒地不起，西格蒙德追悔莫及，背着他回到小屋，坐在他身边，诅咒那两张狼皮。这时，他看见两只鼬鼠，一只咬了另一只的喉咙，然后跑进树林，衔来一片叶子，放在伤口上，那只鼬鼠就活了过来。一只渡鸦给西格蒙德衔来了同样的叶子，他把叶子放在辛菲奥特利的伤口上，辛菲奥特利立刻跳了起来，完好如初。到了第十天，他们终于脱下了狼皮，把它们扔进火里烧掉了。
body_en: Thinking Sinfjötli too young, Sigmundr hardened him first; they roamed the forest through the summer killing men for plunder, Sigmundr still believing the boy was Siggeir's son. They came to a house where two men slept wearing thick gold rings, with wolf-skins hanging over them — kings' sons under a spell who could come out of the skins only every tenth day. Sigmundr and Sinfjötli put on the skins and could not take them off; they became wolves and howled like wolves. They agreed that whoever met more than seven men would howl for the other; but Sinfjötli met eleven and killed them all alone without calling. In anger Sigmundr leapt on him and bit him in the throat. Repenting, he carried him back to the house and cursed the skins; then he saw a weasel bite another in the throat and run into the wood for a leaf that healed it, and a raven brought him such a leaf, and Sinfjötli sprang up whole. On the tenth day they could take the skins off, and they burned them.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第8章。

body_zh: 复仇的时候到了。西格蒙德和辛菲奥特利来到西格尔的王宫，藏在大厅前面放酒桶的屋子里。西格妮知道他们来了。西格尔和西格妮的两个年幼的孩子在大厅里玩金环，一个金环滚进了酒桶屋，孩子跑去捡，看见了两个陌生的大个子，赶紧跑回去告诉父亲。西格妮对西格蒙德说：这两个孩子出卖了你们，杀了他们吧。西格蒙德不肯，辛菲奥特利却拔剑杀死了两个孩子，把尸体扔进了大厅。西格尔的人一拥而上，经过一场激战，父子二人被擒。西格尔下令把他们活埋在一座大坟堆里，坟堆中间用一块巨大的石板隔开，让他们看得见彼此，却碰不到彼此，慢慢饿死。就在人们往坟堆上盖草皮的时候，西格妮抱着一捆稻草走来，扔进了辛菲奥特利那一边，里面裹着一块猪肉，猪肉里藏着西格蒙德的那把剑。夜里，父子二人用这把剑锯开了石板，那把剑锋利无比，石板被锯成了两半。他们从坟堆里爬出来，来到西格尔的大厅，在大厅四周堆满了木柴，放起火来。西格尔被火惊醒，问是谁放的火。西格蒙德说：是我和我外甥辛菲奥特利，我们要让你知道，沃尔松格家的人并没有死光。他请妹妹出来。西格妮走出火海，对哥哥说出了真相：辛菲奥特利是她和他的儿子，她为了复仇做了一切，现在她已经不能再活下去了。她亲吻了哥哥和儿子，转身走回燃烧的大厅，与丈夫一起死在了火中。
body_en: The time for vengeance came. Father and son hid in the ale-store before Siggeir's hall. Two young children of Siggeir and Signý, playing with gold rings, saw them when a ring rolled in, and told their father. Signý told Sigmundr to kill them for betraying them; he would not, but Sinfjötli slew them and flung them into the hall. After hard fighting the two were taken, and Siggeir had them buried alive in a great mound divided by a stone slab, so they could see but not reach each other. As the turf was laid, Signý threw straw into Sinfjötli's side with pork wrapped round Sigmundr's sword; in the night they sawed through the slab with it, climbed out, piled wood round Siggeir's hall and set it on fire. When Siggeir asked who had lit it, Sigmundr said it was he and his sister's son Sinfjötli, to show that not all the Völsungs were dead. He called his sister out; Signý told him that Sinfjötli was her son by him, that she had done everything for vengeance and could not live after it; she kissed her brother and son, went back into the burning hall and died with her husband.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第8章。

body_zh: 在莱茵河以南，有一个名叫居基的国王，他有三个儿子：贡纳尔、霍格尼和年纪最小的古托姆，还有一个女儿古德伦，她是那里最美丽的少女。王后格里姆希尔德是一个懂得魔法、心肠很硬的女人。有一天，古德伦做了一个梦，梦见自己有一只美丽的猎鹰，羽毛是金色的，她觉得这只鹰比她所有的珍宝都珍贵，可是不久它就死了。她闷闷不乐，侍女们劝她去问问布伦希尔德，因为布伦希尔德最懂得解梦。古德伦带着侍女们来到布伦希尔德的住处，坐在金色的座位上，讲起了自己的梦，又说了另一个梦：她梦见一头金色的大鹿，比所有的鹿都美，她想得到它，可是布伦希尔德在她的面前把鹿射死了。布伦希尔德听了，直截了当地说出了梦的意思：西古尔德会来到你父亲的宫中，你会嫁给他，可是你的母亲会用诡计让他忘记我，你们不会长久，你将失去他。我会害死他，然后你会嫁给匈人的国王阿特利，失去你的兄弟们，然后杀死阿特利。古德伦听了，悲伤而惊恐，说：我真不愿知道这些事。说完就回家去了。
body_en: South of the Rhine ruled King Gjúki, with three sons, Gunnarr, Högni and the youngest, Guttormr, and a daughter, Guðrún, the fairest of maidens; his queen Grímhildr was skilled in magic and hard of heart. Guðrún dreamed she had a fair hawk with golden feathers, dearer to her than all her treasures, and it soon died; her maids urged her to ask Brynhildr, who was wisest in dreams. She went with them to Brynhildr, sat in a golden seat, told that dream and another, of a great golden hart, fairest of all, which she longed for but which Brynhildr shot before her eyes. Brynhildr read them plainly: Sigurðr would come to her father's court and marry her, but her mother would make him forget Brynhildr by guile; they would not be together long; Brynhildr would bring about his death, and Guðrún would then marry Atli, king of the Huns, lose her brothers, and kill Atli. Guðrún, grieved and afraid, said she wished she had not learned it, and went home.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第25章。

body_zh: 西古尔德被剑刺穿，醒了过来。他抓起放在床边的格拉姆，向正在逃跑的古托姆扔了过去。宝剑击中了古托姆的后背，把他从腰部劈成了两段，上半身倒在房间里面，下半身和双脚倒在门外。古德伦正睡在西古尔德的怀里，她在血泊中醒来，看见丈夫浑身是血，悲痛地哭喊起来。西古尔德对她说：不要哭，我的亲人们都还活着。我们的儿子还太小，不懂得防备敌人。这件事是布伦希尔德一手造成的，她爱我胜过爱任何人。可是我可以作证，我从来没有对贡纳尔做过任何不义的事，我一直遵守着我们的誓言，从来没有做过他妻子的情人。如果我早知道这一切，提前防备，我就能和这些人对抗。说完这些话，西古尔德死去了。古德伦发出一声长长的叹息，她的哭声传遍了整个宫殿，院子里的鹅也惊叫起来。布伦希尔德在自己的房间里听见了古德伦的哭声，竟然大笑起来。贡纳尔问她为什么笑，难道她是在为这件可怕的事高兴吗？布伦希尔德说：我梦见过这一切，你们背弃了誓言，杀死了比你们好得多的人，你们的结局也不会好。
body_en: Run through, Sigurðr woke, seized Gram beside the bed and hurled it after the fleeing Guttormr; it struck him in the back and cut him in two at the waist, so that his head and arms fell inside the chamber and his legs outside the door. Guðrún, asleep in Sigurðr's arms, woke in his blood and cried out in grief. Sigurðr told her not to weep: her brothers were alive, and their son was too young to guard himself against his enemies; Brynhildr had brought this about, who loved him above all men; and he swore he had never wronged Gunnarr, but had kept their oaths and never been his wife's lover. Had he known of it, he could have stood against them. Then he died. Guðrún heaved a great sigh, and her wailing rang through the hall so that the geese in the yard cried out. Brynhildr, hearing it, laughed. When Gunnarr asked whether she rejoiced at the dreadful deed, she said she had dreamed it all: they had broken their oaths and killed a far better man, and their own end would be evil.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第30章。

body_zh: 古德伦坐在西古尔德的尸体旁，一动不动，一滴眼泪也流不出来，人们都害怕她会因悲伤而死去。贵族的妇人们来到她身边，一个个讲述自己一生中遭遇过的最大的不幸，想让她明白，世上的人都有痛苦，好让她哭出来。一个妇人说，她失去了丈夫和孩子；另一个说，她的兄弟们都被杀死了，自己也成了俘虏。可是古德伦仍然没有哭。最后，她的姐姐揭开了盖在西古尔德身上的布，把他的头放在古德伦的膝上，对她说：看看你所爱的人吧，亲吻他，就像他还活着时那样。古德伦看了一眼，看见他美丽的头发上沾满了鲜血，他锐利的眼睛已经失去了光彩，他的胸膛被剑刺穿了。她终于伏在他身上，放声大哭，泪水像雨水一样流了下来，院子里的鹅也和她一起叫了起来。萨迦说，古德伦对着西古尔德的尸体，说她的西古尔德在居基的儿子们中间，就像高高的韭葱长在青草之上，像一颗明亮的宝石镶在金带上，现在她失去了他，在王宫里就像风中的一片树叶那样渺小。
body_en: Guðrún sat by Sigurðr's body, motionless and dry-eyed, and they feared she would die of grief. Noble women came and each told the greatest sorrow of her life — one had lost husband and children, another her brothers and her freedom — to make her weep, but she could not. At last her sister drew the covering from Sigurðr and laid his head in Guðrún's lap, bidding her look on her beloved and kiss him as if he lived. She saw his fair hair clotted with blood, his keen eyes dimmed, his breast pierced by the sword, and she fell on him weeping until her tears ran like rain, and the geese in the yard cried with her. Over his body, says the saga, she said her Sigurðr among the sons of Gjúki had been like a tall leek above the grass, like a bright gem on a golden band, and now she was as small in the hall as a leaf in the wind.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第31章。

body_zh: 布伦希尔德对贡纳尔说：我做了一个梦，梦见所有的人都会为这件事付出代价。她预言了居基家族的未来：古德伦将嫁给她的哥哥阿特利，贡纳尔和霍格尼将死在阿特利的手里，古德伦又将为兄弟们报仇。说完，她把自己的金子分给侍女们，穿上金色的铠甲，用剑刺进了自己的身体。贡纳尔赶来时，她已经奄奄一息了。她对贡纳尔说出了最后的请求：请为西古尔德和我建一座宽大的火葬堆，让我躺在他的身边，就像我们曾经同床的那三夜一样，在我们中间放一把出鞘的宝剑；把西古尔德的随从、两只猎鹰、几条狗，还有我的侍女们都放在火葬堆上，让我们一同到另一个世界去，这样，地狱的门就不会砸在他的脚后跟上。贡纳尔照她的话做了。西古尔德和布伦希尔德一起被火化了，火焰熊熊燃起，人们都说，世上再也不会出现像西古尔德这样的人了。萨迦接下来还讲了古德伦与阿特利的故事，以及那批黄金如何最后沉入莱茵河，那将是另一个故事了。
body_en: Brynhildr told Gunnarr she had dreamed that all would pay for the deed, and foretold the fate of Gjúki's house: Guðrún would marry her brother Atli, Gunnarr and Högni would die at Atli's hands, and Guðrún would avenge them. Then she gave her gold to her maids, put on a golden byrnie and stabbed herself with a sword. As she lay dying, she asked Gunnarr to build one broad pyre for Sigurðr and herself, to lay her by his side as in the three nights they shared, with a naked sword between them, and to lay on it Sigurðr's men, two hawks, hounds and her maids, so that they would go together into the other world and the door of Hel would not fall on his heels. Gunnarr did as she asked, and Sigurðr and Brynhildr were burned together; men said no one like Sigurðr would ever be born again. The saga goes on to tell of Guðrún and Atli and how the gold sank at last into the Rhine — but that is another story.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第32章。

body_zh: 不久，西古尔德骑着格拉尼，带着法夫纳的黄金，来到了居基王的宫廷。人们从没见过这样高大英俊、装束华丽的骑士，国王和王子们热情地款待了他，他在那里住了很久。他每天都想着布伦希尔德，常常说起她。王后格里姆希尔德看出了西古尔德的高贵和他拥有的巨大财富，心想如果能让他娶了自己的女儿，对她的家族将是多么大的好处。她调制了一种魔法的酒，在一次宴会上亲手递给西古尔德，说：我们都很喜欢你，居基王愿意做你的父亲，我愿意做你的母亲，我的儿子们愿意做你的兄弟。西古尔德喝下了这杯酒。酒一下肚，他就把布伦希尔德忘得干干净净，一点也想不起来了。不久，他娶了古德伦为妻，婚礼持续了许多天。西古尔德又和贡纳尔、霍格尼按照古老的习俗，让鲜血流在一起，在一块草皮下面立誓结为兄弟，发誓像亲兄弟一样彼此忠诚。西古尔德给了古德伦一块法夫纳的心，她吃了以后变得更加冷酷，也更加聪明。他们生了一个儿子，取名西格蒙德。
body_en: Soon Sigurðr came to Gjúki's court riding Grani with Fáfnir's gold. No one had seen a knight so tall, fair and splendidly arrayed, and he stayed there long, honoured by the king and his sons, yet he thought of Brynhildr and often spoke of her. Queen Grímhildr, seeing his nobility and wealth, wished him married to her daughter. At a feast she gave him a horn of mead she had brewed with magic, saying that Gjúki would be his father, she his mother and her sons his brothers. He drank, and at once forgot Brynhildr entirely. He married Guðrún, with a feast lasting many days, and he, Gunnarr and Högni swore brotherhood in the old way, letting their blood run together under a strip of turf. Sigurðr gave Guðrún some of Fáfnir's heart to eat, and she became grimmer and wiser; they had a son named Sigmundr.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第26章。

body_zh: 格里姆希尔德又对儿子贡纳尔说：你应该娶一个妻子，最合适的就是布伦希尔德。她是一位尊贵的女子，你若娶了她，我们的家族就更加强大了。贡纳尔愿意去求婚，西古尔德也答应陪他一起去。他们先去见布伦希尔德的父亲布德利国王，国王说：我女儿自己决定嫁给谁，她发誓只嫁给能骑马穿过她厅堂四周燃烧的火墙的人。他们又去找赫米尔，赫米尔也说，这要由布伦希尔德自己来定。他们来到布伦希尔德住的地方，只见她的厅堂四周燃着熊熊的火焰，火光直冲天空。贡纳尔骑着他的马冲向火墙，可是马一靠近火焰就惊恐地退了回来，怎么也不肯往前走。西古尔德说：你骑我的格拉尼试试吧。贡纳尔骑上格拉尼，可是格拉尼一动也不动，因为它只听西古尔德的。贡纳尔没有办法了。这时，他们想起了格里姆希尔德教给他们的魔法：西古尔德和贡纳尔交换容貌。于是西古尔德变成了贡纳尔的样子，贡纳尔变成了西古尔德的样子。
body_en: Grímhildr told Gunnarr he should take a wife, and the best match was Brynhildr. Gunnarr was willing, and Sigurðr agreed to ride with him. Her father, King Buðli, said Brynhildr would choose for herself, for she had vowed to marry only the man who rode through the fire burning round her hall; Heimir said the same. They came to her hall and saw the flames blazing up to the sky. Gunnarr rode at the fire, but his horse shied back and would not go on. Sigurðr lent him Grani, but Grani would not move under him, for he would bear no one but Sigurðr. Then they used the craft Grímhildr had taught them: Sigurðr and Gunnarr exchanged shapes, Sigurðr taking Gunnarr's likeness and Gunnarr Sigurðr's.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第27章。

body_zh: 西古尔德以贡纳尔的样子骑上了格拉尼，手握格拉姆，金色的马刺踢向马腹。格拉尼一感觉到马刺，就向火墙冲去。大地震动，火焰冲天，可是格拉尼毫不畏惧地穿过了火海，仿佛火焰在他们面前自动熄灭了一样。西古尔德走进厅堂，布伦希尔德坐在高座上，像一只坐在水面上的天鹅，头戴头盔，手握宝剑。她问他是谁，他说：我是居基的儿子贡纳尔，你发过誓，谁能穿过火墙，你就嫁给谁，现在我来了。布伦希尔德一时不知如何回答，她想起了自己的誓言，又想起了西古尔德，可是誓言不能违背，她只好同意嫁给他。西古尔德在那里住了三夜，他们同睡在一张床上，可是西古尔德把出鞘的格拉姆放在两人中间。布伦希尔德问他为什么这样做，他说：命运要求我这样迎娶我的新娘，否则我就会死去。临别时，他从布伦希尔德的手上取下了那枚安德瓦拉诺特戒指——那正是当年他亲手送给她的——又从法夫纳的财宝中取出另一枚戒指给她。然后他骑马穿过火墙，回到同伴那里，两人换回了自己的容貌。
body_en: In Gunnarr's shape Sigurðr mounted Grani with Gram in hand and golden spurs on his heels, and Grani leapt at the fire as soon as he felt the spurs; the earth shook and the flames rose to heaven, but Grani went through as if the fire died down before them. In the hall Brynhildr sat on a high seat like a swan on the waves, with helm and sword. Asked who he was, he said he was Gunnarr, son of Gjúki, come through the fire as her vow required. She did not know what to answer, thinking of her vow and of Sigurðr, but the vow could not be broken, and she consented. Sigurðr stayed three nights and they lay in one bed, but he laid the naked sword Gram between them; when she asked why, he said it was fated that he should wed his bride so or die. When he left he took from her the ring Andvaranautr — the very ring he had given her — and gave her another from Fáfnir's hoard. He rode back through the fire to his comrade, and they took their own shapes again.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第27章。

body_zh: 布伦希尔德回到父亲那里，对赫米尔说：一个名叫贡纳尔的国王穿过了我的火墙，我只好嫁给他。可是我曾对你说过，在赫利姆谷许下誓言的是西古尔德，只有他才能做到这件事。她心中充满了疑惑。不久，盛大的婚礼在居基王的宫中举行，贡纳尔娶了布伦希尔德。宴会持续了很多天。就在婚宴结束的时候，西古尔德忽然想起了他对布伦希尔德许下的所有誓言，那杯遗忘之酒的魔力消失了。可是他已经娶了古德伦，布伦希尔德也已经成了他结拜兄弟的妻子。他什么也没有说，默默地忍受着这一切。萨迦说，从那以后，西古尔德和布伦希尔德在同一个宫廷里生活了很长时间，两人见面时都不露声色，可是布伦希尔德的心中一直有一个疑问：为什么穿过火墙的不是西古尔德？西古尔德心里藏着真相，不能说出来，因为那会让他的结拜兄弟蒙羞。表面的平静之下，悲剧正在一天天逼近。
body_en: Brynhildr went to her father and told Heimir that a king called Gunnarr had ridden her fire and she must marry him — though she had told him that Sigurðr, to whom she had sworn at Hlymdalir, was the only man who could do it. Doubt filled her heart. The wedding of Gunnarr and Brynhildr was held at Gjúki's court with a feast of many days; and when the feast ended, Sigurðr remembered all his oaths to Brynhildr, for the drink's magic had passed. But he was married to Guðrún and she to his sworn brother, and he said nothing and bore it in silence. So they lived long at the same court, giving no sign when they met; yet Brynhildr always wondered why it was not Sigurðr who had come through the fire, and Sigurðr kept the truth hidden, for telling it would shame his sworn brother. Beneath the calm, the tragedy drew nearer every day.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第27章。

body_zh: 有一天，布伦希尔德和古德伦一起到莱茵河里洗头。布伦希尔德往河里走得更远，古德伦问她为什么。布伦希尔德说：在这件事上，我为什么要和你平起平坐？我的父亲比你的父亲更有权势，我的丈夫做了许多大事，骑马穿过了燃烧的火墙，而你的丈夫只不过是希亚尔普雷克国王的一个奴仆。古德伦大怒，说：你还是闭嘴为好，我的丈夫杀死了法夫纳和雷金，得到了那些黄金，而穿过火墙的正是他，不是贡纳尔。在你身边睡了三夜、把宝剑放在你们中间的，就是西古尔德。布伦希尔德不相信。古德伦伸出手来，说：你看看我手上的这枚戒指，你认得它吗？布伦希尔德一看，那正是安德瓦拉诺特。她的脸一下子变得像死人一样惨白，一句话也没有说，转身回家去了。萨迦说，从这一天起，她再也不说话，整天躺在床上。两个王后之间的这一场争吵，把隐藏了多年的秘密全部揭开了，安德瓦利的诅咒终于开始在这枚戒指的主人们身上应验。
body_en: One day Brynhildr and Guðrún went to the Rhine to wash their hair, and Brynhildr waded further out. When Guðrún asked why, Brynhildr said she would not be on a level with her in this: her father was mightier, and her husband had done great deeds and ridden through the burning fire, while Guðrún's was a thrall of King Hjálprekr. Guðrún, angered, said she had better be silent: her husband had slain Fáfnir and Reginn and won the gold, and it was he, not Gunnarr, who rode through the fire and lay three nights beside her with the sword between them. When Brynhildr would not believe it, Guðrún held out her hand and asked if she knew this ring — and it was Andvaranautr. Brynhildr went pale as death, said nothing, and went home, and from that day, says the saga, she lay in her bed and would not speak. The queens' quarrel laid bare the long-hidden secret, and Andvari's curse began to work on the ring's owners.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第28章。

body_zh: 布伦希尔德躺在床上，一连几天不吃不喝，也不说话。贡纳尔、霍格尼和古德伦先后来看她，她都不理睬。贡纳尔来问她到底怎么了，她才开口，痛苦地责备他：你骗了我。那个穿过火墙的人不是你，是西古尔德。当年我发誓只嫁给最勇敢的人，那就是西古尔德，可是你们用诡计让我嫁给了你。你的母亲格里姆希尔德是最坏的女人，是她给西古尔德下了遗忘的药。我宁愿去死，也不愿再看见你们。她诅咒居基王的家族，说他们背弃了誓言，必将遭到报应。贡纳尔无言以对。她的悲伤和愤怒越来越深，宫里的人听见她的叹息声，都觉得可怕。萨迦说，布伦希尔德的愤怒像火一样燃烧，任何人都不敢靠近她，就连西古尔德自己，也感到心中沉重，他知道这件事不会有好的结局。贡纳尔去找西古尔德，请他去和布伦希尔德谈一谈，也许只有他能平息她的怒火。
body_en: Brynhildr lay in her bed for days without eating, drinking or speaking, and paid no heed to Gunnarr, Högni or Guðrún. When Gunnarr asked what ailed her, she reproached him bitterly: he had deceived her; it was Sigurðr, not he, who rode through the fire; she had vowed to marry the bravest man, and that was Sigurðr, yet by guile they had wedded her to Gunnarr; his mother Grímhildr was the worst of women, who had given Sigurðr the drink of forgetfulness; she would rather die than see them. She cursed the house of Gjúki as oath-breakers who would be repaid. Gunnarr had no answer. Her grief and wrath grew until the household dreaded her sighs; even Sigurðr's heart was heavy, knowing no good could come of it. Gunnarr asked Sigurðr to speak with her, hoping he alone could calm her.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第29章。

body_zh: 西古尔德走进布伦希尔德的房间，对她说：醒醒吧，布伦希尔德，太阳照着整个宫殿，你睡得够久了，不要再悲伤了。布伦希尔德说：你怎么敢来见我？你比任何人都更狠心地背叛了我。西古尔德说：我并没有骗你，那杯遗忘之酒让我忘记了你，等我想起来的时候，一切都已经晚了。可是我很快就认出了你，我对你的爱，和我对自己的爱一样深。他说：我宁愿你嫁给了我，现在我对你的心从来没有变过。如果能让你不再痛苦，我愿意抛弃古德伦，娶你为妻。布伦希尔德回答：我不愿意要两个丈夫在同一个大厅里，我宁愿死也不会背叛贡纳尔。我曾经发过誓，要嫁给那个穿过火墙的人，我也会遵守这个誓言，哪怕它让我失去性命。西古尔德沉默了很久，走出房间时，他的悲伤是那么巨大，萨迦说，他胸前的锁子甲的环子都被撑断了。两个曾经互相许下誓言的人，因为一杯酒、一个诡计和一枚戒指，走到了无法回头的地步。
body_en: Sigurðr went in and bade Brynhildr wake, for the sun shone over the hall and she had slept long enough. She asked how he dared come to her, who had betrayed her worst of all. He had not deceived her, he said; the drink of forgetfulness had made him forget her, and when he remembered it was too late; he loved her as he loved himself. He would rather she were his wife; his heart toward her had never changed, and to end her grief he would leave Guðrún and marry her. She answered that she would not have two husbands in one hall, and would rather die than betray Gunnarr; she had sworn to wed the man who rode the fire and would keep that oath though it cost her life. Sigurðr was long silent, and when he went out his grief was so great, says the saga, that the rings of his mail-coat burst asunder. Two who had sworn to each other were brought by a drink, a deceit and a ring to a place from which there was no return.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第29章。

body_zh: 布伦希尔德对贡纳尔说：你若想要我活下去，就必须杀死西古尔德和他的儿子，否则我就离开你，回到我的亲人那里去。她说，西古尔德在火中的那三夜背叛了贡纳尔——这不是真的，可是她要用这句话逼贡纳尔下手。贡纳尔十分苦恼，他和霍格尼商量。霍格尼说：我们和西古尔德发过结拜兄弟的誓言，不能违背誓言亲手杀他。贡纳尔说：那就让古托姆去做吧，他年纪小，没有参加我们的誓言。他们用狼肉和蛇肉做成食物，又加上了别的东西，给古托姆吃了，让他变得凶狠暴躁，又答应给他大量的黄金和土地，怂恿他去杀死西古尔德。第一天清晨，古托姆走进西古尔德的卧室，西古尔德醒着，用锐利的目光看着他，古托姆不敢下手，退了出去。第二天清晨也是这样。第三天清晨，西古尔德睡着了，古托姆拔出剑，一剑刺穿了他的身体，剑尖一直刺进了床下的木板。
body_en: Brynhildr told Gunnarr that if he wished her to live, he must kill Sigurðr and his son, or she would leave him — claiming falsely that Sigurðr had betrayed him in those three nights beyond the fire. Gunnarr, sorely troubled, took counsel with Högni, who said they were bound by their oaths of brotherhood and could not kill him with their own hands. Then let Guttormr do it, said Gunnarr, for he was young and had sworn no oath. They fed Guttormr the flesh of wolf and serpent and other things to make him fierce, and promised him gold and lands. Twice at dawn Guttormr went into Sigurðr's chamber and found him awake, looking at him with keen eyes, and dared not strike; the third morning Sigurðr was asleep, and Guttormr drew his sword and thrust it through him so that the point stood in the bedding beneath.
evidence_note: 《沃尔松格萨迦》第30章。

body_zh: 达费德的王子皮威尔统治着七个坎特雷夫的土地。有一天，他在阿伯斯的宫殿里，忽然想去打猎，就来到了格林·库赫，那里是他最喜欢的狩猎场。他放出猎犬，吹响号角，追赶一头鹿，和同伴们走散了。他听见另一群猎犬的叫声，那群猎犬也在追赶一头雄鹿，在一片林间空地上，它们把雄鹿扑倒了。皮威尔看着这群猎犬，大吃一惊：他从没见过这样的猎犬，它们全身雪白，耳朵却是鲜红的，白得发亮，红得发亮。皮威尔赶走了那群陌生的猎犬，让自己的猎犬去吃那头鹿。这时，一个骑着高大灰马的人赶来了，他身穿灰褐色的猎装，脖子上挂着号角。那人说：王子，我认识你，可是我不向你问好，你太无礼了。我从没见过有人像你这样，赶走别人猎犬扑倒的鹿，让自己的猎犬去吃。皮威尔问他是谁。那人说：我是安农的国王阿拉文。皮威尔诚恳地道歉，问怎样才能赎罪，赢得他的友谊。阿拉文说：在我的国土旁边，有一个名叫哈夫甘的国王，他总是和我作对。你如果能替我除掉他，就能赢得我的友谊。
body_en: Pwyll, prince of Dyfed, lord of seven cantrefs, was at Arberth when he wished to hunt and went to Glyn Cuch. Separated from his companions while following a stag, he heard another pack and saw it bring down a stag in a clearing — hounds such as he had never seen, of shining white with shining red ears. He drove them off and set his own hounds on the stag. A rider on a great grey horse came up, dressed in grey-brown hunting garb with a horn at his neck, and said he knew Pwyll but would not greet him, for he had never seen worse discourtesy than to drive off the hounds that had killed the stag and bait one's own upon it. Asked who he was, he said: 'Arawn, a crowned king in Annwn.' Pwyll asked how he might make amends and win his friendship. There was a king called Hafgan whose land bordered his, said Arawn, and who warred against him continually; by ridding him of Hafgan, Pwyll would win his friendship.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·格林·库赫的狩猎。

body_zh: 格温特·伊斯·科伊德的领主泰尔农·特威尔夫·里安特有一匹母马，是他国土上最美的马。每年五月节的前夜，这匹母马都会生下一匹马驹，可是马驹生下来后，没有一个人知道它去了哪里，总是凭空消失。泰尔农对妻子说：今年我一定要弄个明白。五月节前夜，他把母马牵进马厩，自己全副武装地守在里面。天黑后，母马生下了一匹高大漂亮的马驹，马驹刚站起来，泰尔农就听见一阵巨大的声响，一只巨大的手爪从窗户里伸了进来，一把抓住了马驹的鬃毛。泰尔农拔出剑，向那只手臂砍去，把它从肘部砍断了，断臂和马驹一起留在了马厩里。外面传来一声惨叫。泰尔农冲出门去追，可是夜太黑了，什么也看不见。他想起门没有关，赶紧跑回来，看见门口放着一个裹在锦缎襁褓里的婴儿。他抱起孩子，看他是个强壮的男孩，就把他抱给妻子看。妻子说：我们没有孩子，就把他当作我们的儿子吧，我会对人说是我自己生的。他们给孩子取名为“金发的格利”，因为他头上的头发像金子一样黄。
body_en: Teyrnon Twrf Liant, lord of Gwent Is Coed, had the fairest mare in his land; every May Eve she foaled, and no one knew what became of the foal. This year, he told his wife, he would find out. On May Eve he brought the mare into the stable and watched there armed. At nightfall she bore a large, handsome foal, and as it stood up he heard a great noise and a huge claw came through the window and seized the foal by the mane. Teyrnon drew his sword and struck off the arm at the elbow, so that it and the foal remained inside, and outside there was a scream. He rushed out but could see nothing in the dark; remembering the open door, he ran back and found at the threshold an infant boy wrapped in a mantle of satin. He took the strong child to his wife, who, being childless, said they would rear him as their own and she would say she had borne him. They named him Gwri Golden-hair, for his hair was yellow as gold.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·泰尔农的马驹。

heading_en: The boy who looked like Pwyll
body_zh: 这个孩子长得飞快，一岁时就像三岁的孩子一样会走路，两岁时像六岁的孩子一样强壮，不到四岁，就要和马夫们讨价还价，要他们让他把马牵到河边去饮水。泰尔农的妻子说：我们那一夜得到的马驹在哪里？把它驯好，送给这孩子吧。泰尔农就把那匹马驹送给了男孩。就在这时，他们听说了里安农的事：她因为孩子失踪受到了惩罚。泰尔农为她感到难过，他仔细地看着这个男孩，越看越觉得他长得像皮威尔——他从前曾经在皮威尔手下做过侍从，熟悉王子的模样。男孩的面容和皮威尔一模一样。泰尔农想：留下别人的孩子是不对的，让那位贵妇人为了一件没有犯过的罪受苦更是不对。他把这个想法告诉了妻子，妻子虽然舍不得，也同意了，她说：我们会因此得到三样好处：让里安农摆脱惩罚，得到皮威尔的感谢，还有这孩子将来的报答——如果他是一个高尚的人，就会成为我们的养子。于是，泰尔农带着男孩，骑马向阿伯斯出发了。
body_en: The boy grew wondrously: at one year he walked like a child of three, at two he was as big as a child of six, and before he was four he was bargaining with the grooms to let him lead the horses to water. Teyrnon's wife asked for the foal of that night to be broken in and given to the boy, and it was. Then they heard of Rhiannon's punishment for her lost son. Teyrnon, grieving for her, looked closely at the boy and saw that he was the image of Pwyll, whom he had once served and knew well. It was wrong, he thought, to keep another's son, and worse that the lady should suffer for a crime she had not done. His wife, though loath, agreed: they would gain three things — Rhiannon's release, Pwyll's thanks, and the boy's gratitude, for if he proved noble he would be their foster-son. So Teyrnon set out for Arberth with the boy.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·像皮威尔的男孩。

body_zh: 泰尔农带着男孩和两个骑士来到阿伯斯，看见里安农坐在宫门边的上马石旁。她站起来对他们说：大人们，请停下，我要把你们每个人背进宫去，这是我的惩罚，因为我杀死了自己的儿子。泰尔农说：夫人，我们谁也不会让你背。他们走进宫殿，皮威尔热情地款待了他们。宴会上，泰尔农讲述了母马、手爪和孩子的故事，然后对里安农说：夫人，这就是你的儿子，那些诬告你的人说了谎。大厅里所有的人一看见这个男孩，都认出他和皮威尔长得一模一样。里安农说：如果这是真的，我的忧虑就结束了。威尔士语里，“忧虑”这个词叫作“普雷德里”。贵族彭达兰·达费德说：您给您的儿子取了一个好名字，就叫他普雷德里吧。于是男孩被叫作普雷德里，是皮威尔安农之主的儿子。皮威尔要给泰尔农丰厚的报酬，泰尔农谢绝了。普雷德里被交给彭达兰·达费德抚养，长大后成了达费德最出色的青年。皮威尔去世后，普雷德里继承了达费德的七个坎特雷夫，又征服了更多的土地，娶了基格瓦为妻。第一支就这样结束了。
body_en: Teyrnon came to Arberth with the boy and two knights and found Rhiannon by the horse-block. She rose and offered to carry each of them into the court, for that was her penance for slaying her son; none of them would let her. Pwyll welcomed them, and at the feast Teyrnon told the story of the mare, the claw and the child, and said to Rhiannon: 'Lady, here is your son; those who accused you lied.' Everyone in the hall saw that the boy was the image of Pwyll. 'If this is true,' said Rhiannon, 'I am delivered of my anxiety' — pryder, in Welsh. 'Well have you named your son,' said the nobleman Pendaran Dyfed: 'Pryderi.' So the boy was called Pryderi son of Pwyll, Head of Annwn. Teyrnon refused the rich rewards Pwyll offered. Pryderi was fostered by Pendaran Dyfed and grew to be the finest youth in Dyfed; after Pwyll's death he ruled the seven cantrefs, won more lands, and married Cigfa. So ends the First Branch.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·普雷德里。

body_zh: 阿拉文说：我会把你变成我的样子，让你代替我在安农做一年的国王，我的王国里没有一个人会认出你，连我的妻子也不会；而我会变成你的样子，替你统治达费德。一年后的今天，我们在这里相见。一年后，你要在浅滩上与哈夫甘决斗，你只能打他一下，他就会死；即使他求你再打第二下，你也绝不能答应，因为如果再打一下，他第二天就会像从前一样恢复过来。皮威尔答应了。阿拉文领着他来到安农的宫殿，那里有华丽的大厅和卧室，满是金银器皿和锦缎衣裳，人们都以为他就是国王，殷勤地侍候他。王后是皮威尔见过的最美丽的女人，她穿着金色的锦缎，与他谈笑，非常和蔼可亲。可是到了夜里，他们上床以后，皮威尔就转过身去，背对着她，一句话也不说，直到天亮。白天，他像国王一样和王后说笑、宴饮，到了夜里，又是一样。就这样，整整一年过去了，每一夜都是如此。皮威尔在安农打猎、宴饮、处理国事，享受着彼世的一切荣华，却始终没有辜负阿拉文的信任。
body_en: Arawn said he would give Pwyll his own shape so that he could reign in Annwn for a year, and no one, not even Arawn's wife, would know him; Arawn would take Pwyll's shape and rule Dyfed. A year from that day they would meet there. At the end of the year Pwyll would meet Hafgan at the ford and must strike him only one blow, which would kill him; though Hafgan begged for a second, he must not give it, for with a second blow Hafgan would be as well as ever next day. Pwyll agreed. In Annwn's palace, with its halls and chambers full of gold vessels and brocaded robes, all took him for the king, and the queen, the fairest woman he had ever seen, in golden brocade, was kind and gracious to him by day. But each night in bed he turned his face to the wall and said not a word till morning, and so it was every night for a whole year; he hunted, feasted and governed in all the splendour of the Otherworld, yet never betrayed Arawn's trust.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·安农的一年。

body_zh: 约定的那一天到了，皮威尔带着安农的贵族们来到浅滩，哈夫甘也带着他的人马来了。一个骑士站出来宣布：各位贵族，请听好，这是两位国王之间的决斗，事关土地和统治权，其他人都不要插手，让他们两人一决胜负。两位国王驾着马，从浅滩的两边向中间冲去。第一次交锋，皮威尔一枪刺中了哈夫甘的盾牌中心，把盾牌劈成了两半，长矛穿透了他的铠甲，把哈夫甘从马背上掀了下去，一直摔出了一枪一臂的距离，哈夫甘受了致命的伤。哈夫甘说：你有什么权利要我的命？我从没冒犯过你，也不知道你为什么要杀我。可是既然你已经开始了，看在上天的份上，你就结束我的生命吧。皮威尔说：我可能会后悔做我已经做过的事。你去找别人杀你吧，我不会再打你了。哈夫甘对他的贵族们说：抬走我吧，我的末日到了，我再也不能保护你们了。皮威尔对哈夫甘的人说：请你们想一想，谁应该做我的臣民。于是，哈夫甘的贵族们都向皮威尔表示臣服，安农的两个王国从此合而为一，都归在阿拉文的名下。
body_en: On the appointed day Pwyll went to the ford with the nobles of Annwn, and Hafgan came with his host. A knight proclaimed that this was a contest between two kings for land and rule, and all others should stand aside. The kings rode at each other from either side of the ford; at the first encounter Pwyll struck the centre of Hafgan's shield so that it split in two and the spear pierced his armour, and Hafgan was thrown a spear's and an arm's length over his horse's crupper, mortally wounded. 'What right have you to my death?' said Hafgan; 'I never wronged you. But since you have begun, for heaven's sake finish it.' 'I may repent of what I have done,' said Pwyll; 'let whoever will slay you; I will not strike again.' Hafgan bade his nobles carry him away, for his end had come. Pwyll asked Hafgan's men to consider whose subjects they should be, and they all did homage to him, and the two kingdoms of Annwn were united under Arawn's name.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·浅滩之战。

body_zh: 一年期满，皮威尔来到格林·库赫，与阿拉文相见，两人各自恢复了原来的模样。阿拉文说：愿上天报答你对我的友谊，我已经听说了你为我做的一切。阿拉文回到安农，与贵族们谈话，发现他们都说他今年比往年更加慈爱、更加贤明，又得到了哈夫甘的国土。夜里，他与王后同床，和她说话、亲热，王后惊讶地说：你这一年来夜里从不和我说话，从不转过身来对着我，今夜怎么变了？阿拉文这才明白，皮威尔一整年都没有碰过他的妻子。他说：哎呀，我的朋友是多么忠实可靠啊。于是他把一切都告诉了王后，王后也说：你真有一个忠诚的朋友。皮威尔回到达费德，也问贵族们这一年他统治得怎么样，贵族们说：您从没有像今年这样公正、慷慨、贤明。皮威尔把真相告诉了他们，贵族们说：请您以后继续这样统治我们吧。从此，皮威尔和阿拉文结下了深厚的友谊，互相赠送马匹、猎犬、猎鹰和各种珍宝。因为他在安农做了一年国王，又把两个王国合在一起，人们不再叫他达费德的皮威尔，而叫他“安农之主”皮威尔。
body_en: At the year's end Pwyll met Arawn at Glyn Cuch and each took his own shape again. Arawn returned to Annwn and found his nobles praising him for a year of greater kindness and wisdom than ever, and for winning Hafgan's land. That night, when he spoke lovingly to his queen, she wondered that he did so, for in a whole year he had not spoken to her or turned toward her at night. Then Arawn knew that Pwyll had kept faith, and said, 'How faithful a friend I have found,' and told her everything, and she agreed. In Dyfed Pwyll asked his nobles how he had ruled that year; never so justly, generously and wisely, they said, and when he told them the truth they asked him to go on ruling so. Pwyll and Arawn became firm friends and sent each other horses, hounds, hawks and treasures; and because Pwyll had ruled a year in Annwn and joined its kingdoms, he was called no longer Pwyll of Dyfed but Pwyll, Head of Annwn.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·安农之主。

heading_en: The lady on the white horse
body_zh: 有一天，皮威尔在阿伯斯的王宫里举行宴会，宴罢之后，他走上了宫殿上方一座名叫戈尔塞斯·阿伯斯的土丘。人们说，任何一个贵族坐在这座土丘上，都会遇到两件事之一：要么被打伤，要么看见奇迹。皮威尔说：在这么多人中间，我不怕被打伤，倒很想看见奇迹。他在土丘上坐下来。不一会儿，他看见一位女子骑着一匹高大的纯白色骏马，身穿闪亮的金色锦缎，从大路上缓缓走来。皮威尔问身边的人：你们谁认识这位女子？没有人认识。他派一个人去追她，那人跑到大路上，女子从他身边经过，他拼命追赶，可是追得越快，女子离他越远，她的马却始终是那样不紧不慢地走着。第二天，皮威尔又派了一个骑着最快的马的人去追，结果还是一样，马跑得越快，她离得越远。第三天，皮威尔亲自骑马去追，他用尽全力，仍然追不上。最后他喊道：姑娘，看在你最爱的人的份上，请你停下来等我。女子说：我很乐意停下来，如果你早一点这样请求，你的马也就不用受这么多罪了。
body_en: One day after a feast at Arberth, Pwyll went up the mound above the court called Gorsedd Arberth, of which it was said that any noble who sat on it would either receive wounds or see a wonder. He was not afraid of wounds among so many, he said, but would gladly see a wonder. As he sat, he saw a lady on a great pure-white horse, in a garment of shining gold brocade, coming slowly along the highway. No one knew her. He sent a man after her on foot, but the faster he ran, the further she drew ahead, though her horse kept the same slow pace. Next day he sent a rider on the swiftest horse, with the same result. The third day Pwyll rode after her himself and, failing with all his speed, called out: 'Maiden, for the sake of him you love best, stay for me.' 'I will stay gladly,' she said, 'and it would have been better for your horse if you had asked long ago.'
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·阿伯斯土丘。

body_zh: 女子揭开面纱，皮威尔觉得自己从没见过这样美丽的面容。她说：我是老赫菲德的女儿里安农，他们要把我嫁给一个我不愿意嫁的男人，因为我爱的是你。我来，就是想听你的回答。皮威尔说：在世上所有的女子中，我只愿意选择你。里安农说：那么一年以后的今天，在我父亲的宫殿里举行婚宴。一年后，皮威尔带着一百个骑士来到赫菲德的宫殿，婚宴非常丰盛。宴会正热闹时，一个身材高大、头发褐色、穿着锦缎的年轻人走进大厅，向皮威尔问候，说：我来是向你请求一个恩惠。皮威尔不假思索地说：无论你要求什么，只要我能做到，我都给你。里安农惊叫道：你为什么要这样回答！年轻人说：好，各位贵族都听见了。我要的是你今晚要娶的这位新娘，还有这场婚宴。皮威尔哑口无言。里安农说：你就沉默吧，从来没有人像你这样笨嘴拙舌的。这个人就是克卢德的儿子格瓦尔，我就是被许配给他的。可是一个贵族说出的话不能收回，皮威尔只好答应。里安农悄悄对他说：把我交给他，可是我决不会成为他的人。一年后，他会来这里举行婚宴，到时候你带着一百个骑士躲在果园里，再带上我给你的这只小口袋。
body_en: She lifted her veil and he thought he had never seen a fairer face. 'I am Rhiannon, daughter of Hefeydd the Old,' she said, 'and they would give me to a husband against my will, because I love you; I have come for your answer.' Of all women in the world, said Pwyll, he would choose her. Then a year from that night, she said, there would be a wedding feast at her father's court. A year later Pwyll came with a hundred knights. In the midst of the feast a tall auburn-haired youth in brocade greeted Pwyll and asked a boon, and Pwyll said without thinking that whatever he asked, if it were in his power, he would have. 'Why did you answer so?' cried Rhiannon. 'Bear witness, nobles,' said the youth: 'I ask for the bride and the feast.' Pwyll was silent. 'Be silent as long as you will,' said Rhiannon; 'never was a man more slow-witted. This is Gwawl son of Clud, to whom they would give me.' A noble's word could not be taken back, so Pwyll had to agree; but Rhiannon whispered that she would never be Gwawl's, and that in a year, when Gwawl came for his feast, Pwyll should hide in the orchard with a hundred knights and bring the little bag she would give him.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·轻率的许诺。

body_zh: 一年后，格瓦尔来赴他的婚宴。皮威尔穿上破烂的衣服，脚上套着笨重的旧鞋，扮成一个乞丐，带着里安农给他的小口袋走进大厅，向格瓦尔请求一个恩惠：只求你把我这只小口袋装满食物。格瓦尔说：这个要求不算过分，就给他装吧。仆人们往口袋里装食物，装了一盘又一盘，可是口袋怎么也装不满。格瓦尔问：你这口袋什么时候才能装满？皮威尔说：除非有一位拥有土地和财富的贵人站起来，用双脚把里面的食物踩实，说一声“装够了”，否则它永远也装不满。里安农对格瓦尔说：快去踩吧。格瓦尔站起身，把两只脚伸进了口袋里，皮威尔立刻把口袋往上一拉，盖过了格瓦尔的头，扎紧了袋口，然后吹响了号角。藏在果园里的骑士们冲进大厅，把格瓦尔的随从都抓了起来。每个骑士走进来，都用脚踢一下口袋，或者用棍子打一下，问：这里面是什么？其他人回答：是一只獾。这就是“口袋里的獾”游戏的来历。格瓦尔在口袋里求饶，赫菲德劝皮威尔饶了他，条件是格瓦尔放弃对里安农的一切要求，不再报复，并找来担保人。格瓦尔答应了。皮威尔和里安农终于成了婚，回到达费德，人民都欢迎他们。
body_en: A year later Gwawl came to his feast. Pwyll, in ragged clothes and clumsy old shoes like a beggar, came into the hall with Rhiannon's little bag and asked Gwawl for a boon: only to fill the bag with food. Gwawl granted it, but dish after dish went in and the bag was no fuller. When Gwawl asked when it would be full, Pwyll said not until a nobleman with lands and riches stood up and trod down the food with both feet and said 'Enough has been put in.' Rhiannon urged Gwawl to do it; he put both feet in, and Pwyll pulled the bag up over his head, tied it and blew his horn. His knights rushed in from the orchard and seized Gwawl's men, and each who came in struck the bag with foot or staff and asked, 'What is here?' — 'A badger,' the others answered; and that was the first playing of Badger in the Bag. Gwawl begged for mercy; at Hefeydd's counsel Pwyll released him on condition that he give up all claim to Rhiannon and seek no vengeance, with sureties. So Pwyll and Rhiannon were married and went home to Dyfed, where the people welcomed them.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·口袋里的獾。

body_zh: 皮威尔和里安农幸福地统治着达费德，可是过了两年，他们还没有孩子。第三年，贵族们聚集在一起，劝皮威尔另娶一个能生育的妻子，免得王位没有继承人。皮威尔说：我们结婚的时间还不长，再等一年，如果到时还没有孩子，我就听你们的。就在那一年里，里安农生下了一个儿子。在孩子出生的那一夜，六个女人被派来守护母亲和婴儿。半夜里，她们都睡着了，里安农也睡着了。天快亮时，女人们醒来，发现孩子不见了，四处寻找都找不到。她们害怕受到惩罚，竟商量出了一个恶毒的主意：她们杀了一只小猎犬，把它的血涂在熟睡的里安农的脸上和手上，把骨头扔在她的床边，然后一口咬定，是里安农在夜里吃掉了自己的孩子，她们六个人怎么也拦不住她。里安农醒来，问孩子在哪里，女人们就这样诬告她。里安农说：你们不要撒谎了，我知道你们是害怕受罚，如果你们说出真相，我会保护你们。可是她们坚持自己的谎言。
body_en: Pwyll and Rhiannon ruled Dyfed happily, but after two years they had no child, and in the third year the nobles urged Pwyll to take another wife who could bear him an heir. They had not been married long, said Pwyll; let them wait a year more. In that year Rhiannon bore a son. On the night of the birth six women were set to watch mother and child, but at midnight they and Rhiannon fell asleep, and toward dawn the women woke to find the boy gone. Fearing punishment, they killed a staghound pup, smeared its blood on the sleeping Rhiannon's face and hands, scattered the bones by her bed, and swore that she had devoured her son in the night and the six of them could not stop her. When Rhiannon woke and asked for her son, they accused her; she begged them not to lie, promising to protect them if they told the truth, but they held to their lie.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·失踪的婴儿。

body_zh: 消息传开了，贵族们要求皮威尔休掉里安农，皮威尔说：他们要我休妻，理由是她不能生育；可是她已经生了孩子，我不会休掉她。如果她犯了罪，就让她受罚吧。里安农请来了教士和贤人，与其和那些女人争辩，不如接受惩罚。她被判处了这样的惩罚：在阿伯斯的宫门外，有一块上马石，她要在那里坐七年，每天对每一个来到宫门的陌生人讲述她犯下的罪行，并请求背着客人和外乡人进宫，如果他们愿意让她背的话。可是很少有人愿意让她背。这位曾经骑着白马、从彼世来到阿伯斯土丘上的女子，就这样每天坐在宫门边，向路过的人讲述一件她从没犯过的罪行。皮威尔没有抛弃她，可是他也无法为她洗清冤屈。里安农默默地忍受着这一切，她相信总有一天，真相会大白。故事在这里转向了另一个地方：在邻近的格温特，有一个名叫泰尔农的领主，他有一匹美丽的母马。
body_en: The nobles demanded that Pwyll put her away. They had asked him to put her away for being childless, he said; she had borne a child, and he would not; if she had done wrong, let her do penance. Rhiannon, taking counsel with teachers and wise men, chose to accept penance rather than wrangle with the women. Her penance was to sit for seven years beside the horse-block outside the gate of Arberth, to tell every stranger who came the tale of her deed, and to offer to carry guests and strangers on her back into the court — though few would let her. The lady who had come from the Otherworld on a white horse to the mound of Arberth now sat each day at the gate telling of a crime she had not committed. Pwyll did not put her away, but he could not clear her; she bore it in silence, trusting that the truth would come out. Here the tale turns to Gwent nearby, where a lord called Teyrnon had a beautiful mare.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第一支·里安农的惩罚。

body_zh: 李尔的儿子本迪盖德弗兰是这个岛屿——“强者之岛”不列颠——戴着伦敦王冠的国王。一天下午，他坐在哈勒赫海边的岩石上，身边有他的兄弟马纳维丹，还有他的两个同母异父的兄弟：尼辛和埃夫尼辛。这两个兄弟性格截然相反：尼辛是个善良的青年，总能让敌对的人和好；埃夫尼辛却专爱挑起争端，让最亲密的兄弟反目成仇。他们看见十三艘船从爱尔兰的南方驶来，船帆美丽，船上飘着锦缎的旗帜，一艘船的船头高高举着一面盾牌，盾尖朝上，表示他们是为和平而来。来的是爱尔兰的国王马索卢赫，他来向本迪盖德弗兰求亲，要娶他的妹妹布兰雯——她是这个岛上三位最尊贵的女子之一，也是世上最美的少女——让不列颠和爱尔兰结成同盟，两国更加强大。本迪盖德弗兰与谋士们商量后，答应了这门亲事。婚礼在安格尔西的阿伯弗劳举行，因为没有一座房子能容得下本迪盖德弗兰这样高大的人，宴会就在帐篷里举行。那一夜，布兰雯成了马索卢赫的妻子。
body_en: Bendigeidfran son of Llŷr was crowned king of this island, the Island of the Mighty, with the crown of London. One afternoon he sat on the rock at Harlech above the sea with his brother Manawydan and his two half-brothers, Nisien, a good youth who could make peace between the bitterest foes, and Efnysien, who could set the most loving brothers at strife. They saw thirteen ships coming from southern Ireland with fair sails and satin banners, one bearing a shield raised point upward as a sign of peace. It was Matholwch, king of Ireland, come to ask for Bendigeidfran's sister Branwen — one of the three chief ladies of the island and the fairest maiden in the world — so that Britain and Ireland might be allied and stronger. After counsel the match was agreed, and the wedding was held at Aberffraw in Anglesey in tents, for no house could hold Bendigeidfran. That night Branwen became Matholwch's wife.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第二支·马索卢赫求亲。

body_zh: 在这场大战中，本迪盖德弗兰的脚被一支毒矛刺伤了。活下来的七个人是：普雷德里、马纳维丹、格利弗厄、诗人塔列辛、伊纳格、格鲁迪厄和海林。本迪盖德弗兰知道自己活不成了，命令他们砍下他的头，说：你们把我的头带到伦敦的白山上去，把它埋在那里，脸朝着法兰西的方向。你们会在路上走很久：在哈勒赫，你们会宴饮七年，里安农的鸟儿会为你们歌唱；然后在彭弗罗的格瓦勒斯，你们会度过八十年，我的头会和你们在一起，不会腐烂，就像我活着的时候一样好陪伴你们，直到你们打开那扇朝着康沃尔的门。一旦你们打开那扇门，就再也不能停留，必须赶快到伦敦去埋葬我的头。七个人照他说的做了，砍下了他的头，带着它和布兰雯一起渡海回到不列颠。这颗不朽的头颅，后来被人们称为“受福之首”，被葬在伦敦以后，只要它还埋在那里，任何外敌都无法侵犯这个岛屿。
body_en: In the battle Bendigeidfran was wounded in the foot by a poisoned spear. The seven who survived were Pryderi, Manawydan, Glifieu, Taliesin the poet, Ynawg, Gruddieu and Heilyn. Knowing he would die, Bendigeidfran bade them cut off his head and bear it to the White Mount in London and bury it with its face toward France. They would be long on the road: at Harlech they would feast seven years while the birds of Rhiannon sang to them, and at Gwales in Penfro they would spend eighty years, and the head would be as good company as when it was on his body, uncorrupted, until they opened the door facing Cornwall; after that they could stay no longer, but must hasten to London to bury it. They cut off his head and crossed back to Britain with it and with Branwen. That head, called the Blessed Head, was buried in London, and while it lay there no invasion could come upon the island.
evidence_note: 《马比诺吉昂》第二支·受福之首。

body_zh: 七个人带着本迪盖德弗兰的头和布兰雯，在安格尔西的阿劳河口上了岸。他们坐下来休息，布兰雯望着爱尔兰，又望着强者之岛不列颠，她看得见两个岛屿，说：上帝之子啊，我为什么要出生！两个美丽的岛屿都因为我而毁灭了。她发出一声长长的叹息，心碎了。人们在阿劳河岸边为她造了一座四方形的坟墓，把她葬在那里。七个人继续向哈勒赫走去，路上遇见了一群男男女女，向他们打听消息，那些人说：卡斯瓦隆，贝利的儿子，征服了强者之岛，在伦敦戴上了王冠。本迪盖德弗兰留下的七个守护者，除了一个人之外都被杀死了，卡拉多格看见一个只有剑、没有人的手在杀他的人，心碎而死——那是隐身的卡斯瓦隆。而在爱尔兰，只有五个怀孕的妇女躲在一个荒野的山洞里活了下来，她们各自生下了儿子，这些孩子长大后娶了彼此的母亲，后来，爱尔兰的五个省份就是这样重新住满了人。
body_en: The seven landed with the head and Branwen at Aber Alaw in Anglesey and sat down to rest. Branwen looked toward Ireland and toward the Island of the Mighty, both of which she could see. 'Alas, Son of God,' she said, 'woe is me that I was ever born: two good islands have been laid waste because of me.' She heaved a great sigh, and her heart broke. They made her a four-sided grave on the bank of the Alaw and buried her there.
