At last the brahmin Parṇāda came back and reported that at Ayodhyā a charioteer of Ṛtuparṇa named Bāhuka, hearing the words, had sighed and answered: 'A good woman, even when abandoned, guards her own virtue.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第六十七至七十节（甘古利译本）。

heading_zh: 百由旬的车程与骰子的学问
heading_en: The hundred-yojana drive and the science of dice
body_zh: 达摩衍蒂听了帕尔纳达的报告，心里明白了，就想出一个办法。她请婆罗门须提婆到阿逾陀去，对利图帕尔纳说：毗陀婆的达摩衍蒂要举行第二次选婿，就在明天日出的时候，你若想去，就要赶快。从阿逾陀到毗陀婆有一百由旬远，只有一天的时间。利图帕尔纳召来巴胡迦，巴胡迦听了，心如刀割，以为妻子真要改嫁，可还是挑选了几匹瘦弱却有好血统的马，驾着车飞驰起来，快得像鸟儿在天上飞。途中，利图帕尔纳的上衣被风吹落，他想停车去拾，巴胡迦说：已经跑出一由旬远了。路过一棵毗毗陀迦树，利图帕尔纳为了炫耀自己的计数本领，说出了树上的叶子和果实的数目。巴胡迦停下车，把树砍倒一数，果然分毫不差。他说：请把这门学问教给我，我把驾驭马匹的学问教给你。利图帕尔纳把骰子的学问传给了他。就在那一刻，迦利从那罗的身体里出来，吐出了迦尔郭吒迦的毒液，钻进了那棵毗毗陀迦树。
body_en: Hearing Parṇāda's report, Damayantī understood and devised a plan. She sent the brahmin Sudeva to Ayodhyā to tell Ṛtuparṇa that Damayantī of Vidarbha would hold a second svayaṃvara at sunrise the next day, and that if he wished to go he must hurry. From Ayodhyā to Vidarbha was a hundred yojanas, with only a day to cover them. Ṛtuparṇa summoned Bāhuka, who was cut to the heart, thinking his wife meant to remarry, yet chose some lean horses of good breed and drove so fast that the chariot flew like a bird through the sky. On the way Ṛtuparṇa's upper garment blew off, and he wanted to stop for it; 'We are already a yojana past it,' said Bāhuka. Passing a Vibhītaka tree, Ṛtuparṇa, to show off his skill with numbers, told the number of its leaves and fruits. Bāhuka stopped, felled the tree and counted, and the number was exact. 'Teach me this science,' he said, 'and I will teach you the science of horses.' Ṛtuparṇa taught him the science of dice. At that moment Kali came out of Nala's body, vomiting Karkoṭaka's venom, and entered the Vibhītaka tree.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第七十一至七十二节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 利图帕尔纳的车隆隆地驶进毗陀婆的都城，车声震动了宫殿，达摩衍蒂一听就知道，只有那罗能把车驾得这样快。可是走出来的车夫却矮小丑陋。达摩衍蒂不敢确定，就派侍女盖希妮去试探他。盖希妮回来说：这个车夫很奇怪：他走到低矮的门前，门会自己升高；水罐会自己装满水；他把草拿在手里，草会燃起火来；他碰过的花朵，反而开得更加鲜艳。达摩衍蒂又让人把巴胡迦做的饭菜拿来尝了一口，正是那罗做菜的味道。她又让侍女带着两个孩子去见他，巴胡迦一见孩子，就抱着他们痛哭起来。达摩衍蒂终于把他请进屋里。她穿着那半件衣服，哭着问他：你为什么在森林里丢下熟睡的妻子？那罗说：那是迦利做的，如今他已经离开了我。可你为什么又要举行第二次选婿？达摩衍蒂说：那只是为了把你找回来。天上传来风神的声音，证明她一直忠贞不二。那罗想起迦尔郭吒迦，穿上那件神衣，恢复了本来的模样。夫妻二人紧紧相拥。
body_en: Ṛtuparṇa's chariot thundered into the capital of Vidarbha, the noise shaking the palace, and Damayantī knew at once that only Nala drove like that. But the charioteer who stepped down was short and misshapen. Unsure, she sent her maid Keśinī to test him. Keśinī came back and said: 'This charioteer is strange. When he comes to a low doorway it rises for him; water-jars fill themselves; grass in his hand bursts into flame; flowers he touches bloom brighter.' Damayantī had food that Bāhuka had cooked brought and tasted it: it was Nala's cooking. She sent her maid with their two children to him, and Bāhuka, seeing them, clasped them and wept. At last she called him in. Wearing the half garment, she asked him weeping: 'Why did you leave your sleeping wife in the forest?' Nala said: 'That was Kali's doing, and now he has left me. But why are you holding a second svayaṃvara?' 'Only to bring you back,' said Damayantī. A voice from the sky — the wind god — bore witness that she had been faithful throughout. Nala thought of Karkoṭaka, put on the divine garment and resumed his true form, and husband and wife held each other close.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第七十三至七十六节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 利图帕尔纳知道了真相，向那罗道歉，那罗也把驾驭马匹的学问教给了他，两人友好地分别。那罗在毗陀婆住了一个月，然后带着一辆车、十六头大象、五十匹马和六百名步兵，回到尼沙陀，来到弟弟补湿迦罗的面前，说：我们再来掷骰子吧。我用我的一切财富和达摩衍蒂作赌注，你用你的王国作赌注；如果你不愿意掷骰子，我们就用弓箭决一胜负。补湿迦罗以为自己一定会赢，笑着说：好啊，我早就想赢得达摩衍蒂了。可这一次，那罗已经掌握了骰子的学问，只掷了一把，就赢回了全部的王国和财富。补湿迦罗吓得面无人色，以为必死无疑。那罗却对他说：这一切不是你的过错，而是迦利做的。你仍然是我的弟弟，我宽恕你，你可以平安地回到你的城里去。他把妻子儿女接回尼沙陀，重新统治了王国。巨马对坚战说：那罗遭受的苦难比你更深，而他终于等到了好日子。你也会这样。他还把骰子的学问传授给了坚战。
body_en: Learning the truth, Ṛtuparṇa asked Nala's pardon; Nala taught him the science of horses, and they parted friends. After a month in Vidarbha, Nala went back to Nishadha with a chariot, sixteen elephants, fifty horses and six hundred foot-soldiers, and stood before his brother Pushkara: 'Let us play again. I stake all my wealth and Damayantī; you stake your kingdom. If you will not play, let us decide it with the bow.' Sure of winning, Pushkara laughed: 'Gladly — I have long wished to win Damayantī.' But Nala now had the science of dice, and with a single throw he won back the whole kingdom and its wealth. Pushkara went pale, expecting death. But Nala said: 'None of this was your fault; it was Kali's doing. You are still my brother. I forgive you; go back safely to your city.' He brought his wife and children home to Nishadha and ruled his kingdom again. Bṛhadaśva said to Yudhiṣṭhira: 'Nala suffered more deeply than you, and at last his good days came; so will yours.' And he taught Yudhiṣṭhira the science of dice.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第七十七至七十九节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 从前，尼沙陀国有一位国王，名叫那罗，是英雄维罗森那的儿子。他英俊得像爱神一样，力量强大，精通吠陀，善于驾驭马匹，只有一个弱点：喜欢掷骰子。在毗陀婆国，国王毗摩有一个女儿，名叫达摩衍蒂，美丽得连天上的仙女都比不上。人们在那罗面前常常赞美达摩衍蒂，在达摩衍蒂面前也常常赞美那罗，两人还没有见过面，就已经彼此倾心。有一天，那罗在宫中的花园里抓住了一只金翅膀的天鹅。天鹅对他说：国王，不要杀我，我会到达摩衍蒂那里去，在她面前赞美你，让她除了你谁也不想嫁。那罗放了天鹅。天鹅飞到毗陀婆，落在达摩衍蒂和侍女们的身边，达摩衍蒂追着去抓它，天鹅就用人的语言对她说：尼沙陀国有一位国王，名叫那罗，在男子中他就像天神一样，你和他正好相配。达摩衍蒂说：你也去对他说同样的话吧。
body_en: Long ago there was a king of the Nishadhas named Nala, son of Vīrasena. He was handsome as the god of love, mighty, learned in the Vedas and skilled with horses; his one weakness was a love of dice. In Vidarbha, King Bhīma had a daughter named Damayantī, more beautiful than the nymphs of heaven. People praised Damayantī before Nala and Nala before Damayantī, so that the two loved each other before they had met. One day Nala caught a swan with golden wings in his palace garden. The swan said: 'King, do not kill me. I will go to Damayantī and praise you before her, so that she will want no one but you.' Nala let it go. The swan flew to Vidarbha and alighted near Damayantī and her maidens; when she ran to catch it, it spoke to her in human speech: 'In Nishadha there is a king named Nala, like a god among men; you and he are made for each other.' Damayantī said: 'Go and say the same to him.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十三节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 达摩衍蒂从此心神不宁，日渐消瘦。父亲毗摩王看出女儿到了出嫁的年纪，就宣布为她举行选婿大会，让天下的国王都来，由她亲自挑选夫婿。消息传到了天上。天神之王因陀罗、火神阿耆尼、水神伐楼那和死神阎摩，听仙人那罗陀说起达摩衍蒂的美貌，也都想去参加选婿。四位天神在路上遇见了正赶往毗陀婆的那罗，见他英俊非凡，就停下来对他说：尼沙陀王，你是一个守信的人，请你答应为我们做一件事，做我们的使者。那罗双手合十，答应了。他问：你们是谁？要我做什么？因陀罗说：我们是天神，为了达摩衍蒂而来。你去对她说，四位天神都要娶她，请她在我们之中挑选一位做丈夫。那罗说：我也是为了她而来的，怎么能去替别人求婚呢？天神说：你已经答应了，就要信守诺言。
body_en: Damayantī grew restless and pale. Seeing that his daughter was of an age to marry, King Bhīma proclaimed a svayaṃvara, a gathering where she herself would choose her husband from the kings of the earth. The news reached heaven. Indra king of the gods, Agni god of fire, Varuṇa god of the waters and Yama god of death, hearing from the sage Nārada of Damayantī's beauty, all wished to go. On the way they met Nala hurrying to Vidarbha, and seeing how handsome he was they stopped and said: 'King of the Nishadhas, you are a man true to his word; promise to do us a service and be our messenger.' Nala joined his palms and promised. 'Who are you, and what would you have me do?' Indra said: 'We are gods, come for Damayantī. Go and tell her that the four gods wish to wed her, and that she should choose one of us as her husband.' Nala said: 'I have come for her myself; how can I woo her for others?' The gods said: 'You have promised; keep your word.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十四节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 天神让那罗隐去身形，他一路畅通无阻地走进了毗陀婆王宫的后宫。达摩衍蒂和侍女们看见一个英俊的男子忽然出现在面前，都吃了一惊，又羞又喜。达摩衍蒂问他：你是谁？怎么进来的？宫中守卫森严啊。那罗说：我叫那罗，是天神的使者。因陀罗、阿耆尼、伐楼那和阎摩四位天神都想娶你，请你在他们之中选一位做丈夫。是天神的力量让我进来，没有被人看见。达摩衍蒂向天神行了礼，然后笑着对那罗说：国王，我的心早已属于你。我愿意把自己和一切都交给你。天鹅的话一直在我心里燃烧，正是为了你，我才召集了这许多国王。如果你拒绝我，我就服毒、投火、投水，或者自缢而死。那罗说：天神们都在那里，你怎么能选一个凡人？天神是世界的主宰，我连他们脚下的尘土都比不上。达摩衍蒂哭了，然后想出了一个办法：我会当着天神的面选你，这样你就不算违背承诺。
body_en: The gods made Nala invisible, and he passed unhindered into the inner palace of Vidarbha. Damayantī and her maidens were startled, shy and delighted to see a handsome man suddenly before them. 'Who are you, and how did you come in? The palace is closely guarded.' 'I am Nala,' he said, 'messenger of the gods. Indra, Agni, Varuṇa and Yama wish to marry you; choose one of them as your husband. It was the gods' power that brought me in unseen.' Damayantī bowed to the gods, then smiled and said to Nala: 'King, my heart has long been yours; I give myself and all I have to you. The swan's words burn in my heart; it was for you that I called these kings together. If you reject me I will take poison, or fire, or water, or the rope.' Nala said: 'With the gods there, how can you choose a mortal? They are the lords of the world; I am not worth the dust of their feet.' Damayantī wept, then found a way: 'I will choose you in the presence of the gods, so that you will not have broken your promise.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十五至五十六节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 选婿大会的日子到了。国王们佩着香花、戴着耳环，坐满了金柱撑起的大厅。达摩衍蒂走进来，她的美貌吸引了所有人的目光。侍从们一一念出国王们的名字，她走到那罗的座位前，却愣住了：那里并排坐着五个一模一样的那罗。原来四位天神都变成了那罗的模样，坐在他的身边。达摩衍蒂无法分辨，心中焦急，就在心里向天神祈祷：自从听了天鹅的话，我就选定了那罗做丈夫，我的心、我的言语从未离开过他；天神们啊，如果这是真的，请显出你们本来的样子，让我认出那罗。天神被她的诚心感动，显出了天神的特征：他们身上不流汗，眼睛不眨，花环鲜艳不凋，衣上没有灰尘，双脚不沾地面，也没有影子。只有一个人身上有影子，花环已经开始凋萎，额上沾着汗珠和尘土，双脚踏在地上，眼睛会眨——那就是真正的那罗。达摩衍蒂羞涩地拉住他的衣角，把花环戴在了他的颈上。
body_en: The day of the svayaṃvara came. Kings garlanded and wearing earrings filled the hall on its golden pillars. Damayantī entered, drawing every eye. Her attendants named the kings one by one, and when she came to Nala's seat she stopped short: five Nalas sat side by side, all alike. The four gods had taken Nala's form and sat beside him. Unable to tell them apart, she prayed in her heart: 'Ever since I heard the swan I have chosen Nala as my husband; my heart and my words have never left him. Gods, if this is true, show your own forms and let me know Nala.' Moved by her truth, the gods showed the marks of gods: they did not sweat, their eyes did not blink, their garlands were fresh and unfaded, their clothes free of dust, their feet did not touch the ground, and they cast no shadow. Only one cast a shadow, his garland beginning to fade, sweat and dust on his brow, his feet on the ground, his eyes blinking — the real Nala. Shyly Damayantī took the hem of his garment and placed her garland round his neck.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十七节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 四位天神没有生气，他们都很高兴，各自赐给那罗两个恩惠：因陀罗让他在祭祀时能亲眼看见天神，并能到达天界；阿耆尼让他想要火的时候火就会出现，并让他拥有像火一样光明的世界；阎摩赐给他烹调的美味和对正法的坚定；伐楼那让他想要水的时候水就会出现，并赐给他永不凋谢的花环。那罗和达摩衍蒂结了婚，回到尼沙陀，生下了一儿一女，过着幸福的生活，那罗举行了许多盛大的祭祀。可是，天神们在回天上的路上，遇见了迦利和达婆波罗——争斗与混乱时代的化身——正要去参加选婿。天神告诉他们，达摩衍蒂已经选了那罗。迦利大怒，说：她竟然在天神面前选了一个凡人，我要惩罚她。天神劝他说，那罗德行完美，选他是正当的。迦利不听，对达婆波罗说：我要住进那罗的身体里，夺走他的王国，让他和达摩衍蒂分离。你要钻进骰子里帮助我。
body_en: The four gods were not angry but pleased, and each gave Nala two boons: Indra, that he would see the gods with his own eyes at sacrifices and reach the heavenly worlds; Agni, that fire would appear whenever he wished and that he would have worlds bright as fire; Yama, skill in fine cooking and steadfastness in dharma; Varuṇa, that water would appear whenever he wished, and garlands that never faded. Nala and Damayantī married, went home to Nishadha, and lived happily; they had a son and a daughter, and Nala performed many great sacrifices. But on their way back to heaven the gods met Kali and Dvāpara, personifications of the ages of strife and confusion, who were on their way to the svayaṃvara. The gods told them Damayantī had chosen Nala. Kali flew into a rage: 'She chose a mortal in the presence of the gods; I will punish her.' The gods said Nala was perfect in virtue and the choice was just. Kali would not listen and said to Dvāpara: 'I will enter Nala's body, take his kingdom and part him from Damayantī. You enter the dice and help me.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十七至五十八节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 迦利来到尼沙陀，等着那罗犯下一个过失。他足足等了十二年。终于有一天，那罗小解之后，没有洗脚就去做黄昏的祈祷。迦利趁机钻进了他的身体。接着，迦利去找那罗的弟弟补湿迦罗，对他说：去和那罗掷骰子吧，有我的帮助，你一定能赢得他的王国。补湿迦罗就来向那罗挑战，那罗被迦利迷住了心窍，无法拒绝。两人掷起了骰子，那罗把金子、银子、车辆、马匹、衣服一样样地输了出去，越输越赌，赌了好几个月。大臣和百姓都来劝他，达摩衍蒂也一次次请他停下，可他像着了魔一样，一句话也听不进去。达摩衍蒂知道大势已去，就叫来车夫瓦尔施奈耶，让他驾车把两个孩子送回毗陀婆的娘家。最后，那罗输掉了全部王国，只剩身上的一件衣服。补湿迦罗笑着问他：你还有什么可以赌的？只剩下达摩衍蒂了，把她押上吧。那罗心如刀绞，一言不发，脱下身上所有的饰物，只穿着一件衣服走出了城，达摩衍蒂也穿着一件衣服跟在他身后。
body_en: Kali came to Nishadha and waited for Nala to commit some fault. He waited twelve full years. At last one day Nala, after answering a call of nature, said his evening prayers without washing his feet, and Kali entered his body. Then Kali went to Nala's brother Pushkara: 'Play dice with Nala; with my help you will win his kingdom.' Pushkara challenged Nala, and Nala, his mind clouded by Kali, could not refuse. They played, and Nala lost his gold, his silver, his chariots, his horses, his clothes, staking more as he lost more, for months on end. His ministers and people came to beg him to stop, and Damayantī pleaded again and again, but he was as one possessed and would hear nothing. Knowing all was lost, Damayantī called the charioteer Vārṣṇeya and had him drive their two children to her father's house in Vidarbha. At last Nala lost the whole kingdom and had nothing but the cloth he wore. Pushkara laughed: 'What have you left to stake? Only Damayantī — stake her.' Heartbroken, Nala said nothing, took off all his ornaments, and left the city in a single garment, Damayantī following in a single garment behind him.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第五十九至六十一节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 补湿迦罗下令：谁要是收留那罗，就处死谁。那罗和达摩衍蒂只好离开都城，在城外住了三天，只靠喝水度日，然后走进了森林。那罗饥饿难忍，看见几只金色的鸟，就脱下身上唯一的衣服去罩它们，鸟儿却叼起衣服飞上天空，说：我们就是骰子，我们来是为了夺走你最后的一件衣服。那罗赤着身子，羞愧万分，对达摩衍蒂说：这里有许多条路，这条通往阿般提，那条通往毗陀婆，你父亲的国家。他一再指给她看去毗陀婆的路。达摩衍蒂哭着说：你是要丢下我吗？我不会离开你。两人共披着达摩衍蒂的一件衣服，来到一间破旧的歇脚处，躺在地上睡着了。半夜，那罗醒来，心中被迦利搅得翻腾不止。他想：如果我离开她，她也许会回到父亲那里，过上安稳的日子。他找到一把刀，割下了达摩衍蒂衣裳的一半披在自己身上，看了熟睡的妻子一眼又一眼，走开又回来，回来又走开，最后还是被迦利驱使着，丢下她独自走进了森林。
body_en: Pushkara proclaimed that anyone who sheltered Nala would die. So Nala and Damayantī left the capital, lived three days outside the city on water alone, and went into the forest. Faint with hunger, Nala saw some golden birds and took off his only garment to throw over them, but the birds carried it off into the sky, crying: 'We are the dice! We came to take even your last garment.' Naked and ashamed, Nala said to Damayantī: 'Here many roads part; this goes to Avanti, that to Vidarbha, your father's land,' and pointed out the road to Vidarbha again and again. Weeping, she said: 'Do you mean to leave me? I will not leave you.' Sharing her single garment, they came to a ruined rest-house and lay down on the ground to sleep. At midnight Nala woke, his mind tossed by Kali. 'If I leave her, perhaps she will go to her father and live in peace.' Finding a knife, he cut away half of Damayantī's garment to cover himself, looked again and again at his sleeping wife, went away and came back and went away again, and at last, driven by Kali, left her and went alone into the forest.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第六十一至六十二节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 达摩衍蒂醒来，不见了丈夫，哭喊着在森林里四处寻找。她走着走着，被一条巨大的蟒蛇缠住了身子，正在呼救，一个猎人赶来，砍死了蟒蛇救了她。可这个猎人见她美丽，起了邪念，想要侵犯她。达摩衍蒂愤怒地诅咒他，猎人当即倒地而死。她继续在森林中游荡，向山、向树、向苦行者打听丈夫的下落，苦行者们安慰她说，她终会与那罗重逢，说完就连同净修林一起消失了。后来她遇见一支商队，跟着他们赶路，夜里在湖边宿营，一群野象冲进营地，把商人们踩死了许多。幸存的人说她是个不祥的女人，达摩衍蒂只好又独自上路，衣衫褴褛，蓬头垢面，来到了车底国的都城。城里的孩子们跟在她身后看热闹。王太后从宫楼上看见了她，觉得她虽然落魄却气质不凡，就把她接进宫里，让她做公主的侍女。达摩衍蒂提出条件：不吃剩饭，不替人洗脚，不和别的男人说话。王太后答应了。
body_en: Damayantī woke to find her husband gone and searched the forest weeping and calling. As she went, a huge python coiled around her; she cried for help, and a hunter came and killed the snake. But the hunter, seeing her beauty, meant to assault her. In her anger Damayantī cursed him, and he fell dead. She wandered on, asking the mountain, the trees and some ascetics where her husband was; the ascetics comforted her that she would meet Nala again, and then vanished with their hermitage. Later she joined a caravan of merchants, but as they camped by a lake at night a herd of wild elephants stampeded through the camp and trampled many of them. The survivors called her a woman of ill omen, and she went on alone, ragged and dishevelled, until she came to the capital of the Chedis, with children trailing after her. The queen mother saw her from the palace terrace, sensed nobility beneath the rags, and took her in as a companion to the princess. Damayantī made conditions: she would not eat leavings, would not wash anyone's feet, and would speak with no other men. The queen mother agreed.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》那罗故事第六十三至六十五节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 坚战在森林里问仙人摩根德耶：世上可曾有过像我们的黑公主那样贤德、那样忠于丈夫的女子？摩根德耶说：有的，大王，请听莎维德丽的故事。从前，摩德罗国有一位国王，名叫马主王。他虔诚守法，慷慨仁慈，深受百姓爱戴，只有一件心事：他已经年老，却没有一个孩子。为了求得子嗣，他严格地守戒、节制饮食，每天念诵十万遍莎维德丽祷词，向祭火献上供品，只在每天的第六个时辰进一点食物。他这样坚持了整整十八年。到了第十八年，女神莎维德丽被他的虔诚打动，从祭火中现出身形，满面喜悦地对他说：国王，我对你的苦行、你的守戒和你的虔诚都很满意。你想要什么恩惠，就说吧，只是不要违背正法。这个故事收在《森林篇》里，名为“贞妇颂”，意思是称颂忠贞妻子的篇章。坚战之所以这样问，是因为黑公主曾在俱卢族的大殿上受尽屈辱，却始终坚定地站在丈夫们一边。
body_en: In the forest Yudhiṣṭhira asked the sage Mārkaṇḍeya: 'Has there ever been a woman as virtuous and as devoted to her husband as our Draupadī?' 'There has, king,' said Mārkaṇḍeya; 'hear the story of Sāvitrī. Long ago in the land of Madra there was a king named Aśvapati, righteous, generous and kind, beloved of his people. He had one sorrow: he was growing old and had no child. To win offspring he kept strict vows and fasting, recited the Sāvitrī prayer a hundred thousand times a day, made offerings into the sacred fire, and ate only a little at the sixth hour. So he persevered for eighteen full years. In the eighteenth year the goddess Sāvitrī, pleased with his devotion, rose in bodily form from the sacrificial fire and said to him joyfully: King, I am pleased with your austerities, your vows and your devotion. Ask whatever boon you wish, only let it not go against dharma.' The story stands in the Forest Book under the name Pativratā-māhātmya, the glory of the faithful wife. Yudhiṣṭhira asks because Draupadī had suffered humiliation in the Kuru hall yet stood steadfast beside her husbands.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十一节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 莎维德丽悲伤地跟在阎摩身后走去。阎摩回过头说：回去吧，莎维德丽，去为他举行葬礼。你已经尽了妻子的责任，你能走到的地方已经到了尽头。莎维德丽说：我的丈夫被带到哪里，我就该跟到哪里，这是永恒的正法。凭着我的苦行、我对长辈的敬重、我对丈夫的爱、我的守誓，以及你的恩典，我的路不会被阻挡。智者说，同行七步，就成了朋友。凭着这份友谊，请听我说几句话。接着，她谈起了自制、守法与善人之道。阎摩听了很高兴，说：你说得好，你可以向我求一个恩惠，除了萨谛梵的生命。莎维德丽说：我的公公双目失明，被逐出王国，住在林中。请让他恢复视力，变得像太阳一样强壮。阎摩说：我答应你。现在回去吧，你走得太累了。莎维德丽说：跟在丈夫身边，我怎么会累？丈夫去哪里，我就去哪里。
body_en: Sorrowing, Sāvitrī followed Yama. He turned and said: 'Go back, Sāvitrī, and perform his funeral rites. You have done your duty as a wife; you have come as far as you may.' Sāvitrī said: 'Wherever my husband is taken, there I must go; that is the eternal dharma. By my austerity, my reverence for elders, my love for my husband, my vows and your grace, my way cannot be barred. The wise say that seven steps taken together make friends. By that friendship, hear a few words of mine.' And she spoke of self-restraint, of dharma and of the way of the good. Pleased, Yama said: 'You speak well. Ask me a boon — anything except Satyavān's life.' Sāvitrī said: 'My father-in-law is blind and exiled from his kingdom, living in the forest. Let him regain his sight and become strong as the sun.' 'I grant it,' said Yama. 'Now go back; you are weary from walking.' Sāvitrī said: 'How can I be weary at my husband's side? Where my husband goes, there I go.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十五节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 莎维德丽一边走，一边继续说话：与善人相处，哪怕只有一次，也是值得追求的；和善人交朋友，比什么都可贵，所以人应该和善人在一起。阎摩说：你的话对智者也有益处，再求一个恩惠吧，除了萨谛梵的生命。莎维德丽说：请让我的公公重新得到失去的王国，不再偏离正法。阎摩答应了，又让她回去。她又说起了正法与慈悲，阎摩又赐她第三个恩惠：她求父亲马主王得到一百个儿子，延续家族。阎摩答应了，说：你已经走得太远了，回去吧。她又赞美阎摩是正法之王，以公正对待众生，阎摩被打动了，说：你说出的话是我从未听过的，求第四个恩惠吧，除了萨谛梵的生命。莎维德丽说：请让我和萨谛梵生下一百个儿子，强壮而勇敢，延续我们两家的血脉。阎摩说：我答应你，你会有一百个儿子。莎维德丽说：正法之王啊，你已经许诺我会和萨谛梵生下一百个儿子，可是没有萨谛梵，这个恩惠怎能实现？我不求别的，只求萨谛梵活过来，否则我宁愿像死了一样。阎摩终于说：好吧，我解开绳索，把你的丈夫还给你。
body_en: As she walked Sāvitrī spoke on: 'To meet the good even once is to be sought; friendship with the good is above all things; so one should keep company with the good.' 'Your words profit even the wise,' said Yama; 'ask a second boon, except Satyavān's life.' 'Let my father-in-law regain his lost kingdom and never stray from dharma.' Yama granted it and again bade her return. She spoke of dharma and compassion, and he gave her a third boon: she asked that her father Aśvapati might have a hundred sons to continue his line. 'Granted,' said Yama; 'you have come too far; go back.' She praised him as the king of dharma who deals justly with all beings, and Yama, moved, said: 'Such words I have never heard; ask a fourth boon, except Satyavān's life.' Sāvitrī said: 'Let Satyavān and me have a hundred sons, strong and brave, to continue both our lines.' 'Granted; you shall have a hundred sons.' Then Sāvitrī said: 'King of dharma, you have promised me a hundred sons by Satyavān; how can that boon be fulfilled without Satyavān? I ask nothing else — only that Satyavān live; without him I am as one dead.' At last Yama said: 'So be it. I loosen the noose and give you back your husband.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十五节（甘古利译本）。

heading_en: The way home through the night
body_zh: 阎摩解开了绳索，带着灵魂离去，并告诉莎维德丽，萨谛梵将活四百年，与她一起享受幸福。莎维德丽回到丈夫躺着的地方，坐在地上，又把他的头放在膝上。萨谛梵醒了过来，像一个远行归来的人，深情地看着妻子，说：我睡了好久，你为什么不叫醒我？那个拉着我的黑色的人去了哪里？莎维德丽说：你在我的膝上睡了很久，那位神就是阎摩，他已经走了。天已经黑了，明天我再把一切告诉你。萨谛梵站起来，看见四周一片漆黑，说：我的父母一定在为我担心，他们年老体弱，我晚回去一会儿，他们就会焦急万分。他一想到父母，就哭了起来。莎维德丽替他擦干眼泪，扶着他，把他的斧头扛在自己肩上，把装满果子的篮子挂在树枝上，两人借着星光，在黑夜的森林里摸索着往回走。
body_en: Yama loosened the noose and departed, telling Sāvitrī that Satyavān would live four hundred years and share happiness with her. Sāvitrī went back to where her husband lay, sat down and took his head into her lap again. Satyavān woke like one returned from a long journey, looked lovingly at his wife and said: 'I have slept a long time; why did you not wake me? Where is that dark man who was dragging me away?' 'You slept long in my lap,' said Sāvitrī; 'that god was Yama, and he has gone. It is night now; tomorrow I will tell you everything.' Satyavān rose and saw darkness all around. 'My parents must be anxious,' he said; 'they are old and frail, and if I am even a little late they grow frantic.' Thinking of them, he wept. Sāvitrī dried his tears and supported him, put his axe on her own shoulder and hung the basket of fruit on a branch, and the two felt their way home through the dark forest by starlight.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十六节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 就在那天，盲王迪尤摩特舍那忽然重见了光明。他和妻子却因为儿子和媳妇迟迟未归而焦急万分，到处寻找，在净修林附近的河边和树林里奔走呼唤。林中的婆罗门们安慰他们说：莎维德丽守过苦行，品德高尚，她的丈夫一定活着；你重见光明，正是吉祥的征兆。萨谛梵和莎维德丽终于在夜里回到了净修林，众人围坐在火边，问他们为什么回来得这么晚。萨谛梵说他在林中头痛睡着了。婆罗门们说：你父亲突然复明，其中的缘故你并不知道，莎维德丽应该告诉我们。莎维德丽就把那罗陀的预言、三夜的斋戒、阎摩的到来和五个恩惠一一说了出来。第二天早晨，沙尔瓦国的大臣们来到净修林，报告说：篡位的人已经被他的大臣杀死，百姓请迪尤摩特舍那回去做国王。迪尤摩特舍那回到了王国，后来马主王果然有了一百个儿子，莎维德丽也生下了一百个儿子。摩根德耶对坚战说：莎维德丽就是这样用她的德行救了自己、父母、公婆和丈夫，黑公主也会这样拯救你们。
body_en: That same day the blind king Dyumatsena suddenly regained his sight. But he and his wife were frantic because their son and daughter-in-law had not come home, and searched by the rivers and woods near the hermitage, calling. The brahmins of the forest comforted them: 'Sāvitrī is rich in austerity and virtue; her husband must be alive; your regaining your sight is an auspicious sign.' At last, in the night, Satyavān and Sāvitrī reached the hermitage, and all sat round the fire and asked why they were so late. Satyavān said he had fallen asleep in the forest with a headache. The brahmins said: 'You do not know why your father has suddenly regained his sight; Sāvitrī should tell us.' Then Sāvitrī told them of Nārada's prophecy, her three-night fast, Yama's coming and the five boons. The next morning ministers came from Śālva to say that the usurper had been killed by his own minister and the people asked Dyumatsena to return as king. Dyumatsena returned to his kingdom; in time Aśvapati had a hundred sons, and Sāvitrī bore a hundred sons. Mārkaṇḍeya said to Yudhiṣṭhira: 'So Sāvitrī by her virtue saved herself, her parents, her husband's parents and her husband; so too will Draupadī save you.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十六至二百九十七节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 马主王说：女神啊，我所求的只是子嗣，为了延续家族，我才守戒修行。婆罗门们告诉我，子嗣是最大的功德。如果你满意，就请赐给我许多儿子吧。女神说：国王，我已经知道你的心意，也已经为你向梵天说过了。由于梵天的恩典，你很快就会有一个光彩照人的女儿。这是自生者梵天的旨意，你不要再说什么了。说完，女神就消失了。不久，王后怀了孕，生下一个女儿，眼睛像莲花一样美丽。因为她是女神莎维德丽所赐，父亲和婆罗门们就给她取名叫莎维德丽。公主一天天长大，美丽得像天上的吉祥天女，人们看见她，都以为是一位天上的女神下凡来了。她的光芒就像祭火一样明亮，让人不敢直视。女神莎维德丽本是那首每天念诵的祷词的化身，公主就以她的名字为名，仿佛她本身就是一句祈祷的回应。
body_en: Aśvapati said: 'Goddess, I ask only for offspring; it was for the continuance of my line that I kept these vows. The brahmins tell me offspring is the highest merit. If you are pleased, grant me many sons.' The goddess said: 'King, I knew your wish and have already spoken for you to Brahmā. By his grace you will soon have a radiant daughter. This is the will of the Self-born; say no more.' With that the goddess vanished. Soon the queen conceived and bore a daughter with eyes as lovely as lotuses. Because she was the goddess Sāvitrī's gift, her father and the brahmins named her Sāvitrī. The princess grew up as beautiful as Śrī, goddess of fortune, and those who saw her thought a goddess had come down from heaven. Her radiance was as bright as the sacrificial fire, so that people could hardly look at her. The goddess Sāvitrī is the embodiment of the prayer recited each day, and the princess bore her name as though she were herself the answer to a prayer.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十一节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 莎维德丽到了出嫁的年纪，可她的美丽和光彩让所有的人都望而却步，竟然没有一个人敢来向她求婚。有一天，她斋戒沐浴，在祭火前礼拜之后，捧着供过神的花环来到父亲面前，向父亲行礼。马主王看着已经长大的女儿，心中忧愁，对她说：女儿，你出嫁的时候到了，可是没有人来向你求婚。我自己也找不到配得上你的人。圣典上说，女儿到了年纪而父亲不让她出嫁，父亲是要受责备的。所以，你自己去吧，去寻找一个与你相配的丈夫，选中了谁，就告诉我，我会按你的心意把你嫁给他。马主王派了年老的大臣陪伴她，给了她车辆和随从。莎维德丽向父亲行了礼，乘上金车，出发去拜访各地的王家仙人的净修林，在那些圣地中寻找自己的夫婿。她走遍了许多圣地，在每一处都向婆罗门布施财物，在一座座净修林之间寻访。
body_en: Sāvitrī came of age to marry, but her beauty and radiance daunted everyone, and no one dared to ask for her hand. One day, after fasting and bathing and worshipping before the sacred fire, she came to her father carrying the garland that had been offered to the gods and bowed to him. Aśvapati looked at his grown daughter with a troubled heart and said: 'Daughter, your time to marry has come, but no one comes to seek you, and I myself can find no one worthy of you. The scriptures blame a father who does not give his daughter in marriage when she is of age. So go yourself and seek a husband who is your equal; tell me whom you choose, and I will give you to him as you wish.' He sent old ministers with her and gave her chariots and attendants. Sāvitrī bowed to her father, mounted a golden chariot, and set out to visit the hermitages of the royal sages, seeking her husband among those holy places. She travelled to many holy places, giving wealth to the brahmins at each, and went from hermitage to hermitage.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十一节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 过了一些日子，莎维德丽回来了。她走进宫殿时，仙人那罗陀正坐在马主王的身边谈话。马主王问女儿选中了谁。莎维德丽说：沙尔瓦国有一位国王，名叫迪尤摩特舍那，他双目失明以后，被宿敌夺走了王国，带着妻子和年幼的儿子流落到森林里，在那里过着苦行者的生活。他的儿子生在城里，长在净修林里，名叫萨谛梵。我心里已经选定他做我的丈夫。那罗陀听了，叹息说：哎呀，莎维德丽做了一件不幸的事。萨谛梵的父亲说话诚实，母亲说话诚实，所以婆罗门给他取名萨谛梵，意思是“说真话的人”。他光彩如太阳，智慧如祭主，勇敢如因陀罗，宽厚如大地，慷慨、守法、英俊。马主王问：那么他有什么缺点吗？那罗陀说：他只有一个缺点，没有别的：从今天算起，一年以后，萨谛梵的寿命就要终结，他会离开这个世界。
body_en: Some time later Sāvitrī returned. When she entered the palace, the sage Nārada was sitting and talking with Aśvapati. Her father asked whom she had chosen. She said: 'In the land of Śālva there was a king named Dyumatsena. When he went blind, an old enemy seized his kingdom, and he went into the forest with his wife and his young son to live as an ascetic. His son, born in the city and raised in the hermitage, is named Satyavān. In my heart I have chosen him for my husband.' Hearing this, Nārada sighed: 'Alas, Sāvitrī has done an unhappy thing. His father speaks truth and his mother speaks truth, so the brahmins named him Satyavān, the truthful one. He is as radiant as the sun, as wise as Bṛhaspati, as brave as Indra, as patient as the earth, generous, righteous and handsome.' 'Has he then any fault?' asked Aśvapati. Nārada said: 'One fault only and no other: a year from today, Satyavān's life will end and he will leave this world.'
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十二节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 马主王听了，对女儿说：莎维德丽，你去另选一个丈夫吧，萨谛梵这个缺点盖过了他所有的美德，一年之后他就会死去。莎维德丽回答说：父亲，一个人一生只能分一次家产，女儿一生只能嫁一次，一个人一生只能说一次“我给你”——这三件事都只做一次。不管他是长寿还是短命，有德还是无德，我已经选定了丈夫，就绝不会再选第二个。心里决定的事，嘴里说出来，再用行动去做，我的心已经认定了他。那罗陀说：国王，你女儿的心意坚定，不会改变正法的道路。萨谛梵的美德别人都没有，就把女儿嫁给他吧。马主王说：仙人的话是不可违背的，就这样办吧。那罗陀祝福了他们，升上天空，回到了天界。马主王本想劝女儿回心转意，听了这番话，也明白再说什么都是徒劳的。一年的期限，从这一天就开始计算了。
body_en: Aśvapati said to his daughter: 'Sāvitrī, go and choose another husband. This one fault outweighs all Satyavān's virtues: in a year he will die.' Sāvitrī answered: 'Father, an inheritance is divided only once, a daughter is given in marriage only once, and a man says I give only once — these three things happen once. Whether he is long-lived or short-lived, virtuous or not, I have chosen my husband once, and I will not choose a second. What the mind resolves, the tongue speaks and the deed performs; my mind has fixed on him.' Nārada said: 'King, your daughter's mind is firm and will not stray from the path of dharma. No one else has Satyavān's virtues; give her to him.' 'The sage's word cannot be set aside,' said Aśvapati; 'so be it.' Nārada blessed them, rose into the sky and returned to heaven. Aśvapati had hoped to change his daughter's mind, but after these words he knew further argument was useless. The year began to run from that day.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十二节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 马主王选了一个吉日，带着婆罗门和祭司，用车载着结婚的用品，带着莎维德丽来到迪尤摩特舍那所住的净修林。他看见那位盲眼的国王坐在一棵娑罗树下的草垫上，就上前行礼，说明了来意。迪尤摩特舍那说：我们失去了王国，住在森林里，过着苦行者的生活，你的女儿怎能忍受这里的艰苦？马主王说：我的女儿和我都知道幸福和苦难是会来去的，她不会在乎这些。我满怀希望而来，请不要拒绝我。迪尤摩特舍那答应了。于是在净修林里，当着所有婆罗门的面，莎维德丽和萨谛梵举行了婚礼。父亲走后，莎维德丽脱下了华丽的衣服和首饰，换上了树皮衣和红褐色的布衣，像苦行者一样生活。她侍奉公婆，温柔谦恭，节制言语，用她的品德让萨谛梵和他的父母都满心欢喜。
body_en: On an auspicious day Aśvapati, with brahmins and priests and chariots laden with things for the wedding, brought Sāvitrī to the hermitage where Dyumatsena lived. Finding the blind king seated on a mat of grass beneath a sal tree, he bowed and made known his purpose. Dyumatsena said: 'We have lost our kingdom and live in the forest as ascetics; how could your daughter bear the hardships here?' Aśvapati answered: 'My daughter and I know that happiness and misery come and go; she will not mind them. I have come full of hope; do not refuse me.' Dyumatsena agreed, and in the hermitage, before all the brahmins, Sāvitrī and Satyavān were married. When her father had gone, Sāvitrī laid aside her fine clothes and ornaments and put on bark and a garment of reddish-brown cloth, living as an ascetic. She served her husband's parents, gentle and modest and sparing of speech, and her virtues filled Satyavān and his parents with joy.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十三节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 日子一天天过去，在快乐的净修林生活里，莎维德丽的心中却始终压着那罗陀的话，日日夜夜地数着日子。她没有把这件事告诉任何人。终于，离萨谛梵的死期只剩下四天了。莎维德丽决定守“三夜之誓”：三天三夜不吃不喝，站立着守戒。迪尤摩特舍那听说了，忧心地对她说：公主，你立下的誓太艰苦了，三夜不吃不喝，实在难以做到。莎维德丽说：父亲，不要担心，我一定能守完这个誓言，这是我用决心立下的。迪尤摩特舍那说：我不能叫你破誓，我只能说：愿你完成它。莎维德丽一动不动地站着，像一根木头一样，度过了三天三夜。到了第四天，就是萨谛梵要死去的那一天。她想：今天就是那一天了。她清早起来，献了供，向年长的婆罗门们和公婆一一行礼，接受他们“愿你永不守寡”的祝福，默默地在心里接受了这句话。
body_en: The days went by in the happy hermitage life, but Nārada's words weighed on Sāvitrī's heart, and day and night she counted the days, telling no one. At last only four days remained before Satyavān's death. Sāvitrī resolved to keep the three-night vow: three days and nights without food or drink, standing. Hearing of it, Dyumatsena said anxiously: 'Princess, this vow is too hard; three nights without food or drink is almost impossible.' 'Do not fear, father,' she said; 'I will keep this vow; it is made with resolve.' Dyumatsena said: 'I cannot tell you to break your vow; I can only say, may you fulfil it.' Sāvitrī stood motionless as a post through three days and nights. The fourth day was the day Satyavān was to die. 'Today is the day,' she thought. She rose early, made her offerings, bowed to the elder brahmins and to her husband's parents, and received their blessing, may you never be a widow — which she silently accepted in her heart.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十四节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 那一天，萨谛梵扛起斧头，要到林中去砍柴、采果子。莎维德丽说：今天我也跟你一起去，我不愿意离开你。萨谛梵说：你从来没有进过森林，林中的路难走，你又斋戒了三天，身体虚弱，怎么能走路呢？莎维德丽说：斋戒并没有让我疲倦，我很想去，请你不要阻止我。萨谛梵说：那你就去问问我的父母，他们同意了，我就不会怪你。莎维德丽去请求公婆，说：我的丈夫要进林去采果子，我想跟他一起去。我嫁过来已经快一年了，还从来没有看过林中开花的景象。公婆答应了。于是莎维德丽跟着丈夫走进了森林。萨谛梵一路指给她看孔雀，看清澈的溪流，看开满鲜花的树木，莎维德丽微笑着应答，心里却像被撕裂了一样，时时刻刻注视着丈夫，想着那罗陀的话，觉得他此刻就已经是一个将死的人。
body_en: That day Satyavān shouldered his axe to go into the forest for wood and fruit. 'I will come with you today,' said Sāvitrī; 'I do not want to leave you.' 'You have never been into the forest,' said Satyavān; 'the paths are hard, and you are weak from three days of fasting; how can you walk?' 'Fasting has not wearied me,' she said; 'I long to go; do not stop me.' 'Then ask my parents,' said he; 'if they agree, I will not blame you.' She went to them and said: 'My husband is going into the forest for fruit, and I wish to go with him. I have been married almost a year and have never seen the forest in flower.' They gave their consent. So Sāvitrī went into the forest with her husband. All along the way Satyavān pointed out the peacocks, the clear streams and the trees in blossom, and Sāvitrī answered with a smile, while her heart was torn, her eyes always on her husband, thinking of Nārada's words and seeing him already as a man about to die.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十四节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 萨谛梵采了果子，装满了篮子，又开始砍柴。砍着砍着，他浑身冒汗，头痛得厉害，对莎维德丽说：我砍柴砍得头痛，四肢也痛，心里像被火烧一样，我好像病了，站也站不住，我想睡一会儿。莎维德丽走过去，坐在地上，把丈夫的头放在自己的膝上。她知道，那罗陀所说的时刻已经到了。就在这时，她看见一个人站在面前：他穿着红衣，头戴王冠，身躯高大，光芒像太阳一样耀眼，皮肤黝黑，眼睛发红，手里拿着一根绳索，样子令人畏惧。他站在萨谛梵身旁，注视着他。莎维德丽轻轻放下丈夫的头，站起来，双手合十，颤抖着问：您是哪一位天神？来做什么？那人说：莎维德丽，你忠于丈夫，又有苦行的功德，所以我才和你说话。我是阎摩。你丈夫的寿命已经到了，我要把他带走。他是有德之人，所以我亲自来，没有派我的使者。说完，阎摩从萨谛梵的身体里，用绳索拉出一个拇指大小的灵魂，带着他向南方走去。
body_en: Satyavān gathered fruit and filled his basket, then began to cut wood. As he worked he broke into a sweat and his head ached sorely. 'Cutting wood has given me a headache,' he said to Sāvitrī; 'my limbs ache and my heart burns; I feel ill and cannot stand; I want to sleep.' Sāvitrī sat down on the ground and took her husband's head into her lap. She knew the hour Nārada had spoken of had come. Then she saw a figure standing before her, clad in red, crowned, tall, radiant as the sun, dark of skin and red of eye, holding a noose, fearful to look upon. He stood beside Satyavān, gazing at him. Sāvitrī gently laid her husband's head down, rose, joined her palms and asked trembling: 'Which god are you, and why have you come?' He said: 'Sāvitrī, you are devoted to your husband and rich in austerity, so I speak to you. I am Yama. Your husband's span is ended and I must take him. Because he is virtuous I have come myself and not sent my messengers.' Then with his noose Yama drew from Satyavān's body a soul the size of a thumb, and set off with it towards the south.
evidence_note: 《摩诃婆罗多·森林篇》贞妇颂第二百九十五节（甘古利译本）。

body_zh: 《古事记》的正文从天地开辟写起。它说：天地刚刚分开的时候，在高天原上出现了三位神：天之御中主神、高御产巢日神和神产巢日神。张伯伦把后两个名字分别译作“高贵而能生成万物的奇妙之神”和“神圣而能生成万物的奇妙之神”。这三位神都是独自出现的，出现以后就隐去了身形，书中没有讲他们的样子，也没有讲他们做了什么。那时候，下面的国土还很年轻，像漂在水上的油脂一样，像水母一样随波漂流，没有一处是固定的。就在这时，有一样东西像芦苇的嫩芽一样萌发出来，从中又出现了两位神：宇摩志阿斯诃备比古迟神和天之常立神。这五位神被称为“别天神”，也就是与后来诸神不同的、特别的天神，他们同样是独自出现、随即隐去身形的神。其中的高御产巢日神和神产巢日神，在后面的故事里还会一次次出现：一位主持高天原上的商议，一位把死去的大国主救活。故事就从这样一个漂浮不定、还没有固定下来的世界开始。
body_en: The Kojiki proper opens at the time when heaven and earth first began. In the Plain of High Heaven there came into being three deities: Ame-no-minaka-nushi, Takami-musubi and Kami-musubi, the last two of whom Chamberlain renders the High-August-Producing-Wondrous Deity and the Divine-Producing-Wondrous Deity. All three came into being alone and hid their persons; the text says nothing of how they looked or what they did. The land below was still young, like floating oil, drifting about like a jellyfish, with nothing yet fixed. Then, from something that sprouted up like a reed-shoot, two more deities came into being, Umashi-ashi-kabi-hiko-ji and Ame-no-toko-tachi, who likewise came alone and hid their persons. These five are set apart as the separate Heavenly Deities. Takami-musubi and Kami-musubi will return again and again: the one presiding over the councils of High Heaven, the other bringing the dead Ōkuninushi back to life. The story begins in a world still afloat and not yet made firm.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第一节。

heading_en: The Ugly Females of Yomi and the three peaches
body_zh: 伊邪那岐看见这副情景，吓得转身就逃。伊邪那美说：你让我蒙受了羞辱！她派黄泉丑女去追赶他。伊邪那岐取下头上的黑色发饰扔在身后，发饰立刻变成了葡萄，丑女们停下来捡葡萄吃；吃完了又追上来，他又折下右边发髻上的梳子扔出去，梳子变成了竹笋，丑女们又停下来拔竹笋吃。伊邪那美又派八位雷神，率领一千五百名黄泉的军队来追。伊邪那岐拔出十拳剑，一边在身后挥舞，一边逃跑。追到黄泉比良坂——黄泉与人间交界的山坡——的坡脚下时，他摘下长在那里的三个桃子，向追兵投去，追兵全都逃回去了。伊邪那岐对桃子说：你们帮助了我，以后苇原中国的人们遇到苦难的时候，你们也要像这样帮助他们。他给桃子取名意富加牟豆美命。
body_en: Terrified at the sight, Izanagi turned and fled. 'You have put me to shame!' cried Izanami, and sent the Ugly Females of Yomi after him. He threw down his black head-dress, which turned into grapes, and while they stopped to eat he fled on; when they came after him again he broke the comb from the right bunch of his hair and threw it, and it turned into bamboo shoots, which they pulled up and ate. Then she sent the eight thunder deities with fifteen hundred warriors of Yomi. He drew his ten-grasp sword and fled brandishing it behind him. At the foot of the Even Pass of Yomi, the slope between Yomi and the living world, he took three peaches growing there and smote the pursuers with them, and they all fled back. He said to the peaches: 'As you have helped me, so help the people of the Central Land of Reed-Plains when they are in trouble,' and named them Oho-kamu-dzu-mi.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第九节。

body_zh: 最后，伊邪那美亲自追来了。伊邪那岐搬来一块要一千个人才拉得动的大石头——千引石，堵住了黄泉比良坂。两位神隔着石头面对面站着，说出了诀别的话，书中称之为“度事户”，一般理解为宣告断绝夫妻关系的话。伊邪那美说：我亲爱的哥哥，既然你这样做，我就每天把你国家的人勒死一千个。伊邪那岐回答：我亲爱的妹妹，如果你那样做，我就每天建起一千五百座产房。所以，世上每天必定有一千人死去，也必定有一千五百人出生。从此生与死被这块石头隔开，而活着的人总是比死去的多。伊邪那美从此被称为黄泉津大神，又因为她追上了伊邪那岐，也被叫作道敷大神。堵住黄泉坡的那块石头，被称为道反之大神，也叫塞坐黄泉户大神。书中说，所谓黄泉比良坂，就是现在出云国的伊赋夜坂。
body_en: Last of all Izanami herself came in pursuit. Izanagi pulled up a rock that would take a thousand men to lift and blocked the Even Pass of Yomi with it. Standing face to face on either side of the rock, they spoke the words of parting, which the text calls the exchange of the door of words, usually understood as a declaration ending the marriage. Izanami said: 'My beloved elder brother, if you do this, I will strangle a thousand of the people of your land every day.' Izanagi answered: 'My beloved younger sister, if you do that, I will set up fifteen hundred birth-houses every day.' That is why a thousand people surely die every day and fifteen hundred are surely born: the rock divides life from death, and the living always outnumber the dead. Izanami was thenceforth called the Great Deity of Yomi, and also the Road-Reaching Great Deity because she had overtaken him. The rock is called the Great Deity of the Road-Turning-Back. The Even Pass of Yomi, the text says, is the pass of Ifuya in Izumo.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第九节。

heading_en: Purification and the three noble children
body_zh: 伊邪那岐说：我去了一个丑恶污秽的国家，必须洗净我的身体。他来到筑紫日向的橘之小门的阿波岐原，在河口举行禊祓。他把手杖、腰带、袋子、衣服、裤子、帽子和左右手的手镯一件件扔掉，每扔下一件，就生出一位神，从手杖生出的是冲立船户神，一共生出了十二位神。接着他说：上游水太急，下游水太缓。就走进中游的水里洗身，先生出了由黄泉污秽而来的八十祸津日神和大祸津日神，又生出了纠正灾祸的神直毘神、大直毘神和伊豆能卖神，然后在水底、水中、水面洗涤，生出了三位绵津见神和三位筒之男神。书中说，三位绵津见神是阿昙连一族祭祀的祖神，三位筒之男神是墨江的三位大神。最后，他洗左眼时生出了天照大神，洗右眼时生出了月读命，洗鼻子时生出了建速须佐之男命。故事从这里接到下一部：三位尊贵的孩子即将各自领受父亲的命令。
body_en: 'I have been to a hideous and polluted land,' said Izanagi, 'so I must purify my body.' He came to the plain of Ahagi by the river-mouth of Tachibana in Himuka in Tsukushi and performed purification. As he threw down his staff, girdle, bag, garment, trousers, hat and the bracelets of each arm, a deity was born of each — from the staff, Tsuki-tatsu-funa-do — twelve in all. Then, saying that the upper waters were too swift and the lower too sluggish, he went down into the middle reach to wash. First were born the two deities of calamity, Ya-so-maga-tsu-bi and Oho-maga-tsu-bi, from the pollution of Yomi; then Kamu-nahobi, Oho-nahobi and Idzu-no-me to set the calamity right; then, as he washed at the bottom, in the middle and on the surface of the water, three Wata-tsu-mi deities and three Tsutsu-no-wo deities. The text adds that the three Wata-tsu-mi are the ancestral deities worshipped by the Adzumi clan, and the three Tsutsu-no-wo the three great deities of Suminoe. Last, as he washed his left eye, Amaterasu was born; his right eye, Tsukuyomi; his nose, Take-haya-Susanoo. The story passes here to the next part, where the three noble children receive their father's charge.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第十节。

body_zh: 接着出现的是国之常立神和丰云野神，他们也是独自出现、隐去身形的神。此后诸神开始成对出现：宇比地迩神与须比智迩神，角杙神与活杙神，意富斗能地神与大斗乃辨神，於母陀流神与阿夜诃志古泥神，最后是伊邪那岐神与伊邪那美神。张伯伦把这最后两个名字译作“邀请之男神”和“邀请之女神”：名字里的“伊邪那”有邀请、招呼的意思，“岐”和“美”分别表示男和女。从国之常立神到伊邪那岐、伊邪那美，被称为“神世七代”：前面两位独自出现的神各算一代，后面每一对男女神合算一代。这些名字的意思并不都清楚，有的像在说泥土和沙，有的像在说木桩，有的像在说宽大的门户，有的像在说完满的面貌和敬畏的言辞，像是一步步描写大地成形、万物有了模样的过程，但书中并没有讲他们做了什么。真正开始动手造国的，是最后出现的这一对兄妹神。
body_en: Next came into being Kuni-no-toko-tachi and Toyo-kumo-nu, who also came alone and hid their persons. After them the deities came in pairs: U-hiji-ni and Su-hiji-ni, Tsunu-guhi and Iku-guhi, Oho-to-no-ji and Oho-to-no-be, Omo-daru and Aya-kashiko-ne, and last of all Izanagi and Izanami, whom Chamberlain renders the Male-Who-Invites and the Female-Who-Invites: izana- carries the sense of inviting, and -ki and -mi mark male and female. From Kuni-no-toko-tachi to Izanami are called the Seven Divine Generations: the two single deities count a generation each, and each pair counts as one. The meanings of the names are not all clear; some seem to speak of mud and sand, of posts, of great doorways, of a perfect face and of awe, as if the land were slowly taking shape, but the text does not say what these deities did. The work of making the land falls to the last pair.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二节。

body_zh: 天上的众神一齐命令伊邪那岐和伊邪那美：去把这片漂浮的国土整治好，使它坚固，把它生出来。众神的命令里有三件事——整治、巩固、生出——后面的故事，正是一步步完成这三件事。众神赐给他们一支装饰着美玉的长矛，叫作天之沼矛。两位神站在天之浮桥上，把长矛伸进下面的海水里，“咕噜咕噜”地搅动起来——这是书中模仿搅动海水的声音。他们把长矛提起来，从矛尖滴下的海水层层堆积，变成了一座岛，这就是淤能碁吕岛。张伯伦把这个名字译作“自凝岛”，意思是“自己凝结而成的岛”。这是天地间第一块坚固的土地。淤能碁吕岛究竟在哪里，书中没有说，后世有许多说法，都只是推测。两位神从天之浮桥上走下来，降落到这座岛上。造国的工作，就要从这里开始了。
body_en: All the heavenly deities commanded Izanagi and Izanami to make, consolidate and give birth to the drifting land — three tasks that the rest of the story works through one by one — and granted them a jewelled spear, the Ame-no-nuhoko. Standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, the two pushed the spear down and stirred the brine until it went curdle-curdle, the text imitating the sound. When they drew the spear up, the brine that dripped from its point piled up and became an island: Onogoro, which Chamberlain renders Self-Curdling Island. It was the first firm ground. Where Onogoro lies the text does not say; later identifications are only conjecture. The two deities descended from the Floating Bridge onto the island, and from there the making of the land began.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三节。

heading_en: The heavenly pillar and the leech-child
body_zh: 两位神在岛上竖起了一根天之御柱，又建起一座八寻殿——“寻”是两臂张开的长度，八寻就是极言其宽大。伊邪那岐问伊邪那美：你的身体是怎样长成的？伊邪那美说：我的身体长成了，只有一处没有长合。伊邪那岐说：我的身体也长成了，只有一处长得多余。我想用多余的地方填补你没有长合的地方，生出国土，你看怎样？伊邪那美说：好。伊邪那岐说：那么我们绕着天之御柱走，相遇以后结为夫妻。你从右边绕，我从左边绕。两人绕柱相遇时，伊邪那美先开口说：啊，多么好的男子！伊邪那岐接着说：啊，多么好的少女！说完他又说：女子先开口是不吉利的。可他们还是结合了，生下的第一个孩子是水蛭子。书中没有描写他的样子，只说他们把这个孩子放进芦苇编的小船里，任它漂走了。接着又生了淡岛，也不算在他们的孩子之中。
body_en: On the island they set up a heavenly pillar and built a hall eight fathoms wide. Izanagi asked Izanami how her body was formed. She answered that it was fully formed except for one place that had not grown together; he said his was fully formed except for one place that had grown to excess, and proposed to fill her place with his and so give birth to lands. She agreed. 'Then let us walk round this heavenly pillar,' he said, 'and meet and be joined. You go round from the right, I from the left.' When they met, Izanami spoke first: 'Ah, what a fair and lovely youth!' Then Izanagi: 'Ah, what a fair and lovely maiden!' Afterwards he said it was unlucky for the woman to speak first. Yet they came together, and their first child was a leech-child, whom they put into a boat of reeds and let float away. Next they bore the island of Aha, which also was not reckoned among their children.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四节。

body_zh: 两位神商量说：我们生的孩子不好，应该去问问天上的众神。他们一起回到天上，请求众神的指示。天上的众神用太占——一种烧鹿肩骨看裂纹的占卜——占了一卦，说：因为女子先开口，所以不好。回去重新说一遍吧。两人回到岛上，像以前一样绕着天之御柱走，这一次伊邪那岐先说：啊，多么好的少女！伊邪那美再说：啊，多么好的男子！这样结合以后，他们生下的是一个个岛屿：先是淡路岛；接着是伊予之二名岛，它一个身体有四张脸，每张脸都有名字：伊予国叫爱比卖，赞岐国叫饭依比古，粟国叫大宜都比卖，土左国叫建依别；然后是隐岐岛；筑紫岛也是一个身体四张脸，分别是筑紫国、丰国、肥国和熊曾国；再往后是壹岐岛、对马岛、佐渡岛，最后是大倭丰秋津岛，也就是本州。因为这八个岛最先生出，所以这片土地被称为“大八岛国”。之后他们又生下了六个小岛。
body_en: The two took counsel: 'The children we have borne are not good. We should report this before the heavenly deities.' They went up together, and the heavenly deities divined by grand divination — reading the cracks in a burned deer's shoulder-blade — and said: 'It was not good because the woman spoke first. Go down again and say it anew.' So they walked round the pillar as before, and this time Izanagi spoke first. Then they gave birth to islands: Awaji first; then Iyo-no-futana, one body with four faces, each named — Iyo called Ehime, Sanuki called Iiyori-hiko, Aha called Ōgetsu-hime and Tosa called Takeyori-wake; then Oki; then Tsukushi, likewise one body with four faces, the lands of Tsukushi, Toyo, Hi and Kumaso; then Iki, Tsushima, Sado, and last Ō-yamato-toyo-aki-tsu-shima. Because these eight islands were born first, the country is called the Land of the Eight Great Islands. After them they bore six smaller islands.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第五节。

body_zh: 生完了国土，伊邪那岐和伊邪那美又接着生神。书中把这些神的名字一个个记下来：大事忍男神，石土毘古神，石巢比卖神，大户日别神，天之吹男神，大屋毘古神，风木津别之忍男神；然后是海神大绵津见神，河口之神速秋津日子神和速秋津比卖神——这一对河口之神又生下了沫那艺、沫那美、颊那艺、颊那美等掌管水沫与水面的神；接着是风神志那都比古神，树木之神久久能智神，山神大山津见神，原野之神鹿屋野比卖神，又名野椎神，大山津见神和野椎神又生下了掌管土地、雾气、山谷的许多神。他们还生下了一位叫作“鸟之石楠船”的神，又叫天鸟船，是诸神乘坐的船；又生下了掌管食物的大宜都比卖。有的名字一长串，读起来就像是在点数天地间的万物：石头、门户、屋顶、海浪、水沫、雾气、山谷……世界就这样一样样有了自己的神灵。可是，在这一连串的诞生之后，等待着他们的却是一场灾祸。
body_en: Having borne the lands, Izanagi and Izanami went on to bear deities, and the text records each name: Oho-koto-oshi-wo, Iha-tsuchi-biko, Iha-su-hime, Oho-to-hi-wake, Ame-no-fuki-wo, Oho-ya-biko, Kaza-mo-tsu-wake-no-oshi-wo; the great sea deity Oho-wata-tsu-mi; the river-mouth deities Haya-aki-tsu-hiko and Haya-aki-tsu-hime, who in turn bore deities of foam and of the water's surface; the wind deity Shina-tsu-hiko, the tree deity Kuku-no-chi, the great mountain deity Oho-yama-tsu-mi and the moor goddess Kaya-nu-hime, also called Nu-dzu-chi, who together bore deities of earth, mist and valleys. They bore the Bird's Rock-Camphor-Boat, also called the Heavenly Bird-Boat, and the food goddess Oho-ge-tsu-hime. Some names are very long, so that the list reads like a counting of everything in heaven and earth: rocks, doorways, roofs, waves, foam, mist, valleys. So, thing by thing, the world received its deities. But at the end of this long run of births a calamity was waiting.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第六节。

body_zh: 最后，伊邪那美生下了火之迦具土神，也叫火之夜艺速男神、火之炫毘古神。因为生下了火神，她的阴部被烧伤，从此一病不起。她在病中呕吐，从呕吐物中生出了金山毘古神和金山毘卖神，也就是金属之神；从粪便中生出了波迩夜须毘古神和波迩夜须毘卖神，也就是黏土之神；从尿中生出了水神弥都波能卖神，以及和久产巢日神，和久产巢日神的女儿就是掌管食物的丰宇气毘卖神。即使在病痛之中，她的身体也还在不停地生出新的神来：金属、黏土、水和五谷，都是从这位垂死的母神身上来的。可是终于，伊邪那美因为生下火神而离开了人世——《古事记》用的说法是“神避”，也就是神的隐去。书中总结说，伊邪那岐与伊邪那美一起生下的岛屿共十四个，神共三十五位。创造了国土和万物之神的母亲，就这样因为生下火而死去，这是《古事记》里第一次出现死亡。
body_en: Last of all Izanami bore the fire deity Kagutsuchi, also called Hi-no-yagi-haya-wo and Hi-no-kaga-biko. In bearing this child her private parts were burned, and she lay down sick. From her vomit were born Kana-yama-biko and Kana-yama-bime, deities of metal; from her dung, Hani-yasu-biko and Hani-yasu-bime, deities of clay; from her urine, the water goddess Mitsu-ha-no-me and Waku-musubi, whose daughter is Toyo-uke-bime, goddess of food. Even in sickness her body went on bringing forth deities: metal, clay, water and grain all came from the dying mother. But at last, because she had borne the fire deity, Izanami divinely retired — the Kojiki's word for her passing away. The text sums up that together the pair had borne fourteen islands and thirty-five deities. So the mother of the lands and their deities dies from giving birth to fire; it is the first death in the Kojiki.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第六节。

heading_en: Mourning and the slaying of the fire deity
body_zh: 伊邪那岐悲痛地说：我亲爱的妹妹啊，我怎么能用你换来这一个孩子！他匍匐在伊邪那美的枕边和脚边痛哭，从他的眼泪里生出了一位女神，叫作泣泽女神，住在香山下的畝尾木本。伊邪那岐把伊邪那美安葬在出云国与伯伎国交界的比婆山上。接着，他拔出佩带的十拳剑，砍下了儿子迦具土神的头。剑尖上溅出的血落在岩石上，生出了石拆神、根拆神和石筒之男神；剑锷附近的血溅出来，生出了甕速日神、樋速日神和建御雷之男神，也就是后来降服出云的建御雷神；从剑柄上滴下、从指缝间漏出的血，又生出了暗淤加美神和暗御津羽神两位山谷之水的神。从迦具土神被砍杀的身体各处——头、胸、腹、阴部、左右手、左右脚——又生出了八位山神。伊邪那岐用来斩杀火神的这把剑，名叫天之尾羽张，又名伊都之尾羽张。
body_en: Izanagi cried: 'Oh my beloved younger sister! That I should have exchanged you for this single child!' He crept weeping round her pillow and her feet, and from his tears was born the goddess Naki-sawa-me, who dwells at the foot of the trees on the hill of Unewo by Mount Kagu. He buried Izanami on Mount Hiba on the border of Izumo and Hahaki. Then he drew the ten-grasp sword at his side and cut off the head of his son Kagutsuchi. The blood on the point of the sword splashed on the rocks and became Iha-saku, Ne-saku and Iha-tsutsu-no-wo; the blood near the guard became Mika-haya-bi, Hi-haya-bi and Take-mika-dzu-chi-no-wo, the Takemikazuchi who will later bring Izumo to submission; the blood dripping from the hilt through his fingers became Kura-okami and Kura-mitsu-ha, deities of the valley waters. From Kagutsuchi's head, chest, belly, loins, hands and feet eight mountain deities were born. The sword was named Ame-no-wo-ha-bari, also Itsu-no-wo-ha-bari.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第七至八节。

heading_en: Yomi: do not look at me
body_zh: 伊邪那岐思念妻子，追到了黄泉国。伊邪那美从宫殿紧闭的门里出来迎接他，伊邪那岐就隔着门对她说：我亲爱的妹妹啊，我和你一起造的国土还没有完成，请你回来吧！伊邪那美说：可惜你没有早一点来。我已经吃了黄泉灶火煮的食物——这句话的意思是，她已经属于黄泉了。不过，既然我亲爱的哥哥特意来了，我想回去。我要去和黄泉的神商量一下。在这期间，请你千万不要看我。她说完回到殿里，过了很久都没有出来。伊邪那岐等不下去了，他折下插在左边发髻上的多齿梳子的一根边齿，点起火来，走进殿里察看。只见伊邪那美的身上爬满了蛆虫，八位雷神盘踞在她身上：头上是大雷，胸口是火雷，腹部是黑雷，阴部是拆雷，左手是若雷，右手是土雷，左脚是鸣雷，右脚是伏雷。这就是后来故事里所说的“黄泉八雷神”。
body_en: Wishing to see his wife again, Izanagi followed her to the Land of Yomi. She came out to meet him from the closed door of the palace. 'My beloved younger sister,' he said, 'the lands that you and I were making are not yet finished. Come back!' She answered: 'Alas that you did not come sooner! I have eaten of the food of the furnace of Yomi. Yet since my beloved elder brother has come, I wish to return; I will discuss it with the deities of Yomi. Do not look at me.' She went back in and stayed so long that he could not wait. He broke off an end tooth of the comb in the left bunch of his hair, lit it, and went in. Maggots were swarming over her, and eight thunder deities had been born on her body: Great-Thunder on her head, Fire-Thunder on her breast, Black-Thunder on her belly, Crack-Thunder below, Young-Thunder on her left hand, Earth-Thunder on her right, Sounding-Thunder on her left foot and Reclining-Thunder on her right.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第九节。

heading_en: The five names of the Master of the Great Land
body_zh: 《古事记》在讲完须佐之男在出云建宫、娶栉名田比卖之后，接着列出了他的子孙：须佐之男和栉名田比卖生下八岛士奴美神，此后一代代往下传，传到天之冬衣神，天之冬衣神娶了刺国大神的女儿刺国若比卖，生下的就是这一部故事的主人公——从须佐之男往下数，正好是第六代。书中说他有五个名字：大国主神、大穴牟迟神、苇原色许男神、八千矛神、宇都志国玉神。这些名字后来会在故事里一个个出现：年轻时人们叫他大穴牟迟；在根之国，须佐之男叫他苇原色许男，也就是“苇原中国的丑男子”；求婚时他叫八千矛神，也就是“拥有八千支矛的神”；最后，须佐之男在黄泉比良坂上命令他成为“大国主”和“宇都志国玉”，也就是统治人间国土的神。他还有许多兄弟，书中称为八十神。他的母亲刺国若比卖，在后面的故事里两次哭着去救他。故事开始的时候，他还只是兄弟中最受欺负的一个。
body_en: After telling how Susanoo built his palace in Izumo and married Kushinada-hime, the Kojiki lists his descendants: their son Yashima-jinumi, and so on down the generations to Ame-no-fuyu-kinu, who married Sashikuni-waka-hime, daughter of the great deity of Sashikuni, and fathered the hero of this part — the sixth generation from Susanoo. The text gives him five names: Ōkuninushi, Ōnamuji, Ashihara-shiko-wo, Yachihoko and Utsushi-kunitama. They surface one by one in the story: as a youth he is Ōnamuji; in the Nether-Distant-Land Susanoo calls him Ashihara-shiko-wo, the Ugly Male of the Reed-Plains; as a wooer he is Yachihoko, the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears; and at the Even Pass of Yomi Susanoo charges him to become Ōkuninushi and Utsushi-kunitama, ruler of the living land. He has many brothers, the Eighty Deities, and a mother, Sashikuni-waka-hime, who twice goes weeping to save him. When the story begins he is the most put-upon of the brothers.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十节。

heading_en: The songs of the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears
body_zh: 以八千矛神为名的大国主，又到遥远的越国去向沼河比卖求婚。他站在她家门前唱歌，唱自己怎样听说越国有一位聪明美丽的女子，怎样远道而来，拉着门板等到天明，林中的鸟已经开始啼叫。沼河比卖隔着门回唱：请你不要着急，等到夜里，我就会是你的。第二天夜里，两人结为夫妻。正妻须势理毘卖为此十分嫉妒。大国主准备从出云上大和去，一只手搭在马鞍上，一只脚踏在马镫里，唱歌给她听：他换了三套衣服，黑色的不合适，翠鸟一样青色的也不合适，最后换上山田里的染料染成的衣服，才觉得合适；又说，你将来会像山上孤零零的芒草一样哭泣。须势理毘卖举起大酒杯走到他身边，唱道：你是男子，到处都有妻子，而我是女子，除了你没有别的丈夫。两人用酒杯立下誓约，手搭着彼此的脖子，从此和睦相处，书中说他们直到今天仍安然相守。
body_en: As Yachihoko, the Deity of Eight Thousand Spears, he went to distant Koshi to woo Princess Nunakawa. Standing at her door he sang how he had heard of a wise and beautiful woman in Koshi, how he had come from afar and stood pulling at her door until dawn while the birds of the forest began to cry. She sang back through the door: be not impatient; when night comes I will be yours. The next night they were married. His chief wife Suseri-bime was deeply jealous. As he was about to go up from Izumo to Yamato, one hand on the saddle and one foot in the stirrup, he sang to her: of three robes he had tried, the black was not right and the kingfisher-blue was not right, but the robe dyed with the juice of the dye-plant sown in the mountain fields suited him; and she would weep like a single clump of grass on the mountain. Suseri-bime came to him lifting a great wine-cup and sang: you are a man and have wives wherever you go, but I am a woman and have no husband but you. They pledged each other with the cup, their hands on each other's necks, and the text says they are at peace together to this day.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十四至二十五节。

body_zh: 有一天，大国主在出云的美保岬，看见一位神乘着用萝藦豆荚做成的小船，踏着浪花漂过来，身上穿着用整张剥下来的小动物的皮做的衣服——原文的字一说是鹅，一说指飞蛾。大国主问他的名字，他不回答；问随从的众神，谁也不知道。这时，一只蛤蟆说：久延毘古一定知道。大国主召来久延毘古，久延毘古说：这是神产巢日神的儿子少名毘古那神。大国主去问神产巢日神，神产巢日神说：他确实是我的孩子，是我那些孩子中从我的指缝间漏下去的那一个。你们两个结为兄弟，一起把国土造好、巩固起来吧。从此，大国主和少名毘古那一起造国。后来，少名毘古那渡海去了常世国。书中说，那位知道他名字的久延毘古，就是今天田里的稻草人，虽然不能走路，却知道天下所有的事情。
body_en: Once, at Cape Miho in Izumo, Ōkuninushi saw a deity riding the crests of the waves in a little boat made from a seed-pod of the kagami plant, clothed in the whole stripped skin of some small creature — the character is read by some as a goose and by others as a moth. Asked his name, he did not answer, and none of the attendant deities knew it. Then a toad said: 'Kuyebiko will surely know.' Kuyebiko, called for, said: 'This is Sukuna-bikona, the son of Kami-musubi.' When Ōkuninushi asked Kami-musubi, she said: 'He is truly my child, the one of my children who slipped through between my fingers. Be brothers, and make and consolidate the land together.' So the two made the land together, until Sukuna-bikona crossed over the sea to the Eternal Land. Kuyebiko, the text says, is the scarecrow in the fields today, who cannot walk but knows everything under heaven.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十七节。

body_zh: 少名毘古那走了，大国主忧愁地说：我一个人怎么能把这片国土造好呢？要和哪一位神一起造才好？这时，海面上亮起光来，一位神照着海面过来，说：你要是好好地供奉我，我就和你一起把国土造成。不然的话，国土是造不成的。大国主问：那么，要怎样供奉你呢？那位神说：你把我供奉在大和那青翠如垣墙的群山东边的山上。书中说，这就是住在御诸山上的神。御诸山也就是今天奈良的三轮山。《古事记》在这里没有写出这位神的名字；《日本书纪》的一段异文则说，这位从海上来的神是大国主自己的“幸魂奇魂”。至此，大国主造国的故事告一段落。书中接着列出了大年神的子孙，然后，高天原上的众神开始关心下界的这片国土了。这座山在后来的故事里一直被视为神所居住的山。
body_en: With Sukuna-bikona gone, Ōkuninushi said in sorrow: 'How can I make this land alone? With what deity should I make it?' Then a light shone over the sea, and a deity came illuminating it and said: 'If you will worship me well, I will make the land together with you. Otherwise it cannot be made.' Ōkuninushi asked how he should worship him, and the deity said: 'Worship me on the eastern mountain of the green fence of Yamato.' This, says the text, is the deity who dwells on Mount Mimoro, the mountain now called Miwa in Nara. The Kojiki gives the deity no name here; a variant in the Nihon shoki says that the deity from the sea was Ōkuninushi's own spirit of good fortune and wondrous spirit. Here the making of the land rests. The text goes on to list the children of the Great-Harvest Deity, and then the deities of the Plain of High Heaven turn their attention to the land below. The mountain remains, throughout the later stories, a mountain where a deity dwells.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十八节。

body_zh: 天照大神说：丰苇原的瑞穗国应该由我的儿子天忍穗耳命来统治。天忍穗耳命站在天之浮桥上往下一看，说：下面吵闹得很！就回来报告了。高御产巢日神和天照大神在天安河边召集众神商议，思金神出主意，先派了天菩比神下去，他却去讨好大国主，三年都没有回来复命。于是又派天若日子，赐给他天之麻迦古弓和天之波波矢。天若日子一到下界，就娶了大国主的女儿下照比卖，想把这片国土据为己有，八年都没有复命。众神又派了一只名叫鸣女的雉鸡去问他。雉鸡停在天若日子门前的桂树上，传达了天神的问话。天佐具卖劝他射死这只鸟，天若日子就用天神赐的弓箭射穿了雉鸡，箭一直飞到天安河边高木神的面前。高木神看见箭羽上有血，说：如果天若日子没有违命，射的是恶神，这支箭就不要射中他；如果他有邪心，就让他死于此箭。他把箭从箭孔投回去，正射中躺在床上的天若日子的胸口，天若日子当场死去。书中说，“当心还矢”这句话就由此而来。
body_en: Amaterasu declared that the Luxuriant Reed-Plains Land of Fresh Rice-Ears should be ruled by her son Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi. He looked down from the Floating Bridge of Heaven, said that the land below was in a great uproar, and went back to report. Takami-musubi and Amaterasu assembled the deities by the Tranquil River of Heaven, and on Omoikane's counsel they sent Ame-no-hohi, who curried favour with Ōkuninushi and sent no report for three years. Next they sent Ame-no-Wakahiko with the heavenly deer-bow and feathered arrows. He married Ōkuninushi's daughter Shitateru-hime, schemed to take the land for himself, and sent no report for eight years. The deities sent a pheasant, Naki-me, to question him. She perched on the cassia tree at his gate and spoke the heavenly deities' words. Urged by Ama-no-sagu-me, he shot the pheasant with the heavenly bow; the arrow passed through her and flew up to Takagi-no-kami by the Tranquil River. Seeing blood on its feathers, Takagi said: 'If Ame-no-Wakahiko has not disobeyed and shot at evil deities, let this arrow not strike him; if he has an evil heart, let him die by it,' and threw it back down through the hole it had made. It struck Ame-no-Wakahiko in the chest as he lay on his bed, and he died. Hence, says the text, the saying 'beware a returning arrow'.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十至三十一节。

heading_en: Takemikazuchi and the yielding of the land
body_zh: 众神最后派出了建御雷神，由天鸟船神陪同。两位神降落到出云国伊那佐的小滨，建御雷神拔出十拳剑，剑尖朝上倒插在浪头上，盘腿坐在剑尖上，问大国主：天照大神和高木神派我们来问你：你统治的苇原中国，是天神之子应当统治的国土，你意下如何？大国主说：我不能回答，我的儿子八重事代主神会回答，可他到美保岬打鸟钓鱼去了。天鸟船神把事代主找来，事代主说：遵命，把这国土献给天神之子吧。说完踏翻了自己的船，拍出“天之逆手”，把船变成青柴垣，藏身其中。另一个儿子建御名方神用指尖托着千引石走来，要和建御雷比力气。他一抓建御雷的手，那只手就变成了冰柱，又变成了剑刃；建御雷反过来抓住他的手，像抓一根嫩芦苇一样捏碎扔开。建御名方逃到信浓的州羽海，求饶说：我决不离开这里，也不违背父亲和事代主的话。大国主终于说：这片国土就献出去吧。只请为我建一座宫殿，宫柱深深立在地底岩石上，屋梁高高架到高天原，我就隐退在弯弯曲曲的道路深处。于是人们在出云的多艺志小滨建起了宫殿，建御雷神回到天上复命。
body_en: Last, the deities sent Takemikazuchi, with Ame-no-tori-fune. The two came down to the little shore of Inasa in Izumo. Takemikazuchi drew his ten-grasp sword, stood it upside down on the crest of a wave, sat cross-legged on its point and asked Ōkuninushi: 'Amaterasu and Takagi-no-kami have sent us to ask: the Central Land of Reed-Plains that you rule is the land the heavenly deity's child should rule. What is your mind?' Ōkuninushi said: 'I cannot answer. My son Yae-Kotoshironushi will answer, but he has gone to Cape Miho to hunt birds and fish.' Fetched, Kotoshironushi said: 'I obey; offer this land to the heavenly deity's child.' He trod on his boat to overturn it, clapped his hands in the heavenly backward clap, turned the boat into a green fence and hid within it. Then another son, Takeminakata, came carrying a thousand-draught rock on his fingertips and challenged Takemikazuchi to a trial of strength. When he grasped Takemikazuchi's hand it turned into an icicle and then into a sword-blade; Takemikazuchi grasped his in return like a young reed, crushed it and flung it away. Takeminakata fled to the sea of Suwa in Shinano and begged for his life, vowing never to leave it and not to go against his father or Kotoshironushi. At last Ōkuninushi said: 'Let this land be offered. Only build me a dwelling with pillars set deep in the bedrock and cross-beams raised to the Plain of High Heaven, and I will retire into the winding ways.' A palace was built on the shore of Tagishi in Izumo, and Takemikazuchi went back up to report.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十二节。

body_zh: 八十神都想娶稻羽的八上比卖，一起出发去求婚，让大穴牟迟背着袋子，像仆人一样跟在后面。走到气多岬，他们看见一只被剥光了皮的兔子躺在地上。八十神对兔子说：你去海里洗个澡，然后躺在高山顶上吹风。兔子照做了，海水干了以后，它的皮肤被风吹得裂开，痛得直哭。大穴牟迟最后赶到，问它为什么哭。兔子说：我本来住在淤岐岛，想渡海过来，就骗海里的和迩说，我们来比一比谁的族人多，你们排成一行，我从你们背上踩过去数一数。和迩们排好了队，我一路踩着它们的背走过来，快到岸时却说了一句：你们上当了！最后那只和迩就抓住我，剥光了我的衣服。大穴牟迟教它到河口用淡水洗身，再把蒲草的花粉铺在地上，在上面打滚。兔子照做，身体恢复如初。书中说，这就是稻羽的白兔，现在叫作兔神。兔子对他说：八十神得不到八上比卖，虽然你背着袋子，她一定会嫁给你。
body_en: The Eighty Deities all wished to marry Princess Yakami of Inaba, and set out together, making Ōnamuji carry their bag like a servant. At Cape Keta they found a hare lying stripped of its fur. They told it to bathe in the sea and lie on a high mountain in the wind; it did, and as the salt dried its skin split, and it lay weeping with pain. Ōnamuji came last and asked why it wept. The hare said: 'I lived on the island of Oki and wanted to cross. I tricked the wani of the sea, saying, let us count whose tribe is larger; line up and I will count you as I step across your backs. They lined up and I trod across, but just before landing I said, you have been deceived! The last wani seized me and stripped off all my clothing.' Ōnamuji told it to wash in the fresh water of the river-mouth and roll in the pollen of the sedges. It did, and its body was restored. This, says the text, is the White Hare of Inaba, now called the Hare Deity. The hare said: 'The Eighty Deities will not win the princess. Though you carry the bag, she will be yours.'
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十一节。

heading_en: The red boar of Mount Tema
body_zh: 八上比卖果然对八十神说：我不听你们的话，我要嫁给大穴牟迟。八十神大怒，商量要杀死大穴牟迟。他们把他带到伯伎国手间山的山脚下——伯伎国大致在今天鸟取县的西部——对他说：山上有一头红色的野猪，我们把它赶下来，你在下面等着抓住它。要是抓不住，就杀了你。他们在山上把一块像野猪那样大的石头用火烧得通红，推下山去。大穴牟迟去抓那块石头，被烧得粘在石头上死了。他的母亲哭着上天，向神产巢日神求救。神产巢日神派了两位女神下来：蚶贝比卖和蛤贝比卖，她们的名字就是赤贝和蛤蜊。蚶贝比卖刮下贝壳上的粉末，蛤贝比卖取来水，把两样东西调和成像母亲的乳汁一样的药，涂遍他的全身。大穴牟迟又活了过来，变成了一个英俊的年轻人，到处走动。这是他第一次死而复生。
body_en: Princess Yakami told the Eighty Deities: 'I will not listen to you. I will marry Ōnamuji.' Furious, they plotted to kill him. They took him to the foot of Mount Tema in Hahaki, roughly the west of present-day Tottori, and said: 'There is a red boar on this mountain. We will drive it down; you wait below and catch it. If you fail, we will kill you.' Then they heated in fire a great stone shaped like a boar and rolled it down. Ōnamuji caught it, was burned fast to it and died. His mother went up weeping to heaven and begged Kami-musubi for help, and Kami-musubi sent down two women, Princess Cockle-Shell and Princess Clam, named for the ark-shell and the clam. Princess Cockle-Shell scraped powder from her shell and Princess Clam brought water, and they mixed them like a mother's milk and smeared it over him. He came to life again as a handsome young man and walked about. It was the first time he died and lived again.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十二节。

body_zh: 八十神看见他又活了，再次设下圈套。他们把大穴牟迟带进山里，砍倒一棵大树，在树干的裂缝里打进一个楔子，让他站进裂缝中间，然后猛地拔掉楔子，把他夹死在树干里。母亲又一次哭着到处寻找，终于找到了他，劈开大树，把他取出来救活了。这已经是他第二次死而复生。母亲对他说：你再住在这里，终究会被八十神害死的。她把他送到木国——也就是后来的纪伊国——的大屋毘古神那里躲避，张伯伦把这位神的名字译作“大屋之王子”。可是八十神一路追到了木国，拉满了弓，向大屋毘古神要人。大屋毘古神就让大穴牟迟从一棵树的树杈之间悄悄逃走，对他说：你到须佐之男所在的根之坚洲国去吧，那位大神一定会为你出主意。大穴牟迟就这样离开了人间，去寻找自己的祖先。
body_en: Seeing him alive again, the Eighty Deities set another trap. They led Ōnamuji into the mountains, felled a great tree, drove a wedge into the cleft of the trunk, made him stand in the cleft, and then pulled out the wedge and crushed him to death. Again his mother searched for him weeping, found him, split the tree, took him out and restored him — the second time he had died and lived again. She said: 'If you stay here, you will be destroyed by the Eighty Deities in the end,' and sent him to the deity Oho-ya-biko, Chamberlain's Great-House-Prince, in the land of Ki, later called Kii. But the Eighty Deities pursued him there, fitting arrows to their bows and demanding him. Oho-ya-biko let him slip away through the fork of a tree, telling him: 'Go to the Nether-Distant-Land where Susanoo dwells. That great deity will surely counsel you.' So Ōnamuji left the living world to seek his ancestor.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十二节。

body_zh: 根之坚洲国——张伯伦译作“幽远之国”——就是当年须佐之男哭着要去的母亲之国，如今他住在这里。大穴牟迟来到须佐之男的宫殿，须佐之男的女儿须势理毘卖出来迎接，两人四目相对，一见钟情，当即结为夫妻。须势理毘卖回到殿里对父亲说：来了一位非常英俊的神。须佐之男出来一看，说：这是苇原色许男啊。“色许男”字面是“丑男子”，也有人理解为强悍的男子。须佐之男把他叫进来，却让他睡在满是毒蛇的蛇室里。须势理毘卖偷偷把一条驱蛇的领巾交给丈夫——领巾是一种披在肩上的长巾——对他说：蛇要咬你的时候，你就把这条领巾挥三下，把它们赶开。大穴牟迟照她的话做了，蛇都安静下来，他安安稳稳地睡了一夜，第二天平安走了出来。这是须佐之男给他的第一次考验，此后还有三次。
body_en: The Nether-Distant-Land, the mother's land that Susanoo had once wept to go to, was now his dwelling. When Ōnamuji came to Susanoo's palace, Susanoo's daughter Suseri-bime came out; they looked at each other and were married at once. She went in and told her father: 'A very handsome deity has come.' Susanoo went out, looked at him and said: 'This is the Ugly Male of the Reed-Plains' — shiko-wo, literally ugly male, though some read it as a fierce one. He called him in, but made him sleep in a room full of snakes. Suseri-bime secretly gave her husband a snake-scarf, a long cloth worn over the shoulders, and said: 'When the snakes are about to bite you, wave this scarf three times to drive them off.' He did as she said, the snakes grew quiet, and he slept peacefully and came out unharmed in the morning. It was the first of Susanoo's trials; three more were to follow.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。

heading_en: The room of centipedes and wasps
body_zh: 第二天晚上，须佐之男又让他睡在一间满是蜈蚣和马蜂的屋子里。须势理毘卖又交给他一条领巾，书中叫作“蜈蚣与蜂之比礼”，像上一次一样教他在危急的时候挥动。大穴牟迟又平安地度过了一夜，第二天照样走了出来。须佐之男的考验并没有到此为止。这位大神当年在高天原上也曾胡作非为，被众神驱逐出天界，如今轮到他来考验来娶自己女儿的年轻人。在这位暴躁的大神眼里，这个年轻人还远远没有证明自己。而在故事里，每一次真正救了大穴牟迟的，都是须势理毘卖的智慧与爱。她站在丈夫一边，悄悄地违背父亲的意愿；在《古事记》里，这样在关键时刻出手相助的女子并不少见，后面的丰玉毘卖和弟橘比卖也是如此。一次次的考验，也让这个曾被兄长们欺负的年轻人渐渐成为能统治国土的神。
body_en: The next night Susanoo put him in a room full of centipedes and wasps. Again Suseri-bime gave him a scarf, which the text calls the centipede-and-wasp scarf, and taught him to wave it in danger as before, and again he came out unharmed. Susanoo's trials were not over. The great deity who had once run riot in High Heaven and been driven out by the gods now tested the young man who had come for his daughter, and in his eyes the youth had proved nothing yet. In the story it is Suseri-bime's wit and love that save Ōnamuji each time: she takes her husband's side and quietly works against her father's will. Women who step in at the decisive moment are not rare in the Kojiki; Toyotama-bime and Oto-tachibana-hime will do the same later on. Trial by trial, the young man once bullied by his brothers was becoming a deity fit to rule the land.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。

heading_en: The burning moor and the mouse
body_zh: 须佐之男又把一支鸣镝——箭头上装着中空的响器、射出去会呼啸作响的箭——射进一片大草原，命令大穴牟迟去把箭找回来。等他走进草原深处，须佐之男就从四面放火，烧起了整片原野。火从四面围上来，大穴牟迟找不到出路。这时一只老鼠出来对他说：里面空荡荡，外面窄窄窄。他明白了老鼠的意思，用脚一踩地面，就掉进了一个地洞，躲在里面，大火从头顶烧了过去。不久，老鼠又把那支鸣镝衔来交给他，箭上的羽毛已经被小老鼠们啃光了。须势理毘卖以为丈夫已经死了，哭着拿着办丧事的器具来到原野上；须佐之男也以为他死了，走出来站在烧过的原野上。大穴牟迟却拿着那支箭走了出来，把箭献给了须佐之男。老鼠的那两句话，在原文里是“内者富良富良，外者须夫须夫”，读起来就像一句咒语。在高天原上，众神曾用火与笑声把天照大神请出岩户；在这里，救下大穴牟迟的却是一只地洞里的小老鼠。
body_en: Next Susanoo shot a whizzing arrow into a great moor and sent Ōnamuji to fetch it. When he was deep in the moor, Susanoo set fire to it all round. Ōnamuji could find no way out, until a mouse came and said: 'Inside, hollow-hollow; outside, narrow-narrow.' Understanding, he stamped on the ground, fell into a hole, and hid there while the fire passed over him. Soon the mouse brought him the whizzing arrow in its mouth; its feathers had been eaten by the mouse's children. Suseri-bime, thinking her husband dead, came weeping with the things for a funeral, and Susanoo, thinking the same, stood on the burned moor. But Ōnamuji came out with the arrow and presented it to him. The mouse's words in the original, uchi wa hora-hora, soto wa subu-subu, sound almost like a spell. In High Heaven the gods had drawn Amaterasu from her cave with fire and laughter; here it is a small mouse in a burrow that saves Ōnamuji.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。

body_zh: 须佐之男把大穴牟迟带回家里，叫进一间八寻宽的大屋子，让他替自己捉头上的虱子。大穴牟迟一看，须佐之男头上爬的根本不是虱子，而是一只只蜈蚣。须势理毘卖悄悄递给丈夫一把椋树的果实和一些红土。椋树的果实是黑紫色的小果子，嚼碎了就像碾碎的虫子。大穴牟迟把椋树果放进嘴里咬碎，再和着红土一起吐出来。须佐之男以为他在把蜈蚣一只只咬碎吐掉，原文说他“心里觉得这个年轻人可爱”，就放心地睡着了。从蛇室、蜈蚣与蜂之室，到火烧原野，再到头上的“虱子”，须佐之男的考验一次比一次危险，而每一次都被他的女儿悄悄化解。这是最后一次考验，也是大穴牟迟逃走的机会。须佐之男曾经在出云斩杀八岐大蛇、救下栉名田比卖，如今他睡着时，命运却交到了这个年轻人手里。
body_en: Susanoo took him back into the house, called him into a great room eight fathoms wide, and made him pick the lice from his head. But the creatures on Susanoo's head were centipedes. Suseri-bime secretly gave her husband berries of the muku tree, small dark fruit that look like crushed insects when chewed, and some red earth. Ōnamuji chewed the berries and spat them out with the red earth, and Susanoo, thinking he was biting the centipedes to pieces and spitting them out, felt fond of him in his heart — the text's own words — and fell asleep. From the snake room to the centipedes and wasps, the burning moor and now the 'lice', each trial was more dangerous than the last, and each was quietly undone by his daughter. It was the last trial, and Ōnamuji's chance to escape. Susanoo, who once slew the eight-forked serpent in Izumo and saved Kushinada-hime, now lay asleep with his fate in the young man's hands.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。

heading_zh: 生太刀、生弓矢与天诏琴
heading_en: The sword of life, the bow and the speaking lute
body_zh: 大穴牟迟趁须佐之男睡着，把他的头发一缕缕绑在屋子的椽子上，用一块要五百个人才拉得动的大石头堵住屋门，背起妻子须势理毘卖，带上须佐之男的生太刀、生弓矢和天诏琴，逃了出去。逃跑时天诏琴碰到了树，大地都震动起来。须佐之男被惊醒，一拉头发，把整座屋子都拉倒了。等他把绑在椽子上的头发解开，两人已经逃得很远。须佐之男一直追到黄泉比良坂，远远望着他们喊道：用你拿走的生太刀和生弓矢，把你的兄弟们赶到山坡下、河滩上去！你要成为大国主神，成为宇都志国玉神，让我的女儿须势理毘卖做你的正妻，在宇迦山下把宫柱深深地立在地底的岩石上，把屋梁高高地架到高天原，住在那里吧，你这家伙！大穴牟迟照他的话赶走了八十神，开始造国。八上比卖也来到他身边，但她害怕正妻须势理毘卖，把生下的孩子夹在树杈之间就回去了。
body_en: While Susanoo slept, Ōnamuji tied his hair to the rafters of the room, blocked the door with a rock that would take five hundred men to move, took his wife Suseri-bime on his back, and fled carrying Susanoo's great sword of life, his bow and arrows of life, and his heavenly speaking lute. The lute brushed against a tree and the earth resounded. Susanoo woke and pulled the whole house down with his hair; by the time he had untied it from the rafters they were far away. He pursued them to the Even Pass of Yomi and, gazing after them, called out: 'With the sword of life and the bow of life drive your brothers down the slopes and into the river-beds! Become Ōkuninushi, become Utsushi-kunitama, make my daughter Suseri-bime your chief wife, and at the foot of Mount Uka set your palace pillars deep in the bedrock and raise your cross-beams to the Plain of High Heaven, and dwell there, you rascal!' He did so, drove away the Eighty Deities and began to make the land. Princess Yakami came to him too, but in fear of the chief wife she left her child in the fork of a tree and went home.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第二十三节。

body_zh: 建御雷神回到天上，报告苇原中国已经平定。天照大神和高木神——也就是高御产巢日神——就命令天照大神的儿子天忍穗耳命：现在国土已经平定了，你就照原先的委托，降下去统治那片国土吧。天忍穗耳命回答说：我正在准备降临的时候，生了一个儿子，名叫天迩岐志国迩岐志天津日高日子番能迩迩艺命。应该派这个孩子降下去。这个孩子是天忍穗耳命和高木神的女儿万幡丰秋津师比卖命所生，也就是说，他同时是天照大神和高木神的孙子。于是两位大神对迩迩艺命下令：这丰苇原的瑞穗国，是交给你统治的国土。你就照着命令降下去吧。张伯伦把迩迩艺命的长名字逐字译出，大意是“天地丰饶、天日高照的稻穗丰熟之王子”。这位“天孙”，就是这一部故事的主人公之一。
body_en: Takemikazuchi went back up and reported that the Central Land of Reed-Plains had been pacified. Amaterasu and Takagi-no-kami — Takami-musubi — then commanded Amaterasu's son Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi: 'The land is now pacified; go down and rule it as we entrusted it to you.' He answered: 'While I was making ready to descend, a son was born to me, named Ame-nigishi-kuni-nigishi-ama-tsu-hi-daka-hiko-ho-no-ninigi. This child should be sent down.' The child was born of Ame-no-oshi-ho-mimi and Takagi-no-kami's daughter Yorozu-hata-toyo-aki-tsu-shi-hime, so that he was grandson both of Amaterasu and of Takagi. The two great deities commanded Ninigi: 'This Luxuriant Reed-Plains Land of Fresh Rice-Ears is the land you are to rule. Descend as commanded.' Chamberlain translates the long name word by word, roughly Heaven's-Plenty-Earth's-Plenty-Heaven's-Sun-Height-Prince-Rice-ear-Ruddy-Plenty. This August Grandchild is one of the heroes of this part.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三节。

heading_en: The jewel in the vessel and the sea deity's daughter
body_zh: 海神的女儿丰玉毘卖的侍女，拿着玉做的水器来井边打水，看见井水里映出了光，抬头一看，树上坐着一位英俊的男子，觉得十分奇怪。火远理命向她要水喝，侍女就打了水，盛在玉器里献给他。他却没有喝，而是解下颈上的玉，含在嘴里，吐进玉器中。那颗玉粘在器皿上，怎么也取不下来。侍女只好把粘着玉的器皿拿去交给丰玉毘卖。丰玉毘卖觉得奇怪，亲自出门去看，一见到他就被他迷住了，两人四目相对。她回去告诉父亲：我们家门口有一位很美的人。海神亲自出来一看，说：这是天津日高的儿子虚空津日高啊。他把火远理命请进宫里，铺上八层海驴皮的垫子，上面再铺八层绸缎的垫子，请他坐下，摆上一百桌礼物宴请他，把女儿丰玉毘卖嫁给了他。火远理命就在海神之宫住了三年。
body_en: A maid of the sea deity's daughter Toyotama-bime came to the well with a jewelled vessel to draw water. She saw a light in the water, looked up, and saw a handsome man in the tree, and wondered at it. Hoori asked her for water; she drew it and offered it in the jewelled vessel. He did not drink, but loosened a jewel from his neck, took it in his mouth and spat it into the vessel. The jewel stuck fast and could not be removed, so the maid took the vessel, jewel and all, to Toyotama-bime. Wondering, the princess went out to look, was charmed at the sight of him, and they exchanged glances. She told her father: 'There is a beautiful person at our gate.' The sea deity went out himself and said: 'This is Sora-tsu-hi-daka, the son of Ama-tsu-hi-daka.' He brought Hoori in, spread eight layers of rugs of sea-asses' skins and eight layers of silk rugs over them, seated him, feasted him with a hundred tables of gifts, and gave him his daughter Toyotama-bime in marriage. Hoori lived in the sea palace for three years.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十节。

body_zh: 三年过去，火远理命想起往事，长长地叹了一口气。丰玉毘卖告诉父亲：他住了三年从不叹气，昨夜却长叹了一声。海神问他缘故，他就讲了鱼钩的事。海神把大大小小的鱼都召集起来，问：有没有哪条鱼拿了这个鱼钩？鱼们说：最近鲷鱼说喉咙里卡了东西，吃不下饭，一定是它。一查鲷鱼的喉咙，果然找到了鱼钩。海神把鱼钩洗干净交给火远理命，教他说：你把鱼钩还给哥哥时，要说“这是个忧郁的钩、焦躁的钩、贫穷的钩、愚蠢的钩”，背过手去交给他。哥哥如果在高处种田，你就在低处种；他在低处种，你就在高处种。我掌管着水，三年之内你哥哥一定会穷下去。他要是因此怨恨来攻打你，你就拿出潮盈珠让潮水淹没他；他要是求饶，就拿出潮干珠让潮水退去救他。海神又召来众鳄，一只长一寻的鳄鱼说一天就能送他回去。火远理命骑着它回到人间，把佩带的小刀系在它的脖子上作为谢礼。回去以后，一切都如海神所说：哥哥越来越穷，凶狠地来攻打他，被潮盈珠淹得求饶，又被潮干珠救起，最后叩头说：从今以后，我日夜做你的守卫。书中说，隼人一族至今还表演溺水的动作，就是由此而来。
body_en: After three years Hoori remembered the past and heaved a great sigh. Toyotama-bime told her father: 'In three years he never sighed, but last night he heaved a great sigh.' The sea deity asked him why, and he told of the hook. The sea deity summoned all the fishes great and small and asked whether any had taken it. They said: 'The sea-bream has lately complained of something stuck in its throat and cannot eat; surely it is that.' The hook was found in the bream's throat, washed and given to Hoori, with this counsel: 'When you give it back to your brother, say: this hook is a gloomy hook, a fretful hook, a poor hook, a silly hook — and hand it to him behind your back. If he makes high fields, make yours low; if low, make yours high. I rule the waters, and in three years he will grow poor. If he attacks you in resentment, use the tide-flowing jewel to drown him; if he begs for mercy, use the tide-ebbing jewel to save him.' Then he summoned the wani, and a one-fathom wani said it could carry Hoori home in a day; Hoori rode it home and tied his small sword to its neck in thanks. All fell out as the sea deity said: the elder grew poor, attacked fiercely, was drowned by the tide-flowing jewel until he begged, was saved by the tide-ebbing jewel, and bowed down: 'Henceforth I will be your guard day and night.' That, says the text, is why the Hayato still perform the motions of drowning.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十至四十一节。

heading_en: The birth-hut thatched with cormorant feathers
body_zh: 后来，丰玉毘卖亲自从海里出来，对火远理命说：我怀孕了，现在就要生了。天神的孩子不能生在海里，所以我出来了。她在海边建起一座产屋，用鸬鹚的羽毛做屋顶，可是屋顶还没有盖完，她就要生了，只好走进屋里。临产前她对丈夫说：凡是别国的人生孩子的时候，都会变回自己本来的样子。我现在也要变回本来的样子生产，请你千万不要看我。火远理命觉得奇怪，偷偷往里一看，只见妻子变成了一条八寻长的大鳄，在地上爬动扭曲。他吓得转身逃走。丰玉毘卖知道他偷看了，羞愧难当，留下孩子，说：我本想永远通过海路来往，可是你偷看了我的样子，我实在羞耻。她关闭了海与陆地之间的通路，回到了海里。孩子取名为鹈葺草葺不合命，意思是“鸬鹚羽毛还没有盖完的屋顶”。丰玉毘卖虽然怨恨丈夫偷看，却忍不住思念，便让妹妹玉依毘卖来抚养孩子，托她带去一首歌：红色的玉啊，连穿玉的线都在发光；可是像白玉一样的你的模样，更加高贵。火远理命答歌说：在野鸭飞来的海岛上，与我共寝的妻子啊，我一生都不会忘记你。火远理命住在高千穗宫五百八十年。后来，鹈葺草葺不合命娶了姨母玉依毘卖，生下四个儿子，最小的儿子神倭伊波礼毘古命，就是后来的神武天皇。《古事记》的上卷到这里结束。
body_en: Later Toyotama-bime herself came out of the sea and said to Hoori: 'I am with child and my time has come. The child of a heavenly deity must not be born in the sea, so I have come out.' On the shore she built a birth-hut thatched with cormorant feathers, but before the roof was finished her pains came and she went inside. She said to her husband: 'All people of other lands, when they give birth, return to their native form. I too shall take my native form to bear the child. I beg you not to look at me.' Wondering, he peeped in, and saw that his wife had become a wani eight fathoms long, crawling and writhing. He fled in fear. Knowing he had looked, she was overcome with shame, left the child and said: 'I meant always to come and go by the road of the sea, but you have seen my form, and I am ashamed.' She closed the boundary between sea and land and went back down into the sea. The child was named Ugaya-fuki-aezu, Cormorant-Thatch-Meeting-Incompletely. Though she resented his peeping, she could not stop longing for him, and sent her younger sister Tamayori-bime to nurse the child, with a song: red jewels — even their string shines; but you, like white jewels, are nobler still. He answered: my wife, with whom I slept on the island where the wild ducks come, I shall not forget you all my life. Hoori dwelt in the palace of Takachiho five hundred and eighty years. Ugaya-fuki-aezu later married his aunt Tamayori-bime and had four sons, the youngest of whom, Kamu-yamato-ihare-biko, is the future Emperor Jimmu. Here the first volume of the Kojiki ends.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十二至四十三节。

body_zh: 迩迩艺命正要降临的时候，在天之八衢——天上八条道路交会的地方——站着一位神，他身上发出的光，向上照亮了高天原，向下照亮了苇原中国。天照大神和高木神命令天宇受卖神说：你虽然是个柔弱的女子，却是一位能与任何神面对面而不退缩的神。你去问问他：天神的儿子要降临，是谁在这里挡路？天宇受卖神就是当年在天之岩户前狂舞、逗得众神大笑的那位女神。她上前去问，那位神回答说：我是国津神，名叫猿田毘古神。我听说天神的儿子要降临，所以前来迎接，愿意做天孙的向导。原来这位在路口放光的神，并不是来阻拦，而是来引路的。张伯伦把他的名字译作“猿田之王子神”。原文说天宇受卖命是“与神相对而能胜过对方”的神，所以众神派她去问话。《古事记》没有细写猿田毘古的样子；《日本书纪》的一段异文则说他鼻长七咫，背长七尺多，眼睛像八咫镜一样闪闪发亮。
body_en: As Ninigi was about to descend, at the heavenly eight-forked crossroads stood a deity whose light shone up to the Plain of High Heaven and down to the Central Land of Reed-Plains. Amaterasu and Takagi-no-kami commanded Ame-no-Uzume: 'Though you are a delicate woman, you are a deity who can face down any deity. Go and ask him who stands in the way where our child is to descend.' She was the goddess who had once danced before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling and set the gods roaring with laughter. When she asked, the deity answered: 'I am an earthly deity named Sarutahiko. I heard that the child of the heavenly deities was to descend, and I have come to meet him and to serve as his guide.' The shining deity at the crossroads had come not to bar the way but to lead it. Chamberlain renders his name the Deity Prince of Saruta. The text says Ame-no-Uzume was a deity who could outface any deity, which is why she was sent. The Kojiki does not describe Sarutahiko; a variant in the Nihon shoki says his nose was seven hands long, his back more than seven feet tall, and his eyes shone like an eight-hand mirror.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三节。

heading_en: The regalia and the five chiefs
body_zh: 天照大神为迩迩艺命安排了五位随从的神，称为“五伴绪”：天儿屋命、布刀玉命、天宇受卖命、伊斯许理度卖命和玉祖命，他们都是当年在天之岩户前出过力的神。天照大神又把当年把她从岩户里引出来的八尺勾玉和镜子，以及须佐之男从大蛇尾中得到的草薙剑交给他，还派了思金神、天手力男神和天石门别神同行。天照大神说：这面镜子，你要把它当作我的御魂，像祭拜我一样祭拜它。又说：思金神，你要承担起祭祀的事务，掌管政事。书中接着说，这两位神如今在五十铃宫受到祭祀，也就是伊势的神宫。故事里的镜、玉、剑，在这里第一次被一起交到天孙手中。书中还一一记下了五位随从神的后人：天儿屋命是中臣连的祖先，布刀玉命是忌部首的祖先，天宇受卖命是猿女君的祖先，伊斯许理度卖命是作镜连的祖先，玉祖命是玉祖连的祖先；天石门别神又名栉石窗神、丰石窗神，是守护宫门的神。
