body_en: Amaterasu assigned to Ninigi five attendant deities, the five chiefs of companies: Ame-no-koyane, Futo-tama, Ame-no-Uzume, Ishi-kori-dome and Tama-no-oya, all of whom had played their part before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling. She gave him the curved jewels and the mirror that had drawn her out of the rock-dwelling, and the Kusanagi sword that Susanoo had taken from the serpent's tail, and sent with him Omoikane, Ame-no-tajikarao and Ame-no-iwato-wake. She said: 'Regard this mirror as my august spirit, and reverence it as you would reverence me,' and: 'Omoikane, take charge of the rites and carry on the government.' The text adds that these two are worshipped at the shrine of Isuzu, the shrine at Ise. Mirror, jewels and sword are here placed together in the hands of the August Grandchild for the first time in the story. The text also records the descendants of the five chiefs: Ame-no-koyane is ancestor of the Nakatomi, Futo-tama of the Imbe, Ame-no-Uzume of the Saru-me, Ishi-kori-dome of the mirror-makers and Tama-no-oya of the jewel-makers; Ame-no-iwato-wake, also called Kushi-iwa-mado and Toyo-iwa-mado, is the deity who guards the palace gates.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三节。

body_zh: 迩迩艺命离开了天上的岩座，分开天上层层叠叠的八重云，威风凛凛地开出一条道路，经过天之浮桥，降落在筑紫日向的高千穗的久士布流多气峰上。天忍日命和天津久米命背着天上的石箭袋，佩着头椎大刀，拿着天上的波士弓和真鹿儿矢，走在天孙的前面开路；书中说，他们是大伴连和久米直两族的祖先。迩迩艺命站在那里说：这里正对着韩国，有一条笔直的路通到笠沙的岬角，早晨的太阳直直照来，傍晚的太阳也照得明亮。所以这里是非常好的地方。他在那里把宫柱深深地立在地底的岩石上，把屋梁高高地架到高天原，住了下来。从高天原到人间的这一段路，就这样走完了。日向的高千穗峰究竟在哪里，后世有宫崎县的高千穗和雾岛山的高千穗峰等不同说法，《古事记》本身没有给出更多线索。
body_en: Ninigi left the heavenly rock-seat, pushed apart the eight-fold heavenly clouds, and with mighty way-dividing made his way down by the Floating Bridge of Heaven to the peak of Kuji-furu-take of Takachiho in Himuka in Tsukushi. Ame-no-oshi-hi and Ama-tsu-kume went before him carrying heavenly rock-quivers, girded with mallet-headed swords, holding heavenly bows and true-deer arrows; the text names them as ancestors of the Ōtomo and Kume clans. Ninigi said: 'This place faces Kara; a straight road runs through to the cape of Kasasa; it is a land where the morning sun shines straight and the evening sun shines bright. This is an exceedingly good place.' There he set his palace pillars deep in the bedrock, raised its cross-beams to the Plain of High Heaven, and dwelt. So the road from High Heaven to the human world was travelled. Where the peak of Takachiho in Himuka lies is disputed — later traditions point to Takachiho in Miyazaki or to the Takachiho peak of the Kirishima mountains — and the Kojiki itself gives no further clue.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十三至三十四节。

heading_en: The Duchesses of Saru and the sea-slug
body_zh: 迩迩艺命对天宇受卖命说：你送那位为我们引路的猿田毘古神回去吧。是你把他的名字问出来的，你就承受他的名字，侍奉他吧。所以，书中说，猿女君一族的女子都带着猿田毘古这位男神的名字，被称为“猿女”。后来，猿田毘古神在阿邪诃打鱼，手被比良夫贝夹住，沉进海里淹死了：他沉到海底时，生出了底度久御魂；海水冒泡时，生出了都夫多都御魂；水泡破开时，生出了阿和佐久御魂。天宇受卖命送猿田毘古回去以后返回，把大大小小的鱼都召集起来，问它们：你们愿意侍奉天神的儿子吗？鱼们都说：愿意侍奉。只有海参一声不吭。天宇受卖命说：这张嘴就是不肯回答的嘴！就用小刀把海参的嘴割开了。所以，书中说，海参的嘴至今仍是裂开的。书中还说，此后每一代天皇在位的时候，志摩国进献的海产初物都要分一份给猿女君。
body_en: Ninigi said to Ame-no-Uzume: 'Escort Sarutahiko, who served as our guide, back home. Since it was you who learned his name, take his name and serve him.' Therefore, says the text, the women of the Saru-me clan bear the name of the male deity Sarutahiko and are called the Duchesses of Saru. Later, while fishing at Azaka, Sarutahiko had his hand caught by a hirabu shell and sank and drowned in the sea; as he sank to the bottom, as the water bubbled, and as the bubbles burst, three deities were born. Ame-no-Uzume, coming back from escorting him, gathered all the fishes broad of fin and narrow of fin and asked: 'Will you serve the child of the heavenly deities?' All said they would — except the sea-slug, which said nothing. 'This is a mouth that gives no answer!' said Ame-no-Uzume, and slit its mouth with her small knife. That, says the text, is why the sea-slug's mouth is slit to this day. The text adds that in every reign a share of the first fruits of the sea sent from Shima is granted to the Saru-me.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十五至三十六节。

heading_zh: 木花之佐久夜毘卖与石长比卖
body_zh: 迩迩艺命在笠沙的岬角遇见一位美丽的少女，问她是谁的女儿。少女说：我是大山津见神的女儿，名叫神阿多都比卖，又叫木花之佐久夜毘卖——意思是“像树上的花一样灿烂盛开的公主”。迩迩艺命说：我想娶你，你看怎样？她说：我不能回答，我的父亲大山津见神会回答。迩迩艺命派人去求婚，大山津见神非常高兴，让她的姐姐石长比卖和她一同出嫁，还带上了满满一百桌的礼物。可是石长比卖长得非常丑陋，迩迩艺命一见就害怕，把她送了回去，只留下了妹妹木花之佐久夜毘卖，与她共度一夜。大山津见神因为石长比卖被送回而深感羞耻，说：我把两个女儿一起献上，是有用意的：有石长比卖在，天神子孙的寿命就会像岩石一样长久，不论风雪；有木花之佐久夜毘卖在，他们就会像树上的花一样繁荣。如今你只留下了木花之佐久夜毘卖，天神子孙的寿命就会像树上的花一样短暂。书中说，所以直到今天，历代天皇的寿命都不长久。
body_en: At the cape of Kasasa, Ninigi met a beautiful maiden and asked whose daughter she was. She said: 'I am the daughter of the great mountain deity Ōyamatsumi; my name is Kamu-ata-tsu-hime, also Konohana-sakuya-hime' — the Princess Blossoming like the Flowers of the Trees. He said: 'I wish to marry you. What do you say?' She answered: 'I cannot say; my father Ōyamatsumi will answer.' When Ninigi sent to ask, Ōyamatsumi was delighted, and sent her elder sister Iwanaga-hime with her, together with a hundred tables of gifts. But Iwanaga-hime was very ugly; Ninigi took fright at the sight of her and sent her back, keeping only the younger sister, with whom he spent one night. Ōyamatsumi, ashamed at Iwanaga-hime's return, said: 'I sent both daughters for a purpose: with Iwanaga-hime, the lives of the heavenly deity's descendants would endure like the rocks through snow and wind; with Konohana-sakuya-hime, they would flourish like the blossoms of the trees. Since you have kept only Konohana-sakuya-hime, their lives will be as brief as the blossoms of the trees.' That, says the text, is why the lives of the Heavenly Sovereigns down to this day are not long.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十七节。

body_zh: 过了些日子，木花之佐久夜毘卖来对迩迩艺命说：我怀孕了，就要生产了。天神的孩子不能私下里生，所以来告诉你。迩迩艺命却说：只过了一夜就怀孕了？这一定不是我的孩子，一定是哪个国津神的孩子。木花之佐久夜毘卖说：如果我怀的是国津神的孩子，生产时就不会平安；如果是天神的孩子，就一定平安。她建起一座八寻宽、没有门的大殿，走进去以后用泥土把四面封死，到生产的时候，就在殿里放起火来。在熊熊大火之中，她生下了三个儿子：火势正旺时生的叫火照命，书中说他是阿多隼人的祖先；接着生的叫火须势理命；最后生的叫火远理命，又名天津日高日子穗穗手见命。张伯伦把火照命和火远理命分别译作“火之照耀”和“火之消退”。三个孩子都平安降生，母亲用这场大火证明了自己的清白。
body_en: After some time Konohana-sakuya-hime came to Ninigi and said: 'I am with child and my time is near. The child of a heavenly deity must not be born in secret, so I have come to tell you.' But Ninigi said: 'With child after a single night? It cannot be mine. It must be the child of some earthly deity.' She answered: 'If the child I carry is an earthly deity's, the birth will not go well; if it is the heavenly deity's, it will surely go well.' She built a doorless hall eight fathoms wide, went inside, sealed it all round with clay, and when her time came set fire to the hall. In the midst of the flames she bore three sons: the first, born when the fire blazed brightest, Hoderi, whom the text names ancestor of the Hayato of Ata; next Hosuseri; and last Hoori, also called Ama-tsu-hi-daka-hiko-ho-ho-de-mi. Chamberlain renders Hoderi and Hoori as Fire-Shine and Fire-Subside. All three were born safely, and the mother proved her truth by fire.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十八节。

heading_en: The luck of the sea and the luck of the mountains
body_zh: 火照命成了海幸彦，用鱼钩捕捞海里大大小小的鱼；火远理命成了山幸彦，用弓箭猎取山里大大小小的野兽。“幸”在这里指的是猎具和收获，张伯伦说英语里没有合适的词，只好译作“运气”。有一天，火远理命对哥哥说：我们交换一下猎具用吧。他请求了三次，哥哥都不答应，最后才勉强换了。火远理命拿着哥哥的鱼钩去钓鱼，一条鱼也没有钓到，还把鱼钩弄丢在海里了。哥哥火照命来要回自己的鱼钩，说：山的猎具是山的，海的猎具是海的，我们还是各自换回来吧。弟弟说：你的鱼钩我钓鱼时丢了。哥哥一定要他还。弟弟就把自己佩带的十拳剑打碎，做成五百个鱼钩来赔，哥哥不要；又做了一千个鱼钩来赔，哥哥还是不要，说：我只要我原来的那个鱼钩。三兄弟的名字都与火有关：火照、火须势理、火远理，像是记下了他们在火中出生时火势的起落。
body_en: Hoderi became the Luck of the Sea, catching fish broad of fin and narrow of fin with his hook; Hoori became the Luck of the Mountains, taking beasts rough of hair and soft of hair with his bow. The word sachi here means both the hunting gear and its yield, and Chamberlain says English has no satisfactory equivalent, so he renders it luck. One day Hoori asked his brother to exchange their gear. Three times he asked and was refused, and at last the elder reluctantly agreed. Hoori took the fish-hook to sea, caught not a single fish, and lost the hook in the water. Hoderi came to ask for it back: 'Mountain luck to the mountain, sea luck to the sea — let us each have our own again.' The younger said he had lost it fishing, but the elder insisted. So Hoori broke up his ten-grasp sword and made five hundred hooks in recompense, but his brother would not take them; he made a thousand, and still his brother refused: 'I want my own hook.' All three brothers' names speak of fire — Fire-Shine, Fire-Climax, Fire-Subside — as if recording the rise and fall of the flames in which they were born.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第三十九节。

heading_en: The salt deity and the road to the sea palace
body_zh: 火远理命在海边哭泣，这时盐椎神来了，问他：天津日高日子，你为什么哭？他说出了鱼钩的事。盐椎神说：我来为你想个好办法。他编了一艘缝隙紧密、不透水的竹笼小船，让火远理命坐进去，对他说：我把船推出去以后，你就顺着漂一会儿，会遇到一股好的潮流，你就跟着潮流走。前面会有一座宫殿，像鱼鳞一样一层层盖起来的，那就是绵津见神——海神——的宫殿。到了海神宫门口，旁边有一口井，井边有一棵枝叶繁茂的桂树。你就坐在那棵树上，海神的女儿看见你，会替你出主意的。火远理命照着他的话，乘着小船顺着潮流漂去，果然来到了那座鱼鳞般的宫殿前，爬上井边的桂树坐了下来。张伯伦把盐椎神译作“盐之主神”；那艘小船，原文叫“无间胜间之小船”，意思是编得严密、没有一点缝隙的竹笼船。火远理命独自坐在这样的小船里，离开陆地，顺着潮流漂向大海深处。
body_en: As Hoori wept on the seashore, the salt deity Shio-tsuchi came and asked: 'Why do you weep, Sky's Sun-Height?' He told the story of the hook. Shio-tsuchi said: 'I will make a good plan for you.' He wove a little boat of bamboo so tightly that no water could enter, set Hoori in it and said: 'When I push the boat off, drift for a while and you will meet a pleasant current; follow it. You will come to a palace built like the scales of fishes: the palace of Watatsumi, the sea deity. By its gate there is a well, and by the well a many-branched cassia tree. Sit in that tree, and the sea deity's daughter will see you and counsel you.' Hoori did as he was told, drifted with the current, came to the palace built like fish-scales, and climbed the cassia tree by the well and sat there. Chamberlain renders Shio-tsuchi as the Deity Salt-Possessor; the boat is called in the original a small boat of closely woven bamboo without interstices. Alone in it, Hoori left the land behind and drifted with the current into the depths of the sea.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第四十节。

body_zh: 景行天皇在缠向的日代宫统治天下，他有许多儿子，其中有一对兄弟：哥哥叫大碓命，弟弟叫小碓命，也叫倭男具那命。有一天，天皇对小碓命说：你哥哥为什么早晚都不来一起用膳？你去好好教导他。过了五天，大碓命还是没有来。天皇问小碓命：你哥哥怎么还不来？你是不是没有教导他？小碓命回答：我已经教导过了。天皇问：你是怎么教导的？小碓命说：清早他去厕所的时候，我等着把他抓住，折断了他的手脚，用草席包起来扔掉了。这段话在书中说得很直接，本篇只交代结果。天皇听了，对这个儿子凶猛暴烈的性情感到害怕。这位少年后来的名字叫倭建命，他的英雄故事，就从父亲的这份恐惧开始。书中在前面的部分还记了一件事：天皇曾派大碓命去美浓召两位少女进宫，大碓命却把她们据为己有，另找别的女子冒名献上；天皇心里明白，却一直闷闷不乐。
body_en: The Heavenly Sovereign Keikō ruled from the palace of Hishiro at Makimuku. Among his many sons were two brothers: the elder, Oho-usu, and the younger, Wo-usu, also called Yamato-woguna. One day the sovereign said to Wo-usu: 'Why does your elder brother not come to the morning and evening meals? Go and teach him.' Five days passed and still the elder brother did not come. The sovereign asked: 'Why does your brother still not come? Have you not taught him?' Wo-usu said he had. 'How did you teach him?' Wo-usu answered that he had waited for his brother at dawn when he went to the privy, seized him, broken his limbs, wrapped him in matting and thrown him away. The text tells it bluntly; this retelling gives only the outcome. The sovereign was afraid of his son's fierce and violent heart. The boy would later be called Yamato Takeru, and his hero's story begins with his father's fear. An earlier part tells that the sovereign had sent Oho-usu to summon two maidens of Mino to court, and that Oho-usu took them for himself and sent other women under their names; the sovereign knew and was troubled.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第七十九节。

body_zh: 倭建命从甲斐越过科野，平定了科野坂的神，回到尾张，进了美夜受比卖的家，履行当初的约定。两人以歌相答，结为夫妻。随后，他把草薙剑留在美夜受比卖的身边，空着手去讨伐伊服岐能山——伊吹山——的神，说：这座山的神，我空手就能把他抓住。他登上山去，在山坡上遇见一头白色的野猪，大得像一头牛。倭建命大声说：这头变成白猪的，是山神的使者吧。现在不杀它，等我回来的时候再杀。说完就继续往上走。可是那头白猪并不是使者，正是山神本人。因为他说了这样的大话，山神降下了猛烈的冰雹，打得倭建命神志昏迷。这把一路保护他的剑，此刻已经不在他的身边。书中还记下，宴会上倭建命看见她外衣的下摆沾着月事的血迹，便以歌相问，她以歌相答，说日月流转，等他等得月亮都已升起。伊吹山在今天滋贺与岐阜的交界处。后世注释家认为，倭建命对着山神口出狂言——原文称为“言举”——正是招来灾祸的原因。
body_en: From Kai Yamato Takeru crossed Shinano, subdued the deity of the Shinano pass, and came back to Owari, to Miyazu-hime's house, to keep his pledge. They exchanged songs and were married. Then he left the Kusanagi sword with Miyazu-hime and went bare-handed to take the deity of Mount Ibuki, saying: 'As for the deity of this mountain, I will take him with my bare hands.' Climbing the mountain, he met on its slope a white boar as big as an ox. He said aloud: 'This one that has turned into a white boar must be the messenger of the mountain deity. I will not kill it now; I will kill it on my way back,' and went on climbing. But the white boar was no messenger; it was the deity himself. Because of these boastful words the deity sent down a great storm of hail that struck Yamato Takeru senseless. The sword that had protected him all the way was no longer at his side. The text also tells that at the feast he saw the stain of her monthly blood on the hem of her robe and questioned her in song, and she answered in song that months had passed and the moon had risen while she waited for him. Mount Ibuki lies on the border of present-day Shiga and Gifu. Later commentators see his boastful speech against the deity — kotoage, speaking out — as what brought the disaster on him.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十七至八十八节。

heading_en: Legs like a triple-bent rice cake
body_zh: 倭建命下了山，来到玉仓部的清泉边休息，神志稍稍清醒了一些，所以那眼泉被叫作居寤清水。他继续往前走，到了当艺野，说：我的心本来总想在天空中飞翔，可现在我的脚却走不动了，变得蹒跚踉跄。所以那里叫作当艺。他又拄着手杖慢慢地走，那段坡就叫杖衡坂。到了尾津岬的一棵孤松下，他发现以前在这里吃饭时忘下的一把刀，竟然还在原处。他唱道：尾津岬那棵孤松啊，我的兄长，你若是人，我就给你佩上刀，给你穿上衣服。到了三重村，他说：我的腿像三重弯曲的年糕一样，累极了。所以那里叫作三重。书中一路记下他留下的地名，像是记下了他越来越沉重的脚步。当艺在今天的岐阜一带，尾津岬在伊势的桑名附近，据说今天三重县的名字也与这里有关。那棵孤松下的刀，原来一直在等着它的主人。
body_en: Coming down the mountain, he rested by the clear spring of Tamakurabe and his mind cleared a little, so the spring is called the Awakening Spring. He went on to the moor of Tagi and said: 'My heart always longed to fly through the sky, but now my feet will not walk; they stagger.' So the place is called Tagi. Leaning on a staff he walked slowly on, and the slope is called the Staff Slope. At the single pine on Cape Otsu he found a sword he had left there once while eating, still lying where he had left it, and he sang: single pine of Cape Otsu, my elder brother — if you were a man, I would gird you with a sword and clothe you. At the village of Mie he said: 'My legs are like a rice cake bent three times; I am utterly weary.' So the place is called Mie. The text records the place-names he left behind, as if marking his ever heavier steps. Tagi lies in present-day Gifu and Cape Otsu near Kuwana in Ise; the name of Mie Prefecture is said to come from this place. The sword under the lone pine had been waiting all along for its master.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十九节。

heading_en: The songs of home and the white bird
body_zh: 到了能烦野，倭建命思念故乡，唱道：大和是国中最好的地方，层层叠叠的青山像垣墙一样环绕，大和啊，多么美好。又唱：愿那些性命完好的人，把平群山上的熊白梼叶插在头上。又唱：啊，从我家那边升起的云啊。病势沉重的时候，他唱了最后一首歌：我把那把大刀留在了少女的床边——那把刀啊！唱完就死了。使者把消息报告给京城。他的妃子和孩子们赶来，在那里修了陵墓，在周围的稻田里爬来爬去，哭着唱歌。这时，倭建命化作一只八寻长的白鸟，飞上天空，向海边飞去。妃子和孩子们在后面追，赤脚被竹子的残茬划破也不觉得痛，一边追一边唱。书中说，这四首歌都在他的葬礼上唱过，所以直到今天，天皇的大葬还唱这些歌。白鸟飞到河内的志几停了下来，人们在那里修了陵墓，叫作白鸟御陵。可是白鸟又从那里飞上天空，飞走了。
body_en: At the moor of Nobo, longing for his home, he sang: Yamato is the best of lands; the green mountains fold round it like a fence; Yamato, how lovely. And: let those whose lives are whole put leaves of the bear-oak of Mount Heguri in their hair. And: ah, the clouds rising from the direction of my home. When his sickness grew grave he sang a last song: by the maiden's bed I left my great sword — that sword! — and when he had sung it he died. Messengers carried the news to the capital. His consorts and children came down, made a tomb there, and crawled about the rice fields around it, weeping and singing. Then Yamato Takeru turned into a great white bird eight fathoms long, rose into the sky and flew towards the shore. His consorts and children followed, their bare feet cut on bamboo stubble, feeling no pain, singing as they went. The text says these four songs were all sung at his funeral, and so they are sung at the great funerals of the Heavenly Sovereigns to this day. The white bird stopped at Shiki in Kawachi, and a tomb was made there called the Tomb of the White Bird. But from there it rose into the sky again and flew away.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十九至九十节。

body_zh: 天皇说：西方有两个熊曾建，他们不肯归顺，没有礼数，你去把他们杀了。就派小碓命去了西方。那时小碓命还很年轻，头发在额前束成少年的发髻。他向姑母倭比卖命讨来她的上衣和裙子，又把一把短剑藏在怀里，出发了。到了熊曾建的家，只见房子四周围着三重军士，熊曾兄弟正在新建一座石室，准备举行落成的宴会，到处都是人声。小碓命在附近转了转，等着宴会的日子。到了那一天，他把束起的头发放下来梳成少女的样子，穿上姑母的衣裙，完全变成了一个少女，混在女人们中间，走进了石室。熊曾建兄弟一眼看中了这个少女，就让她坐在两人中间，一起饮酒作乐。倭比卖命是天皇的妹妹，在伊势侍奉天照大神；熊曾大致在今天九州的南部。一个束着少年发髻的皇子，就这样穿着姑母的衣裳，独自走进了敌人的宴席。
body_en: The sovereign said: 'In the west there are two Kumaso bravoes who will not submit and have no respect. Go and kill them,' and sent Wo-usu west. He was still young, his hair bound up at the forehead in a boy's knot. He begged from his aunt Yamato-hime her upper robe and skirt, hid a short sword in his bosom, and set out. At the Kumaso bravoes' house he found it surrounded by three rings of warriors; the brothers were building a new cave-dwelling for a housewarming feast, and the place was full of noise. Wo-usu walked about nearby, waiting for the day of the feast. When it came he let down his hair like a girl's, put on his aunt's robe and skirt, became in every way a young girl, mingled with the women and went into the dwelling. The two Kumaso bravoes were taken with the maiden at once, seated her between them, and feasted. Yamato-hime was the sovereign's sister, serving Amaterasu at Ise; Kumaso lay roughly in the south of present-day Kyushu. So a prince with a boy's hair-knot walked alone into his enemies' feast in his aunt's clothes.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十节。

body_zh: 宴会正热闹的时候，小碓命从怀里拔出短剑，抓住哥哥熊曾建的衣领，一剑刺穿了他的胸膛。弟弟熊曾建吓得转身就逃，小碓命追到石室的台阶下，从背后抓住他，把剑刺了进去。弟弟熊曾建说：不要动这把剑，我有话要说。小碓命就按住他，听他说。熊曾建问：您是谁？小碓命说：我是统治大八岛国、住在缠向日代宫的大带日子淤斯吕和气天皇的儿子，名叫倭男具那王。天皇听说你们熊曾建两个不肯归顺、没有礼数，派我来杀你们。熊曾建说：确实是这样。在西方，没有比我们兄弟两个更勇猛强悍的人了；可是在大倭国，却有比我们更勇猛的男子。我要献给你一个名号：从今以后，你就叫倭建御子吧。说完，小碓命就把他杀了。从此，人们称他为倭建命。“建”在这里是勇猛的意思，“倭建”就是“大和的勇士”。他一生最有名的这个名字，竟是一位敌人临死前送给他的赞许。
body_en: When the feast was at its height, Wo-usu drew the sword from his bosom, seized the elder Kumaso bravo by the collar and thrust the sword through his chest. The younger bravo fled in terror; Wo-usu pursued him to the foot of the steps of the dwelling, caught him from behind and thrust the sword into him. The younger bravo said: 'Do not move the sword. I have something to say.' Holding him down, Wo-usu listened. 'Who is your augustness?' 'I am the son of the Heavenly Sovereign Ōtarashi-hiko-oshiro-wake, who dwells in the palace of Hishiro at Makimuku and rules the Land of the Eight Great Islands; my name is King Yamato-woguna. The sovereign heard that you two Kumaso bravoes would not submit and had no respect, and sent me to kill you.' The bravo said: 'It is true. In the west there are none so brave and strong as we two; but in great Yamato there is a man braver than we. I will offer you a name: henceforth be called the August Child Yamato Takeru.' When he had spoken, Wo-usu killed him. From then on he was called Yamato Takeru. Takeru here means brave: Yamato Takeru is the brave one of Yamato. The name he is best known by was a tribute from a dying enemy.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十节。

heading_en: The Izumo bravo and the wooden sword
body_zh: 倭建命回京的路上，把山神、河神和海峡之神一一平定，然后进入出云国，想要杀死出云建。他先和出云建结为朋友，又暗中用赤梼木做了一把假刀，佩在身上。有一天，两人一起在肥河里洗澡。倭建命先从河里出来，把出云建解下的刀佩在自己身上，说：我们来交换刀吧。出云建从河里出来，就佩上了倭建命的那把木刀。倭建命说：来，我们比比刀法吧。两人各自拔刀，出云建拔不出那把木刀，倭建命就拔出真刀，把出云建杀了。他唱了一首歌，大意是：出云建佩的那把刀，刀鞘上缠着一层又一层的藤蔓，看起来很好，里面却没有刀身，真是可怜啊。他平定了西方，回到京城，向天皇复命。这两件事，一靠扮成少女，一靠交换刀剑，都是用计取胜。同样的木刀计和同一首歌，在《日本书纪》里被放进另一个故事：出云的一对兄弟之间。两部书在这里各有各的讲法。
body_en: On his way back Yamato Takeru subdued the deities of the mountains, the rivers and the straits, and then went into Izumo intending to kill the Izumo bravo. First he made friends with him, and secretly made a false sword of ichii wood, which he wore. One day they bathed together in the river Hi. Yamato Takeru came out first, girded on the sword the Izumo bravo had taken off, and said: 'Let us exchange swords.' The Izumo bravo came out and girded on the wooden sword. 'Come,' said Yamato Takeru, 'let us cross swords.' Each drew; the Izumo bravo could not draw the wooden sword, and Yamato Takeru drew the real one and killed him. He sang a song whose sense is: the sword the Izumo bravo wore, its scabbard wound with creepers many times — fine to look at, but with no blade inside, alas. Having subdued the west, he returned to the capital and reported to the sovereign. Both deeds, the girl's disguise and the exchange of swords, were won by trickery. The same wooden-sword trick and the same song appear in the Nihon shoki in a different story, between two brothers of Izumo; the two books tell it each in their own way.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十一节。

body_zh: 倭建命刚刚回来，天皇又命令他说：你去把东方十二道那些凶暴的神和不肯归顺的人平定了。天皇派吉备臣的祖先御锄友耳建日子跟他同行，又赐给他一支柊木做的八寻长矛。倭建命出发去东方，先到了伊势，参拜神宫，对在那里侍奉的姑母倭比卖命说：天皇是不是想让我死？他派我去打西方那些凶暴的人，我回来还没有多久，又不给我军队，就要派我去平定东方十二道的凶暴之人。这样想来，天皇一定是想让我死啊。他一边诉说，一边哭泣。临走时，倭比卖命把草薙剑交给他——这就是须佐之男从八岐大蛇尾中得到、天孙降临时带到人间的那把剑——又给了他一个袋子，说：如果遇到紧急的事情，就打开这个袋子。那支长矛，原文叫“比比罗木之八寻矛”，比比罗木就是柊树。至于袋子里装着什么，他当时并不知道。一个刚刚立下大功的皇子在姑母面前哭泣，这是《古事记》里少有的、写英雄软弱的一幕。
body_en: No sooner had Yamato Takeru returned than the sovereign commanded him again: 'Go and subdue the savage deities and unsubmissive people of the twelve roads of the East.' He sent with him Mi-suki-tomo-mimi-take-hiko, ancestor of the Kibi lords, and gave him a holly-wood spear eight fathoms long. On his way east Yamato Takeru went first to Ise, worshipped at the shrine, and said to his aunt Yamato-hime, who served there: 'Does the sovereign wish me dead? He sent me to strike the savage people of the west, and I have hardly come back before, without giving me any troops, he sends me to subdue the savage people of the twelve roads of the East. Thinking of this, I can only believe he wishes me to die.' He wept as he spoke. When he left, Yamato-hime gave him the Kusanagi sword — the sword Susanoo took from the serpent's tail and the August Grandchild brought down from heaven — and a bag, saying: 'If anything urgent happens, open the mouth of this bag.' The spear is called in the original an eight-fathom spear of hihiragi, the holly. What the bag held he did not yet know. A prince fresh from great deeds weeping before his aunt is one of the rare scenes in the Kojiki that show a hero's weakness.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十二节。

heading_en: The fire on the moor of Sagamu
body_zh: 倭建命到了尾张国，进了尾张国造的祖先美夜受比卖的家，本想娶她为妻，转念一想，等回来时再娶吧，就和她立下婚约，继续往东去了。他把山河间凶暴的神和不肯归顺的人一一平定。到了相武国，那里的国造骗他说：这片原野里有一个大沼泽，住在沼泽里的神非常凶暴。倭建命就走进原野去看那位神。国造在原野上四面放火。倭建命知道上了当，打开姑母给的袋子，里面是一块打火石。他先用草薙剑割开身边的草，再用打火石点起一圈逆火，把烧来的大火挡了回去，平安地走了出来。他回过头来，把那些国造全部杀死，放火烧掉，所以那个地方至今叫作烧津。《日本书纪》说这把剑因为割草而得名“草薙”，而《古事记》在更早的大蛇故事里就已经这样称呼它了。书中把这件事记在相武国，而“烧津”这个地名今天在骏河，也就是静冈县，这一点历来被注释家讨论。
body_en: In Owari, Yamato Takeru entered the house of Miyazu-hime, ancestress of the rulers of Owari, and thought to marry her; then, deciding to marry her on his return, he pledged himself to her and went on east. He subdued the savage deities and unsubmissive people of the mountains and rivers one by one. In Sagamu the local ruler deceived him: 'In this moor is a great marsh, and the deity of the marsh is very violent.' Yamato Takeru went into the moor to see the deity, and the ruler set fire to the moor all round. Knowing he had been deceived, he opened his aunt's bag and found a fire-striker. First he mowed the grass around him with the Kusanagi sword, then lit a counter-fire with the striker and drove back the oncoming fire, and came out safe. He turned back, killed all those rulers and burned them, so that the place is still called Yaizu, Burning Ford. The Nihon shoki says the sword was named Kusanagi, Grass-Mower, from this deed; the Kojiki already calls it so in the earlier serpent story. The text places this in Sagamu, while the name Yaizu belongs today to Suruga, in Shizuoka — a discrepancy long discussed by commentators.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十三节。

body_zh: 倭建命从那里出发，渡过走水海。海峡的神掀起大浪，船在原地打转，无法前进。这时，倭建命的妃子弟橘比卖命说：我代替皇子进入海中吧。皇子应当完成被派来做的事，回去向天皇复命。她要入海的时候，在浪上铺了八层菅草垫子、八层皮垫子和八层绸缎垫子，坐在上面，沉入了海中。汹涌的波浪自己平息下来，船又能前进了。弟橘比卖临走前唱了一首歌，大意是：在相武那群山耸立的小原野上，熊熊大火之中，你站在火里还在问我是否平安——啊，你啊。七天以后，她的梳子漂到了岸边。倭建命拾起那把梳子，为她修了陵墓，把梳子安放在里面。这首歌让人知道，在相武原野的大火里，她一直在丈夫的身边。走水海大致是今天东京湾口的浦贺水道一带，水流湍急，所以叫作“走水”。
body_en: From there Yamato Takeru crossed the sea of Hashirimizu. The deity of the strait raised great waves; the boat spun round and could not go forward. Then his consort Oto-tachibana-hime said: 'I will enter the sea in the prince's stead. The prince must accomplish the task he was sent on and report to the sovereign.' When she was about to enter the sea, she spread eight layers of sedge rugs, eight layers of skin rugs and eight layers of silk rugs on the waves, sat on them, and sank into the sea. The raging waves calmed of themselves and the boat could go on. Before she went she sang a song whose sense is: on the little moor of Sagamu among the standing peaks, in the midst of the burning fire, you stood and asked after me — ah, you. Seven days later her comb drifted ashore. Yamato Takeru took up the comb, made her a tomb and laid the comb in it. Her song shows that in the fire on the moor of Sagamu she had been at her husband's side. The Hashirimizu sea is roughly the Uraga channel at the mouth of Tokyo Bay, its current so swift that it was called Running Water.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十四节。

heading_en: The white deer on the Ashigara pass
body_zh: 倭建命继续深入东方，把凶暴的虾夷人都平定了，又平定了山河间凶暴的神，然后踏上了回程。来到足柄坂下，他正在吃干粮，那座山坡的神变成一只白鹿，走过来站在他面前。倭建命拿起吃剩的野蒜，等白鹿走近时扔过去，正好打中了它的眼睛，把它打死了。他登上足柄坂，回望来路，想起沉入海中的弟橘比卖，长叹了三声：吾妻哉！——“啊，我的妻子！”所以，书中说，从此人们就把那片土地叫作“阿豆麻”，也就是“东国”。这一声叹息，成了一个地方的名字。倭建命一路征战，从不诉苦，只在这里流露了一次深深的悲伤。虾夷指当时东方不服从朝廷的人们；足柄坂在今天神奈川与静冈交界的山上。白鹿被野蒜打中眼睛，这样细小的一笔，让这位山神的死显得格外突然。
body_en: Yamato Takeru went on deep into the East, subdued all the savage Emishi, pacified the savage deities of the mountains and rivers, and set out to return. At the foot of the Ashigara pass, as he was eating his dried rice, the deity of the pass changed into a white deer and came and stood before him. He took up the leftover end of the wild chive he had been eating, waited for the deer to come near, threw it, struck it in the eye and killed it. Then he climbed the pass, looked back the way he had come, remembered Oto-tachibana-hime who had sunk into the sea, and sighed three times: 'Azuma haya!' — 'Alas, my wife!' Therefore, says the text, the land has been called Azuma, the East. A sigh became the name of a land. Through all his fighting Yamato Takeru never complained; only here does he show his deep grief. The Emishi were the peoples of the East who did not submit to the court; the Ashigara pass lies in the mountains on the border of present-day Kanagawa and Shizuoka. The small detail of the wild chive striking the deer's eye makes the mountain deity's death all the more sudden.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十五节。

body_zh: 倭建命越过足柄坂，进入甲斐国，住在酒折宫里。有一天，他唱了一句歌：越过新治和筑波，已经睡了几夜？——意思是说，离开东方的新治与筑波以来，已经过了多少个夜晚了？身边的人没有一个能接下去。这时，一个在旁边看守火堆的老人接着唱道：数一数日子，夜是九夜，日是十日。倭建命十分赞赏这个老人，就封他为东国造。这一问一答的两句歌，后世被看作日本连歌的起源之一。在征战的长途中，这是少有的安静时刻：一位疲倦的皇子数着离家的日子，一位卑微的老人替他把日子数了出来。新治与筑波都在今天的茨城县，甲斐就是今天的山梨县，酒折宫的旧址在今天的甲府。身边的随从没有一个答得上来，答出这一句的，却是一个看火的老人。
body_en: Crossing from the pass into Kai, Yamato Takeru stayed at the palace of Sakaori. One day he sang a line: since passing Niibari and Tsukuba, how many nights have I slept? — that is, how many nights since leaving Niibari and Tsukuba in the East? None of his followers could answer it. Then an old man who was tending the fire took it up: counting the days, of nights there have been nine, of days ten. Yamato Takeru praised the old man and made him ruler of the Eastern Land. This exchange of two lines has been seen in later times as one of the beginnings of linked verse in Japan. On the long campaign it is a rare quiet moment: a weary prince counting the days away from home, and a humble old man counting them for him. Niibari and Tsukuba are in present-day Ibaraki, Kai is present-day Yamanashi, and the site of Sakaori is in today's Kofu. None of his attendants could answer; it was the old man watching the fire who did.
evidence_note: 《古事记》张伯伦译本第八十六节。

body_zh: 凯·卡乌斯继承了伊朗的王位，坐在宝座上，看着满朝的勇士和堆积如山的财宝，以为天下再也没有人比他更强大。有一天，宫门口来了一个陌生的歌手，请求在国王面前献唱。他其实是一个魔鬼变的。他弹起琴，唱起了马赞德兰：那里四季鲜花盛开，夜莺在花园里歌唱，山上长满了郁金香，空气温暖而芬芳，城里堆满了金子和宝石，美丽的少女多得数不清。凯·卡乌斯听得入了迷，当即宣布：我要率军去征服马赞德兰，把那里的财富和美景都收归伊朗。满朝的勇士都惊呆了，他们知道马赞德兰是魔鬼居住的地方，以前的贤明君王贾姆希德和法里东都不敢去冒犯。他们不敢劝阻国王，就悄悄派人连夜赶到扎布尔斯坦，去请扎尔。
body_en: Kay Kāvus inherited the throne of Iran and, seated in state with his champions around him and treasure heaped high, thought no one in the world more mighty than he. One day a strange minstrel came to the palace gate asking to sing before the king. He was in truth a demon. He struck his lute and sang of Māzandarān: flowers bloom there in every season, nightingales sing in the gardens, tulips cover the hills, the air is warm and fragrant, the cities are heaped with gold and jewels, and its fair maidens are past counting. Kay Kāvus was enchanted and declared at once: 'I will march and conquer Māzandarān and add its wealth and beauty to Iran.' The champions were aghast, for they knew Māzandarān was the home of demons, which even the wise kings Jamshīd and Fereydūn had not dared to attack. Not daring to oppose the king, they secretly sent a messenger riding through the night to Zābulistān to fetch Zāl.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 鲁斯塔姆带着白魔的肝走出洞穴，阳光照在他满是鲜血的身上，乌拉德看见他，吓得以为是魔鬼出来了，直到他开口说话才放下心来。鲁斯塔姆说：我已经杀死了白魔，打开了马赞德兰的大门，你的功劳我不会忘记。两人一起回到关押国王的地方。鲁斯塔姆把白魔肝中的血滴进凯·卡乌斯的眼睛里，国王的眼睛立刻亮了起来，又看见了阳光，看见了眼前的鲁斯塔姆。接着，鲁斯塔姆又把血滴进伊朗勇士们的眼睛里，所有的人都重见了光明。被囚禁的伊朗军队欢呼起来，他们拥抱鲁斯塔姆，赞美他是伊朗的救星，是勇士中的勇士。凯·卡乌斯坐在宝座上，命令摆设盛大的宴席，一连七天庆祝胜利，向造物主献上感恩的祷告。他对鲁斯塔姆说：没有你，就没有伊朗的国王。
body_en: Rostam came out of the cave with the White Demon's liver, the sunlight on his blood-soaked body; Olād, seeing him, took him for a demon and was terrified until he spoke. 'I have killed the White Demon and opened the gates of Māzandarān,' said Rostam; 'I will not forget your service.' Together they went back to where the king was held. Rostam dropped blood from the White Demon's liver into Kay Kāvus's eyes, and at once the king's eyes were bright again; he saw the sunlight and Rostam before him. Then Rostam dropped the blood into the eyes of the champions of Iran, and all of them saw again. The captive Iranian host cheered, embraced Rostam and praised him as the saviour of Iran, the champion of champions. Kay Kāvus took his throne and ordered a great feast to celebrate the victory for seven days, with prayers of thanks to the Creator. He said to Rostam: 'But for you, Iran would have no king.'
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

heading_en: The king who became a rock
body_zh: 凯·卡乌斯恢复了力量，写信给马赞德兰的国王，命令他前来投降，交出财宝，做伊朗的属国。马赞德兰国王收到信，傲慢地拒绝了，召集了魔鬼和人组成的大军，带着战象前来迎战。两军在平原上激战了七天，不分胜负。第八天，鲁斯塔姆冲到马赞德兰国王面前，举起长矛刺去，眼看就要刺中，那位会魔法的国王忽然把自己变成了一块巨大的岩石，长矛刺在石头上，再也伤不了他。伊朗的勇士们都惊呆了，谁也搬不动这块岩石。鲁斯塔姆跳下马，一个人把岩石扛了起来，一直扛回伊朗的营地，扔在国王的帐篷前，对着岩石说：快出来，否则我就用铁锤把你砸成碎块，扔到火里烧掉！岩石里的国王害怕了，从石头里走了出来，变回了人形。凯·卡乌斯下令处死了这个作恶多端的魔法师。鲁斯塔姆履行了诺言，请国王封乌拉德为马赞德兰的统治者。伊朗的大军满载着战利品，凯旋回国。
body_en: Restored to strength, Kay Kāvus wrote to the king of Māzandarān commanding him to come and submit, surrender his treasure and become a vassal of Iran. The king of Māzandarān haughtily refused, gathered a host of demons and men with war-elephants, and came out to battle. For seven days the armies fought on the plain without either winning. On the eighth day Rostam reached the king of Māzandarān and thrust his spear at him, but just as it was about to strike, the sorcerer king turned himself into a huge rock; the spear struck stone and could not harm him. The Iranian champions were astonished, and none could move the rock. Rostam leapt down, lifted the rock alone, carried it all the way back to the Iranian camp, threw it down before the king's tent and said to it: 'Come out, or I will smash you to pieces with my hammer and throw you into the fire!' The king inside the rock was afraid, came out of the stone and took human shape again. Kay Kāvus had the wicked sorcerer put to death. Keeping his promise, Rostam asked the king to make Olād ruler of Māzandarān, and the army of Iran returned home laden with spoils.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 可是凯·卡乌斯并没有因为这次教训变得谨慎。后来，一个魔鬼又来迷惑他，对他说：你已经统治了整个大地，为什么不去统治天空呢？天上的日月星辰，难道不该属于你吗？凯·卡乌斯又动了心。他问智者们怎样才能飞上天空，最后想出一个办法：他让人从鹰巢里捉来四只小鹰，用最好的肉喂养长大，然后造了一个宝座，在宝座的四角各竖一根长矛，矛尖上挂着一块羊肉，再把四只饿了好几天的鹰绑在宝座的四角。鹰想吃矛尖上的肉，拼命往上飞，就把宝座带上了天空。凯·卡乌斯坐在宝座上，越飞越高，越过了云层。可是鹰飞累了，再也飞不动了，宝座从空中坠落下来，跌进了一片荒凉的森林。凯·卡乌斯侥幸没有摔死，却困在林中又饿又怕。鲁斯塔姆和勇士们四处寻找，终于找到了他。勇士们严厉地责备他：你一次又一次地听信魔鬼，像个疯子一样。凯·卡乌斯羞愧难当，从此闭门忏悔了许多日子。
body_en: But Kay Kāvus did not grow cautious from this lesson. Later a demon came again to tempt him: 'You rule the whole earth; why not rule the sky? Should not the sun, moon and stars be yours as well?' Again Kay Kāvus was tempted. He asked his wise men how to fly to the sky, and at last hit on a plan: he had four young eagles taken from their nests and reared on the choicest meat; then he had a throne made, set a long spear upright at each of its corners with a piece of mutton hanging from each spear-point, and bound four eagles that had been starved for days to its four corners. Straining for the meat above them, the eagles flew upward and carried the throne into the sky. Kay Kāvus rose higher and higher, above the clouds. But the eagles tired and could fly no more, and the throne fell from the sky into a desolate forest. Kay Kāvus escaped death but lay trapped in the forest, hungry and afraid. Rostam and the champions searched far and wide and at last found him. The champions rebuked him sharply: 'Again and again you listen to demons; you act like a madman.' Ashamed, Kay Kāvus shut himself away in penitence for many days.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“凯·卡乌斯的更多愚行”一节。

body_zh: 扎尔赶到宫中，恳切地劝国王：马赞德兰是魔鬼的国度，他们会用魔法迷惑人，以前的国王都不敢去，你不要拿伊朗的勇士和自己的性命去冒险。凯·卡乌斯却说：我比贾姆希德和法里东更强大，我有更多的勇士和财宝，魔鬼又能把我怎样？你若是怕，就留在家里吧。扎尔无可奈何，只好告辞。凯·卡乌斯率领大军进入马赞德兰，烧杀抢掠，掳走了许多财宝和人口。马赞德兰的国王大为惊恐，派人去请魔鬼的首领白魔。白魔连夜召来一片乌云，天地间一片漆黑，接着降下了石头和冰雹，伊朗的军队在黑暗中乱成一团。等到天亮，凯·卡乌斯和他的勇士们全都瞎了眼睛，被魔鬼们抓住，关进了地牢。凯·卡乌斯在黑暗中后悔不已，偷偷派人给扎尔送信：我没有听你的话，如今落得这样的下场，快来救我吧。
body_en: Zāl hastened to court and earnestly urged the king: 'Māzandarān is the land of demons; they bewitch men with magic. No king before you has dared to go; do not risk the champions of Iran and your own life.' But Kay Kāvus said: 'I am mightier than Jamshīd and Fereydūn, with more champions and more treasure; what can demons do to me? If you are afraid, stay at home.' Zāl could do nothing but take his leave. Kay Kāvus led his army into Māzandarān, burning and plundering, carrying off treasure and captives. In terror the king of Māzandarān sent for the White Demon, chief of the demons. In the night the White Demon summoned a black cloud that plunged the world into darkness, then rained down stones and hail, and the Iranian army fell into confusion in the dark. When day came Kay Kāvus and all his champions were blind, and the demons seized them and cast them into a dungeon. In the darkness Kay Kāvus repented bitterly and secretly sent a message to Zāl: 'I did not listen to you, and this is my fate; come quickly and save me.'
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 扎尔收到信，对儿子鲁斯塔姆说：国王落难了，只有你能救他。从这里到马赞德兰有两条路：一条长而安全，要走六个月；另一条短而凶险，只要两个星期，可路上有狮子、恶龙、女巫和魔鬼。鲁斯塔姆说：我选那条近路，愿神保佑我。他穿上虎皮做的战袍，带上祖父的铁杵，骑上拉赫什出发了，一天走两天的路程。第一天傍晚，他在一片芦苇荡边打了一头野驴，烤来吃了，然后摘下拉赫什的辔头，让它去吃草，自己躺在芦苇丛里睡着了。半夜，一头凶猛的狮子回到它的巢穴，看见熟睡的人和马，就向拉赫什扑过来。拉赫什像火一样跳起来，用前蹄猛击狮子的头，用牙齿咬住狮子的背，把它摔在地上踩死了。鲁斯塔姆醒来，看见死狮，却责备拉赫什说：谁让你去和狮子打？要是你被它咬死了，我怎么背着铁杵、穿着战袍走到马赞德兰去？下次遇到危险，先把我叫醒。
body_en: When Zāl received the letter he said to his son Rostam: 'The king is in peril, and only you can save him. Two roads lead to Māzandarān: one long and safe, six months' journey; the other short and perilous, only two weeks, but beset by lions, dragons, witches and demons.' 'I choose the short road,' said Rostam; 'may God protect me.' He put on his war-coat of tiger-skin, took his grandfather's mace, mounted Rakhsh and set out, covering two days' journey in each day. On the first evening he killed a wild ass by a reed-bed, roasted it and ate, then took off Rakhsh's bridle to let him graze and lay down to sleep among the reeds. At midnight a fierce lion came back to its lair, saw the sleeping man and horse, and sprang at Rakhsh. Rakhsh leapt up like fire, struck the lion's head with his forefeet, seized its back in his teeth, threw it down and trampled it to death. Waking to find the dead lion, Rostam scolded Rakhsh: 'Who told you to fight a lion? If it had killed you, how would I have walked to Māzandarān with my mace and war-coat? Next time danger comes, wake me first.'
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 第二天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片炎热的沙漠，烈日像火一样烤着大地，四周没有一滴水，也没有一片树荫。走了很久，人和马都渴得精疲力竭，拉赫什的脚步越来越慢，鲁斯塔姆也从马上摔了下来，躺在滚烫的沙子上，舌头干裂，眼看就要渴死了。他抬起头，向造物主祈祷：神啊，你知道我是为了去救国王才走上这条路的，我不怕任何敌人，可是我不愿意渴死在这荒野里，求你救救我吧。就在这时，一只肥壮的公羊从他身边走过。鲁斯塔姆想：这只羊一定是去喝水的。他挣扎着站起来，拿着剑跟在公羊后面，走了不远，果然看见了一眼清澈的泉水。他和拉赫什痛痛快快地喝足了水，洗净了身上的尘土。鲁斯塔姆没有伤害那只公羊，而是向天空祝福它，感谢造物主派它来救了自己的性命。
body_en: The next day Rostam entered a scorching desert; the sun burned the earth like fire, and there was not a drop of water nor a patch of shade. After a long march man and horse were spent with thirst; Rakhsh slowed, and Rostam fell from his back and lay on the burning sand, his tongue cracked, close to dying of thirst. He raised his head and prayed: 'O God, you know I took this road to save the king. I fear no enemy, but I would not die of thirst in this wilderness; save me.' At that moment a fat ram passed close by him. 'This ram must be going to drink,' thought Rostam. He struggled to his feet and followed it, sword in hand, and not far off he found a clear spring. He and Rakhsh drank their fill and washed off the dust. Rostam did not harm the ram, but blessed it towards heaven and thanked the Creator for sending it to save his life.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 那天夜里，鲁斯塔姆睡在泉水边，叮嘱拉赫什：不要再自己去和野兽打斗，有危险就叫醒我。半夜，一条巨大的恶龙从洞里爬了出来，它长八十腕尺，吐出的气像火一样，连大象都不敢靠近这片草地。拉赫什看见恶龙，连忙跑到鲁斯塔姆身边，用蹄子刨地、嘶叫，把他叫醒。鲁斯塔姆醒来四处张望，恶龙却用魔法隐去了身形，他什么也没看见，就骂拉赫什打扰他睡觉，又躺下了。恶龙又出现了，拉赫什又把他叫醒，恶龙又不见了，鲁斯塔姆大怒，说：你再这样无缘无故地吵我，我就砍下你的头，自己走到马赞德兰去。恶龙第三次出现，拉赫什不顾一切地又跑来叫醒他。这一次，造物主让鲁斯塔姆看见了恶龙。他拔出剑，和恶龙搏斗起来，恶龙太强大了，几乎要把他压倒。拉赫什冲上去，一口咬住恶龙的肩膀，把它的皮肉撕开，鲁斯塔姆趁机一剑砍下了恶龙的头。他向拉赫什道歉，感谢这匹忠诚的马救了他的命。
body_en: That night Rostam slept by the spring, telling Rakhsh not to fight beasts alone again but to wake him at any danger. At midnight a huge dragon crawled from its den, eighty cubits long, its breath like fire, so fearsome that not even elephants dared enter that meadow. Seeing it, Rakhsh ran to Rostam, pawing the ground and neighing to wake him. Rostam woke and looked around, but the dragon had hidden itself by magic, and he saw nothing; he cursed Rakhsh for disturbing his sleep and lay down again. The dragon came again, Rakhsh woke him again, and again it vanished. Rostam in fury said: 'Wake me again for nothing and I will cut off your head and walk to Māzandarān myself.' The dragon came a third time, and Rakhsh, heedless of the threat, ran again to wake him. This time the Creator let Rostam see the dragon. He drew his sword and fought it, but the dragon was so strong it nearly crushed him. Rakhsh rushed in, bit the dragon's shoulder and tore its flesh, and Rostam struck off its head. He begged Rakhsh's pardon and thanked the faithful horse for saving his life.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 第四天，鲁斯塔姆穿过一片美丽的山谷，来到一眼泉水边，只见树荫下铺着华丽的毯子，摆满了烤好的羊肉、面包、水果和一瓶美酒，旁边还放着一把琴。原来这是女巫们设下的筵席。鲁斯塔姆饿了，坐下来大吃大喝，拿起琴弹了起来，唱道：我鲁斯塔姆是个漂泊的人，一生没有安宁的日子，每天不是和狮子打，就是和恶龙斗，很少能见到这样的筵席和美丽的花园。歌声传开，一个女巫听见了，把自己变成一个美丽的少女，脸颊像春天的花朵，走到他的身边坐下。鲁斯塔姆很高兴，倒了一杯酒递给她，并说出了造物主的名字，感谢神赐给他美酒和佳人。可是女巫一听见神的名字，脸色就变了，她的美貌消失了，变回了一个又老又丑的黑脸巫婆。鲁斯塔姆看穿了她，抛出套索套住她的脖子，拔剑把她砍成了两半。
body_en: On the fourth day Rostam crossed a lovely valley to a spring, where beneath the trees rich carpets were spread with roast lamb, bread, fruit and a flask of wine, and a lute lay beside them. It was a feast laid by witches. Hungry, Rostam sat down, ate and drank, took up the lute and sang: 'I, Rostam, am a wanderer who never knows a day of rest; every day I fight lions or dragons, and seldom do I find such a feast and so fair a garden.' A witch heard the song, changed herself into a beautiful girl with cheeks like spring flowers, and came and sat beside him. Pleased, Rostam poured a cup of wine and gave it to her, naming the Creator and thanking God for the wine and the fair companion. But at the name of God the witch's face changed; her beauty vanished and she became again a black-faced, wrinkled old hag. Seeing through her, Rostam cast his lasso around her neck and cut her in two with his sword.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 第五天，鲁斯塔姆走进了一片没有日月、伸手不见五指的黑暗之地，他让拉赫什自己找路，走了很久，终于重见光明，来到一片绿油油的田野。他又累又困，就脱下被汗浸透的战袍，让拉赫什在田里吃庄稼，自己躺下睡着了。看守田地的人跑来，用棍子打他的脚，骂他放马糟蹋庄稼。鲁斯塔姆醒来，一言不发，抓住那人，一把拧下了他的两只耳朵。看田人捂着头跑去向当地的领主乌拉德哭诉。乌拉德带着一群武士赶来，要惩罚这个陌生人。鲁斯塔姆骑上拉赫什迎战，把乌拉德的武士杀得四散奔逃，又抛出套索，活捉了乌拉德。鲁斯塔姆对他说：如果你给我带路，带我找到白魔的洞穴和国王被关押的地方，等我打败了马赞德兰，我就让你做这片土地的国王；如果你骗我，我就要你的命。乌拉德答应了，从此做了鲁斯塔姆的向导。
body_en: On the fifth day Rostam entered a land of darkness without sun or moon, where he could not see his hand before him; he let Rakhsh find the way, and after a long time came out into the light, to green fields. Weary and sleepy, he took off his sweat-soaked war-coat, let Rakhsh graze in the crops and lay down to sleep. The keeper of the fields came running, struck his feet with a stick and cursed him for letting his horse spoil the crops. Rostam woke, said nothing, seized the man and wrenched off both his ears. Holding his head, the keeper ran to complain to the local lord, Olād. Olād came with a band of warriors to punish the stranger. Rostam rode out on Rakhsh, scattered Olād's men, and caught Olād alive with his lasso. 'If you guide me to the White Demon's cave and to where the king is held,' said Rostam, 'when I have conquered Māzandarān I will make you king of this land; if you deceive me, your life is forfeit.' Olād agreed, and became Rostam's guide.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 乌拉德带着鲁斯塔姆向前走，告诉他：前面是魔鬼阿尔章的营地，他是马赞德兰魔鬼军队的首领之一，守着通往国王监牢的道路；过了那里，再往前是七座大山，白魔就住在山中的一个洞穴里，他身边有成千上万的魔鬼守卫。鲁斯塔姆把乌拉德绑在一棵树上，等到天亮，独自骑着拉赫什冲进了阿尔章的营地，发出一声雷鸣般的怒吼，震得魔鬼们心惊胆战。阿尔章听见吼声，从帐篷里冲出来迎战。鲁斯塔姆策马上前，伸手抓住阿尔章的头和耳朵，把他的头从身子上拧了下来，扔到魔鬼们中间。魔鬼们看见首领的头滚落在地，吓得魂飞魄散，四散逃命，许多魔鬼在逃跑中自相践踏而死。鲁斯塔姆杀散了阿尔章的军队，回到乌拉德身边，给他松了绑，让他继续带路，去找被关押的国王。
body_en: Olād led Rostam on and told him: 'Ahead is the camp of the demon Arzhang, one of the chiefs of the demon host of Māzandarān, who guards the road to the king's prison; beyond it lie seven great mountains, and in a cave among them lives the White Demon with thousands of demons on guard.' Rostam tied Olād to a tree, waited for dawn, then rode alone on Rakhsh into Arzhang's camp with a roar like thunder that shook the demons' hearts. Hearing it, Arzhang rushed out of his tent to fight. Rostam spurred forward, seized Arzhang by the head and ears, wrenched his head from his body and flung it among the demons. Seeing their chief's head roll on the ground, the demons fled in terror, many trampling one another to death as they ran. Having scattered Arzhang's host, Rostam went back to Olād, untied him, and bade him lead on to the imprisoned king.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 鲁斯塔姆找到了被关押的凯·卡乌斯和伊朗的勇士们，他们都瞎了眼睛，在黑暗中受苦。国王听见鲁斯塔姆的声音，悲喜交加，对他说：只有白魔心脏里的血滴进我们的眼睛，我们才能重见光明。鲁斯塔姆就让乌拉德带他去白魔的住处。他们越过七座大山，来到一个深不见底的洞穴前，洞口有许多魔鬼守卫。乌拉德说：等太阳升到最高、天气最热的时候再进去，那时魔鬼们都会睡觉。鲁斯塔姆等到正午，冲向洞口，杀死了守卫的魔鬼，走进了漆黑的洞中。洞里黑得像地狱一样，他擦了擦眼睛，才看见一个巨大的身影躺在那里，像一座山，脸是黑的，头发是白的，那就是白魔。鲁斯塔姆没有趁他睡着下手，大吼一声把他叫醒。白魔跳起来，拿起一块磨盘大的石头冲了过来。两人在洞中殊死搏斗，鲁斯塔姆一剑砍断了白魔的一条腿，白魔仍用一条腿扑上来和他扭打，鲜血和汗水流满了洞穴。最后，鲁斯塔姆把白魔举起来摔在地上，用匕首刺进他的胸膛，挖出了他的肝。
body_en: Rostam found Kay Kāvus and the champions of Iran in their prison, all blind and suffering in darkness. Hearing Rostam's voice, the king wept with joy and said: 'Only blood from the White Demon's heart dropped in our eyes can restore our sight.' So Rostam had Olād guide him to the White Demon's lair. They crossed the seven mountains to the mouth of a bottomless cave guarded by many demons. Olād said: 'Wait until the sun is highest and the heat greatest; then the demons sleep.' At noon Rostam rushed the entrance, killed the guards and went into the black cave. It was dark as hell; he rubbed his eyes and at last saw a huge form lying there like a mountain, its face black and its hair white: the White Demon. Rostam would not strike him sleeping, but woke him with a great shout. The White Demon sprang up, seized a stone like a millstone and charged. They fought for their lives in the cave; Rostam cut off one of the demon's legs, yet still it grappled him on one leg, and blood and sweat ran through the cave. At last Rostam lifted the White Demon, dashed him to the ground, plunged his dagger into his breast, and tore out his liver.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“进军马赞德兰”一节。

body_zh: 有一天，鲁斯塔姆心中烦闷，就带上弓箭和套索，骑着拉赫什到伊朗与图兰交界的地方去打猎。他在一片原野上射死了一头野驴，用树枝生起火来，烤了野驴，吃饱以后，摘下拉赫什的辔头让它去吃草，自己躺在草地上睡着了。这时，一群图兰的骑手路过，看见这匹骏马在原野上独自吃草，就抛出套索把它套住，牵回城里去了。鲁斯塔姆醒来，四处寻找，不见拉赫什的踪影，心中又急又恼：没有了拉赫什，他穿着沉重的铠甲，带着铁杵，只能徒步行走，图兰人会怎样嘲笑他？他顺着马蹄印一路追去，一直追到了萨曼甘国的城门口。萨曼甘的国王和贵族们听说鲁斯塔姆来了，都出城迎接，国王对他说：英雄啊，在我的国土上，没有人敢伤害你，你的马一定能找回来，今晚请到我的宫中做客吧。
body_en: One day, restless in heart, Rostam took his bow and lasso and rode Rakhsh to hunt on the border between Iran and Tūrān. On a plain he shot a wild ass, kindled a fire of branches, roasted it and ate his fill, then took off Rakhsh's bridle to let him graze and lay down on the grass to sleep. A band of Turanian riders passed, saw the splendid horse grazing alone, cast their lassos over him and led him off to their city. Rostam woke and searched everywhere, but there was no trace of Rakhsh. He was anxious and vexed: without Rakhsh he must walk in his heavy armour carrying his mace — how the Turanians would mock him! He followed the hoofprints all the way to the gate of the city of Samangān. When the king and nobles of Samangān heard that Rostam had come they rode out to meet him, and the king said: 'Hero, no one in my land would dare to harm you; your horse will surely be found. Be my guest in the palace tonight.'
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

heading_en: The ruse of the second day
body_zh: 第二天，苏赫拉布一见到鲁斯塔姆，就笑着迎上去说：昨夜你睡得好吗？我们为什么要打仗呢？我心里对你有说不出的亲近，我们放下武器，坐下来一起喝酒吧。告诉我，你真的不是鲁斯塔姆吗？鲁斯塔姆说：我们昨天约好了要摔跤，不要再说这些话了。两人下马摔跤，从早晨一直扭打到中午，苏赫拉布像一头狮子扑向猎物一样，把鲁斯塔姆摔倒在地，骑在他的胸口上，拔出匕首就要砍下他的头。鲁斯塔姆急中生智，说：年轻人，在我们伊朗有一个规矩：两个勇士摔跤，第一次把对手摔倒的人不能杀他，要第二次摔倒对手才能取他的性命。苏赫拉布年轻而骄傲，相信了这番话，就放开了他。回到营中，胡曼听说了这件事，责备苏赫拉布说：你放走了一头已经落进网里的狮子，你会为此后悔的。苏赫拉布却不以为意。
body_en: On the second day, as soon as Sohrāb saw Rostam he came to meet him smiling: 'Did you sleep well? Why should we fight? My heart feels a kinship with you I cannot explain; let us lay down our arms and sit and drink together. Tell me — are you truly not Rostam?' Rostam said: 'We agreed yesterday to wrestle; say no more of this.' They dismounted and wrestled from morning till noon, and Sohrāb, like a lion falling on its prey, threw Rostam to the ground, sat on his chest and drew his dagger to cut off his head. Quick-witted in his peril, Rostam said: 'Young man, among us in Iran there is a custom: when two champions wrestle, the one who first throws his foe may not kill him; only when he throws him a second time may he take his life.' Young and proud, Sohrāb believed it and let him go. Back in camp Hūmān heard of it and rebuked him: 'You have let go a lion already in the net; you will regret it.' But Sohrāb thought little of it.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 鲁斯塔姆脱身以后，来到一条溪边，洗净了身体，跪在地上向造物主祈祷。据说他年轻的时候力气大得惊人，走在岩石上，双脚都会陷进石头里，他曾经请求神收回一部分力量，好让他能像常人一样行走。现在，他祈求神把那份力量还给他。神应允了他的祈祷。第三天，两人又在战场上相遇，又一次摔起跤来。这一次，鲁斯塔姆恢复了全部的力量，他抓住苏赫拉布的头和腰，像拔起一棵树一样把他举起来，重重地摔在地上。他知道这个年轻人不会被压在地上太久，就迅速拔出匕首，刺进了苏赫拉布的胸膛。苏赫拉布在血泊中翻过身来，叹息着说：这是我自作自受，命运把我的钥匙交到了你的手里。可是你要知道，无论你逃到哪里，就算你变成水里的鱼、天上的星，我的父亲也会找到你，为我报仇。我的父亲就是鲁斯塔姆。我来这里，只是为了找他。
body_en: Having escaped, Rostam went to a stream, washed himself, knelt and prayed to the Creator. It is told that in his youth his strength had been so great that when he walked on rock his feet sank into the stone, and he had asked God to take back part of it so that he could walk like other men. Now he prayed God to give that strength back, and God granted his prayer. On the third day they met again and wrestled once more. This time, with all his strength restored, Rostam seized Sohrāb by the head and waist, lifted him like an uprooted tree and dashed him to the ground. Knowing the young man would not stay down long, he drew his dagger and drove it into Sohrāb's breast. Sohrāb turned over in his blood and sighed: 'I have brought this on myself; fate gave the key of my life into your hand. But know this: wherever you flee, though you become a fish in the sea or a star in the sky, my father will find you and avenge me. My father is Rostam. I came here only to find him.'
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 鲁斯塔姆听见这句话，眼前一黑，昏倒在地。醒来后，他颤抖着问：你有什么能证明你是鲁斯塔姆的儿子？我就是鲁斯塔姆！苏赫拉布说：解开我的铠甲，看看我的手臂。鲁斯塔姆解开铠甲，看见了那枚自己当年留给塔米娜的臂环。他撕扯着自己的衣服和头发，痛哭失声，说：我亲手杀死了我的儿子。苏赫拉布说：哭也没有用了，这是命中注定的。鲁斯塔姆派古达尔兹去见凯·卡乌斯，请求国王赐给他宫中珍藏的长生药，能治好一切创伤。凯·卡乌斯却心想：如果这个年轻人活下来，父子二人联手，我的王位还能保得住吗？他迟迟不肯给药。鲁斯塔姆决定亲自去求，还没有走到国王那里，就有人追上来报告：苏赫拉布已经死了。鲁斯塔姆悲痛欲绝，想用匕首自尽，被众人拦住。他烧掉了自己的帐篷和宝座，用金色的锦缎包裹儿子的遗体，带回扎布尔斯坦安葬。消息传到萨曼甘，塔米娜撕碎了衣裳，日夜痛哭，抱着儿子的战袍和骏马，不到一年，就随着儿子离开了人世。
body_en: At these words the world went dark before Rostam's eyes and he fell senseless. When he came to, he asked trembling: 'What token have you that you are Rostam's son? I am Rostam!' Sohrāb said: 'Undo my armour and look at my arm.' Rostam undid the armour and saw the armlet he had once left with Tahmineh. He tore his clothes and his hair and cried aloud: 'I have killed my own son with my own hand.' Sohrāb said: 'Weeping is useless now; this was fated.' Rostam sent Gūdarz to Kay Kāvus to beg the elixir kept in the king's treasury that heals every wound. But Kay Kāvus thought: if this young man lives and father and son join together, will my throne be safe? and he delayed. Rostam resolved to go and beg it himself, but before he reached the king a messenger overtook him: Sohrāb was dead. In his grief Rostam would have killed himself with his dagger, but the others held him back. He burned his tent and his throne, wrapped his son's body in golden brocade and carried it home to Zābulistān for burial. When the news reached Samangān, Tahmineh tore her clothes and wept day and night, clasping her son's armour and his horse, and within a year she followed her son out of the world.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 萨曼甘的国王为鲁斯塔姆举行了盛大的宴会，鲁斯塔姆喝了酒，被领到一间铺着锦缎的卧室里休息。夜深了，房门忽然悄悄打开，一个侍女提着一支点燃的蜡烛走进来，身后跟着一位美丽的少女，她的脸像月亮，身段像柏树，眉毛像弯弓，头发像黑色的套索。鲁斯塔姆惊奇地问她是谁，深夜来做什么。少女说：我是萨曼甘国王的女儿，名叫塔米娜，在这片土地上没有人见过我的面容。我听过许多关于你的故事：你怎样不怕狮子、恶龙和魔鬼，你的铁杵怎样让大地颤抖。我早就倾心于你，暗暗发誓除了你谁也不嫁。如今神把你送到了我们的城里，我来是要告诉你：如果你愿意，我想做你的妻子，为你生一个像你一样勇敢的儿子。而且，我会让人把你的拉赫什找回来。鲁斯塔姆见她既美丽又聪慧，心中欢喜，第二天就请一位智慧的祭司向国王求婚。国王非常高兴，当即按照礼仪把女儿嫁给了他。
body_en: The king of Samangān held a great feast for Rostam, and when he had drunk he was led to a chamber hung with brocade to rest. Deep in the night the door opened softly; a slave-girl came in carrying a lighted candle, and behind her a beautiful maiden, her face like the moon, her figure like a cypress, her brows like bows and her hair like a dark lasso. Astonished, Rostam asked who she was and why she came at night. 'I am the daughter of the king of Samangān,' she said; 'my name is Tahmineh, and no one in this land has seen my face. I have heard many tales of you — how you fear neither lion nor dragon nor demon, how the earth trembles at your mace. I have long given you my heart and secretly vowed to marry no one but you. Now God has brought you to our city, and I have come to tell you: if you will, I wish to be your wife and bear you a son as brave as you. And I will have your Rakhsh found.' Seeing her as wise as she was beautiful, Rostam was glad, and the next day he sent a wise priest to ask the king for her hand. The king rejoiced and gave him his daughter by the proper rites.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 婚后不久，人们找回了拉赫什，鲁斯塔姆必须回到伊朗去了。临别时，他从自己的手臂上解下一枚臂环——上面镶着一颗宝石，是一件人人都认得的珍宝——交给塔米娜，说：好好保管它。如果神赐给你一个女儿，就把它编进她的头发里，愿它保佑她平安；如果你生了一个儿子，就把它系在他的手臂上，让他像我一样成为勇敢的人，让他凭着这件信物来找我。说完，他拥抱了塔米娜，跨上拉赫什，向伊朗的方向驰去，从此再也没有回到萨曼甘。九个月以后，塔米娜生下了一个儿子，他的脸像月亮一样明亮，笑起来像花一样灿烂，人们说他长得和鲁斯塔姆、和祖父萨姆一模一样。塔米娜给他取名为苏赫拉布，把那枚臂环系在了他的手臂上。
body_en: Soon after the marriage Rakhsh was found, and Rostam had to return to Iran. At parting he took from his arm an armlet set with a jewel, a treasure known to all, and gave it to Tahmineh: 'Keep this well. If God gives you a daughter, braid it into her hair and may it keep her safe; if you bear a son, bind it on his arm, that he may become brave as I am, and by this token let him come to find me.' He embraced Tahmineh, mounted Rakhsh and rode off towards Iran, and never came back to Samangān. Nine months later Tahmineh bore a son with a face bright as the moon and a smile like a flower, and people said he was the very image of Rostam and of his grandfather Sām. Tahmineh named him Sohrāb and bound the armlet on his arm.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 苏赫拉布长得出奇地快：一个月大时就像一岁的孩子，三岁时就学会了骑马射箭，五岁时有了狮子般的勇气，到了十岁，萨曼甘没有一个人能和他比武。他胸膛宽阔，手臂粗壮，跑起来像风一样快。有一天，他来到母亲面前，问她：我为什么比别的孩子都高大强壮？我的父亲是谁？别人问起我的家世，我该怎样回答？塔米娜说：孩子，不要生气，你的父亲就是伟大的鲁斯塔姆，扎尔的儿子，萨姆的孙子，世上没有比他更勇敢的英雄。她拿出鲁斯塔姆寄来的信和三颗宝石给他看，又叮嘱他：千万不要让图兰王阿夫拉西亚布知道这件事，他是鲁斯塔姆的仇敌，会想办法害你；也不要让你父亲知道你已经长成了一个勇士，否则他会把你从我身边叫走。苏赫拉布听了，热血沸腾，说：我要率领大军进攻伊朗，推翻凯·卡乌斯，让我的父亲鲁斯塔姆坐上王位；然后再去打败阿夫拉西亚布，让天下不再有两个国王。
body_en: Sohrāb grew astonishingly fast: at one month he was like a child of a year, at three he rode and shot, at five he had a lion's courage, and at ten no one in Samangān could match him in arms. Broad-chested and strong-armed, he ran swift as the wind. One day he came to his mother and asked: 'Why am I taller and stronger than other children? Who is my father? What shall I say when people ask about my birth?' Tahmineh said: 'Do not be angry, child. Your father is the great Rostam, son of Zāl, grandson of Sām; there is no braver hero in the world.' She showed him a letter Rostam had sent and three jewels, and warned him: 'Never let Afrāsiyāb, king of Tūrān, know this; he is Rostam's enemy and would seek to harm you. Nor let your father know you have grown into a warrior, or he will call you away from me.' Sohrāb's blood was fired: 'I will lead an army against Iran, overthrow Kay Kāvus and set my father Rostam on the throne; then I will defeat Afrāsiyāb, so that the world has no longer two kings.'
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 苏赫拉布为自己挑选了一匹配得上他的骏马，召集了一支军队。消息传到图兰王阿夫拉西亚布那里，他心中暗喜，想出了一个阴险的计策。他派出两位将领胡曼和巴尔曼，带着一万二千名精兵和许多礼物去投奔苏赫拉布，表面上是支持他攻打伊朗。他在私下里对两位将领说：这件事一定要保守秘密，千万不能让父子二人相认。如果苏赫拉布在战场上遇见鲁斯塔姆，就要想办法让他们彼此不知道对方是谁。也许这个年轻的勇士会杀死鲁斯塔姆，那样伊朗就失去了最强的支柱；也许鲁斯塔姆会杀死这个孩子，那样鲁斯塔姆的心也会被悲伤压垮。不论哪一种，对我们图兰都有好处。胡曼和巴尔曼领了命令，带着礼物和阿夫拉西亚布的书信来到萨曼甘，苏赫拉布高兴地接待了他们，一点也不知道这背后的阴谋。
body_en: Sohrāb chose himself a horse worthy of him and gathered an army. When the news reached Afrāsiyāb, king of Tūrān, he secretly rejoiced and devised a wicked plan. He sent two generals, Hūmān and Bārmān, with twelve thousand picked men and many gifts to join Sohrāb, as though to support his attack on Iran. In private he told the two: 'Keep this secret: father and son must never know each other. If Sohrāb meets Rostam in battle, contrive that neither knows who the other is. Perhaps the young warrior will kill Rostam, and Iran will lose its strongest pillar; perhaps Rostam will kill the boy, and grief will break Rostam's heart. Either way Tūrān gains.' Hūmān and Bārmān took their orders and came to Samangān with gifts and a letter from Afrāsiyāb, and Sohrāb welcomed them gladly, knowing nothing of the plot behind them.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

heading_en: The warrior maiden of the White Castle
body_zh: 苏赫拉布率领大军进入伊朗，来到边境上的白堡。守城的勇士哈吉尔出城迎战，几个回合就被苏赫拉布打下马来，成了俘虏。城中的人们惊慌失措。这时，城里有一位名叫戈尔达法丽德的少女，她是守将的女儿，勇敢而精通武艺。她把头发藏进头盔里，穿上铠甲，骑马出城，向苏赫拉布挑战。两人交战，她射出的箭像雨点一样密集，苏赫拉布用盾牌挡住，冲上前去，用长矛挑落了她的头盔，她的长发一下子披散下来，苏赫拉布这才发现对手是一个少女，心中又惊又爱。戈尔达法丽德见势不妙，就对他说：你若在两军面前和一个女子交战，会被人笑话的。不如我们讲和，城堡和城里的一切都归你，我在城中等你。苏赫拉布相信了她，跟到城门前，她却一闪身进了城，关上城门，在城墙上笑着对他说：图兰的勇士啊，你还是回去吧，等鲁斯塔姆来了，你就没有好日子过了。当天夜里，城里的人们从一条秘密的地道逃走了，第二天苏赫拉布攻进城时，城中已经空无一人。
body_en: Sohrāb led his army into Iran and came to the White Castle on the border. Its champion Hajīr rode out against him and was unhorsed and taken prisoner within a few passes. The people in the castle were in dismay. Among them was a maiden named Gordāfarid, daughter of the commander, brave and skilled in arms. She hid her hair in a helmet, put on armour, rode out and challenged Sohrāb. They fought; her arrows fell thick as rain, but Sohrāb took them on his shield, charged, and with his spear knocked off her helmet, and her long hair tumbled down. Only then did he see his foe was a maiden, and he was astonished and drawn to her. Seeing her peril, Gordāfarid said: 'You will be mocked if you fight a woman before both armies. Let us make peace: the castle and all in it are yours, and I will wait for you within.' Sohrāb believed her and followed her to the gate, but she slipped inside, shut the gate, and laughed at him from the walls: 'Warrior of Tūrān, go home; when Rostam comes, your good days are over.' That night the people of the castle escaped by a secret passage, and when Sohrāb stormed it the next day it was empty.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 白堡失守的消息传到凯·卡乌斯那里，国王惊恐万分，立刻写信给鲁斯塔姆，派勇士吉夫日夜兼程送到扎布尔斯坦，请他火速前来抵挡这个年轻的敌人。鲁斯塔姆读了信，听说图兰来了一个年轻的勇士，心中奇怪：图兰怎么会有这样的英雄？我只在萨曼甘有过一个孩子，可他还小，不可能是他。他并不着急，留吉夫在家中饮酒作乐，一连几天才出发。等他们来到凯·卡乌斯的宫廷，国王勃然大怒，骂鲁斯塔姆藐视王命，下令把他和吉夫一起吊死。鲁斯塔姆怒不可遏，说：我是伊朗的守护者，不是你的奴隶！你这次自己去对付那个年轻人吧。他骑上拉赫什扬长而去。众位勇士都慌了，年老的古达尔兹赶去追他，劝他说：人们会说鲁斯塔姆是怕了那个年轻人才走的。鲁斯塔姆听了，不愿背上胆怯的名声，就回到了宫中，凯·卡乌斯也向他道了歉。
body_en: When news of the White Castle's fall reached Kay Kāvus, the king was terrified and at once wrote to Rostam, sending the champion Gīv riding day and night to Zābulistān to beg him to come with all speed against the young enemy. Reading the letter and hearing of a young champion from Tūrān, Rostam wondered: 'How could Tūrān have such a hero? I had only one child, in Samangān, and he is still small; it cannot be he.' He was in no hurry, kept Gīv feasting at his house for several days, and only then set out. When they reached the court, Kay Kāvus flew into a rage, accused Rostam of scorning the royal command, and ordered him and Gīv hanged. Rostam was furious: 'I am the guardian of Iran, not your slave! Deal with the young man yourself this time.' He mounted Rakhsh and rode off. The champions were dismayed; old Gūdarz rode after him and said: 'People will say Rostam left because he feared the young man.' Unwilling to bear the name of coward, Rostam returned to court, and Kay Kāvus begged his pardon.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 伊朗大军来到白堡前，与图兰军队隔着平原对阵。夜里，鲁斯塔姆换上图兰人的衣服，悄悄潜入敌营，想亲眼看看这个年轻的勇士。他看见苏赫拉布坐在宴席的主位上，身材高大，像一棵挺拔的柏树，相貌英武，鲁斯塔姆心中暗暗称奇。坐在苏赫拉布身边的，是塔米娜的兄弟赞德·拉兹姆，塔米娜派他随军，就是为了在战场上把鲁斯塔姆指认给苏赫拉布。赞德·拉兹姆出帐时，在暗处撞见了陌生的鲁斯塔姆，喝问他是谁，鲁斯塔姆一拳打在他的头上，把他打死了。唯一认得鲁斯塔姆的人，就这样死去了。第二天早晨，苏赫拉布登上高处，让俘虏哈吉尔把伊朗军中每一位勇士的帐篷指给他看，他特别问到一座绿色的大帐篷，帐前竖着一面绘着龙的旗帜，旁边拴着一匹高大的骏马。哈吉尔心想：如果说出这是鲁斯塔姆，这个年轻人一定会去找他决斗，也许会把他杀死。于是他撒谎说：那是一位从中国来的盟友，鲁斯塔姆不在军中，他在扎布尔斯坦过节。
body_en: The Iranian army came before the White Castle and faced the Turanians across the plain. At night Rostam put on Turanian clothes and stole into the enemy camp to see the young champion for himself. He saw Sohrāb seated at the head of the feast, tall and straight as a cypress, noble of face, and marvelled in his heart. Beside Sohrāb sat Zende-razm, Tahmineh's brother, whom she had sent with the army to point out Rostam to Sohrāb on the field. As Zende-razm left the tent he met the stranger in the dark and challenged him; Rostam struck him on the head with his fist and killed him. So the one man who knew Rostam by sight was dead. In the morning Sohrāb climbed a height and had the captive Hajīr point out the tent of each Iranian champion; he asked especially about a great green tent with a banner painted with a dragon before it and a tall horse tethered beside it. Hajīr thought: if I say this is Rostam's, the young man will seek him out and may kill him. So he lied: 'That is an ally from China; Rostam is not with the army; he is in Zābulistān for a festival.'
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 苏赫拉布骑马冲到伊朗军前，大声挑战，又冲进营中，砍倒了凯·卡乌斯帐前的旗帜，伊朗的勇士们没有一个敢出来应战。凯·卡乌斯只好请鲁斯塔姆出战。鲁斯塔姆穿上虎皮战袍，骑着拉赫什来到两军之间。他看着眼前这个年轻人，心中涌起一种说不出的感情，对他说：年轻人，你还这样年轻，何必来送死？我见过许多战场，打败过无数魔鬼和勇士，我可怜你，不忍心杀你。苏赫拉布望着这位老英雄，心中也忽然生出一种奇怪的亲切感，问道：请你告诉我实话，你是不是鲁斯塔姆，扎尔的儿子？鲁斯塔姆为了不让对方知道自己的身份，回答说：我不是鲁斯塔姆，我只是他的一个手下，他是一位大英雄，而我连马厩都没有。苏赫拉布失望极了。两人用长矛、刀剑和铁杵交战，长矛断了，刀剑卷了刃，铁杵弯了，两人都汗流浃背，筋疲力尽，直到黄昏也分不出胜负，只好约定第二天再战。
body_en: Sohrāb rode up before the Iranian host and shouted his challenge, then charged into the camp and cut down the banner before Kay Kāvus's tent, and not one Iranian champion dared come out. Kay Kāvus had to ask Rostam to fight. Rostam put on his tiger-skin coat and rode Rakhsh out between the armies. Looking at the young man, he felt a stirring he could not name, and said: 'Young man, you are still so young; why come to your death? I have seen many battlefields and overcome countless demons and champions; I pity you and would not kill you.' Gazing at the old hero, Sohrāb too felt a strange kinship and asked: 'Tell me truly, are you Rostam, son of Zāl?' To keep his name hidden, Rostam answered: 'I am not Rostam, only one of his men; he is a great hero, and I have not even a stable of my own.' Sohrāb's hope fell. They fought with spears, swords and maces until the spears broke, the swords were notched and the maces bent; both ran with sweat and were spent, and when evening came neither had won, and they agreed to fight again the next day.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆与苏赫拉布”一节。

body_zh: 在马努切赫尔国王统治伊朗的时候，扎布尔斯坦的领主萨姆是国王最英勇的勇士，他什么都不缺，只盼望有一个儿子。终于，他的妻子生下了一个男孩，孩子的脸像月亮一样美丽，身体健壮，可是满头的头发却像老人一样雪白。侍女们不敢告诉萨姆，过了好几天，才有一个侍女鼓起勇气去报喜。萨姆来看孩子，见他一头白发，心中又羞又怕，说：人们看见这个孩子，会说什么呢？他们会说这是魔鬼的孩子，会嘲笑我生了一个怪物。我怎么能把这样的儿子带到勇士们面前？他转过脸去，命令仆人把孩子抱走，丢到远离人烟的厄尔布尔士山上，让野兽去处置他。仆人们照办了，把这个刚出生的婴儿放在了荒凉的山顶上，任凭风吹日晒。《列王纪》是诗人菲尔多西在公元一千年前后写成的长篇史诗，讲述伊朗历代国王与英雄的事迹；萨姆、扎尔、鲁斯塔姆祖孙三代，是其中最有名的英雄家族，而这个家族的故事，就从一次抛弃开始。
body_en: When King Manūchehr ruled Iran, Sām, lord of Zābulistān, was the bravest of his champions; he lacked nothing except a son. At last his wife bore a boy, his face fair as the moon and his body strong, but his hair as white as an old man's. The women dared not tell Sām, and it was days before one of them found the courage to bring him the news. Sām came to see the child, and at the sight of the white hair he was filled with shame and fear. 'What will people say when they see this child? They will say he is a demon's child and mock me for fathering a monster. How can I bring such a son before the warriors?' He turned away and commanded his servants to carry the child off and leave him on Mount Alborz, far from all human dwellings, for the beasts to deal with. The servants obeyed and left the newborn on the bare summit, exposed to wind and sun. The Shahnameh, the Book of Kings, is the long epic the poet Ferdowsi completed around the year 1000, telling of the kings and heroes of Iran; Sām, Zāl and Rostam, grandfather, father and son, are its most famous family of heroes — and their story begins with an abandonment.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔”一节。

body_zh: 扎尔带着国王的许可，日夜兼程回到扎布尔斯坦，又赶往喀布尔。喀布尔城里张灯结彩，到处是音乐和欢笑，街道上撒满了麝香和玫瑰水，大象背上驮着鼓手，人们用金银和珠宝迎接新郎。萨姆也来了，辛多赫特领着他去看鲁达贝。萨姆一见这位美丽的儿媳，就满心欢喜，赞叹不已。扎尔和鲁达贝按照古老的礼仪结为夫妻，坐在同一张宝座上，接受众人的祝福。婚礼的庆典一连举行了许多天。之后，扎尔带着新娘回到扎布尔斯坦，萨姆把领地交给儿子治理，自己又出征去了。曾经被父亲抛弃在山上的白发婴儿，如今有了自己的家，也有了一位为他放下长发的妻子。星象家们预言的那位英雄，很快就要降生了。两家都拿出了最贵重的礼物，庆祝这桩来之不易的婚事；伊朗和喀布尔之间的战事，也因为这场婚礼而平息了。
body_en: With the king's consent Zāl rode day and night back to Zābulistān and on to Kābul. The city was hung with lamps and garlands and filled with music and laughter; the streets were strewn with musk and rosewater, drummers rode on elephants, and the people welcomed the bridegroom with gold, silver and jewels. Sām came too, and Sindokht led him to see Rūdābeh; at the sight of his lovely daughter-in-law he was filled with joy and admiration. Zāl and Rūdābeh were married by the ancient rites and sat together on one throne to receive the blessings of all. The feasting lasted many days. Then Zāl brought his bride home to Zābulistān, and Sām gave his son the rule of his lands and went off to war again. The white-haired baby once cast away on the mountain now had a home of his own and a wife who had let down her hair for him. The hero the astrologers had foretold would soon be born. Both houses brought out their costliest gifts to celebrate a marriage so hard won, and the threatened war between Iran and Kābul was laid to rest by the wedding.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔与鲁达贝”一节。

heading_en: The hard labour and the Simorgh's feather
body_zh: 不久，鲁达贝怀了孕。她的身体一天天沉重起来，腹中的孩子大得出奇，她日夜疼痛，脸色像枯萎的花一样苍白。到了生产的时候，孩子却怎么也生不下来，鲁达贝昏死过去，宫中一片哭声，人人都以为她要死了。扎尔想起了西摩格的话，取出那根羽毛，点起火来焚烧。天空立刻暗了下来，西摩格从云中飞落，问他为何如此悲伤。扎尔说了妻子的危难。西摩格说：不要哭，你的妻子会生下一个狮子般的儿子。去请一位手法娴熟的祭司来，先让鲁达贝喝下掺了药的酒，让她沉睡，不觉得痛，再剖开她的腹侧，把孩子取出来，然后把伤口缝好，把我给你的药草捣碎了和着牛奶敷上，再用我的羽毛轻轻抚过伤口，她就会痊愈。扎尔照着做了。孩子被取了出来，大得像一个满一岁的孩子。鲁达贝醒来，看见孩子，说：我终于解脱了！在波斯语里，“解脱”这个词的读音就像“鲁斯塔姆”，孩子就这样得了名字。
body_en: Soon Rūdābeh was with child. Her body grew heavier day by day, the child within her was wondrously large, she was in pain day and night, and her face grew pale as a withered flower. When her time came the child would not be born; Rūdābeh fainted, the palace filled with weeping, and all thought she would die. Zāl remembered the Simorgh's words, took out the feather and set it alight. At once the sky darkened and the Simorgh came down from the clouds and asked why he grieved. He told her of his wife's peril. The Simorgh said: 'Do not weep; your wife will bear a lion of a son. Fetch a skilled priest; first let Rūdābeh drink wine mixed with a drug so that she sleeps and feels no pain; then let him open her side and draw out the child, and sew up the wound; crush the herb I give you with milk and lay it on, and stroke the wound with my feather, and she will heal.' Zāl did all this. The child was drawn out, as big as a year-old infant. When Rūdābeh woke and saw him she cried: 'I am delivered!' — and because in Persian the word sounds like Rostam, so the child was named.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆”一节。

body_zh: 鲁斯塔姆长得飞快，十个乳母都喂不饱他，断奶以后，他一个人吃的饭比五个大人还多。他长得像柏树一样高，力气像大象一样大。有一天夜里，鲁斯塔姆正在熟睡，忽然听见外面一片喧哗：国王的一头白象挣脱了锁链，发了疯，在城里横冲直撞，人们四散奔逃。鲁斯塔姆跳起来，抓起祖父萨姆留下的铁杵冲出门去，守门人怕他出事，拦着不让走，他一拳打倒守门人，砸开了门，迎着白象冲上去，一杵就把白象打倒在地。后来，鲁斯塔姆要为自己挑一匹马。人们把扎布尔和喀布尔的马群赶到他面前，他用手按在马背上，马就压得弯下腰来，没有一匹承受得住。最后，他看见一匹母马身后跟着一匹小马，毛色像玫瑰花瓣点缀在藏红花上，四肢有力，胸膛宽阔。牧马人说：这匹马叫拉赫什，许多人想要它，可谁也不敢碰它，它的母马会像狮子一样冲上来保护它。鲁斯塔姆抛出套索套住了小马，母马冲过来，被他一声大喝吓退。鲁斯塔姆问牧马人这匹马的价钱，牧马人说：如果你是鲁斯塔姆，就骑上它去保卫伊朗吧，它的价钱就是整个伊朗。从此，鲁斯塔姆和拉赫什再也没有分开过。
body_en: Rostam grew so fast that ten nurses could not satisfy him, and once weaned he ate more than five grown men. He grew tall as a cypress and strong as an elephant. One night as he slept he heard an uproar outside: the king's white elephant had broken its chains and run mad through the city, and people were fleeing. Rostam leapt up, seized the iron mace his grandfather Sām had left, and ran to the door; the gatekeepers, fearing for him, tried to stop him, but he knocked them down, broke the door open, charged the elephant and felled it with a single blow. Later Rostam wanted a horse of his own. The herds of Zābul and Kābul were driven before him, but when he pressed his hand on a horse's back it sank down under him; none could bear his weight. At last he saw a colt following a mare, its coat like rose-petals scattered on saffron, its legs strong and its chest broad. The herdsman said: 'This is Rakhsh. Many have wanted him, but no one dares touch him; his mother rushes to defend him like a lion.' Rostam cast his lasso over the colt; the mare charged, and he drove her back with a great shout. When he asked the price, the herdsman said: 'If you are Rostam, ride him and defend Iran; his price is the land of Iran.' From then on Rostam and Rakhsh were never parted.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“鲁斯塔姆”一节。

body_zh: 厄尔布尔士山的高处，住着一只神鸟，名叫西摩格。它的巢筑在山巅，离星星很近，巢里有它嗷嗷待哺的雏鸟。西摩格飞出去为孩子们觅食，看见山坡上躺着一个婴儿，饿得哭泣，正在吮吸自己的手指。它俯冲下来，用爪子抓起婴儿，带回巢中，本想把他喂给雏鸟。可是当它把婴儿放在巢里，看着这个哭泣的孩子时，心中忽然生出了怜悯。它不仅没有伤害他，还把他和自己的孩子们一起抚养，给他最柔软的肉吃。就这样，扎尔在西摩格的巢里一天天长大，长成了一个高大英俊的青年。路过山下的商队常常抬头看见山上有一个人影，在神鸟的巢边走动，消息渐渐传遍了四方，说厄尔布尔士山上有一个由神鸟养大的年轻人。厄尔布尔士山在伊朗北部，是伊朗传说中最高、最神秘的山，西摩格就住在那里，被人们视为一只充满智慧的神鸟。
body_en: High on Mount Alborz lived a great bird called the Simorgh. Her nest was on the summit, close to the stars, and in it were her hungry young. Flying out to find food for them, she saw a baby lying on the slope, crying with hunger and sucking his fingers. She swooped down, caught him up in her claws and carried him to her nest, meaning to feed him to her young. But when she set the baby in the nest and looked at the weeping child, pity stirred in her heart. Far from harming him, she raised him with her own young, giving him the tenderest meat. So Zāl grew up day by day in the Simorgh's nest into a tall and handsome youth. Caravans passing below often looked up and saw a figure moving about beside the great bird's nest, and word spread far and wide that on Mount Alborz there lived a young man raised by the Simorgh. Mount Alborz in the north of Iran is the highest and most mysterious mountain of Iranian legend, and the Simorgh who lives there is held to be a bird of great wisdom.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔”一节。

body_zh: 有一天夜里，萨姆梦见一个骑着阿拉伯骏马的人从印度方向疾驰而来，告诉他：你的儿子还活着。萨姆醒来，把梦告诉了祭司们，问他们这是什么意思。祭司们说：连野兽和飞鸟都会照料自己的幼崽，你却抛弃了自己的儿子，只因为他有白头发。这是不义的，你应当去把他找回来。萨姆心中悔恨。第二天夜里，他又做了一个梦：一个英俊的青年举着旗帜，带着大军向他走来，一位贤者在旁边责备他说：你连自己的孩子都不要，又怎么配做勇士的首领？萨姆从梦中惊醒，再也坐不住了，带着随从赶到厄尔布尔士山下。他抬头望去，看见山顶上神鸟的巢，巢边站着一个青年。可是山峰陡峭，无路可上。萨姆跪在地上，向造物主祈祷，忏悔自己的罪过，求神让他找回儿子。一个曾经因为一头白发抛弃儿子的父亲，如今跪在山下，向造物主请求宽恕。
body_en: One night Sām dreamed that a rider on an Arab horse came galloping from the direction of India and told him: 'Your son is alive.' He woke and told the priests his dream, asking what it meant. They said: 'Even the beasts and birds care for their young, yet you cast off your own son only because his hair was white. It was unjust; you must go and find him.' Sām was filled with remorse. The next night he dreamed again: a handsome youth came towards him with a banner at the head of an army, and a wise man beside him rebuked Sām: 'You would not keep your own child; how are you fit to lead warriors?' Sām woke with a start and could rest no longer; with his followers he hurried to the foot of Mount Alborz. Looking up, he saw the great bird's nest on the summit and a youth standing beside it. But the peak was sheer, with no path to the top. Sām knelt and prayed to the Creator, confessing his sin and begging to be given back his son. A father who had cast off his son for his white hair now knelt at the foot of the mountain and begged the Creator's forgiveness.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔”一节。

heading_en: Zāl returns to the world of men
body_zh: 西摩格看见山下的萨姆，知道他是来找儿子的。它对扎尔说：你的父亲来了，他是世上最伟大的勇士，你该回到他身边去，回到人间去了。扎尔流着泪说：难道你厌倦了我吗？你的巢就是我的家，你就是我的母亲。西摩格说：我并不是要赶你走，我只是想让你得到你应有的荣耀。我给你取名叫“达斯坦”。它从自己的胸前拔下一根羽毛，交给扎尔说：带着这根羽毛，如果有一天你遇到危难，就把它烧掉，我会立刻来到你身边。说完，它用翅膀托着扎尔飞下山峰，把他放在父亲面前。萨姆抱住儿子，哭着请求他原谅。他给儿子取名为扎尔，意思是“白发老人”。父子俩一同回到扎布尔斯坦，后来又到了马努切赫尔国王的宫廷，国王召来星象家为扎尔占卜，星象家说：这个年轻人将成为伊朗最伟大的勇士之一。
body_en: The Simorgh saw Sām below and knew he had come for his son. She said to Zāl: 'Your father has come, the greatest of warriors; you must go back to him and to the world of men.' Zāl wept: 'Are you weary of me? Your nest is my home and you are my mother.' The Simorgh said: 'I do not send you away; I want you to have the glory that is yours. I name you Dastān.' She plucked a feather from her breast and gave it to him: 'Keep this feather. If ever you are in danger, burn it, and I will be with you at once.' Then she bore Zāl down from the peak on her wings and set him before his father. Sām embraced his son and wept, begging his forgiveness, and named him Zāl, meaning the white-haired old one. Father and son returned to Zābulistān and later went to the court of King Manūchehr, who had his astrologers read the youth's stars; they said he would be among the greatest champions of Iran.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔”一节。

body_zh: 萨姆奉国王之命出征，把扎布尔斯坦交给扎尔治理。扎尔四处巡游，来到了喀布尔。喀布尔的国王梅赫拉布出城迎接他，两人一见如故。梅赫拉布是一个英俊而有智慧的国王，可是他的祖先是那个肩上长着两条毒蛇、以人脑为食的暴君佐哈克。扎尔的随从中有人对他说：梅赫拉布有一个女儿，名叫鲁达贝，她比太阳还要美丽，头发像黑色的麝香一样垂到脚踝，身段像柏树一样挺拔。扎尔听了，心中就念念不忘。另一边，梅赫拉布回到宫中，在妻子辛多赫特和女儿面前不住地称赞扎尔，说他英俊、勇敢、谦和，只可惜头发是白的。鲁达贝听了，也悄悄爱上了这个从未见过面的年轻人。她把心事告诉了五个侍女，侍女们先是责备她，说他是被鸟养大的白发人，后来见她心意坚决，就答应帮她。
body_en: Sent by the king to war, Sām left Zābulistān in Zāl's charge. Zāl travelled through the land and came to Kābul. Mehrāb, king of Kābul, rode out to meet him, and the two took to each other at once. Mehrāb was a handsome and wise king, but his ancestor was Zahhāk, the tyrant with two serpents growing from his shoulders who fed them on men's brains. One of Zāl's company told him: 'Mehrāb has a daughter named Rūdābeh, fairer than the sun, her hair dark as musk falling to her ankles, her figure straight as a cypress.' From then on Zāl could think of nothing else. Meanwhile Mehrāb went home and praised Zāl again and again before his wife Sindokht and his daughter — handsome, brave and gentle, if only his hair were not white. Hearing it, Rūdābeh too secretly fell in love with the young man she had never seen. She confided in her five maidens; at first they scolded her — a white-haired man raised by a bird! — but seeing her resolved, they promised to help.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔与鲁达贝”一节。

body_zh: 鲁达贝的侍女们装作去采玫瑰，来到扎尔营地附近的河边。扎尔正好在那里射猎，一箭射下一只水鸟，鸟落在侍女们身边，扎尔的仆人过来拾鸟，侍女们就和他攀谈起来，把公主的美貌和心意都告诉了他。扎尔送给她们许多礼物，约定在夜里与公主相见。到了夜里，扎尔来到鲁达贝的宫殿下面，公主站在高高的塔楼上，月光照在她的脸上。两人隔着塔楼说了许多话。鲁达贝说：英雄啊，你一路走来辛苦了，我把我的头发放下来给你，你抓着它爬上来吧。她解开发辫，把又长又黑的头发从塔上垂了下来。扎尔亲吻着她的头发，说：我怎么能让我心爱的人受这样的痛苦？他取出套索，抛上塔楼的垛口，攀着绳索爬了上去。两人相对而坐，倾诉衷情，彼此立下誓言：除了对方，谁也不嫁、谁也不娶。直到天快亮了，扎尔才依依不舍地离开。
body_en: Rūdābeh's maidens went out as if to gather roses by the river near Zāl's camp. Zāl happened to be hunting there and brought down a water-bird with an arrow; it fell near the maidens, and when his servant came to fetch it they fell into talk with him and told him of the princess's beauty and her heart. Zāl sent them back with many gifts and arranged to meet the princess at night. That night he came beneath Rūdābeh's palace, and she stood on her high tower with the moonlight on her face. They spoke long across the height. Rūdābeh said: 'Hero, you have come far and wearily; I will let down my hair to you; take hold of it and climb up.' She unbound her braids and let her long dark hair fall down from the tower. Zāl kissed her hair and said: 'How could I cause my beloved such pain?' He took his lasso, cast it over the battlements and climbed up by the rope. They sat together and opened their hearts, vowing that neither would marry anyone but the other, and only as dawn drew near did Zāl reluctantly leave.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔与鲁达贝”一节。

heading_en: The opposition of father and king
body_zh: 扎尔召来祭司和贤者，把心事告诉了他们，他们都沉默不语，因为谁都知道梅赫拉布是佐哈克的后裔，伊朗的英雄怎能和暴君的子孙结亲？扎尔就写信给父亲萨姆，提醒他当年抛弃自己的事，请求父亲成全这门婚事。萨姆读了信，心中十分为难：一边是自己亏欠的儿子，一边是暴君的血统。他召来星象家，让他们观察星辰。星象家们算了很久，笑着回来说：萨姆啊，这是一桩吉祥的婚姻，扎尔和鲁达贝会生下一个力大无穷的英雄，他将为伊朗征服世界，扫除一切邪恶。萨姆听了，心中宽慰，答应去向国王求情。可是马努切赫尔国王听说了这件事，非常担心，怕佐哈克的血脉和萨姆的力量结合在一起，将来会危害伊朗。他命令萨姆率军去攻打喀布尔，铲除梅赫拉布一族。佐哈克是《列王纪》里最可怕的暴君，他统治了一千年，最后被英雄法里东推翻，被锁在德马万德山中，所以他的后代总被伊朗人提防。
body_en: Zāl summoned the priests and wise men and told them his heart, but they were silent, for all knew Mehrāb descended from Zahhāk; how could a hero of Iran marry into the tyrant's line? So Zāl wrote to his father, reminding him of how he had once cast him off and begging him to grant this marriage. Reading the letter, Sām was torn between the son he had wronged and the tyrant's blood. He called the astrologers to read the stars. After long reckoning they came back smiling: 'Sām, this is a blessed marriage. Zāl and Rūdābeh will have a son of matchless strength who will conquer the world for Iran and sweep away all evil.' Comforted, Sām promised to plead with the king. But King Manūchehr, hearing of it, was deeply troubled, fearing that Zahhāk's blood joined with Sām's might would one day threaten Iran, and he ordered Sām to march against Kābul and root out Mehrāb's house. Zahhāk is the most terrible tyrant of the Shahnameh, who ruled a thousand years before the hero Fereydūn overthrew him and chained him in Mount Damāvand; so the Iranians always mistrusted his descendants.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔与鲁达贝”一节。

body_zh: 消息传到喀布尔，梅赫拉布才知道女儿的事，他勃然大怒，拔出剑来要杀死鲁达贝，说她给全族带来了灭顶之灾。王后辛多赫特拦住了他，说：不要动手，让我去想办法。辛多赫特是一位聪明而勇敢的女子，她带着无数的礼物——金银、宝石、骏马、大象和奴隶——亲自去见正在进军的萨姆。她没有说出自己是谁，只说是喀布尔王派来的使者。萨姆收下礼物，耐心地听她说话。辛多赫特说：喀布尔的人们有什么罪过，要遭受战火？如果国王有罪，就惩罚国王；百姓是无辜的。最后她才说出自己就是鲁达贝的母亲。萨姆被她的智慧和勇气打动，握住她的手，发誓说：只要我活着，就不会让喀布尔受到伤害，扎尔和鲁达贝的婚事我一定会成全。萨姆派扎尔亲自去国王的宫廷求情。
body_en: When the news reached Kābul, Mehrāb learned for the first time of his daughter's love. In fury he drew his sword to kill Rūdābeh, saying she had brought ruin on the whole house. Queen Sindokht held him back: 'Do not strike; let me find a way.' Wise and brave, Sindokht went herself to meet the advancing Sām with countless gifts — gold, silver, jewels, horses, elephants and slaves. She did not say who she was, only that she came as the king of Kābul's envoy. Sām accepted the gifts and listened patiently. 'What crime have the people of Kābul committed to suffer war? If the king has sinned, punish the king; the people are innocent.' Only at the end did she reveal that she was Rūdābeh's mother. Moved by her wisdom and courage, Sām took her hand and swore: 'While I live, Kābul shall come to no harm, and I will bring about the marriage of Zāl and Rūdābeh.' He sent Zāl himself to plead at the king's court.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔与鲁达贝”一节。

heading_en: The riddles of the wise men
body_zh: 扎尔来到马努切赫尔的宫廷，国王让宫中的智者们用谜语来考验他。第一个智者问：有十二棵高大的柏树，每棵树上长着三十根枝条，这是什么？扎尔回答：这是一年的十二个月，每个月有三十天。第二个智者问：有两匹骏马，一匹黑，一匹白，它们彼此追逐，却永远追不上，这是什么？扎尔说：这是黑夜和白昼。第三个智者问：有三十个骑手，在国王面前经过，有时少了一个，再看又是三十个，这是什么？扎尔说：这是月亮的日子，有的月份少了一天。第四个智者问：有一座美丽的花园，一个人拿着锋利的镰刀走进去，不分青的黄的，把草全都割倒，这是什么？扎尔说：花园就是这个世界，割草的人就是死亡，他不分老少，把所有的人都带走。国王和满朝的人都赞叹扎尔的智慧。第二天，扎尔又在骑射和摔跤中显示了无人能比的本领。马努切赫尔国王终于答应了这门婚事。
body_en: At Manūchehr's court the king had his wise men test Zāl with riddles. The first asked: 'There are twelve tall cypresses, each with thirty branches; what are they?' Zāl answered: 'The twelve months of the year, each with thirty days.' The second asked: 'Two noble horses, one black and one white, chase each other and never overtake; what are they?' 'Night and day.' The third asked: 'Thirty horsemen pass before the king; sometimes one is missing, yet look again and there are thirty; what are they?' 'The days of the moon; some months lack a day.' The fourth asked: 'There is a lovely garden; a man enters with a sharp scythe and mows down all the grass, green and dry alike; what is it?' Zāl said: 'The garden is this world and the mower is death, who takes all, old and young alike.' The king and the whole court marvelled at his wisdom. The next day Zāl showed unmatched skill at riding, archery and wrestling, and King Manūchehr at last consented to the marriage.
evidence_note: 齐默恩《列王纪》转述本“扎尔与鲁达贝”一节。

body_zh: 王充在《雷虚》的开头写道：盛夏的时候，雷电来得又快又猛，劈断树木，毁坏房屋，有时还会打死人。世俗的人认为，劈断树木、毁坏房屋，是上天来取龙；而打死人，是因为那人有暗中的过错，比如给别人吃了不干净的食物，上天发怒，就用雷把他打死。那隆隆的雷声，就是上天发怒的声音，就像人生气时大声呵斥一样。王充说，世上不论是愚笨的人还是聪明的人，没有一个人不这样认为。可是，如果按照人间的道理来推论，这些都是虚妄的说法。这一段话保存了汉代人对雷的普遍信仰：雷电不是自然现象，而是上天意志的表现；它既能取走天上的龙，也能惩罚人间的罪过。在这种信仰里，雷带有强烈的道德色彩，人们畏惧雷，也就是畏惧上天的审判。直到今天，汉语里还有“天打雷劈”这样的说法，用来诅咒做了坏事的人，可见这种观念流传之久。王充写这篇文章，正是要挑战这种人人深信不疑的看法。
body_en: Wang Chong opens 'Lei Xu' thus: in high summer thunder and lightning come swift and fierce, splitting trees, wrecking houses and sometimes killing people. Common people believe that when trees are split and houses wrecked, Heaven is taking a dragon; and when a man is killed, it is for a hidden fault — having fed others unclean food, for instance — so that Heaven in anger strikes him dead.
