body_zh: 第三者说：他们又拿起尤弥尔的头骨，用它造成天空，把它架在大地的上方，四个角各让一个矮人撑着，这四个矮人的名字是奥斯特里、韦斯特里、诺尔德里和苏德里——东、西、北、南。接着，他们从穆斯佩尔飞来、四处飘散的火星和火花中取来一些，把它们放在金伦加鸿沟的中间，高高地挂在天空上，从上面和下面照亮天空和大地。他们给所有的火光都定了位置：有些固定在天空中，有些在天空下游走，他们为它们安排了位置，规定了运行的路线。古诗里说，从那以后，人们才能计算日子和年份。斯诺里引《女巫的预言》说：那时太阳不知道它的居所在哪里，月亮不知道它的力量有多大，星辰不知道它们的位置在何处。这一章把天上的秩序归功于博尔的儿子们：天空是巨人的头骨，四方由矮人支撑，群星是南方火焰之国的火星。世界的每一部分，都来自冰与火之间那场最初的相遇。
body_en: Third said: they also took his skull and made the sky from it, set it up over the earth with four points, and under each corner put a dwarf, named Austri, Vestri, Norðri and Suðri — East, West, North and South. Then they took molten particles and sparks that were flying about uncontrolled, shot out of Muspell, and set them in the middle of Ginnungagap, high in the sky, to give light above and below. They fixed all the lights, some in the sky, while others moved in a wandering course beneath the sky, and they appointed their positions and ordained their paths. So, old poems say, from then on days and years were reckoned. Snorri quotes the Völuspá: the sun did not know where her dwelling was, the moon did not know what power he had, the stars did not know where their places were. This chapter credits the order of the heavens to the sons of Borr: the sky is a giant's skull, its corners held by dwarves, and the stars are sparks from the southern land of fire. Every part of the world comes from that first meeting of ice and fire.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·欺骗古鲁菲》第8章。

body_zh: 《诗语法》第17章讲道：索尔到东方去打巨怪了，奥丁骑着他的八足马斯莱普尼尔来到巨人国，去拜访一个名叫赫朗格尼尔的巨人。赫朗格尼尔问：这个戴着金盔、骑着马在天空和海上奔驰的人是谁？他说，这匹马真是好马。奥丁说，他愿意拿自己的头打赌，在巨人国里找不到一匹能和它相比的马。赫朗格尼尔说，这确实是一匹好马，可他有一匹步子大得多的马，名叫古尔法克西，意思是“金鬃”。赫朗格尼尔生了气，跳上自己的马，去追赶奥丁，想为他的狂言报复他。奥丁全速奔驰，始终跑在前面，翻过了一座小山；赫朗格尼尔怒气冲天，一心追赶，等他回过神来，已经冲进了阿斯加尔德的大门。斯诺里讲这个故事，原本是为了解释诗人们给索尔、给巨人、给磨石起的种种别称，可他把它讲成了北欧神话中最生动的故事之一。故事的开头是一场赛马和一次赌头，这与第35章洛基的赌注遥相呼应：在斯诺里的世界里，众神和巨人的冲突，常常从一句夸口开始。
body_en: Skáldskaparmál 17 tells: Thor had gone east to fight trolls, and Óðinn rode Sleipnir into Jötunheimr and came to a giant called Hrungnir. Hrungnir asked who this was with the golden helmet, riding through air and sea — a fine horse he had. Óðinn said he would wager his head that there was no horse as good in Jötunheimr. Hrungnir said it was a good horse, but he had one with a much longer stride, called Gullfaxi, Gold-mane. Hrungnir grew angry, leapt on his horse and galloped after Óðinn, meaning to pay him back for his boasting. Óðinn galloped so hard that he kept ahead over the next hill; and Hrungnir was in such a giant rage that before he knew it he had come in through the gates of Ásgarðr. Snorri tells the story to explain the many poetic names for Thor, for giants and for whetstones, yet he makes it one of the liveliest tales in Norse myth. It opens with a horse race and a wager of a head, echoing Loki's wager in chapter 35: in Snorri's world, conflicts between gods and giants often begin with a boast.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 提亚尔菲走到索尔身边，想把赫朗格尼尔的腿从他身上搬开，可是怎么也搬不动。所有的阿萨神听说索尔倒下了，都赶了过来，想把那条腿抬开，可是谁也抬不动。这时，马格尼来了，他是索尔和女巨人雅恩萨克萨的儿子，当时才三岁。他一把就把赫朗格尼尔的腿从索尔身上推开，说：父亲，我来晚了，这真是太可惜了，要是我早一点遇见这个巨人，我想我只用拳头就能把他打死，送他去冥界。索尔站起来，欢迎他的儿子，说他长大以后一定会非常强壮。索尔说：我要把赫朗格尼尔的马古尔法克西送给你。奥丁却说，索尔把这样一匹好马送给一个女巨人的儿子，而不是送给他的父亲，是不对的。这一章是马格尼在北欧神话中最重要的出场：一个三岁的孩子，做到了所有神都做不到的事。在《欺骗古鲁菲》里，斯诺里还说，诸神黄昏之后，马格尼和他的兄弟莫迪将继承索尔的锤子妙尔尼尔。这个刚刚学会走路就能举起巨人之腿的孩子，正是未来世界里雷神力量的继承者。
body_en: Thjálfi went to Thor and tried to lift Hrungnir's leg off him, but could not. All the Æsir came when they heard Thor had fallen and tried to lift the leg, and none of them could move it. Then Magni came, son of Thor and the giantess Járnsaxa; he was three years old. He threw Hrungnir's leg off Thor and said: 'What a shame, father, that I came so late; I think I would have sent this giant to Hel with my fist if I had met him.' Thor stood up, welcomed his son and said he would surely grow up strong. 'And I will give you the horse Gullfaxi,' said Thor. But Óðinn said Thor did wrong to give so fine a horse to the son of a giantess and not to his father. This chapter is Magni's most important appearance in Norse myth: a three-year-old does what all the gods could not. In Gylfaginning Snorri also says that after Ragnarök Magni and his brother Móði will inherit Thor's hammer Mjölnir. The child who could lift a giant's leg when scarcely able to walk is the heir of the thunder god's strength in the world to come.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 索尔回到了他的家斯鲁德万加尔，可是那块磨石还嵌在他的头里。于是来了一位女巫，她叫格罗亚，是勇敢的奥尔万迪尔的妻子。她对着索尔唱起咒语，一直唱到磨石开始松动。在北欧人的世界里，像格罗亚这样的女巫，通过唱诵咒语来治病、预言和施法，是一种受人敬畏的本领；《女巫的预言》本身就是一位女巫对奥丁唱出的诗。格罗亚的咒语眼看就要成功了，索尔感觉到磨石正在松动，心里很高兴，想要报答她，让她也高兴高兴。斯诺里在这里写出了索尔性格中温和的一面：这位在战场上毫不留情的雷神，对一个为他治伤的女子满怀感激，想用一个好消息来回报她。可正是这份好意，让事情出了差错。在北欧神话里，好心办坏事并不少见，而这一次的后果，将永远留在雷神的头上。斯诺里为这个小插曲安排了一个出人意料的结局，也借此解释了一条古老的禁忌。
body_en: Thor went home to Þrúðvangar, and the whetstone remained stuck in his head. Then came a seeress called Gróa, wife of Aurvandill the Bold. She chanted her spells over Thor until the whetstone began to work loose. In the Norse world a seeress like Gróa, who healed, prophesied and worked magic by chanting spells, was held in awe; the Völuspá itself is a seeress's song to Óðinn. Gróa's spell was on the point of success; Thor felt the stone loosening and was glad, and wished to reward her and make her glad in turn. Snorri shows a gentle side of Thor here: the thunder god, merciless in battle, is full of gratitude to a woman healing his wound and wants to repay her with good news. Yet it is just that kindness that makes things go wrong. In Norse myth good intentions often lead to bad results, and this time the consequence will stay in the thunder god's head for ever. Snorri gives this small episode an unexpected ending, and uses it to explain an old taboo.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 索尔想让格罗亚高兴，就告诉她一个消息。他说，他曾经从北方涉水渡过埃利伐加尔河，把奥尔万迪尔装在一个篮子里，背在背上，从巨人国一路背了回来。为了证明这件事，他说，奥尔万迪尔有一根脚趾从篮子里伸了出来，被冻僵了，索尔就把它折断，扔到天上，把它变成了一颗星星，叫做“奥尔万迪尔的脚趾”。索尔说，奥尔万迪尔用不了多久就会回到家里。格罗亚听了这个消息，高兴得不得了，竟然忘了她的咒语，磨石也就不再松动，一直留在了索尔的头里。斯诺里在最后说：所以，人们不可以把磨石扔过地板，因为那样的话，索尔头里的那块石头就会动起来。这个故事从一次赛马开始，经过一场决斗，最后落在一条日常的禁忌上。马格尼的力量、提亚尔菲的机智、格罗亚的咒语，都围绕着雷神展开；而那块永远嵌在索尔头里的磨石，成了这场胜利留下的永久的伤痕。
body_en: Thor wanted to make Gróa glad, so he told her some news. He said he had waded from the north across the river Élivágar carrying Aurvandill in a basket on his back out of Jötunheimr. As proof, he said that one of Aurvandill's toes had stuck out of the basket and frozen, so Thor broke it off and threw it up into the sky and made it into a star called Aurvandill's Toe. Thor said it would not be long before Aurvandill came home. Gróa was so delighted at the news that she forgot her spells, and the whetstone stopped coming loose and stayed in Thor's head. Snorri ends: and so it is forbidden to throw a whetstone across the floor, for then the stone in Thor's head stirs. The tale begins with a horse race, passes through a duel, and comes to rest on an everyday taboo. Magni's strength, Thjálfi's wit and Gróa's spells all turn around the thunder god, and the whetstone lodged for ever in Thor's head becomes the lasting scar of his victory.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 赫朗格尼尔骑马冲进了众神的城门，他来到大殿门口时，阿萨神族的众神邀请他进去喝酒。这也许是北欧人待客的规矩：即使来者是巨人，只要他进了门，主人就要以礼相待。赫朗格尼尔走进大殿，要人给他拿酒。众神端来了索尔平常用来喝酒的那两只大碗，赫朗格尼尔把两碗酒都喝得一干二净。在北欧神话里，索尔是出了名的海量，在乌特加尔洛基的城堡里，他曾一口气想要喝干连着大海的角杯；用索尔的酒碗招待巨人，就像是把雷神的座位让给了他。斯诺里没有说众神为什么这样慷慨，也许是因为奥丁觉得这场赛马是自己引起的，也许是因为众神知道赫朗格尼尔是巨人中最强壮的一个，不想在索尔不在的时候和他起冲突。可是好客的主人很快就要后悔了：酒喝得越多，巨人的话就越狂妄，阿斯加尔德的大殿里，一场危机正在酝酿。
body_en: Hrungnir rode in through the gods' gate, and when he came to the hall doors the Æsir invited him in to drink. Perhaps this was the custom of Norse hospitality: even a giant, once he was inside the door, must be treated as a guest. Hrungnir went into the hall and demanded drink. The gods brought the bowls that Thor usually drank from, and Hrungnir drained both. In Norse myth Thor is famous for his thirst — in Útgarða-Loki's castle he tried to drain a horn whose end lay in the sea — and to serve the giant from Thor's bowls is almost to give him the thunder god's seat. Snorri does not say why the gods were so generous; perhaps Óðinn felt the race was his doing, perhaps the gods knew Hrungnir was the strongest of the giants and wanted no fight while Thor was away. But the hospitable hosts were soon to regret it: the more the giant drank, the wilder his words, and a crisis was brewing in the hall of Ásgarðr.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 赫朗格尼尔喝醉了，说起了大话。他说，他要把瓦尔哈拉整个搬起来，带回巨人国去；他要把阿斯加尔德沉入地下，杀死所有的神，只留下芙蕾雅和希芙，把她们带回自己家里。众神中只有芙蕾雅敢给他倒酒。赫朗格尼尔又说，他要把众神所有的麦酒都喝光。众神被他的狂妄激怒了，可是谁也不敢和他动手。在这一幕里，希芙再次以索尔妻子的身份出现在故事中：巨人点名要带走的两位女神，一位是众神中最美的芙蕾雅，一位是索尔的妻子希芙。对巨人来说，夺走雷神的妻子，就是对索尔最大的侮辱。北欧神话里，巨人觊觎女神是一个反复出现的主题：建造城墙的巨人要芙蕾雅、太阳和月亮作报酬，偷走锤子的巨人特里姆要芙蕾雅做新娘。而这一次，巨人的狂言最终让他付出了生命。芙蕾雅为他倒酒的细节也很耐人寻味：在众神都畏缩的时候，只有她敢走到这个醉醺醺的巨人面前。
body_en: Hrungnir got drunk and began to boast. He said he would lift up Valhalla and carry it to Jötunheimr, sink Ásgarðr and kill all the gods except Freyja and Sif, whom he would take home with him. Freyja was the only one who dared pour for him. He said he would drink up all the Æsir's ale. The gods grew weary of his arrogance, yet none dared lay hands on him. In this scene Sif appears again as Thor's wife: the two goddesses the giant names to carry off are Freyja, fairest of the goddesses, and Sif, wife of Thor. For a giant, to take the thunder god's wife would be the greatest insult to Thor. The giant's lust for the goddesses is a recurring theme in Norse myth: the giant builder of the wall demands Freyja, the sun and the moon as his wage, and the giant Þrymr who steals the hammer demands Freyja as his bride. This time the giant's boasting will cost him his life. The detail of Freyja pouring for him is telling: when all the gods shrink back, she alone dares approach the drunken giant.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 众神听够了他的狂言，就喊出了索尔的名字。索尔立刻出现在大殿里，高高举起锤子，怒不可遏。他问：是谁让这个狡猾的巨人坐在这里喝酒？是谁允许赫朗格尼尔待在阿斯加尔德？为什么芙蕾雅像在众神的宴会上一样给他倒酒？赫朗格尼尔用不友善的眼光看着索尔，说是奥丁请他进来喝酒的，他受到奥丁的保护。索尔说，赫朗格尼尔会在离开以前后悔接受这个邀请。赫朗格尼尔说：杀死一个手无寸铁的人，对阿萨·索尔来说没有什么光彩；你若敢在边界的格约特纳加尔德与我决斗，那才算是勇敢。我真是太傻了，把盾牌和磨石留在了家里，要是我带着武器，我们现在就可以较量。你要是杀了一个没有武器的人，就是一个卑鄙的人。他向索尔提出了决斗。斯诺里说，索尔无论如何也不愿意错过这次决斗，因为从来没有人向他挑战过。这是索尔一生中第一次被正式邀请决斗，他的荣誉不允许他拒绝。
body_en: When the gods had had enough of his boasting they called on the name of Thor. At once Thor was in the hall, his hammer raised high, in a towering rage. He asked who had let this cunning giant sit drinking there, who had allowed Hrungnir to be in Ásgarðr, and why Freyja was serving him as at a feast of the Æsir. Hrungnir looked at Thor with no friendly eyes and said Óðinn had invited him to drink and he was under Óðinn's protection. Thor said Hrungnir would regret that invitation before he left. Hrungnir said there was little glory for Ása-Þórr in killing an unarmed man; it would be braver to fight him on the border at Grjótúnagarðar. 'I was a fool to leave my shield and whetstone at home; if I had my weapons we could try it now. You will be a coward if you kill an unarmed man.' So he challenged Thor to single combat. Snorri says Thor would not miss the duel for anything, for no one had ever challenged him before. It was the first time in Thor's life he had been formally challenged, and his honour would not let him refuse.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 赫朗格尼尔骑马飞奔回巨人国。他和索尔的决斗在巨人中间传开了，巨人们都觉得这件事关系重大：如果赫朗格尼尔死了，他们就要从索尔那里吃苦头了，因为赫朗格尼尔是他们中间最强壮的一个。于是巨人们在格约特纳加尔德用黏土造了一个巨人，他有九里高，腋下有三里宽。他们找不到一颗大得能配得上他的心，就取来一匹母马的心装了进去，可是这颗心在索尔到来的时候并不坚定。这个泥巨人名叫默库尔卡尔菲。巨人们的这个计划，透露出他们心里的恐惧：他们不敢完全依靠赫朗格尼尔一个人，就想用一个巨大的帮手来吓住索尔。可是一个用黏土造的巨人，配上一颗母马的心，外表再庞大，内心也是怯懦的。斯诺里用这个细节暗示了接下来的结果：决斗还没开始，巨人一方就已经露出了弱点。这也是北欧神话里难得一见的“造人”情节：巨人们也会像众神用树干造人那样，用泥土造出一个有生命的帮手。
body_en: Hrungnir galloped back to Jötunheimr. His duel with Thor was much talked of among the giants; they thought a great deal hung on it, for if Hrungnir died they would have trouble from Thor, Hrungnir being the strongest of them. So the giants made a man of clay at Grjótúnagarðar, nine leagues tall and three leagues broad under the arms. They could find no heart big enough for him until they took one from a mare, and it was not steady when Thor came. The clay giant was called Mökkurkálfi. The plan betrays the giants' fear: not daring to rely on Hrungnir alone, they hoped a vast helper would daunt Thor. But a giant of clay with a mare's heart, however huge outside, is timid within. Snorri uses the detail to hint at what follows: before the duel has begun, the giants' side already shows its weakness. It is also a rare 'making of a man' in Norse myth: the giants, like the gods who made people from logs, shape a living helper from earth.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 赫朗格尼尔自己的心则是出了名的：它是用坚硬的石头做的，有棱有角，是三角形的，后来人们刻的一种叫做“赫朗格尼尔之心”的符号，就是照着它的样子画的。他的头也是石头做的。他的盾牌也是石头做的，又宽又厚，他在格约特纳加尔德等索尔的时候，就把这面盾牌举在身前；他的武器是一块磨石，他把它扛在肩上，样子十分可怕。在他身边站着那个泥巨人默库尔卡尔菲，泥巨人非常害怕，据说他一看见索尔，就吓得尿了出来。斯诺里在这里把两个巨人对比得非常鲜明：一个是石心石头的强敌，一个是黏土马心的胆小鬼。赫朗格尼尔的石头之身，正好说明了他的力量：他是巨人中最坚硬、最难对付的一个。北欧的吟唱诗人常用“赫朗格尼尔的头骨”“赫朗格尼尔的脚下”等说法来指盾牌和石头，这些肯宁都是从这个故事来的。决斗的场地已经准备好，双方都在等待：一边是石头的巨人和泥巨人，一边即将到来的是雷神和他的仆人。
body_en: Hrungnir himself had a famous heart: it was made of hard stone, spiky and three-cornered, like the carved symbol that has since been called Hrungnir's heart. His head too was of stone. His shield was of stone, broad and thick, and he held it before him as he stood at Grjótúnagarðar waiting for Thor; his weapon was a whetstone, which he carried on his shoulder, and he looked a fearsome sight. Beside him stood the clay giant Mökkurkálfi, who was terrified; they say he wet himself when he saw Thor. Snorri sets the two giants in sharp contrast: one a formidable foe with a stone heart and stone head, the other a coward of clay with a mare's heart. Hrungnir's body of stone shows his might: he is the hardest and most dangerous of the giants. Norse court poets use phrases like 'Hrungnir's skull' and 'the soles of Hrungnir's feet' for shields and stones, kennings that come from this tale. The field is ready and both sides wait: on one, the stone giant and the clay giant; coming toward them, the thunder god and his servant.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 索尔带着他的仆人提亚尔菲前去决斗。提亚尔菲先跑到赫朗格尼尔站的地方，对他说：巨人，你站在这里，把盾牌举在前面，太不小心了。索尔已经看见你了，他会从地底下钻出来，从下面攻击你。赫朗格尼尔听了，就把盾牌放到脚下，站在盾牌上，双手握住磨石。提亚尔菲是索尔在旅途中收下的仆人，在乌特加尔洛基的城堡里，他曾和思想赛跑；在这里，他用一句谎话就让巨人放下了防御。这个诡计说明，北欧神话里的众神一方，并不只靠蛮力取胜。索尔从来不会从地下钻出来——他是雷神，他的到来总是伴着天上的闪电与雷鸣；巨人却信以为真，把唯一能保护自己的盾牌踩在了脚下。斯诺里用这一幕为接下来的决斗做了铺垫：当雷神真的从天上降临时，赫朗格尼尔已经无法用盾牌抵挡了。提亚尔菲的谎话也许不太光彩，可在北欧人看来，用智谋打败强敌，正是一个好仆人的本事。
body_en: Thor went to the duel with his servant Thjálfi. Thjálfi ran ahead to where Hrungnir stood and said: 'Giant, you are standing carelessly with your shield in front of you. Thor has seen you; he will come at you from below, under the ground.' Hrungnir pushed the shield under his feet and stood on it, holding the whetstone in both hands. Thjálfi was the servant Thor took on during his travels; in Útgarða-Loki's castle he raced against Thought. Here, with a single lie, he makes the giant drop his guard. The trick shows that the gods' side in Norse myth does not win by brute force alone. Thor never comes from under the ground — he is the thunder god, and his coming is always with lightning and thunder in the sky — yet the giant believed it and set his only protection under his feet. Snorri thus prepares the duel: when the thunder god truly comes down from the sky, Hrungnir can no longer shield himself. Thjálfi's lie may not be noble, but to the Norse, beating a strong foe by wit was just what a good servant should do.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 接着，赫朗格尼尔看见了闪电，听见了巨大的雷声，然后他看见了索尔带着神的愤怒而来。索尔飞快地冲过来，挥起锤子，从很远的地方就把它掷向赫朗格尼尔。赫朗格尼尔双手举起磨石，也把它掷了出去。锤子和磨石在空中相撞，磨石碎成了两半：一半落在地上，世上所有的磨石山都是从那一半来的；另一半击中了索尔的头，他向前扑倒在地上。而锤子妙尔尼尔正中赫朗格尼尔的头，把他的头颅砸成了碎片。赫朗格尼尔向前倒下，压在索尔身上，一条腿正好横在索尔的脖子上。这一幕是整个故事的高潮，也是斯诺里最精彩的描写之一。锤子和磨石的相撞，不仅决定了胜负，还解释了自然界的一种现象：人们开采磨石的那些岩层，原来是巨人武器的碎片。索尔赢了决斗，却也付出了代价：一块磨石的碎片嵌进了他的头里，而他自己又被死去的巨人压在了地上，动弹不得。胜利的雷神，此刻需要有人来救他。
body_en: Then Hrungnir saw lightning and heard great thunderclaps, and he saw Thor in his godly wrath. Thor came on at tremendous speed, swung up the hammer and threw it from a great distance at Hrungnir. Hrungnir raised the whetstone in both hands and threw it back. Hammer and whetstone met in the air, and the whetstone broke in two: one part fell to the ground, and from it come all whetstone rocks; the other struck Thor's head, so that he fell forward to the ground. But the hammer Mjölnir struck Hrungnir in the middle of the head and smashed his skull into small fragments, and he fell forward over Thor, so that his leg lay across Thor's neck. This is the climax of the tale and one of Snorri's finest descriptions. The clash of hammer and whetstone decides the fight and also explains a natural feature: the rocks from which whetstones are quarried are fragments of a giant's weapon. Thor wins the duel but pays a price: a piece of whetstone is lodged in his head, and he lies pinned under the dead giant. The victorious thunder god now needs someone to rescue him.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 就在索尔和赫朗格尼尔交手的同时，提亚尔菲向泥巨人默库尔卡尔菲发起了攻击。斯诺里只用了一句话来描写这场战斗：泥巨人倒下了，倒得很不光彩。这个九里高、三里宽的庞然大物，本该是巨人们用来吓倒索尔的秘密武器，却被索尔的一个仆人轻易地打倒了。一颗母马的心，终究撑不起一个巨人的身体。北欧的吟唱诗人在描写这场战斗时，常把重点放在索尔和赫朗格尼尔身上，泥巨人只是一个可笑的陪衬。可是这一句话也有它的意义：它说明巨人们的计谋全都落空了，他们以为造一个更大的身体就能战胜雷神，却忘了真正决定胜负的是勇气。提亚尔菲在这个故事里两次立功：一次用谎话让赫朗格尼尔放下盾牌，一次亲手打倒了泥巨人。这个凡间出身的少年，在众神的冒险中一点也不逊色。可是接下来，他就会发现，有一件事是他做不到的。
body_en: While Thor fought Hrungnir, Thjálfi attacked the clay giant Mökkurkálfi. Snorri gives the fight a single sentence: the clay giant fell with little glory. This monster nine leagues tall and three broad, meant to be the giants' secret weapon to terrify Thor, was easily felled by Thor's servant. A mare's heart could not hold up a giant's body. Norse court poets describing the battle usually focus on Thor and Hrungnir, the clay giant being only a comic foil. Yet the sentence matters: it shows that all the giants' schemes came to nothing. They thought a bigger body could beat the thunder god and forgot that courage decides a fight. Thjálfi wins glory twice in this tale — once with the lie that made Hrungnir put down his shield, once by felling the clay giant himself. This boy of mortal birth holds his own in the adventures of the gods. But next he will find there is one thing he cannot do.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第17章。

body_zh: 在斯诺里的《欺骗古鲁菲》里，至高者向古鲁菲一一介绍阿萨神族的众神。说到乌勒尔时，他说：乌勒尔是希芙的儿子，索尔的继子。他是一个出色的弓箭手，又是一个滑雪好手，没有人能和他相比；他相貌英俊，具备战士的种种品质，在一对一的决斗中，向他祈求是很好的。这短短几句话告诉我们：雷神索尔的妻子希芙，在嫁给索尔之前已经有一个儿子，乌勒尔的父亲是谁，斯诺里没有说。在《诗语法》里，乌勒尔被称为“希芙之子”“索尔的继子”“滑雪之神”“弓箭之神”“狩猎之神”和“盾牌之神”，诗人们常用“乌勒尔的船”来指盾牌。至于希芙自己，她在北欧神话里最著名的，就是她那一头金色的头发。在斯诺里的书中，希芙几乎没有开口说话的场面，她出现的地方，总是和她的家人联系在一起：索尔的妻子，乌勒尔的母亲。下面的故事，就从她失去头发的那个早晨开始。
body_en: In Snorri's Gylfaginning, High tells Gylfi about each of the Æsir. Of Ullr he says: Ullr is Sif's son and Thor's stepson. He is such a good archer and skier that no one can rival him; he is beautiful in appearance and has a warrior's qualities, and it is good to pray to him in single combat. These few words tell us that Sif, wife of the thunder god Thor, already had a son before she married Thor; who Ullr's father was, Snorri does not say. In Skáldskaparmál Ullr is called son of Sif, stepson of Thor, ski-god, bow-god, hunting-god and shield-god, and poets call a shield 'Ullr's ship'. As for Sif herself, she is most famous in Norse myth for her golden hair. In Snorri's book she hardly ever speaks; she appears always in relation to her family — Thor's wife, Ullr's mother. The story that follows begins on the morning she lost her hair.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·欺骗古鲁菲》第31章。

body_zh: 洛基先献上他的宝物。他把长矛贡尼尔给了奥丁，把头发给了索尔，让他送给希芙，又把船斯基德布拉德尼尔给了弗雷。他一一说明了这些宝物的好处：这支长矛刺出去，无论刺向什么，都不会停下；这头头发，只要一放到希芙的头上，就会像天生的头发一样生长；这艘船，只要升起船帆，就总有顺风，无论要去哪里都能到达，不用的时候，还能像一块布一样折叠起来，放进口袋里。希芙就这样得回了她的头发，而且是一头真正的金发，从此“希芙的头发”成了黄金的代称。这里，被剪掉的头发终于有了一个完美的结局：失去的东西不但被找了回来，而且变得比原来更加珍贵。至于斯基德布拉德尼尔，斯诺里在《欺骗古鲁菲》里还说，它是所有船中最好的，是由伊瓦尔迪的儿子们造的，而纳吉尔法号是最大的船。贡尼尔则成了奥丁的标志，在诸神黄昏的最后一战中，奥丁也将手持贡尼尔与芬里尔狼作战。
body_en: Loki presented his treasures first. He gave Óðinn the spear Gungnir, Thor the hair for Sif, and Freyr the ship Skíðblaðnir, and he explained the virtues of each: the spear never stops in its thrust; the hair, as soon as it is placed on Sif's head, will grow to her like natural hair; and the ship has a fair wind as soon as the sail is hoisted, wherever it is going, and when not in use it can be folded up like a cloth and put in a pocket. So Sif got back her hair, and real golden hair at that, and ever after 'Sif's hair' meant gold. The shorn hair has its perfect ending: what was lost is not only restored but made more precious than before. Of Skíðblaðnir Snorri says in Gylfaginning that it is the best of all ships, made by the sons of Ívaldi, while Naglfar is the biggest. Gungnir became Óðinn's emblem, and in the last battle at Ragnarök Óðinn will carry Gungnir against the wolf Fenrir.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 接着，勃洛克献上他的宝物。他把指环德劳普尼尔给了奥丁，说每到第九个夜晚，就会从这枚指环上滴落下八枚同样重的金指环。他把金鬃野猪给了弗雷，说它能在空中和海上奔跑，日夜不停，比任何马都快，无论夜晚多么黑暗，无论在什么阴暗的地方，只要它在，它的金鬃就会发出足够的光亮。他把锤子给了索尔，说索尔可以用它随意猛击任何东西，锤子永远不会失手；如果他把锤子扔出去，它永远不会扔偏，也不会飞得太远而回不到他手里；而且只要他愿意，锤子还能变得很小，可以藏在衬衣里。只是它有一个缺陷：锤柄有点短。众神的判决是：这把锤子是所有宝物中最好的，因为有了它，众神就能抵御霜巨人的侵犯。于是他们判定，矮人赢得了这场赌局。斯诺里在这里点出了妙尔尼尔真正的意义：它不只是一件武器，更是整个阿斯加尔德的守护。正因为如此，后来锤子被巨人偷走时，众神才会那样惊慌。
body_en: Then Brokkr presented his treasures. He gave Óðinn the ring, saying that every ninth night eight rings of equal weight would drip from it. He gave Freyr the boar, saying it could run through air and over sea, night and day, faster than any horse, and that it would never be so dark at night or in the worlds of darkness that there would not be light enough wherever it went, so bright did its bristles shine. He gave Thor the hammer, saying that Thor could strike as hard as he liked at whatever he wished and the hammer would never fail; if he threw it, it would never miss and never fly so far that it would not return to his hand; and when he wished, it would be so small that he could carry it inside his tunic. Its one flaw was that the handle was rather short. The gods' verdict was that the hammer was the best of all the treasures, for it was a defence against the frost-giants; and they judged that the dwarf had won the wager. Snorri makes Mjölnir's real meaning clear: not only a weapon but the guard of all Ásgarðr. That is why the gods panic when, in another tale, a giant steals it.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 洛基提出要用钱赎回自己的头，可矮人说没有这回事。洛基说：那你就来抓我吧！勃洛克去抓他时，洛基已经跑远了——他有一双鞋，穿上它能在空中和海上奔跑。矮人请索尔去抓他，索尔把洛基抓了回来。矮人要砍下洛基的头，洛基却说，头是你的，可脖子不是。于是矮人拿来一根皮绳和一把刀，想在洛基的嘴唇上钻孔，把他的嘴缝起来，可是刀扎不进去。矮人说：要是我兄弟的锥子在这里就好了。他话音刚落，锥子就出现在那里，扎穿了洛基的嘴唇。他用一根叫做瓦塔里的皮绳把洛基的嘴唇缝在一起，洛基后来把皮绳从嘴唇上扯了下来。斯诺里在这一章的最后说：这就是为什么金子被称为希芙的头发。从一次剪发开始，到一张被缝上的嘴结束，这个故事让众神得到了贡尼尔、斯基德布拉德尼尔、德劳普尼尔、古林博斯帝、妙尔尼尔，还有希芙那一头会生长的金发；而那个惹出一切麻烦的洛基，最后也为他的恶作剧付出了代价。
body_en: Loki offered to redeem his head, but the dwarf said there was no hope of that. 'Catch me, then,' said Loki, and when Brokkr tried to catch him he was far away, for Loki had shoes in which he could run through air and over sea. The dwarf asked Thor to catch him, and Thor did. The dwarf was going to cut off his head, but Loki said the head was his, but not the neck. So the dwarf took a thong and a knife and tried to bore holes in Loki's lips to stitch his mouth up, but the knife would not cut. Then he said it would be better if his brother's awl were there — and as soon as he spoke the awl was there, and it pierced the lips. He stitched the lips together with a thong called Vartari, and Loki tore the thong out of his lips. At the end of the chapter Snorri says: that is why gold is called Sif's hair. Beginning with a shearing and ending with a sewn mouth, the tale gives the gods Gungnir, Skíðblaðnir, Draupnir, Gullinbursti, Mjölnir and Sif's growing golden hair — and Loki, who caused all the trouble, pays at last for his mischief.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 《诗语法》第35章从一个问题开始：为什么金子被称为“希芙的头发”？斯诺里回答说：狡猾的洛基出于恶作剧，把希芙的头发全部剪掉了。斯诺里没有说洛基为什么要这样做，只说是出于“恶意的玩笑”。在北欧古代的社会里，头发对一个女子来说是美丽和尊严的象征，把一位女神的头发剪光，是极大的侮辱。希芙的头发据说是金色的，这也是后来诗人们用“希芙的头发”来比喻黄金的原因之一。这种用神话典故代替普通名词的说法，叫做“肯宁”，是北欧古诗最重要的修辞手法，《诗语法》这本书就是斯诺里为了教年轻诗人理解这些肯宁而写的。所以，这个故事的讲述方式很特别：它不是为了讲故事而讲故事，而是为了解释一个诗歌用语的来历。可是正是这一次恶作剧，引出了一连串的事件，最后让众神得到了他们最珍贵的几件宝物，包括索尔的锤子妙尔尼尔。
body_en: Skáldskaparmál 35 begins with a question: why is gold called Sif's hair? Snorri answers: Loki Laufeyjarson, for the sake of mischief, cut off all Sif's hair. He gives no reason beyond malicious fun. In old Norse society a woman's hair was a sign of beauty and honour, and to shear a goddess's hair was a grave insult. Sif's hair is said to have been golden, one reason poets later used 'Sif's hair' for gold. This way of replacing an ordinary word with a mythological allusion is called a kenning, the chief ornament of Old Norse verse, and Snorri wrote Skáldskaparmál to teach young poets to understand such kennings. So the tale is told in an unusual way: not for its own sake but to explain where a poetic phrase comes from. Yet this one piece of mischief set off a chain of events that ended with the gods receiving their most precious treasures, among them Thor's hammer Mjölnir.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 索尔发现妻子的头发被剪光后，立刻抓住了洛基。他气得要把洛基身上的每一根骨头都打断。洛基吓坏了，连忙发誓说，他会去请黑精灵——也就是矮人——用金子为希芙做一头新头发，而且这头发要像真的头发一样，能在她头上生长。索尔这才放过了他。在北欧神话里，洛基常常这样：先闯下大祸，然后再想办法弥补，而他想出的办法，往往比原来的局面更好，也更危险。索尔和洛基的关系也很有意思：他们常常一起旅行，比如去乌特加尔洛基的城堡、去寻找被偷走的锤子，可是只要洛基闯了祸，索尔总是第一个抓住他的人。斯诺里在这里对希芙本人的反应只字未提，我们不知道她是哭了还是生气了；故事的焦点很快就从受害的女神转到了两位男神之间的争执，又从争执转到了矮人的铁匠铺。这种叙述方式本身也说明了希芙在神话中的位置：她是故事的起因，却很少是故事的主角。
body_en: When Thor found his wife's hair shorn, he seized Loki and would have broken every bone in his body. Terrified, Loki swore that he would get the black elves — the dwarves — to make Sif a head of hair from gold that would grow like any other hair. Only then did Thor let him go. Loki is often like this in Norse myth: first he causes great trouble, then he finds a way to make it good, and his remedy is often better — and more dangerous — than what came before. Thor and Loki's relationship is interesting too: they often travel together, to Útgarða-Loki's castle or in search of the stolen hammer, yet whenever Loki causes mischief, Thor is the first to lay hands on him. Snorri says nothing here about Sif's own reaction; we do not know whether she wept or raged. The story quickly turns from the wronged goddess to the quarrel between two gods, and from the quarrel to the dwarves' smithy. That itself shows Sif's place in the myths: she is the cause of the story, seldom its hero.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 洛基于是去找那些被称为伊瓦尔迪之子的矮人。他们为希芙打造了一头金发，同时还造了一艘名叫斯基德布拉德尼尔的船，以及一支名叫贡尼尔的长矛——后来它成了奥丁的矛。这三件宝物都非常出色。斯诺里没有描写矮人们是怎样工作的，也没有说洛基许给了他们什么报酬；也许洛基只是用花言巧语说服了他们。在北欧神话里，矮人是最好的工匠，他们住在山里和地下，掌握着神也不具备的锻造技艺。众神手中的许多宝物都出自矮人之手：除了这里的三件，还有束缚芬里尔狼的绳索格莱普尼尔、芙蕾雅的项链布里欣加曼等等。伊瓦尔迪的儿子们只在这个故事里出现，他们的名字也没有被记下来。洛基带着这三件宝物，本可以直接回到阿斯加尔德，平息索尔的怒气；可他偏偏又在矮人中间惹出了另一件事。这一次，他押上的赌注不是别的，而是他自己的头。
body_en: So Loki went to the dwarves called the sons of Ívaldi. They made the hair for Sif, and also the ship Skíðblaðnir and the spear called Gungnir, which became Óðinn's. All three treasures were excellent. Snorri does not describe how the dwarves worked, nor what Loki promised them; perhaps he simply talked them round. In Norse myth dwarves are the finest craftsmen, living in mountains and underground, masters of a smithcraft even the gods lack. Many of the gods' treasures come from dwarves: besides these three there are Gleipnir, the fetter that binds the wolf Fenrir, and Freyja's necklace Brísingamen. The sons of Ívaldi appear only in this tale, and their own names are not recorded. With these three treasures Loki could have gone straight back to Ásgarðr and calmed Thor's anger; but he went and started something else among the dwarves. This time the stake was nothing less than his own head.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 洛基拿着宝物，找到一个名叫勃洛克的矮人，跟他打赌，把自己的头押上：他说勃洛克的兄弟埃特里——有些抄本和后人叫他辛德里——不可能打造出三件和这三件一样好的宝物。勃洛克接受了赌注。斯诺里没有说洛基为什么要冒这个险，也许是为了炫耀，也许只是因为他天生喜欢挑起争端。可这个赌注却成了众神的幸运：正因为洛基想证明伊瓦尔迪之子的宝物无人能比，另一对矮人兄弟才拼尽全力，打造出了更加了不起的东西。北欧神话里常常有这样的赌局：奥丁和巨人瓦夫斯鲁德尼尔以头为注比智慧，索尔和乌特加尔洛基的手下比力气。在这些故事里，“以头为注”是一种极端的赌法，输了的一方就要付出生命。洛基押上自己的头，看起来很勇敢，其实他早已为自己留好了退路，这一点要到故事的最后才会揭晓。勃洛克和埃特里兄弟俩则一起走进了铁匠铺，一个负责打铁，一个负责拉风箱。
body_en: Loki took the treasures and wagered his head with a dwarf called Brokkr that his brother Eitri — called Sindri in some manuscripts and later writers — could not make three treasures as good as these. Brokkr took the wager. Snorri does not say why Loki took the risk — to show off, perhaps, or simply because he loved to stir up trouble. Yet the wager turned out to be the gods' good fortune: because Loki wanted to prove the sons of Ívaldi unmatched, another pair of dwarf brothers strained every nerve to make still more wonderful things. Norse myth is full of such contests: Óðinn wagers his head against the giant Vafþrúðnir in a contest of wisdom, and Thor matches strength with Útgarða-Loki's people. In these tales a wager of one's head is the most extreme stake: the loser pays with his life. Loki's bet looks brave, but he has already prepared his escape, as the end of the story will show. Brokkr and Eitri went into the smithy together, one to work the metal and one to blow the bellows.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 埃特里把一张猪皮放进炉子里，吩咐勃洛克拉风箱，在他把东西从炉子里取出来以前，一刻也不许停下。埃特里一离开铁匠铺，就有一只苍蝇落在勃洛克的手上，狠狠地叮他。可是勃洛克照样拉着风箱，一直等到铁匠回来，从炉子里取出东西——那是一头长着金色鬃毛的野猪。这头野猪后来被称为古林博斯帝，意思是“金鬃”。斯诺里在后面会讲到它的本领。这只苍蝇是谁？斯诺里在这里没有明说，可是读者很容易猜到：会变化形体、又最希望勃洛克失败的，只有洛基。在其他故事里，洛基曾变成母马、鲑鱼、海豹和老妇人，变成一只苍蝇对他来说毫不困难。勃洛克忍着疼痛，没有让风箱停下，这是兄弟俩的第一次胜利。在古代北欧的铁匠铺里，拉风箱是一件非常要紧的活，火候稍有差池，整件作品就会毁掉，所以埃特里才一再叮嘱，无论发生什么都不能停。
body_en: Eitri laid a pigskin in the forge and told Brokkr to blow the bellows and not stop until he took out what he had put in. As soon as Eitri had gone out of the smithy, a fly settled on Brokkr's hand and stung him hard. But Brokkr kept blowing until the smith came back and took the thing out of the forge — a boar with bristles of gold. It is called Gullinbursti, Golden-bristle, and Snorri will tell its powers later. Who was the fly? Snorri does not say here, but the reader can easily guess: the shape-changer who most wanted Brokkr to fail could only be Loki. In other tales Loki becomes a mare, a salmon, a seal and an old woman; a fly is no trouble to him. Brokkr bore the pain and kept the bellows going — the brothers' first victory. In an old Norse smithy working the bellows was vital work; a moment's lapse in the heat could ruin the whole piece, which is why Eitri warned him again and again not to stop, whatever happened.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 接着，埃特里把金子放进炉子里，又吩咐勃洛克拉风箱，在他回来以前不许停下。他走了出去，那只苍蝇又来了，这一次落在勃洛克的脖子上，叮得比上一次厉害一倍。可勃洛克还是不停地拉着风箱，直到铁匠回来，从炉子里取出了一枚金指环，名叫德劳普尼尔，意思是“滴落者”。这枚指环的本领，斯诺里也要到后面才说。在北欧神话里，德劳普尼尔还有另一个故事：在巴德尔的葬礼上，奥丁把这枚指环放在儿子的火葬堆上；后来赫尔莫德到冥界去求赫尔放回巴德尔，巴德尔又把指环交给他带回给奥丁。这说明德劳普尼尔是奥丁最珍爱的宝物之一。在这一次锻造中，苍蝇的攻击比上一次更凶，可勃洛克依然没有动摇。兄弟俩已经做成了两件宝物，离赢得赌局只差最后一件。而洛基——如果那只苍蝇真的是他——也只剩下最后一次机会了。
body_en: Next Eitri laid gold in the forge and bade Brokkr blow and not stop until he came back. He went out, and the fly came again, settling on Brokkr's neck and stinging twice as hard as before. Still Brokkr kept blowing until the smith came back and took out of the forge a gold ring called Draupnir, the Dripper. Its powers, too, Snorri tells later. Draupnir has another story in Norse myth: at Baldr's funeral Óðinn laid the ring on his son's pyre, and when Hermóðr rode to Hel to beg for Baldr's return, Baldr sent the ring back to Óðinn with him. Clearly Draupnir was among Óðinn's most treasured possessions. In this second forging the fly's attack was fiercer than before, yet Brokkr did not waver. The brothers had made two treasures and needed only one more to win the wager. And Loki — if the fly was indeed Loki — had only one chance left.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 最后，埃特里把铁放进炉子里，对勃洛克说，必须一直拉风箱，否则一切都会毁掉。这一次，苍蝇落在勃洛克两眼之间，叮他的眼皮，血流进了他的眼睛，他什么也看不见了。勃洛克只好用手去赶苍蝇，就在这一瞬间，风箱停了下来，炉火也弱了下去。这时铁匠回来了，说炉子里的东西差一点就全毁了。他从炉子里取出的是一把锤子。这就是后来索尔的锤子妙尔尼尔。因为那一瞬间的停顿，锤子的柄做得短了一些——这是它唯一的缺陷。斯诺里把这个细节讲得很清楚：众神最强大的武器，是在一只苍蝇的干扰下诞生的，它的小小缺陷，正是那场恶作剧留下的痕迹。勃洛克把三件宝物收好，带着它们和洛基一起前往阿斯加尔德，去请众神裁决这场赌局。在路上，洛基大概已经在盘算，怎样才能保住自己的脑袋了。
body_en: Last, Eitri laid iron in the forge and told Brokkr he must keep blowing or everything would be spoiled. This time the fly settled between Brokkr's eyes and stung his eyelids, so that blood ran into his eyes and he could not see. He let go of the bellows just long enough to brush the fly away with his hand — and in that moment the bellows stopped and the fire sank. Then the smith came back and said that what was in the forge had come close to being spoiled entirely. He took out a hammer — the hammer that became Thor's, Mjölnir. Because of that moment's pause its handle was rather short; that was its only flaw. Snorri makes the detail plain: the mightiest weapon of the gods was born under the attack of a fly, and its small defect is the mark left by that mischief. Brokkr gathered the three treasures and set off with Loki to Ásgarðr to have the gods judge the wager. On the way, no doubt, Loki was already planning how to keep his head.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 勃洛克带着他的宝物来到阿斯加尔德，洛基也带来了伊瓦尔迪之子的宝物。众神坐上审判的座位，决定由奥丁、索尔和弗雷三位神来裁决，他们说的话就是最后的判决。双方各自把宝物献给这三位神：洛基献给他们伊瓦尔迪之子的作品，勃洛克献给他们埃特里的作品。这是北欧神话里少有的一场“工艺比赛”，评判的标准不是谁的出身更高贵，也不是谁的力气更大，而是哪一件宝物对众神更有用。选出奥丁、索尔和弗雷三位来做裁判，也许是因为每一方的宝物都正好有三件，而每一件都分别送给这三位神中的一位：奥丁得到一件，索尔得到一件，弗雷得到一件。在古代北欧的法律中，重大的争端常常交给公认的裁判或在“庭”上公开裁决，斯诺里的叙述也带着这种色彩：众神像冰岛人在法庭上一样，坐下来听取双方的陈述，然后作出判决。接下来，两边轮流展示宝物。
body_en: Brokkr came to Ásgarðr with his treasures, and Loki brought the treasures of the sons of Ívaldi. The gods took their seats in judgement, and it was agreed that the verdict of Óðinn, Thor and Freyr should stand. Each side presented its treasures to these three: Loki the work of the sons of Ívaldi, Brokkr the work of Eitri. It is a rare 'craft contest' in Norse myth, judged not by birth or strength but by which treasures are more useful to the gods. Óðinn, Thor and Freyr may have been chosen because each side had exactly three treasures, and each treasure went to one of the three — one to Óðinn, one to Thor, one to Freyr. In old Norse law great disputes were often given to acknowledged judges or settled openly at an assembly, and Snorri's account carries that colour: the gods sit down like Icelanders at the Thing, hear both sides and give judgement. Then the two sides present their treasures in turn.
evidence_note: 斯诺里《埃达·诗语法》第35章。

body_zh: 诗歌以对伊南娜的赞美开始：她是掌握可怕神力的女神，身披恐怖，骑在伟大的神力之上。伊南娜手持神圣的阿努纳武器，浑身沾满鲜血，在伟大的战斗中奔驰，把盾牌放在地上，被风暴和洪水所笼罩。伟大的女主人伊南娜，深知如何谋划冲突，她用箭和力量摧毁强大的国度，征服各个地方。在苏美尔人的宗教中，伊南娜是爱与战争的女神，是金星的化身，也是乌鲁克城的守护神。这首颂歌只突出她作为战争女神的一面：她不是温柔的爱人，而是令人畏惧的战士，她的出现就意味着毁灭。“神力”在苏美尔语中叫做“美”，指的是构成文明和宇宙秩序的种种力量与规则，伊南娜被描写成“骑在伟大的神力之上”，说明她掌握着强大的力量。这首诗后来被归于恩赫杜安娜——阿卡德国王萨尔贡的女儿、乌尔的月神女祭司——她是世界上已知最早有名字的作者之一，不过这一归属在学界仍有争议。
body_en: The poem opens in praise of Inana: goddess of the fearsome divine powers, clad in terror, riding on the great divine powers. Inana, holding the holy weapon of the Anuna, drenched in blood, rushes through great battles, her shield resting on the ground, covered in storm and flood. Great lady Inana, knowing well how to plan conflicts, destroys mighty lands with arrow and strength and overpowers lands. In Sumerian religion Inana was goddess of love and war, the planet Venus and patron of Uruk. This hymn stresses only her warrior side: not a tender lover but a fearsome fighter whose coming means destruction. The 'divine powers' — me in Sumerian — are the forces and rules that make up civilisation and the order of the cosmos; Inana 'riding on the great divine powers' shows her command of mighty forces. The poem was later attributed to Enḫeduana, daughter of King Sargon of Akkad and priestess of the moon god at Ur, one of the earliest named authors known in the world, though the attribution is still debated.
evidence_note: 苏美尔文《伊南娜与埃比赫》（ETCSL 1.3.2）开篇颂歌。
uncertainty_note: 本篇按段落定位，不标具体行号；个别诗行残缺或意义不明。

body_zh: 伊南娜站在被毁灭的山上，宣告她的胜利：山脉啊，因为你高耸，因为你巍峨，因为你迷人，因为你美丽，因为你穿着神圣的衣服，因为你伸向天空，因为你没有把鼻子贴到地上，因为你没有用嘴唇亲吻尘土，所以我杀死了你，让你倒下。我像抓住大象一样抓住了你的獠牙，像对付一头巨大的野牛一样，抓住你粗壮的角，把你摔倒在地。我让你感受到了我的力量。接着她说，她在那里建起了神庙、设立了宝座，让她的威名在那里流传。诗的最后一行赞美道：为了毁灭埃比赫，伟大的苏恩之子、少女伊南娜，愿你受到赞美。这篇宣言用一连串“因为”把埃比赫的“罪名”列了出来，其中有许多其实是赞美：高耸、巍峨、美丽，这些都是山的本性。诗人似乎在暗示，埃比赫真正的罪过不是它的美，而是它的骄傲：它以为自己伸向天空，就可以不向女神低头。整首诗从对伊南娜的赞美开始，又以对伊南娜的赞美结束，讲述了一位不容冒犯的女神如何惩罚一座骄傲的山。
body_en: Standing on the ruined mountain, Inana proclaims her victory: Mountain range, because of your elevation, because of your height, because of your attractiveness, because of your beauty, because you wore a holy garment, because you reached up to heaven, because you did not put your nose to the ground, because you did not rub your lips in the dust, I have killed you and brought you low. As one seizes an elephant, I have seized you by your tusks; as with a great wild bull, I have brought you to the ground by your thick horns. I have made you feel my strength. Then she says that she built a temple there and set up a throne, so that her fame would be known there. The last line gives praise: for destroying Ebiḫ, great child of Suen, maiden Inana, be praised. The speech lists Ebiḫ's 'offences' in a string of 'becauses', many of which are really praise — height, loftiness and beauty are simply the mountain's nature. The poet seems to hint that Ebiḫ's real fault was not its beauty but its pride: it thought that reaching to heaven excused it from bowing to the goddess. The poem begins and ends in praise of Inana, telling how a goddess who will not be slighted punishes a proud mountain.
evidence_note: 苏美尔文《伊南娜与埃比赫》（ETCSL 1.3.2）伊南娜的胜利宣言与结尾颂词。
uncertainty_note: 本篇按段落定位，不标具体行号；个别诗行残缺或意义不明。

heading_en: A lion's roar in heaven and on earth
body_zh: 颂歌继续赞美伊南娜：在天上和地上，你像狮子一样吼叫，把人们打倒；你像一头巨大的野牛，在敌对的国度中奔驰；你像一头狮子，用毒液让敌人和反叛者倒下。我的女主人啊，你的手指伸得很长，你的力量令人敬畏。在你的面前，众神都像飞走的鸟一样四散，阿努纳众神像蝙蝠一样飞进裂缝之中，不敢直视你可怕的目光。诗中一连串的比喻——狮子、野牛、风暴、洪水——都在强调伊南娜的力量是无法抵挡的，连其他的神也要在她面前退避。在苏美尔诗歌里，这种连续的比喻和重复是赞美诗的典型写法，诗人用一个个形象叠加起来，营造出一种不断增强的气势。这一部分为后面的故事做了准备：既然伊南娜是这样一位连众神都畏惧的女神，那么一座胆敢不向她低头的山，就犯了不可饶恕的罪。读者也会在后面看到，伊南娜毁灭埃比赫时，用的正是这里所赞美的风暴、洪水和狮子般的力量。
body_en: The hymn goes on: in heaven and on earth you roar like a lion and strike people down; like a huge wild bull you rush through hostile lands; like a lion you make enemies and rebels fall with your venom. My lady, your fingers reach far, your strength inspires awe. Before you the gods scatter like flying birds; the Anuna gods flit like bats into the clefts, not daring to meet your terrible gaze. The string of images — lion, wild bull, storm, flood — insists that Inana's power cannot be withstood, so that even other gods give way before her. In Sumerian poetry such chains of images and repetitions are typical of hymns, the poet heaping figure upon figure to build a rising force. This part prepares the story: since Inana is a goddess even the gods fear, a mountain that dares not bow to her has committed an unforgivable offence. Readers will see later that when Inana destroys Ebiḫ she uses just the storm, flood and lion-like strength praised here.
evidence_note: 苏美尔文《伊南娜与埃比赫》（ETCSL 1.3.2）伊南娜之威的颂歌。
uncertainty_note: 本篇按段落定位，不标具体行号；个别诗行残缺或意义不明。

heading_en: The mountain that would not bow
body_zh: 接着，伊南娜自己开口说话：我，女神，在天上巡行，在地上巡行；我，伊南娜，在天上巡行，在地上巡行，在埃拉姆和苏巴尔图巡行，在卢卢布山区巡行。当我来到群山的中心，当我，女神，走近那座山时，它没有尊敬我；当我，伊南娜，走近那座山时，它没有尊敬我。当我走近埃比赫山时，它没有尊敬我。它没有把鼻子贴到地上，没有用嘴唇去亲吻尘土。在苏美尔人的世界里，“把鼻子贴到地上”“用嘴唇亲吻尘土”是向神或国王表示臣服的姿势。埃比赫山——通常被认为是美索不达米亚东北部的哈姆林山——高耸而美丽，却没有向伊南娜行礼，这对一位以威严著称的女神来说是极大的冒犯。诗人在这里用了重复的手法，把同一句话说了好几遍，既表现了伊南娜的愤怒在一次次加深，也让听众记住了埃比赫的罪名。从神话的角度看，一座山的“不敬”，也许反映了古代美索不达米亚人与东北山地民族之间的冲突。
body_en: Then Inana herself speaks: I, the goddess, was walking around in heaven, walking around on earth; I, Inana, was walking around in heaven and on earth, in Elam and Subir, in the Lulubi mountains. When I came to the heart of the mountains, when I, the goddess, approached the mountain, it showed me no respect; when I, Inana, approached the mountain, it showed me no respect. When I approached the mountain range of Ebiḫ, it showed me no respect. It did not put its nose to the ground for me; it did not rub its lips in the dust for me. In the Sumerian world, putting one's nose to the ground and rubbing one's lips in the dust were gestures of submission to a god or king. Ebiḫ — usually identified with the Jebel Hamrin in north-eastern Mesopotamia — lofty and beautiful, did not bow to Inana, a grave affront to a goddess famed for her majesty. The poet repeats the same words several times, showing Inana's anger growing and fixing Ebiḫ's offence in the listeners' minds. Mythically, a mountain's 'disrespect' may reflect conflicts between the people of Mesopotamia and the peoples of the north-eastern highlands.

body_zh: 伊南娜接着发誓：我要让恐怖充满这座高耸的山脉。我要在它的面前立起攻城锤，在它的身边放上战斧；我要在它的山坡上挑起战斗，准备好箭和箭袋；我要让它的森林燃起大火，用斧子惩罚它的罪恶；我要让净化之神吉比尔在它的水道中施行他的工作。我要在那难以接近的山脉中散布恐怖。就像一座被安诅咒的城市，它将不会被重建；就像一座被恩利尔怒视的城市，它将永远不能再抬起头来。这段誓言里出现了苏美尔的两位最高神：天神安和风暴之神恩利尔。伊南娜把她要毁灭的埃比赫，比作被这两位大神诅咒的城市，说明她认为自己有权像最高的神一样施行惩罚。吉比尔是火神，诗中让他“在水道中施行工作”，可能是指用火烧毁山中的一切。这段誓言充满了战争的意象，让人想起美索不达米亚国王们征伐山地时的铭文。可是伊南娜并没有立刻行动，在出发之前，她还要先去见她的父亲安。
body_en: Inana goes on to vow: I shall fill the soaring mountain range with my terror. Against its flanks I shall set battering rams, against its sides I shall set axes; I shall raise battle on its slopes and make ready arrows and quivers; I shall set fire to its thick forests and take an axe to its evil deeds; I shall make Gibil, the purifier, do his work at its watercourses. I shall spread terror through the inaccessible mountain range. Like a city cursed by An, it will not be restored; like a city on which Enlil has frowned, may it never again lift up its neck. The vow names two of the highest Sumerian gods, An of the sky and Enlil of the storm; Inana likens Ebiḫ to a city cursed by them, claiming the right to punish as the highest gods do. Gibil is the fire god; having him 'work at its watercourses' may mean burning everything in the mountains. The vow is full of the imagery of war, recalling the inscriptions of Mesopotamian kings campaigning in the highlands. Yet Inana does not act at once; before she sets out, she will go to her father An.

body_zh: 月神苏恩的女儿伊南娜穿上了她的衣服，披上了王后的服饰，让喜悦笼罩全身。她在额头上戴上了恐怖与光芒，在神圣的脖子上戴上了红玉髓的花饰，手里握着七个头的权杖，那是她的战斗武器。她在黎明时出发，踏上了青金石的台阶。伊南娜的盛装在苏美尔文学中常常是一个重要的场景：在《伊南娜下冥界》里，她穿戴七件神力出发；在这里，她的打扮同样充满了力量的象征。“恐怖与光芒”是苏美尔诗歌中神的特有属性，被称为“尼”与“美拉姆”，表示神那令人畏惧的光辉。红玉髓和青金石是美索不达米亚最珍贵的宝石，它们常常来自遥远的东方山地——讽刺的是，伊南娜要征伐的，正是这样出产宝石的山区。七个头的权杖则强调她作为战神的身份。诗中说她是“苏恩的女儿”，这是苏美尔传统中常见的说法；在其他传统中，伊南娜也被说成是安的女儿。这首诗里，她称安为“父亲”，两种说法都保留着。
body_en: Inana, daughter of Suen, put on her garments, the garments of queenship, and wrapped herself in joy. She placed terror and radiance on her brow, set rosettes of carnelian around her holy neck, and grasped the seven-headed mace, her weapon of battle. At dawn she set out and placed her foot upon the lapis lazuli steps. Inana's adornment is often a key scene in Sumerian literature: in Inana's Descent she sets out wearing seven divine powers; here too her dress is full of the symbols of power. 'Terror and radiance' — ni and melam in Sumerian — are the particular attributes of the gods, their awe-inspiring splendour. Carnelian and lapis lazuli were the most precious stones in Mesopotamia, often brought from the distant eastern highlands — and ironically it is just such stone-yielding mountains that Inana sets out to conquer. The seven-headed mace marks her as a war goddess. The poem calls her 'daughter of Suen', the moon god, a common Sumerian tradition; elsewhere Inana is said to be the daughter of An. In this poem she calls An her father, and both traditions stand side by side.

body_zh: 伊南娜来到天神安的面前，在他面前俯伏下拜，然后对他说：我的父亲安，我向你致敬！请听我的话。安让我在天上令人畏惧，让我在大地上令人敬畏。在众神的居所中，我是最出众的；在阿努纳众神中，我是最强大的。可是那埃比赫山，当我走近它时，它没有尊敬我；它没有把鼻子贴到地上，没有用嘴唇亲吻尘土。让我去对付它吧，让我用我的力量让它屈服，让它知道我的威严。在苏美尔的众神中，安是天空之神，是众神之父和最古老的神之一，他的神庙在乌鲁克，与伊南娜的神庙伊安那相邻。“伊安那”这个名字本身的意思就是“安的房子”。在神话中，安常常是一位遥远而威严的长者，众神遇到大事时要向他请示。伊南娜在出征之前专程来见安，表明她虽然自信，却仍然尊重天神的权威，希望得到他的认可。这一幕也为下一章安的警告做了铺垫：这位最古老的神，对伊南娜的计划有着不同的看法。
body_en: Inana came before An, the sky god, prostrated herself before him and said: My father An, I greet you! Hear my words. An has made me terrifying in heaven, awesome on earth. Among the dwellings of the gods I am foremost; among the Anuna gods I am mightiest. But Ebiḫ — when I approached it, it showed me no respect; it did not put its nose to the ground nor rub its lips in the dust for me. Let me deal with it; let me bring it low with my power and make it know my majesty. Among the Sumerian gods An is god of the sky, father of the gods and one of the oldest of them; his temple stood at Uruk beside Inana's temple, the Eanna — a name meaning 'House of An'. In myth An is often a distant, majestic elder whom the gods consult on great matters. That Inana comes to him before her campaign shows that, confident as she is, she still respects the sky god's authority and seeks his approval. The scene prepares An's warning in the next chapter: the oldest of the gods sees her plan differently.
evidence_note: 苏美尔文《伊南娜与埃比赫》（ETCSL 1.3.2）伊南娜向安请求。

body_zh: 众神之王安回答她说：我的小女儿要求毁灭那座山——她要去做什么？伊南娜要求毁灭那座山——她要去做什么？她要求毁灭埃比赫——她要去做什么？那座山让可怕的恐怖降落在众神的居所，让恐惧散布在阿努纳众神神圣的住处。它的威严和光芒令人畏惧，它的荣耀遍及四方。它的果实沉甸甸地垂下，繁茂的植物生长着；它的森林里有狮子，有野公羊和雄鹿，有野牛在草地上吃草，有鹿在林中交配。你无法穿过它可怕的地方，那里的恐怖令人生畏。年轻的女子啊，你无法对付它。安的这番话很有意思：他并没有说埃比赫没有冒犯伊南娜，也没有说伊南娜无权惩罚它，而是提醒她，这座山本身就拥有强大的力量，连众神都惧怕它。他描写山中丰美的果实和成群的野兽，既是在警告伊南娜，也像是在赞美这座山。在苏美尔诗歌里，长者的劝告常常被年轻的英雄或女神拒绝——在《吉尔伽美什与胡瓦瓦》中，吉尔伽美什也不顾劝阻前往雪松林。安的警告在这里成了伊南娜愤怒的导火索。
body_en: An, king of the gods, answered her: my little one demands the mountain's destruction — what is she taking on? Inana demands the mountain's destruction — what is she taking on? The young woman demands the destruction of Ebiḫ — what is she taking on? That mountain has made fearsome terror fall on the dwellings of the gods; it has spread fear through the holy places of the Anuna. Its terror and radiance are awesome, its glory spreads abroad. Its fruits hang heavy, its luxuriant growth flourishes; in its forests are lions, wild rams and stags, wild bulls grazing in the meadows, deer mating among the trees. You cannot pass through its fearsome places; its terror is dreadful. Young woman, you cannot go against it. An's words are striking: he does not say Ebiḫ has not offended Inana, nor that she has no right to punish it; he warns her that the mountain itself is mighty, feared even by the gods. His picture of its rich fruit and teeming beasts is both a warning and almost a praise of the mountain. In Sumerian poetry an elder's counsel is often refused by a young hero or goddess — in Gilgameš and Ḫuwawa Gilgameš too sets out for the Cedar Forest against advice. Here An's warning only kindles Inana's anger.

body_zh: 安这样说完，女主人伊南娜在愤怒和狂怒之中，打开了战斗之屋的大门，推开了青金石的城门。她带出了伟大的战斗，召来了巨大的洪水，掀起了邪恶的风暴，让大雨与狂风一同扑向埃比赫。她用可怕的光芒覆盖了它，用恐怖笼罩了它，像风暴一样向它席卷而去。在这一段里，伊南娜不再请求，而是行动。前面颂歌中赞美的风暴、洪水和狮子般的力量，现在全都化成了对埃比赫的攻击。苏美尔诗歌中，神的愤怒常常被描写成自然的灾难：风暴、洪水、火焰；伊南娜作为战争女神，同时也掌握着这些自然力量。青金石城门和战斗之屋的意象，让人想起神庙和城市的防御工事，伊南娜像一位国王一样，从自己的城中出发，率领着无形的大军前去征讨。安的警告没有让她退缩，反而让她更加愤怒：她要证明，就算是连众神都畏惧的山，也必须向她低头。泥板在这一部分有一些残缺，个别诗句的意思不完全清楚，本篇只讲能读通的部分，不补写残缺处。
body_en: When An had spoken, the lady, in her rage and anger, opened the gate of the house of battle and pushed open the lapis lazuli door. She brought out the great battle, summoned the great flood, and raised an evil storm, sending rain and gale together against Ebiḫ. She covered it with fearsome radiance, wrapped it in terror and swept down on it like a storm. Here Inana no longer asks; she acts. The storm, flood and lion-like strength praised in the opening hymn now all turn into an assault on Ebiḫ. In Sumerian poetry divine wrath is often pictured as natural disaster — storm, flood, fire — and Inana, as war goddess, commands these forces too. The lapis lazuli door and the house of battle recall the defences of temples and cities: like a king, Inana sets out from her own city at the head of an invisible army. An's warning has not held her back but only fed her anger: she will prove that even a mountain the gods fear must bow to her. The tablets are somewhat broken in this part, and some lines are not wholly clear; this retelling follows only what can be read and does not fill the gaps.
evidence_note: 苏美尔文《伊南娜与埃比赫》（ETCSL 1.3.2）对埃比赫的进攻。

body_zh: 伊南娜抓住了埃比赫的脖子，像割下一把草一样；她把匕首的利齿刺进它的内部，像雷声一样吼叫。构成埃比赫身体的石头从山坡上哗啦啦地滚落下来，从山的侧面和裂缝里，巨大的蛇吐出毒液。她诅咒了它的森林，咒骂了它的树木，用干旱让它的橡树枯死，在它的山坡上倾倒火焰，让浓烟笼罩着它。女神在这座山上确立了她的权威。在这一段里，诗人把一座山写成了一个有生命的敌人：它有脖子、有内脏，它的石头像骨头一样崩落。这种把自然地貌人格化的写法在苏美尔文学中很常见，山在这里既是一个地方，也是一个与女神对抗的对手。曾经被安描写得果实丰美、草木繁茂的埃比赫，现在只剩下干旱、火焰和浓烟。从现实的角度看，这首诗可能反映了美索不达米亚王国对东北山区的军事征伐，伊南娜作为战争女神，被看作这些征伐的神圣保护者。可是在诗中，这一切都被写成了女神个人的愤怒与胜利：一座山的命运，取决于它是否向女神低头。
body_en: Inana seized Ebiḫ by the neck as one cuts grass; she pressed the teeth of the dagger into its interior and roared like thunder. The stones that formed Ebiḫ's body came clattering down its flanks, and from its sides and crevices great serpents spat venom. She cursed its forests and damned its trees; she killed its oaks with drought, poured fire on its slopes and made its smoke dense. The goddess established her authority over the mountain. Here the poet makes a mountain into a living enemy: it has a neck and an inner body, and its stones fall away like bones. Personifying the landscape is common in Sumerian literature; the mountain is both a place and an adversary who stands against the goddess. Ebiḫ, which An had described as rich in fruit and luxuriant growth, is left with only drought, fire and smoke. Historically the poem may reflect the campaigns of Mesopotamian kingdoms against the north-eastern highlands, Inana as war goddess being seen as their divine patron. But in the poem all of it is the goddess's own anger and victory: a mountain's fate depends on whether it bows to her.

body_zh: KTU 1.3 第一栏开头，风暴之神强大的巴力坐在宴席上。侍者拉德马努侍奉他，在他面前切肉，用刀割下肥美的牛胸，然后站起来，给他斟酒，把一只杯子放进他的手里，一只大杯子，大得要用双手捧着——那是一只连女人都没见过、连阿西拉特都没见过的杯子。一千坛酒倒进这只杯子里，一万坛酒混在一起调和。一位歌手站起来唱歌，声音美妙，手里敲着钹，唱的是英俊的少年巴力在萨方山的高处。这一段写的是巴力最得意的时刻：在前一块泥板里，他刚刚用工匠之神为他造的两根棍棒打败了海神雅姆，成为众神之中的胜利者。宴会上的大杯、千坛美酒和歌手的歌声，都是在庆祝他的胜利和他的王权。可是在这片欢乐之中，有一件事情让巴力不满：他虽然得到了王权，却还没有一座属于自己的宫殿。这个问题将贯穿整整两块泥板。乌加里特的诗歌常常用排比的诗句来描写宴会，一句说一千，下一句说一万，这是古代迦南诗歌的典型风格。
body_en: At the opening of KTU 1.3, column I, Mightiest Baal the storm god sits at a feast. His servant Radmanu waits on him, carving before him, cutting the breast of a fatling with a knife; then he rises, pours drink, and puts a cup into his hands — a great cup, held in both hands, a cup no woman has seen, not even Athirat. A thousand jars of wine go into it, ten thousand are mixed in the mixing. A singer rises and sings in a sweet voice, clashing cymbals, singing of the gracious youth Baal on the heights of Saphon. It is Baal's proudest moment: on the preceding tablet he has defeated Yamm the Sea with the two clubs the craftsman god made for him and become victor among the gods. The great cup, the thousand jars and the singer celebrate his victory and kingship. Yet amid the joy one thing troubles Baal: though he has won kingship, he has no palace of his own. That question runs through two whole tablets. Ugaritic poetry often describes feasts in parallel lines — one line says a thousand, the next ten thousand — the typical style of ancient Canaanite verse.
evidence_note: 乌加里特巴力史诗泥板 KTU 1.3 第一栏。
uncertainty_note: 泥板此处有残缺，栏次划分与断句据现代学者的整理，残缺处不补写。

body_zh: 第四栏里，阿西拉特吩咐她的仆人、渔夫库德什-瓦-阿姆鲁尔：给驴套上鞍子，给驴装上银子的缰绳，金子的鞍具，为我的母驴备好鞍子。库德什-瓦-阿姆鲁尔照着做了。他把阿西拉特扶上驴背，自己像火炬一样走在前面，少女阿娜特跟在后面，巴力则回到了萨方山的高处。阿西拉特来到伊勒那里，在两条河的源头，在两个深渊的泉水之间。她揭开伊勒的帐幕，走进君王、万物之父的居所。她跪在伊勒脚下，俯伏下拜，向他致敬。伊勒看见她，脸上露出了笑容，他把脚放在脚凳上，打了个响指，提高声音说：海上的女王阿西拉特为什么来了？众神的创造者为什么到这里来了？你饿了吗？你走了这么远的路。你渴了吗？你走了一整夜。吃吧，喝吧！桌上有食物，杯中有酒，金杯里有葡萄的血。难道是君王伊勒的爱让你动了心？公牛的情意让你思念了吗？这一段把伊勒写得非常亲切：这位年迈的众神之父看见妻子远道而来，又惊又喜，殷勤地请她吃喝，还开玩笑地问她是不是想念他了。
body_en: In column IV Athirat bids her servant, the fisherman Qodesh-wa-Amrur: saddle the donkey, harness the ass, put on the trappings of silver, the gear of gold, make ready my she-ass. Qodesh-wa-Amrur obeys. He sets Athirat on the donkey's back and goes before her like a torch, the maiden Anat following behind, while Baal returns to the heights of Saphon. Athirat comes to El at the source of the rivers, amid the springs of the two deeps. She opens El's tent and enters the dwelling of the King, Father of Years. At El's feet she bows down and falls prostrate, honouring him. El sees her and smiles; he sets his feet on the footstool, snaps his fingers and lifts his voice: why has Lady Athirat of the Sea come? Why has the creatress of the gods come here? Are you hungry from your journey? Are you thirsty from travelling all night? Eat, drink! There is food on the table, wine in the cups, the blood of the vine in golden goblets. Or has the love of King El stirred you, the affection of the Bull aroused you? The passage paints El with warmth: the aged father of the gods, surprised and pleased to see his wife come so far, presses food and drink on her and teases her whether she has missed him.

body_zh: 阿西拉特回答伊勒说：伊勒啊，你的命令是英明的，你的智慧与永恒同在，你的命令带来幸运的生活。我们的王是强大的巴力，我们的审判者，没有人在他之上。我们都要为他捧杯，都要为他端碗。可是他在哀叹：巴力没有像众神那样的房子，没有像阿西拉特的儿子们那样的庭院。仁慈的伊勒，慈悲的神回答说：难道我是一个奴隶，阿西拉特是一个女仆，要我拿着泥铲做砖吗？让人为巴力建一座像众神那样的房子，像阿西拉特的儿子们那样的庭院吧。阿西拉特高兴地说：伊勒啊，你是伟大的，你的白发给了你智慧。现在巴力将按时降下他的雨水，按季节降下浓雾和雪；他将在云中发出他的声音，向大地闪耀他的闪电。让人为他建一座雪松的房子，一座砖砌的房子吧。在这一段里，伊勒终于答应了巴力的请求，而说服他的，正是阿西拉特对巴力王权的承认。伊勒那句“难道我是奴隶”的反问也很有趣：他的意思是，建房子是工匠们的事，他只需要下令就够了。巴力的宫殿与雨水的关系在这里第一次被说明：有了宫殿，巴力才能按时降雨，大地才会丰收。
body_en: Athirat answers El: your decree, El, is wise, your wisdom is with eternity, your command brings a fortunate life. Our king is Mightiest Baal, our judge, and there is none above him. All of us will bear his cup, all of us bear his bowl. Yet he laments: Baal has no house like the gods, no court like the sons of Athirat. Kindly El, the Compassionate, answers: am I a slave, is Athirat a handmaid, that I should hold the trowel and make bricks? Let a house be built for Baal like the gods, a court like the sons of Athirat. Athirat rejoices: you are great, El, your grey hair has made you wise. Now Baal will appoint the time of his rain, the season of mist and snow; he will give his voice in the clouds and flash his lightning to the earth. Let a house of cedar be built for him, a house of bricks. Here El at last grants Baal's request, and what persuades him is Athirat's acknowledgement of Baal's kingship. El's retort 'am I a slave?' is amusing: building is the craftsmen's business; he need only give the order. The link between Baal's palace and the rain is stated here for the first time: with a palace, Baal can send the rain in its season and the earth will bear.

body_zh: 阿娜特高兴得跳了起来，奔向萨方山，对巴力说：好消息，巴力！你将有一座像你的兄弟们那样的房子，一座像你的亲族们那样的庭院。去召集山上的商队吧，让他们带来金子和银子，带来最好的宝石。巴力欢喜极了，派人把工匠科塔尔-瓦-哈西斯请来，摆上宴席款待他。宴后，巴力吩咐他尽快建造房子。科塔尔说：听我说，强大的巴力，让我在这座房子里开一扇窗户，在宫殿当中开一个窗口。巴力说：不要在房子里开窗户，不要在宫殿当中开窗口。泥板在这里有残缺，巴力拒绝的理由没有完全保存下来，学者们根据残存的字句推测，他担心自己的女儿皮德拉伊和塔莱，也可能是担心海神雅姆借此进入宫殿。科塔尔说：你会回心转意的，巴力，你会再想起我的话。这场关于窗户的争论，成了整个故事最后的悬念：窗户是巴力发出雷声和降下雨水的通道，没有窗户，巴力的力量就无法传到大地上。工匠早已看出这一点，巴力却还要经过一番征战，才会明白过来。
body_en: Anat leaps for joy and speeds to Saphon, telling Baal: good news, Baal! You shall have a house like your brothers, a court like your kin. Summon the caravans of the mountains; let them bring gold and silver and the choicest gems. Baal rejoices and sends for the craftsman Kothar-wa-Khasis, setting a feast before him; after the feast he bids him build the house quickly. Kothar says: listen, Mightiest Baal — let me put a window in the house, a casement in the midst of the palace. Baal says: do not put a window in the house, nor a casement in the midst of the palace. The tablet is broken here, and Baal's reason is not fully preserved; from the surviving words scholars infer that he feared for his daughters Pidray and Tallay, or perhaps that Yamm the Sea might enter by it. Kothar says: you will come back to my word, Baal; you will think again of what I said. The dispute over the window becomes the last suspense of the tale: the window is the channel through which Baal sends thunder and rain; without it his power cannot reach the earth. The craftsman sees this at once; Baal will understand only after a campaign of conquest.

body_zh: 第六栏接着讲房子的建造。人们去黎巴嫩和它的树林，去西里翁山和它最好的雪松，砍下木材。然后，火被放进房子里，火焰被放进宫殿中。第一天，第二天，火在房子里燃烧，火焰在宫殿中吞噬；第三天，第四天，火在房子里燃烧，火焰在宫殿中吞噬；第五天，第六天，火在房子里燃烧，火焰在宫殿中吞噬。到了第七天，火离开了房子，火焰离开了宫殿：银子变成了板，金子变成了砖。强大的巴力欢喜地说：我用银子建造了我的房子，用金子建造了我的宫殿。巴力为宫殿举行了盛大的宴会：他宰杀了牛和羊，宰杀了公牛和肥牛犊、一岁的羊羔和小山羊。他请来了他的兄弟们和亲族，请来了阿西拉特的七十个儿子，给他们斟上葡萄酒：给公羊神斟满杯，给母羊女神斟满碗，给公牛神斟满杯，给母牛女神斟满碗。这一段用“第一天、第二天……第七天”的排比，营造出一种庄严的节奏，学者们常把它与古代近东其他“七日”主题的文献相比较。火中炼成金银之屋的奇迹，说明这座宫殿不是凡人的建筑，而是神圣的作品。
body_en: Column VI goes on with the building. They go to Lebanon and its trees, to Sirion and its choicest cedars, and cut timber. Then fire is set in the house, flame in the palace. On the first day and the second, fire burns in the house, flame consumes in the palace; on the third day and the fourth, fire burns in the house, flame consumes in the palace; on the fifth day and the sixth, fire burns in the house, flame consumes in the palace. On the seventh day the fire leaves the house, the flame leaves the palace: the silver has turned into plates, the gold into bricks. Mightiest Baal rejoices: my house I have built of silver, my palace of gold. Baal holds a great feast for the palace: he slaughters oxen and sheep, bulls and fatted calves, yearling lambs and kids. He invites his brothers and his kin, the seventy sons of Athirat, and pours them wine: to the ram-gods cups of wine, to the ewe-goddesses bowls; to the bull-gods cups, to the cow-goddesses bowls. The repeated 'first day, second day … seventh day' gives the passage a solemn rhythm, and scholars often compare it with other ancient Near Eastern texts on the seven-day pattern. A house of silver and gold refined in fire shows that the palace is no mortal building but a divine work.

body_zh: 第七栏里，巴力离开宫殿，从一座城走到另一座城，从一个镇走到另一个镇，夺取了六十六座城、七十七个镇。然后他回到了自己的房子，对工匠科塔尔-瓦-哈西斯说：我要开窗了，科塔尔，就在今天；让人在房子里开一扇窗，在宫殿当中开一个窗口。科塔尔笑了，提高声音说：我不是早就告诉过你了吗，强大的巴力，你会回心转意的！他在房子里开了一扇窗，在宫殿中开了一个窗口。巴力从云中打开一道裂缝，发出他神圣的声音，巴力的嘴唇一张一合，他的声音让大地震动，群山颤抖，东方和西方的高处都在摇晃。巴力的敌人们逃进了森林，他的对手们躲进了山坡。巴力说：无论是王还是非王，谁能在这片土地上建立统治？我要派一位使者去见伊勒之子穆特，去见伊勒的宠儿、英雄。第八栏里，他吩咐使者古帕努和乌加尔前往穆特的城市，那里的宝座叫“深坑”，那里的土地叫“污秽”，警告他们不要走近穆特，免得被他像羊羔一样放进嘴里。窗户终于打开，巴力的雷声传遍大地；而他向死神发出的宣告，则引出了下一块泥板里巴力与穆特之间更加凶险的斗争。
body_en: In column VII Baal leaves the palace and goes from city to city, town to town, seizing sixty-six cities, seventy-seven towns. Then he returns to his house and says to Kothar-wa-Khasis: I will put it in, Kothar, this very day; let a window be opened in the house, a casement in the midst of the palace. Kothar laughs and lifts his voice: did I not tell you, Mightiest Baal, that you would come back to my word? He opens a window in the house, a casement in the palace. Baal opens a rift in the clouds and gives forth his holy voice; Baal's lips open and shut, and at his voice the earth quakes, the mountains tremble, the high places east and west shake. Baal's enemies flee to the forests, his foes to the mountainsides. Baal says: king or no king, who shall establish dominion in the land? I will send a messenger to Mot, son of El, to the Beloved, the Hero. In column VIII he sends Gupn and Ugar to Mot's city, whose throne is called 'Pit' and whose land is 'Filth', warning them not to come near Mot lest he put them in his mouth like a lamb. The window opens at last and Baal's thunder spreads over the earth; and his message to Death leads to the far more perilous struggle between Baal and Mot on the next tablets.

body_zh: 第二栏讲巴力的妹妹、少女阿娜特。她关上宫殿的大门，在两座城之间的山谷里大战，杀死了海边的人，消灭了日出之处的人。在她脚下，人头像球一样滚动，人手像蝗虫一样飞散。她把人头绑在背上，把人手系在腰带上，在战士的血中蹚到膝盖，在士兵的血污中蹚到脖子。她用棍棒驱赶俘虏，用弓弦拉开敌阵。然后她回到自己的宫中，可是战斗还没有让她满足，她把椅子当作战士，把桌子当作士兵，把脚凳当作英雄，又一次厮杀起来。她的心中充满了欢乐，肝脏里满是喜悦。最后，她用天上的露水和地上的油脂洗净双手——那是驾云者巴力降下的雨水。这一段是古代近东文学中最著名、也最令人震撼的战斗描写之一，学者们对阿娜特战斗的对象和意义有许多不同的看法：有人认为这是一种仪式的象征，有人认为它表现的是战神的本性。本篇只按泥板的文字讲述，不加评判。值得注意的是，这位凶猛的女神最后用的是巴力的雨水来洗手，暗示了她与巴力之间亲密的联系。
body_en: Column II tells of Baal's sister, the maiden Anat. She shuts the gates of her house and fights in the valley between two towns; she smites the people of the seashore and destroys the men of the sunrise. Under her, heads roll like balls, hands fly like locusts. She binds heads to her back and ties hands to her belt; she wades knee-deep in warriors' blood, neck-deep in the gore of soldiers. With her club she drives captives, with her bowstring the foe. Then she returns to her house, but the fighting has not sated her: she makes chairs into warriors, tables into soldiers, footstools into heroes, and fights again. Her heart swells with joy, her liver with gladness. At last she washes her hands in the dew of heaven and the oil of earth — the rain the Rider of the Clouds pours down. It is one of the most famous and startling battle descriptions in ancient Near Eastern literature, and scholars differ widely on whom Anat fights and what it means — some see a ritual symbol, others the nature of a war goddess. This retelling follows the tablet without judging. Notably the fierce goddess washes her hands at last in Baal's rain, a hint of her close bond with him.

body_zh: 第三栏里，巴力派他的两个使者古帕努和乌加尔去找阿娜特。他吩咐他们说：你们去对少女阿娜特、对民族的嫂子说：强大的巴力的话，最强者的话是这样的——把战争从大地上除去，在土地上放下爱情，在大地的中心浇上和平，在田野里洒满爱意。快来吧，赶到我这里来，因为我有一句话要告诉你，一件事要对你说：那是树木的话语，石头的低语，天空对大地、深渊对星辰的叹息。我懂得闪电，那是天空不知道的；那是人们不知道的话语，大地上的众人不懂得的。来吧，我会把它揭示出来，在我的山上，在萨方山的圣地，在我继承的山上，在美好的地方，在力量之山上。这段话是乌加里特诗歌中最优美的段落之一。巴力要阿娜特放下武器，把战场变成充满爱与和平的土地；他所说的“树木的话语、石头的低语”，被许多学者理解为雷声和闪电——风暴之神特有的语言。这也预示了后面的结局：巴力最终要在自己的宫殿里，通过窗户发出他的雷声。
body_en: In column III Baal sends his two messengers, Gupn and Ugar, to Anat. He tells them: say to the maiden Anat, to the sister-in-law of the peoples: the word of Mightiest Baal, the speech of the Mightiest of Warriors — remove war from the earth, set love in the land, pour peace into the heart of the earth, rain love on the fields. Hurry, hasten to me, for I have a word to tell you, a message to recount to you: the word of the tree and the whisper of the stone, the sighing of the heavens to the earth, of the deeps to the stars. I understand the lightning which the heavens do not know, a word that men do not know, nor the multitudes of the earth understand. Come, and I will reveal it, in the midst of my mountain, divine Saphon, in the holy place, on the mountain of my inheritance, in the pleasant place, on the hill of might. This is among the loveliest passages of Ugaritic poetry. Baal asks Anat to lay down her weapons and turn the battlefield into a land of love and peace; his 'word of the tree and whisper of the stone' is taken by many scholars to mean thunder and lightning — the storm god's own language. It also foreshadows the end: Baal will at last send his thunder through the window of his own palace.

body_zh: 阿娜特看见两位使者走来，双脚发抖，腰部打颤，脸上流汗。她问：古帕努和乌加尔为什么来了？是什么敌人起来反对巴力了？是什么对手要攻击驾云者了？难道我没有打败伊勒宠爱的雅姆吗？难道我没有消灭河神纳哈尔吗？难道我没有捆住巨龙图南、给它戴上嘴套吗？我打败了那扭曲的蛇，那七个头的沙利亚特；我打败了伊勒宠爱的阿尔什，消灭了伊勒的小牛阿提克，打败了伊勒的母狗伊沙特，消灭了伊勒的女儿兹巴布。我为了金子而战斗，赶走了那个要把巴力从萨方山的高处赶下去的人。是什么敌人起来反对巴力了？两位使者回答说：没有敌人起来反对巴力，没有对手攻击驾云者。他们转达了巴力的话。阿娜特于是放下一切，奔向萨方山。巴力远远地看见妹妹走来，就打发女人们离开，在她面前摆上一头牛，为她举行宴会。阿娜特列出的这一长串被她打败的敌人，是乌加里特神话中许多已经失传的故事的线索；其中的雅姆与图南，也出现在巴力的故事里，不同文本中由谁打败它们，说法并不一致。
body_en: When Anat saw the two messengers coming, her feet shook, her loins trembled, her face sweated. She asked: why have Gupn and Ugar come? What enemy has risen against Baal, what foe against the Rider of the Clouds? Did I not destroy Yamm, beloved of El? Did I not finish off River, the great god? Did I not muzzle the dragon Tunnan? I destroyed the twisting serpent, Shalyat of the seven heads; I destroyed Arsh, beloved of El, finished off Atik, the calf of El, destroyed Ishat, the bitch of El, finished off Dhabub, daughter of El. I fought for gold and drove out him who would drive Baal from the heights of Saphon. What enemy has risen against Baal? The messengers answered: no enemy has risen against Baal, no foe against the Rider of the Clouds — and they gave Baal's message. Anat set everything aside and sped to Saphon. Baal saw his sister coming from afar, sent the women away and set an ox before her for a feast. Anat's long list of defeated foes is a thread to many lost Ugaritic myths; Yamm and Tunnan also appear in Baal's own story, and the texts do not agree on who defeated them.

body_zh: 在萨方山上，巴力向阿娜特说出了他的苦恼：巴力没有像众神那样的房子，没有像阿西拉特的儿子们那样的庭院。伊勒的住所是他儿子的庇护所，女王阿西拉特的住所是她女儿们的庇护所，皮德拉伊、塔莱和阿尔萨伊——巴力的三个女儿——也都寄住在别人那里。阿娜特听了，说：我要去见公牛伊勒，我的父亲。如果他不给巴力一座房子，我就要像拖羊羔一样把他拖到地上，让他的白发流满鲜血，让他的白胡子沾满血污。她来到伊勒的住处，在两条河的源头，在两个深渊的泉水中间。她闯进伊勒的帐幕，伊勒在七个房间深处、八道门后面回答她：我知道你，我的女儿，女神们中间没有像你这样不受约束的。你想要什么，少女阿娜特？阿娜特说：伊勒啊，你的命令是英明的，你的智慧是永恒的。我们的王是强大的巴力，我们的审判者，没有人在他之上。可是巴力没有像众神那样的房子。泥板在这里有残缺，伊勒的回答没有保存下来；从后文看，阿娜特的威胁没有成功，巴力还需要另一位女神来为他说情。
body_en: On Saphon Baal tells Anat his grief: Baal has no house like the gods, no court like the sons of Athirat. The dwelling of El is the shelter of his son, the dwelling of Lady Athirat the shelter of her daughters; Pidray, Tallay and Arsay — Baal's three daughters — live under others' roofs. Hearing this, Anat says: I will go to Bull El, my father. If he does not give Baal a house, I will drag him like a lamb to the ground, make his grey hair run with blood, his grey beard with gore. She comes to El at the source of the two rivers, amid the springs of the two deeps, and bursts into his tent. From seven chambers within, through eight doors, El answers her: I know you, my daughter; there is none so unrestrained among the goddesses. What do you desire, maiden Anat? Anat says: your decree, El, is wise, your wisdom everlasting. Our king is Mightiest Baal, our judge, and there is none above him. Yet Baal has no house like the gods. The tablet is broken here, and El's answer is lost; from what follows, Anat's threat did not succeed, and Baal will need another goddess to plead for him.

body_zh: 第六栏里，一位使者被派去寻找工匠之神科塔尔-瓦-哈西斯，意思是“灵巧而聪慧的神”。使者要穿过一千里，一万里，越过海洋和许多地方，去到卡夫托尔——科塔尔的宝座所在之地，去到希克普特——他继承的土地。科塔尔在乌加里特神话中是一位伟大的工匠，前一块泥板里，正是他为巴力打造了打败雅姆的两根棍棒。他住在遥远的海外，学者们一般认为“卡夫托尔”指克里特岛，“希克普特”指埃及的孟菲斯，那里正是工匠之神普塔的城市。这样的地理安排说明，在乌加里特人眼中，最好的工艺来自克里特和埃及。泥板的这一部分残缺较多，派遣使者的具体经过不完全清楚；从下一块泥板的开头来看，巴力和阿娜特最终决定先用工匠打造的礼物去打动众神之母阿西拉特，请她到伊勒那里去说情。这是一个聪明的计划：既然威胁不起作用，就用礼物和说情来赢得父亲的同意。
body_en: In column VI a messenger is sent to find the craftsman god Kothar-wa-Khasis, 'Skilful-and-Wise'. The messenger must cross a thousand fields, ten thousand acres, over the sea and many lands, to Kaphtor, the throne where Kothar sits, to Hikpat, the land of his inheritance. Kothar is the great craftsman of Ugaritic myth; on the earlier tablet he made the two clubs with which Baal defeated Yamm. He lives far across the sea; scholars generally take Kaphtor to be Crete and Hikpat to be Memphis in Egypt — the very city of the craftsman god Ptah. The geography shows that, to the people of Ugarit, the finest craft came from Crete and Egypt. This part of the tablet is badly broken, and the details of the mission are not wholly clear; from the opening of the next tablet, Baal and Anat decide first to win over Athirat, mother of the gods, with gifts made by the craftsman, and to ask her to plead with El. It is a shrewd plan: since threats have failed, gifts and intercession may win the father's consent.

body_zh: KTU 1.4 第一栏又一次重复了巴力的哀叹：巴力没有像众神那样的房子，没有像阿西拉特的儿子们那样的庭院。接着，工匠之神科塔尔-瓦-哈西斯走到风箱前，拿起钳子，熔化了银子，倒出了金子。他为众神之母阿西拉特打造礼物：他熔了几千舍客勒的银子，几万舍客勒的金子，打造出一个神圣的宝座，一个用金子做的脚凳，一张用金子装饰的床，一张满是各种动物装饰的桌子，还有来自阿穆鲁地区的碗盏，碗上装饰着像亚姆鲁地区的野兽一样的图案，数以万计。这些礼物被描写得极为华丽，诗句一再强调金银的数量之多，工艺之精。阿西拉特是伊勒的妻子，是众神之母，她的儿子们——七十位神——都住在自己的房子里；而巴力要请她帮忙，就必须先送上配得上她身份的厚礼。在乌加里特社会中，向有权势的人送礼求情是常见的做法，神话中的众神也遵循着同样的规矩。这一段也让我们看到了科塔尔的手艺：他能把金银变成任何东西，后来巴力的宫殿也将由他建造。
body_en: Column I of KTU 1.4 repeats Baal's lament: Baal has no house like the gods, no court like the sons of Athirat. Then the craftsman Kothar-wa-Khasis goes to the bellows, takes the tongs, melts silver and pours out gold. He makes gifts for Athirat, mother of the gods: he casts silver by thousands of shekels, gold by tens of thousands; he makes a divine dais, a footstool of gold, a couch adorned with gold, a table full of every kind of creature, and bowls from the land of Amurru, shaped like the beasts of Yamhad, by the tens of thousands. The gifts are described with great splendour, the verse insisting again and again on the amount of gold and silver and the fineness of the work. Athirat is El's wife and mother of the gods; her sons, the seventy gods, all have their houses; if Baal is to ask her help, he must first bring gifts worthy of her rank. In Ugaritic society bringing gifts to the powerful to win their favour was common practice, and the gods of the myth keep the same custom. The passage also shows Kothar's skill: he can turn gold and silver into anything, and he will build Baal's palace too.

body_zh: 第二栏里，众神之母阿西拉特正在海边。她手里拿着纺锤，纺锤在她手中转动，她把衣服放进海里，把长袍浸在河中。她把锅放在火上，把碗放在炭上，像是在做家务。就在这时，她抬起眼睛，看见强大的巴力和少女阿娜特走来。她的双脚发抖，腰部打颤，脸上流汗。她大声说：强大的巴力为什么来了？少女阿娜特为什么来了？他们是来打我的儿子的吗？还是来消灭我的族人的？可是当她看见那些银子和金子的光芒，看见那些闪闪发亮的礼物，她就高兴了起来，吩咐她的仆人说：去看看那些工匠的手艺吧。她还让她的渔夫仆人去海里撒网捕鱼。阿西拉特在乌加里特神话中被称为“海上的阿西拉特”，与海有着密切的联系。她的恐惧不是没有理由的：巴力刚刚打败了海神雅姆，而雅姆被称为“伊勒的宠儿”，可能也是阿西拉特的孩子之一。在后面的故事里，巴力与阿西拉特的儿子们之间仍然存在着紧张关系。这一幕把一位众神之母的形象写得非常生动：她既威严，又会担心自己的孩子。
body_en: In column II Athirat, mother of the gods, is by the sea. She holds a spindle that turns in her hand; she puts her garments into the sea, her robes into the river; she sets a pot on the fire, a bowl on the coals, as if at household work. Then she lifts her eyes and sees Mightiest Baal and the maiden Anat coming. Her feet shake, her loins tremble, her face sweats. She cries: why has Mightiest Baal come? Why has the maiden Anat come? Have they come to smite my sons, or to make an end of my kin? But when she sees the gleam of the silver and gold, the shining gifts, she rejoices and tells her servant: look at the craftsmen's work. She bids her fisherman servant cast a net into the sea. Athirat is called 'Athirat of the Sea' in Ugaritic myth and is closely linked with it. Her fear has reason: Baal has just defeated Yamm, called 'beloved of El', who may have been one of her own children, and later in the cycle there is still tension between Baal and the sons of Athirat. The scene draws the mother of the gods vividly: majestic, and yet anxious for her children.

body_zh: 第三栏开头残缺，接着是巴力向众神抱怨自己在众神的集会上受到了侮辱：他站起来，说有人在众神的集会上对他吐唾沫。巴力憎恶两种宴会，驾云者憎恶三种：可耻的宴会，卑贱的宴会，女仆们放荡的宴会。在这些宴会上，可耻的事情被看见了，卑贱的事情发生了。巴力和阿娜特来到阿西拉特面前，献上礼物，向她恳求。阿西拉特问他们：你们为什么来恳求海上的阿西拉特？为什么来请求众神的创造者？你们恳求过公牛伊勒、仁慈的神吗？你们请求过万物的创造者吗？少女阿娜特回答说：我们先恳求海上的阿西拉特，请求众神的创造者，然后我们再去恳求他。于是他们一起吃喝，众神一起宴饮，用刀切下肥美的牛肉，用金杯喝着葡萄酒。阿西拉特的疑问很有意思：她提醒巴力和阿娜特，真正有权决定的是伊勒，而不是她。可是阿娜特的回答表明，她们的计划正是要让阿西拉特去说服伊勒。在乌加里特神话里，伊勒是众神的父亲和最高的决策者，阿西拉特则是唯一能直接影响他的人。
body_en: Column III opens broken; then Baal complains that he was insulted in the assembly of the gods: he stood and said someone spat upon him in the gathering of the gods. Two kinds of feast Baal hates, three the Rider of the Clouds: a feast of shame, a feast of baseness, and a feast where handmaids act lewdly — for there shame is seen and baseness done. Baal and Anat come before Athirat, bring their gifts and entreat her. Athirat asks them: why do you entreat Athirat of the Sea, beseech the creatress of the gods? Have you entreated Bull El the Kindly, or beseeched the creator of creatures? The maiden Anat answers: we entreat Athirat of the Sea, beseech the creatress of the gods first; afterwards we shall entreat him. So they eat and drink; the gods feast together, carving fat cattle with knives and drinking wine from golden cups. Athirat's question is telling: she reminds Baal and Anat that the real decision lies with El, not with her. But Anat's reply shows that their plan is exactly to have Athirat persuade El. In Ugaritic myth El is father of the gods and final authority, and Athirat is the one who can sway him directly.
